a23ae884-0691-4afd-aa44-431ef67e8fcc.title: interest rate
a23ae884-0691-4afd-aa44-431ef67e8fcc.description: A percentage at which interest is charged or paid.

29e348d4-54df-4dfb-9aed-fb1ec21457c1.title: numerical variable
29e348d4-54df-4dfb-9aed-fb1ec21457c1.description:
Variables whose values are numbers and for which arithmetic processes, such as adding and subtracting or calculating an average, make sense.

A discrete numerical variable is a numerical variable, each of whose possible values is separated from the next by a definite 'gap'. The most common numerical variables have the counting numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, … as possible values. Others are prices, measured in dollars and cents. For example, the number of children in a family or the number of days in a month.

648b3c2b-7556-414e-af87-2a282913b2b5.title: discrete variable
648b3c2b-7556-414e-af87-2a282913b2b5.description:
Individual and countable items that can be listed.

Extended in Mathematics Advanced: Also known as a discrete random variable.

5fedfd57-2a9a-486c-8483-66e0e1ce9c8c.title: continuous variable
5fedfd57-2a9a-486c-8483-66e0e1ce9c8c.description: A numerical variable that can take any value that lies within an interval. The values taken are subject to the accuracy of the measuring instrument used to obtain these values. For example, height, reaction time to a stimulus and systolic blood pressure.

6cb97161-d8d0-4053-80d5-8289f1671d17.title: budget
6cb97161-d8d0-4053-80d5-8289f1671d17.description: A tool for managing money and achieving financial goals. It is a list of all the expected income and costs for a certain period of time. A budget aims to balance the income and expenses, so that the expenses are less than or equal to the income.

1986fbff-8f9c-4f5e-ad06-f3d654db8948.title: discretionary spending
1986fbff-8f9c-4f5e-ad06-f3d654db8948.description: A type of spending that is not essential or mandatory. It includes expenses, such as entertainment, clothes and gifts, that can be varied based on choice and preference.

de249e0e-50a4-4fd6-afe6-7222dc3d2ab5.title: compass bearing
de249e0e-50a4-4fd6-afe6-7222dc3d2ab5.description: Angles either side of north or south. For example, a compass bearing of N50°E is found by facing north and moving through an angle of 50° to the east.

ee6f553b-9ecf-42e4-b8ad-c2dad9958bdf.title: trigonometric ratios
ee6f553b-9ecf-42e4-b8ad-c2dad9958bdf.description:
The relationship between the angles and sides of right-angled triangles. The 3 basic trigonometric ratios are sine, cosine and tangent.

See sine ratio, cosine ratio and tangent ratio

0750638a-4839-4747-9e28-e0af3e78285f.title: angle
0750638a-4839-4747-9e28-e0af3e78285f.description: Formed by 2 straight lines meeting at a common endpoint, called the vertex. An angle can describe the amount of turn between its 2 arms (lines).

0a9d0239-50bb-4e7a-851e-a9b82358899c.title: skewed
0a9d0239-50bb-4e7a-851e-a9b82358899c.description: A distribution is negatively skewed when its tail is on the left side. A distribution is positively skewed when its tail is on the right side.

13905cdc-5fb9-4f0e-905d-1210c37b1c95.title: maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem
13905cdc-5fb9-4f0e-905d-1210c37b1c95.description: The maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem states that the flow through a network cannot exceed the value of any cut in the network and that the maximum flow equals the value of the minimum cut, i.e. it identifies the bottleneck in the system.

6ac24599-070e-492c-8252-f9e06b7c0f37.title: path (networks)
6ac24599-070e-492c-8252-f9e06b7c0f37.description: A sequence of consecutive edges in a graph. The length of the path is the number of edges traversed.

dcc97f2e-2464-4083-9c67-f5dfb09bd463.title: tree (networks)
dcc97f2e-2464-4083-9c67-f5dfb09bd463.description: A tree is an undirected network in which any 2 vertices are connected by exactly one path.

c2b9cdab-80d4-45f6-965b-4d11f5f721f4.title: spanning tree
c2b9cdab-80d4-45f6-965b-4d11f5f721f4.description: A spanning tree of an undirected network diagram is a tree that includes all the vertices of the original network connected together, but not necessarily all the edges of the original network diagram. A network can have many different spanning trees.

63ee7eb7-1361-4bb8-b2c9-38c4dd4e94a5.title: minimum spanning tree
63ee7eb7-1361-4bb8-b2c9-38c4dd4e94a5.description: A tree of minimum length in a connected, undirected network. It connects all the vertices together with the minimum total weighting for the edges.

91acbc32-b7be-4ccf-ab2a-451ef1112f1e.title: decimal
91acbc32-b7be-4ccf-ab2a-451ef1112f1e.description: Used to describe aspects of the base-10 number system. The decimal point (. or ,) separates the whole number part of a number from its decimal part.

165fe8db-c2ea-44d4-80d1-f52aae60dc84.title: inflation
165fe8db-c2ea-44d4-80d1-f52aae60dc84.description: A general increase in the prices of goods and services over time.

3c54c871-a4e1-4f63-9a7a-650915177162.title: appreciation
3c54c871-a4e1-4f63-9a7a-650915177162.description: An increase in the value of an asset over time. The appreciated value is the value an asset has increased to over that time.

85e16edb-42a4-4df8-9a6f-672ef71e42d8.title: circle
85e16edb-42a4-4df8-9a6f-672ef71e42d8.description: All points equal to a given distance from a fixed point, the centre. When used to describe a shape, a circle includes all points inside the boundary.

6668a596-7d1c-4dc7-89e2-e83d3d6070ef.title: sector
6668a596-7d1c-4dc7-89e2-e83d3d6070ef.description: The plane figure enclosed by 2 radii or a circle and the arc between them.

c2df930b-cbe1-40d0-ba7d-ef9c9afae75b.title: composite shape
c2df930b-cbe1-40d0-ba7d-ef9c9afae75b.description: A shape that is formed by combining other plane shapes. Composite shapes are often described as 'complex' when they are made up of many and different shapes.

3ede57ff-d618-4084-9158-f2f97828b9bd.title: transaction
3ede57ff-d618-4084-9158-f2f97828b9bd.description: A purchase or payment made using a credit card. It can include purchases made in-store or online, cash advances and balance transfers.

f3fa1459-55cd-46c7-9855-0f3ee004ca49.title: balance
f3fa1459-55cd-46c7-9855-0f3ee004ca49.description: The difference between the total debit entries and the total credit entries of an account during a financial period.

82ec330d-698b-4bde-ac3a-0e7807d63070.title: brokerage
82ec330d-698b-4bde-ac3a-0e7807d63070.description: The commission earned by a broker when buying and selling shares. Brokerage can be charged at a flat rate or as a percentage of the sale.

f329ba7d-b9c0-4dc3-9627-716c30275688.title: cost
f329ba7d-b9c0-4dc3-9627-716c30275688.description: The price paid to acquire, produce, accomplish or maintain anything.

4acda2fa-cc7b-43ec-809c-b555ba41e3c2.title: term deposit
4acda2fa-cc7b-43ec-809c-b555ba41e3c2.description: A deposit held in a bank for a fixed term to which a fixed interest rate is applied.

9dff933f-9770-48a8-a6e8-1dc2ec70b467.title: scale drawing
9dff933f-9770-48a8-a6e8-1dc2ec70b467.description: A drawing of a real object with accurate sizes reduced or enlarged by the scale factor.

6c2f8504-5a3a-4f1c-89dd-1d60effc1927.title: line of best fit
6c2f8504-5a3a-4f1c-89dd-1d60effc1927.description: A line drawn through a scatter plot of data points that represents the nature of the relationship between 2 variables.

b89402ed-7191-41b4-bbeb-80069c81355b.title: fraction
b89402ed-7191-41b4-bbeb-80069c81355b.description:
The result of a division. For example, 2 divided by 4 produces quarters. Fractions also represent:

  • a relationship or ratio
  • parts when a whole is partitioned into equal parts
  • numbers between whole numbers
  • units of measure.

78c50333-0dc1-41c8-8393-1d3b247115e0.title: edge
78c50333-0dc1-41c8-8393-1d3b247115e0.description: The line segment formed by the intersection of two faces of a polyhedron, e.g. a cube has 6 faces and 12 edges.

d9080984-2f08-43d5-9d7f-cb0589e49a5a.title: fuel consumption rate
d9080984-2f08-43d5-9d7f-cb0589e49a5a.description: The fuel consumption rate of a vehicle measures how much fuel it uses and is usually measured in litres per 100 kilometres (L/100 km).

e935ee9d-b2c1-40ad-a995-8300a7b0fa81.title: taxable income
e935ee9d-b2c1-40ad-a995-8300a7b0fa81.description: The amount of yearly income that is used to calculate an individual’s or company’s payable income tax.

21a239b0-ebc1-451e-bb03-af27b39b7003.title: deduction
21a239b0-ebc1-451e-bb03-af27b39b7003.description: An expense incurred by a worker in relation to their job or profession and which can be taken away from annual earnings to obtain the taxable income. Deductions form part of an individual’s or a company’s tax return.

9896e901-f3b1-4647-a783-b1f37607961d.title: forward scanning (networks)
9896e901-f3b1-4647-a783-b1f37607961d.description: In critical path analysis, forward scanning identifies the earliest starting time for each activity in an activity network.

e94f5827-4f44-4551-821a-1d954196e582.title: backward scanning (networks)
e94f5827-4f44-4551-821a-1d954196e582.description: The process of systematically determining the latest starting time for each activity as part of critical path analysis.

a34c1a53-61b2-40f1-907f-b5fae9a4b16d.title: earliest starting time (EST)
a34c1a53-61b2-40f1-907f-b5fae9a4b16d.description: The earliest time that any activity can be started after all prior activities have been completed.

a1e78b13-f94b-43c4-89d4-1565cee97f6c.title: latest starting time (LST)
a1e78b13-f94b-43c4-89d4-1565cee97f6c.description: The latest time an activity may be started after all prior activities have been completed and without delaying the project.

7f4841e1-705f-4fe0-a9c6-23e3567d3ab2.title: credit card
7f4841e1-705f-4fe0-a9c6-23e3567d3ab2.description: A method for borrowing funds to purchase goods and services. Banks or financial institutions agree to loan an amount of money to an individual up to a pre-approved limit, and the individual agrees to pay back the amount plus any interest and fees that are charged.

26255d73-3f37-437b-9467-9e4fabc2cb06.title: population
26255d73-3f37-437b-9467-9e4fabc2cb06.description:
The complete set of individuals, objects, places, etc., that we want information about.

Extended in Mathematics Standard and Mathematics Extension 1: In statistics it is the entire dataset from which a statistical sample may be drawn.

34ff576c-150f-4dd1-b2cb-cfe20d7d7827.title: independent variable
34ff576c-150f-4dd1-b2cb-cfe20d7d7827.description: The variable that is deliberately changed, often through a series of pre-set values.

ee4c5696-bb05-4660-b565-cf5ec9dbb64c.title: dataset
ee4c5696-bb05-4660-b565-cf5ec9dbb64c.description: A collection of data combined for a specific purpose.

6afcf1d1-faf7-4686-8a39-fd87d8a919aa.title: infographic
6afcf1d1-faf7-4686-8a39-fd87d8a919aa.description: A chart, diagram or illustration (as in a book or magazine or on a website) that uses graphic elements to present information in a visually striking way.

a3b2806d-3b29-41df-b3b2-778cef2b3c5c.title: float time
a3b2806d-3b29-41df-b3b2-778cef2b3c5c.description: Float time is the amount of time that a task in a project network can be delayed without causing a delay to subsequent tasks.

2d6774ad-ffd3-4644-b5ca-03fa11249ada.title: critical activity (networks)
2d6774ad-ffd3-4644-b5ca-03fa11249ada.description: Activities that must be completed on time to ensure that the project is completed on schedule. These activities have zero float, meaning that any delay in these tasks will extend the project’s timeline.

78584f44-ac7b-4958-b5fa-c29453ea1afd.title: non-critical activities (networks)
78584f44-ac7b-4958-b5fa-c29453ea1afd.description: Activities that can be delayed without affecting the project’s completion time.

643e34ef-e459-4646-839e-8bb3706ab9e2.title: distance–time graph
643e34ef-e459-4646-839e-8bb3706ab9e2.description: A line graph that relates distance and time, with time on the horizontal axis and distance on the vertical axis.

eaff39f1-b778-4dd2-9291-d74810b6f846.title: distance
eaff39f1-b778-4dd2-9291-d74810b6f846.description: The length between 2 points. Distance is a positive scalar quantity.

02c67844-302d-49c2-9e7e-cb7b251d3764.title: five (5)-number summary
02c67844-302d-49c2-9e7e-cb7b251d3764.description: A method for summarising a dataset using 5 statistics: the minimum value, the lower quartile, the median, the upper quartile and the maximum value.

4b14e6a1-83a1-4cdb-abed-d134ef1712f6.title: numerical data
4b14e6a1-83a1-4cdb-abed-d134ef1712f6.description: Data associated with a numerical variable. Also known as quantitative data.

81f8d6e1-34b7-4b5c-b461-da4fec2964da.title: trial
81f8d6e1-34b7-4b5c-b461-da4fec2964da.description:
A single performance of a random experiment. Successive trials refer to repeated performances of the same experiment, each of which will therefore have the same set of possible outcomes (sample space).

When there are only 2 possible outcomes they are known as Bernoulli trials.

ae90c167-bde6-4f7f-aca5-2e0735f29c3e.title: array
ae90c167-bde6-4f7f-aca5-2e0735f29c3e.description: One of several different arrangements that can be used to model multiplicative situations. It is made by arranging a set of objects, such as counters, into columns and rows. Each column must contain the same number of objects as the other columns, and each row must contain the same number of objects as the other rows.

d5c3e90b-2e44-4dc7-a793-6623fcac0f23.title: tree diagram
d5c3e90b-2e44-4dc7-a793-6623fcac0f23.description:
A diagram consisting of line segments (edges) connected to points (vertices) like the branches of a tree. It shows the relationship between sets, events or the set of outcomes of a multi-step random experiment.

See probability tree

c3a28ce2-a59d-4443-bfa3-4b11afa134f2.title: variable
c3a28ce2-a59d-4443-bfa3-4b11afa134f2.description: A factor that can be changed, kept the same or measured in an investigation.

ad3654f3-f298-4dbb-9b3a-64506223781c.title: correlation
ad3654f3-f298-4dbb-9b3a-64506223781c.description: A measure of the strength of the linear relationship between 2 variables.

5487331f-2bd9-4ad2-8613-fa8434620413.title: causal
5487331f-2bd9-4ad2-8613-fa8434620413.description: Two variables with a relationship which indicates that one event is the result of the occurrence of the other event.

08ec5c33-3988-4891-ae45-44e70e4bb2e7.title: minimum payment
08ec5c33-3988-4891-ae45-44e70e4bb2e7.description: The lowest amount of money required for a borrower to pay off their credit card balance each month to remain in good standing with the credit card company.

fb27d748-f16d-4611-926f-be208b673143.title: multiples
fb27d748-f16d-4611-926f-be208b673143.description: Products formed using the same base number multiplied by different whole numbers, e.g. 3, 6, 9, 12 …

b3dad9d9-11c1-4bec-a697-219016a1ffe2.title: interest-free period
b3dad9d9-11c1-4bec-a697-219016a1ffe2.description: A period of time during which no interest is charged or paid on a loan or a credit card. It is usually offered as an incentive for customers to borrow or spend money.

ff757a0f-741c-483a-aed5-b9acb1709b17.title: network
ff757a0f-741c-483a-aed5-b9acb1709b17.description:
A system of interconnected digital devices and/or people.

See social network

1b393be2-7d6a-43e2-a2c2-90e460ac7b77.title: interpolate/interpolation
1b393be2-7d6a-43e2-a2c2-90e460ac7b77.description: Making predictions between known data values. For example, working between 2 known points on a graph to predict a value in between these points.

078bda43-5b72-4881-b52c-4216f23955ac.title: extrapolate/extrapolation
078bda43-5b72-4881-b52c-4216f23955ac.description: Occurs when the fitted model, such as a line of best fit, is used to make predictions using values that are outside the range of the original data upon which the fitted model was based.

4feb28c1-eaa0-483c-86e4-a88fe8ca3000.title: linear model
4feb28c1-eaa0-483c-86e4-a88fe8ca3000.description: A straight-line graph or equation fitted to a practical situation or set of data.

77555aaf-d11a-4f6b-a985-d93b83252f22.title: box plot
77555aaf-d11a-4f6b-a985-d93b83252f22.description:
A synonym for a box-and-whisker plot. A graphical display of a 5-number summary of data. The ‘box’ covers the middle 50% of scores. The ‘whiskers’ extend to the maximum and minimum values in the dataset.

In a box plot, the 'box' covers the interquartile range (IQR). A vertical line in the box is used to indicate the location of the median.

The box plot below has been constructed from the 5-number summary of the resting pulse rates of 17 students.

064c3046-3b3a-4552-b745-5bd14361ef37.title: capture-recapture technique
064c3046-3b3a-4552-b745-5bd14361ef37.description: A method for estimating the size of a population that is difficult to count directly. It involves capturing a random sample of the population, marking them with tags or labels, and releasing them back into the population. After some time, a second random sample is captured, and the number of marked individuals is recorded. Based on the ratio of marked to unmarked individuals in the second sample, the total population size can be estimated.

5551f3b1-f9bb-459c-a1ac-01931cc54368.title: data
5551f3b1-f9bb-459c-a1ac-01931cc54368.description: A discrete representation of information using number codes. Data may include characters (e.g. alphabetic letters, numbers and symbols), images, sounds and/or instructions that, when represented by number codes, can be manipulated, stored and communicated by digital systems. For example, characters may be represented using ASCII code or images may be represented by a bitmap of numbers representing each ‘dot’ or pixel.

dc261d21-472b-46ba-b2aa-b1e4da8ccc7f.title: experiment (random)
dc261d21-472b-46ba-b2aa-b1e4da8ccc7f.description: A process with an observable result. The results of the experiment are the set of possible outcomes called the sample space.

9bd55856-6c47-4d86-b502-2ba102b76c50.title: shape
9bd55856-6c47-4d86-b502-2ba102b76c50.description: To develop, structure and refine a creative work.

ed3ced8b-3547-4100-a857-6e6ddfcf56ab.title: capacity (internal volume)
ed3ced8b-3547-4100-a857-6e6ddfcf56ab.description:
Generally refers to the amount a container can hold.

A term used to describe how much a container will hold. It is often used in relation to the volume of fluids. Units of capacity (volume of fluids or gases) include litres and millilitres.

See internal volume (capacity)

52568f59-c0fb-46ba-8bdf-7aad1a28adac.title: shortest path
52568f59-c0fb-46ba-8bdf-7aad1a28adac.description: A shortest path in a network diagram is a path between 2 vertices in a network where the sum of the weights of its edges are minimised.

1b90898f-0cd8-4378-9e48-96acef2a41b3.title: rate
1b90898f-0cd8-4378-9e48-96acef2a41b3.description: A comparison of 2 quantities of different kinds. For example, a speed of 60km/h is a rate because it compares quantities of distance and time.

40ba7f31-446b-4516-a811-4ad333acd142.title: loan
40ba7f31-446b-4516-a811-4ad333acd142.description: An amount of money borrowed from a bank or other financial institution.

c610c65a-c9a8-4c91-bd81-512e9f1978a6.title: stamp duty
c610c65a-c9a8-4c91-bd81-512e9f1978a6.description: A tax payable to the government for transactions and documents, such as motor vehicle registrations and transfers, insurance policies and mortgages.

a86e2035-3323-456c-8d1f-2e51d33eae54.title: range (of a dataset)
a86e2035-3323-456c-8d1f-2e51d33eae54.description: The difference between the highest and lowest values in a dataset.

54aa43ed-156b-473f-a7c2-5ac4e7259131.title: standard deviation
54aa43ed-156b-473f-a7c2-5ac4e7259131.description:
A measure of the variability or spread of a dataset. It gives an indication of the degree to which the individual data values are spread around their mean.

Extended in Mathematics Standard and Advanced: For a random variable, the standard deviation is the square root of its variance.

It provides a measure of the spread of the probability density function.

38778f01-0cf8-4f99-8647-a182c5c66a27.title: measure of spread
38778f01-0cf8-4f99-8647-a182c5c66a27.description: In statistics, different methods of calculating the variability of a set. The most commonly used measures of spread are the range, interquartile range and standard deviation.

2051f259-0e2c-48a7-b7fe-5b808ef3edec.title: surface area
2051f259-0e2c-48a7-b7fe-5b808ef3edec.description: The measure of the total area of the surface(s) of a three-dimensional shape or object. For example, the surface area of a cube with side length of 5 units is 150 square units.

82c92e54-7f1a-4f0d-a500-820d9d65ed08.title: cylinder
82c92e54-7f1a-4f0d-a500-820d9d65ed08.description: An object that has parallel circular discs of equal radius at the ends that are joined by a curved surface.

bc0f027a-a660-4056-8bc9-074b1b8e82a1.title: deposit
bc0f027a-a660-4056-8bc9-074b1b8e82a1.description: A sum of money that is used for financial reasons. An amount of money that is placed in a bank or other financial institution either as a lump sum or as a regular payment, or an initial payment when purchasing something, with the rest to be payable later.

938aef6b-1816-4fec-9b31-d5190df15ab8.title: repayment
938aef6b-1816-4fec-9b31-d5190df15ab8.description: A set amount, paid at regular intervals over the period of a loan, to pay off a loan.

2ac1c7d0-22d9-4684-9dee-257ef95686b4.title: bias
2ac1c7d0-22d9-4684-9dee-257ef95686b4.description: A systematic favouring of certain outcomes more than others, due to unfair influence (knowingly or otherwise).

a18e913f-8e09-47e3-8427-b4f270af9016.title: culture
a18e913f-8e09-47e3-8427-b4f270af9016.description: The customs, habits, beliefs/spirituality, social organisation and ways of life that characterise different groups and communities. Cultural characteristics give a group or individual a sense of who they are and help them make sense of the world in which they live. Culture is a shared system but inherently diverse – there can be individual and group differences within cultures. Everyone has culture – it is a lens through which we see the world.

22659865-0859-4167-80b7-d0b5633bd5a2.title: wage
22659865-0859-4167-80b7-d0b5633bd5a2.description: An amount of money that is paid for work or services, based on the time spent or the work done. It is usually calculated by the hour, day or week, and paid at regular intervals, such as daily, weekly or fortnightly.

75fbc825-2b4c-4053-a905-7c79596748be.title: penalty rate
75fbc825-2b4c-4053-a905-7c79596748be.description: A rate of pay determined by an award, higher than the usual rate, in compensation for working outside normal hours, such as time-and-a-half and double-time.

8a002a99-812a-42f0-b889-ff77297604be.title: overtime
8a002a99-812a-42f0-b889-ff77297604be.description:
Time worked before or after regular scheduled working hours. A higher rate of pay is often earnt during this time, known as penalty rates.

See penalty rate

8ce981c6-e4bb-4840-8416-a81bf7664567.title: lump-sum payment
8ce981c6-e4bb-4840-8416-a81bf7664567.description: A single amount paid instead of smaller instalments. Often used in the context of a loan or investment.

3fb1dbb7-6268-48c4-b2e5-55b79fc60b44.title: obtuse angle
3fb1dbb7-6268-48c4-b2e5-55b79fc60b44.description: An angle bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight angle (2 right angles, or 180°).

a3008706-c985-4e89-b2bc-27430ee038d4.title: critical path
a3008706-c985-4e89-b2bc-27430ee038d4.description: The sequence of network activities that combine to have the longest overall duration so as to determine the shortest possible time needed to complete a project.

9e7f4659-9423-48fa-91a1-9501717c900d.title: cluster
9e7f4659-9423-48fa-91a1-9501717c900d.description: A group of data points that are close together or have similar values.

87d02b1e-9d65-46b0-b71e-c7e519433ead.title: outlier
87d02b1e-9d65-46b0-b71e-c7e519433ead.description: A data value that appears to stand out from the other members of the dataset by being unusually high or low.

ee9081aa-fa88-4abf-85d2-57d9541aa285.title: declining balance depreciation
ee9081aa-fa88-4abf-85d2-57d9541aa285.description: The value of an asset is depreciated by a fixed percentage of its initial value each year.

e086bbae-f0eb-443b-87ae-04c8baec965f.title: scatter plot
e086bbae-f0eb-443b-87ae-04c8baec965f.description: A graph of 2 variables where individual data points are plotted on a horizontal and vertical axis. Scatter plots are used to observe relationships between variables.

efd3aeef-e175-4f4d-93ad-3822b32b4130.title: outcome
efd3aeef-e175-4f4d-93ad-3822b32b4130.description: Possible result from an experiment or trial.

e98f972a-59a3-4510-952c-cd57321c1cb7.title: tax return
e98f972a-59a3-4510-952c-cd57321c1cb7.description: A tax return is an annual statement of all income, allowable deductions, PAYG tax paid and other personal financial information so as to allow the Australian Taxation Office to calculate the amount of income tax an individual should pay for the financial year.

f94aff5c-ee96-4aa3-8bbf-15ace436922d.title: simultaneous equations
f94aff5c-ee96-4aa3-8bbf-15ace436922d.description: A set of 2 or more equations, each containing 2 or more variables whose values can simultaneously satisfy all the equations in the set, the number of variables being equal to or less than the number of equations in the set.

f0f933e6-32b5-4763-8829-1b24cc6a27a6.title: break-even point
f0f933e6-32b5-4763-8829-1b24cc6a27a6.description: The point at which income from production and cost of production are equal.

ad24a683-8502-4c6c-bc86-f1660f225e55.title: revenue
ad24a683-8502-4c6c-bc86-f1660f225e55.description: The total income generated from normal business operations, such as from the sale of items produced.

9b24a09a-0d6e-4ab0-bbec-73c502f98e5f.title: interest factors
9b24a09a-0d6e-4ab0-bbec-73c502f98e5f.description: The values of an investment at a specific date. A table of these factors can be used to calculate the future value of different amounts of money that are invested at a certain interest rate for a specified period of time.

6cc33933-b019-46d3-acf2-a705a835c303.title: future value
6cc33933-b019-46d3-acf2-a705a835c303.description: The total value of an investment or annuity at the end of a specified term, including all contributions and interest earned.

e9284b7b-68c6-4271-b8c8-27564d5179c1.title: present value
e9284b7b-68c6-4271-b8c8-27564d5179c1.description: The single sum of money (or principal) that could be initially invested to produce a future value over a given period of time.

2c941e7b-b69e-48c9-9637-e56d29fd2d16.title: kilowatt hour (kwh)
2c941e7b-b69e-48c9-9637-e56d29fd2d16.description: A unit of energy that measures how much electricity is used or produced over a period of time. It is equal to the amount of energy delivered by one kilowatt of power for 1 hour.

21308249-6260-4ce9-a1ee-82c723596e23.title: Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)
21308249-6260-4ce9-a1ee-82c723596e23.description: The primary time standard used across the world. It is based on International Atomic Time, which is measured by atomic clocks, with leap seconds added occasionally to keep it close to the earth’s rotation. For every 15° longitude east or west of the Prime Meridian (known as 0° longitude), the time changes by 1 hour.

aa93cf25-447d-478d-9a26-0fa964f39edc.title: commission
aa93cf25-447d-478d-9a26-0fa964f39edc.description: The sum or percentage paid for services, e.g. to an agent or salesperson.

f431a981-9636-41dd-afac-42c3995a5501.title: piecework
f431a981-9636-41dd-afac-42c3995a5501.description: Employment where a worker is paid a fixed rate for each item produced or action performed regardless of the time taken.

147b3b13-2612-42f0-928a-39c1d103ae95.title: royalties
147b3b13-2612-42f0-928a-39c1d103ae95.description: Payment made to the owner or creator of a product or intellectual property, such as a patent, novel, song or artwork. Typically calculated as a percentage of the total sales.

a9fd9383-23c7-42a1-8345-6ecc6640942f.title: government payments
a9fd9383-23c7-42a1-8345-6ecc6640942f.description: Payments made by the government to individuals to provide financial support.

3475db1c-8ff5-4a49-b2c7-e845b22584d5.title: linear
3475db1c-8ff5-4a49-b2c7-e845b22584d5.description: Something that can be represented or modelled by a straight line.

b6ca4481-5320-46a4-8bba-89aeea94f0dd.title: net earnings
b6ca4481-5320-46a4-8bba-89aeea94f0dd.description: The amount of gross pay remaining after tax and other deductions have been made.

a1ee4805-ed41-43d6-aa0f-d3d2110213c2.title: source
a1ee4805-ed41-43d6-aa0f-d3d2110213c2.description: Any written or non-written materials that can be used to investigate the past.

7a3deee1-ee1a-4998-9a45-9190cdd23205.title: sink (networks)
7a3deee1-ee1a-4998-9a45-9190cdd23205.description: In a network flow diagram it is a vertex that has no outgoing edges and only incoming edges. It represents the destination of the flow in the network.

57f617df-06ca-49a8-9e15-88b4b77760cf.title: outflow (networks)
57f617df-06ca-49a8-9e15-88b4b77760cf.description: The amount of flow that leaves a vertex in a network flow diagram. Outflow is calculated as the total flow of the edges exiting a vertex.

a6e3a590-1c4d-4a25-84b4-637c2dfdc3d3.title: inflow (networks)
a6e3a590-1c4d-4a25-84b4-637c2dfdc3d3.description: The amount of flow that enters a vertex in a network flow diagram. Inflow is calculated as the total flow of the edges arriving at a vertex.

71187810-5c32-4934-a5ba-eee5d91603be.title: cut (networks)
71187810-5c32-4934-a5ba-eee5d91603be.description: In a flow network, a cut partitions the vertices of a graph into 2 separate groups so that the source is in one group and the sink in the other.

36091d41-ba70-4cd2-b290-7c6160821489.title: dividend yield
36091d41-ba70-4cd2-b290-7c6160821489.description: The dividend expressed as a percentage of the current share price.

02126b1c-7e62-4d13-a354-8e20e0fde9d9.title: profit
02126b1c-7e62-4d13-a354-8e20e0fde9d9.description: The excess of total revenue above the total cost of selling goods or services.

5055083a-105f-4d61-b2da-ae1727c8926f.title: loss
5055083a-105f-4d61-b2da-ae1727c8926f.description: The difference between the total cost and the total revenue of producing and selling goods or services where the cost is greater than the revenue.

3e30f011-13ea-496e-a69f-f3e601b1e0ae.title: association
3e30f011-13ea-496e-a69f-f3e601b1e0ae.description: Relationship between pairs of numerical variables, e.g. in terms of strength, form and direction.

5b9505ce-eac9-4acf-ab4c-17d7fbf57542.title: mass
5b9505ce-eac9-4acf-ab4c-17d7fbf57542.description: The amount of matter in an object.

0965f09a-1371-479f-979b-35da0ddbd230.title: precedence table
0965f09a-1371-479f-979b-35da0ddbd230.description: A table that lists all the activities involved in a project, along with their expected durations and immediate predecessors.

96390ba3-2af0-465c-a943-71f75dfb4d44.title: dummy activities
96390ba3-2af0-465c-a943-71f75dfb4d44.description: Operations in a network that require no time nor any resources. They are imaginary activities shown in a project network to identify the dependence among activities. They are usually represented by a dashed directed edge.

66c243ea-7db9-44a4-a669-1308d4c88ea6.title: bivariate data
66c243ea-7db9-44a4-a669-1308d4c88ea6.description: Data relating to measurement of 2 variables. It can be categorical data, numerical data or a combination of both.

cf354630-4322-417c-8772-c5e6ce8096e1.title: latitude
cf354630-4322-417c-8772-c5e6ce8096e1.description: The angular distance of a point on the Earth’s surface north or south from the equator.

47528968-a264-4dc7-8798-39e780ad995b.title: longitude
47528968-a264-4dc7-8798-39e780ad995b.description: The angular distance of a point on the Earth’s surface east or west from the Greenwich meridian.

107324bb-64d1-47d6-967c-06e51061e9c9.title: position coordinates
107324bb-64d1-47d6-967c-06e51061e9c9.description: Used to describe the location of a point on the Earth’s surface expressed in degrees of longitude and latitude.

4734c6ca-f40b-4c66-9a8a-3e1780773c57.title: reducing balance loan
4734c6ca-f40b-4c66-9a8a-3e1780773c57.description: A reducing balance loan is a compound interest loan where the loan is repaid by making regular payments and the interest paid is calculated on the amount still owing (the reducing balance of the loan) after each payment is made.

f7fde033-5fb1-42bf-985f-9d4a05617a12.title: interquartile range (IQR)
f7fde033-5fb1-42bf-985f-9d4a05617a12.description: The IQR is the width of an interval that contains the middle 50% (approximately) of the data values.

ea23e207-f381-4891-bd05-7f9ffba786b3.title: equivalent
ea23e207-f381-4891-bd05-7f9ffba786b3.description:
Two things are equivalent if they have the same value.

See equal, equals sign

9bdc8ee4-badd-4ad2-8f6e-7ef0ddb58509.title: least-squares regression line
9bdc8ee4-badd-4ad2-8f6e-7ef0ddb58509.description: The line that minimises the sum of the squares of the residuals. Also known as the least-squares line of best fit.

7129b4fc-b867-4c2b-a402-d5e656c34740.title: buy now, pay later
7129b4fc-b867-4c2b-a402-d5e656c34740.description: A service that allows a consumer to purchase a product and pay the cost in instalments. There is no interest charged on the purchase price, but there may be fees, such as an account set-up fee and late payment fees.

5061d752-002d-4c09-9ea9-26c844aee0a8.title: flow capacity
5061d752-002d-4c09-9ea9-26c844aee0a8.description:
The flow capacity of a network can be found using the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem and depends upon the capacity of each edge in the network.

See maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem

19a47b56-ab63-4d5a-96ce-bbd2ce3857bc.title: saturated edges
19a47b56-ab63-4d5a-96ce-bbd2ce3857bc.description: Edges that have zero excess flow capacity.

a421696e-5934-47d0-9db1-75db6502f20d.title: frequency distribution
a421696e-5934-47d0-9db1-75db6502f20d.description:
A visual display that organises and presents frequency counts of scores so that the information can be interpreted more easily.

Frequency distributions can be displayed in tabular or graphical form.

afffe6e1-0cf5-4048-99ae-03e33c189b92.title: cumulative frequency
afffe6e1-0cf5-4048-99ae-03e33c189b92.description: The accumulating total of frequencies within an ordered dataset.

2c1494c6-6322-4e86-a08c-32bb66158a71.title: mean
2c1494c6-6322-4e86-a08c-32bb66158a71.description: The sum of values in a dataset divided by the total number of values in the dataset. Also called the average.

c8bd5f36-3c30-4bb9-b84e-df1a1819a46f.title: median
c8bd5f36-3c30-4bb9-b84e-df1a1819a46f.description:
The value in a set of ordered data that divides the data into 2 parts. It is frequently called the 'middle value'.

Extended in Mathematics Standard and Advanced: If the number of values in the ordered dataset is even, it is the average of the two middle values. If the number of values in the dataset is odd, the median is the middle value.

36cea914-6762-4653-babb-217290266149.title: mode
36cea914-6762-4653-babb-217290266149.description:
The most frequently occurring value in a set of data.

Extended in 7–10: There can be more than one mode. When there are 2 modes, the dataset is said to be bimodal.

61cc47b8-4c82-4c12-8d57-0606d0b5434b.title: measure of centre
61cc47b8-4c82-4c12-8d57-0606d0b5434b.description: A statistic that is used to summarise a dataset. There are 3 common measures of centre for a dataset: mode, median and mean.

bbf8f22a-98ca-4c80-83c2-5aab5bda5746.title: pattern
bbf8f22a-98ca-4c80-83c2-5aab5bda5746.description: A pattern is made up of a number of elements that repeat or follow a rule.

0aa903f6-b54b-4068-b0d6-017e68d2c81d.title: stem-and-leaf plot
0aa903f6-b54b-4068-b0d6-017e68d2c81d.description:
A method of organising and displaying numerical data in which each data value is split into 2 parts, a 'stem' and a 'leaf'. For example, the stem-and-leaf plot below displays the resting pulse rates of 19 students. The stem is on the left side of the vertical line and the leaves are on the right side.

See back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot

ac3e10a1-36b0-436e-894a-1654f076d710.title: back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot
ac3e10a1-36b0-436e-894a-1654f076d710.description:
A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot is a method for comparing 2 data distributions by attaching 2 sets of 'leaves' to the same 'stem'; e.g. the stem-and-leaf plot below displays the distribution of pulse rates of 19 students before and after gentle exercise.

In this plot, the stem unit is ‘10’ and the leaf unit is ‘1’. Thus, the third row in the plot, 8 8 6 2 | 8 | 6 7 8 8, displays pulse rates of 88, 88, 86, 82 before exercise and 86, 87, 88, 88 after exercise.

6698c75c-0ac9-4acd-aa04-e736b1d5c5ac.title: pronumeral
6698c75c-0ac9-4acd-aa04-e736b1d5c5ac.description: A letter or symbol that is used to represent a value in a problem that can vary or change. Also known as a variable.

83471366-2bf0-4666-aee2-d0bea6c7a774.title: goods and services tax (GST)
83471366-2bf0-4666-aee2-d0bea6c7a774.description: An indirect tax that is levied at a flat percentage (rate) on most goods and services sold in Australia.

9f21814a-eedb-4b52-9fd4-c0be3c28dcfa.title: value-added tax (VAT)
9f21814a-eedb-4b52-9fd4-c0be3c28dcfa.description: A type of sales tax that is added to the purchase price of each item. VAT is used in many countries, usually as a percentage of the purchase price.

592e86c0-b16f-4d3a-baa2-c77a7f0e8685.title: hyperbolic
592e86c0-b16f-4d3a-baa2-c77a7f0e8685.description:
Having the shape of a hyperbola.

See hyperbola

da069c10-bf6a-4115-a1c2-b5061ff9923c.title: annuity
da069c10-bf6a-4115-a1c2-b5061ff9923c.description: A compound interest investment to which payments are made, or a single sum invested from which payments are received, on a regular basis for a fixed period of time.

303edba0-bed8-4b6f-8161-95ae906640e6.title: contribution
303edba0-bed8-4b6f-8161-95ae906640e6.description: An amount of money that is paid into an annuity. The contribution can be made as a lump sum or as a series of payments.

f32be3a3-a48e-4287-b1f9-8312ed3f514e.title: interest
f32be3a3-a48e-4287-b1f9-8312ed3f514e.description: Money paid or received in return for using or lending money.

964c68fd-58e1-498e-9530-13523f44e12e.title: investment
964c68fd-58e1-498e-9530-13523f44e12e.description: An allocation of money or capital into an asset or venture that is expected to generate a profit or return.

04324eee-6bc1-41f3-9027-35d37388799f.title: withdrawal
04324eee-6bc1-41f3-9027-35d37388799f.description: The act of taking money out of a bank account or an investment.

93aa649d-06f6-4297-95e8-840f92b13162.title: radial survey
93aa649d-06f6-4297-95e8-840f92b13162.description: A radial survey can be used to measure the area of an irregular block of land. In a radial survey, a central point is chosen within the block of land and measurements are taken along intervals from this point to each vertex. The angles between these intervals at the central point are also measured and recorded.

bf8eac05-b182-4aea-8e66-3a5d0ca9da9c.title: unit price
bf8eac05-b182-4aea-8e66-3a5d0ca9da9c.description: The price per agreed unit of a product or service, such as per kilogram, per dozen or per item. It is used to compare the cost of different quantities or packages of the same product or service.

a6c257b6-f1ae-41be-a3b3-68ba2bd93f20.title: best buy
a6c257b6-f1ae-41be-a3b3-68ba2bd93f20.description: A product or service that offers the most benefits or quality for the lowest price. It is found by comparing different purchase options and choosing the one that has the best value for money, e.g. by comparing unit prices.

24ffe884-288a-4d14-8352-989b25e91bb0.title: operation
24ffe884-288a-4d14-8352-989b25e91bb0.description: The process of combining numbers or expressions. Operations are arithmetic – addition, subtraction, multiplication and division – and also include exponentiation and substitution.

6c4711b9-a854-43ab-bcc3-65f4cd54b238.title: categorical variable
6c4711b9-a854-43ab-bcc3-65f4cd54b238.description: A variable whose values belong to exactly one of a number of categories. A categorical variable describes a quality or characteristic of something. Sometimes called a discrete variable. There are 2 types of categorical variables: nominal and ordinal. For example, your home state or blood type are categorical variables.

a27388a3-21cb-4616-a892-6ec6242381e5.title: nominal variable
a27388a3-21cb-4616-a892-6ec6242381e5.description: A type of categorical variable whose values have no natural order in which they may be placed, e.g. eye colour.

0087edac-128f-4fa2-9b26-4a47dd7783b4.title: ordinal variable
0087edac-128f-4fa2-9b26-4a47dd7783b4.description: A type of categorical variable whose responses have a natural order. For example, level of happiness: very unhappy, unhappy, neutral, happy, very happy.

14ad6963-dff3-4b92-9202-5eea86d8ef13.title: categorical data
14ad6963-dff3-4b92-9202-5eea86d8ef13.description: Data associated with a categorical variable. Also known as qualitative data.

3572cfb3-8236-4be3-a4a6-2e79ddb3a98b.title: salary
3572cfb3-8236-4be3-a4a6-2e79ddb3a98b.description: A fixed regular payment made by an employer to an employee for their work or services. The amount of salary paid is usually expressed as an annual sum, which is then divided into equal payments over the course of the year such as weekly, fortnightly or monthly.

91753839-7474-4f47-b33e-b23766f542ea.title: pay as you go (PAYG) tax
91753839-7474-4f47-b33e-b23766f542ea.description: A system for making regular tax instalments which are removed from gross pay towards the expected income tax liability for that financial year.

f2f9b65e-8252-4811-9dc6-2214d290580a.title: vertex
f2f9b65e-8252-4811-9dc6-2214d290580a.description:
Where 2 straight sides of a two-dimensional shape meet.

Extended in 7–12: A vertex is a point in the plane where lines meet and do not extend beyond, or a point in space where several edges meet. A vertex can also refer to a node in a network. It is also the turning point of a parabola.

cd89c074-c9a0-4499-9de7-5e6ecd1b69f8.title: degree (networks)
cd89c074-c9a0-4499-9de7-5e6ecd1b69f8.description: The degree of a vertex is the number of edge ends at that vertex.

bd274b27-7e21-435e-b7dc-76726ffc9e04.title: directed network
bd274b27-7e21-435e-b7dc-76726ffc9e04.description: A network whose edges have arrows and travel is only possible in the direction of the arrows.

08c4e10d-e011-4606-9e36-29f8c569dfef.title: weighted edges
08c4e10d-e011-4606-9e36-29f8c569dfef.description: A weighted edge is an edge of a network diagram that has a number assigned to it, which implies some numerical value, such as cost, distance or time.

4ac5c018-ba7a-4328-88a6-4e2473217d3c.title: probability tree
4ac5c018-ba7a-4328-88a6-4e2473217d3c.description:
A diagram demonstrating all the possible outcomes of a series of events. A probability tree has branches that represent each event with the probability of each event written on the branch. The probability of each possible outcome is found by multiplying the probabilities along the branches.

See tree diagram

8124ff71-2629-4d75-894c-b7baff15bc41.title: multistage events
8124ff71-2629-4d75-894c-b7baff15bc41.description: An event that consists of 2 or more simple experiments, e.g. tossing a coin 3 times (repeated trials), or both tossing a coin and rolling a dice (possible outcomes would be H and 5, T and 2).

053aa0e3-3358-491c-a614-b3c346c289f2.title: normal distribution
053aa0e3-3358-491c-a614-b3c346c289f2.description:
A type of continuous distribution whose graph looks like this:

Image long description: The horizontal x-axis is labelled from 100 to 200 in increments of 20 from left to right. The y-axis is labelled from 0 to 50 in increments of 10 from the bottom to the top. Along the x-axis is a series of columns that rise to a peak halfway along the axis and fall back towards 0 on the far right of the x-axis. An orange ‘bell curve’ is laid over the peaks of the columns.

The mean, median and mode are equal and the scores are symmetrically arranged either side of the mean.

The graph of a normal distribution is often called a ‘bell curve’ due to its shape.

102fd6ad-433d-4929-8152-253b3cfaa85f.title: angle of elevation
102fd6ad-433d-4929-8152-253b3cfaa85f.description: The angle between horizontal and the line of sight from an observer to an object that is higher than the observer.

273370c2-18db-4320-8b9e-6242d1e70eab.title: angle of depression
273370c2-18db-4320-8b9e-6242d1e70eab.description: The angle between horizontal and the line of sight from an observer to an object that is lower than the observer.

673a3396-3708-47a2-b06a-0fe2cc0d7a77.title: compound interest
673a3396-3708-47a2-b06a-0fe2cc0d7a77.description: The interest earned by investing a sum of money (the principal) when each successive interest payment is added to the principal for calculating the next interest payment.

70c61136-3c62-4de3-bd74-b2788dcf6445.title: Gantt chart
70c61136-3c62-4de3-bd74-b2788dcf6445.description: A bar chart showing a project schedule including a timeline and horizontal bars representing activities. The position of each bar shows the start time and duration of each activity.

c2b9ed7c-1c7a-4249-89ce-377796ebe7c9.title: exponential model
c2b9ed7c-1c7a-4249-89ce-377796ebe7c9.description: Creating an exponential model involves fitting an exponential curve or equation to a practical situation or set of data.

9bc9b3ba-024c-491d-b5f8-0fda83ca36b0.title: exponential relationship

dbb174d1-785d-44a4-ab09-55660ef571d9.title: Venn diagram
dbb174d1-785d-44a4-ab09-55660ef571d9.description: Graphical representations, using several typically overlapping circles, showing elements of sets in relation to properties or attributes. They are drawn for some specified universal set.

b5f04558-1c88-4314-a424-03c98077de44.title: two-way table
b5f04558-1c88-4314-a424-03c98077de44.description: A common way of displaying the two-way frequency distribution that arises when a group is categorised according to 2 criteria.

584083a0-4ebc-44f0-95f1-d60286ca2120.title: time zones
584083a0-4ebc-44f0-95f1-d60286ca2120.description: The 24 divisions of the globe, where each change of 15 degrees longitude corresponds to one hour. As time zones often align with national or regional boundaries this is an approximate relationship.

eead8250-a1bb-4c52-86a1-5a80bd21d419.title: daylight saving
eead8250-a1bb-4c52-86a1-5a80bd21d419.description: A system of setting clocks 1 hour ahead of the standard in spring to give more hours of daylight to the working day in summer months. In Australia, this practice is observed in some states from October to April.

6eaeee4a-3143-4b20-9bd2-993eec45719c.title: trapezoidal rule
6eaeee4a-3143-4b20-9bd2-993eec45719c.description: A method of approximating the area of an irregular shape, or a region bounded by a curve and an axis, by slicing the area up into trapeziums (trapezia) of equal height.

8d01a7e7-b6de-4a2b-be7f-b4b8090cfbe1.title: axis of symmetry
8d01a7e7-b6de-4a2b-be7f-b4b8090cfbe1.description: A straight line that divides a shape or curve into 2 so that one side is a reflection of the other in the given line.

2605a68f-33aa-4444-9ce8-63717dbbe814.title: Medicare levy
2605a68f-33aa-4444-9ce8-63717dbbe814.description: A tax that finances the national health insurance program, Medicare, for all Australians, calculated as a percentage of taxable income.

822d000b-7713-43b6-83a9-3ba7a1f9b27f.title: share
822d000b-7713-43b6-83a9-3ba7a1f9b27f.description: A share is one of the equal parts into which a company's capital is divided, entitling the shareholder to a portion of the company’s profits.

040165c6-7093-4206-9150-4b1155dfaeef.title: superannuation
040165c6-7093-4206-9150-4b1155dfaeef.description: A retirement fund to which financial contributions are made during a person’s working life.

ebdd8b00-1c2c-46a7-9b4b-76ade7c03ed3.title: sample
ebdd8b00-1c2c-46a7-9b4b-76ade7c03ed3.description: A subset of a population used to estimate characteristics of the population. For example, a randomly selected group of 8-year-olds (sample) selected to estimate the height of 8-year-olds in Australia (population).

c010b84d-8e5e-4b2d-9efe-53f64f45ed0a.title: number line
c010b84d-8e5e-4b2d-9efe-53f64f45ed0a.description: A number line is used to represent numbers according to their distance from a zero point. The representation of a number line can start and end on any number.

0e972d96-9e19-4b60-9572-b0c587d93dba.title: random variable
0e972d96-9e19-4b60-9572-b0c587d93dba.description: A variable whose possible values are outcomes of a statistical experiment or a random phenomenon.

bd716fec-f3fd-4c88-bbe8-743d0bc37ae8.title: tax
bd716fec-f3fd-4c88-bbe8-743d0bc37ae8.description: A compulsory monetary contribution required by a government for its support, levied on incomes, property value, goods purchased.

3a9aa16c-eb91-4bd1-a25e-9acc06ed0c1a.title: estimate
3a9aa16c-eb91-4bd1-a25e-9acc06ed0c1a.description: To judge the value, number or quantity of a calculation roughly.

97bd5e2e-f409-425e-a8a0-2dd401761dd7.title: length
97bd5e2e-f409-425e-a8a0-2dd401761dd7.description: Measure of an object from end to end.

f98bda41-c828-4e21-a3a7-4c0814213439.title: volume
f98bda41-c828-4e21-a3a7-4c0814213439.description: The amount of space occupied by an object.

36859c30-c93d-471d-afd6-a6648d3b0777.title: two-dimensional
36859c30-c93d-471d-afd6-a6648d3b0777.description: Having length and width only (with no depth).

8ee4b61d-5ed7-4fdd-9f3a-3c919a88ec75.title: three-dimensional
8ee4b61d-5ed7-4fdd-9f3a-3c919a88ec75.description: An object is three-dimensional when it possesses the dimensions of height, width and depth. Two-dimensional objects have only length and width. A solid is any geometrical object with 3 dimensions.

bc990dab-11fb-4113-b4e1-a7d2362eb1ca.title: frequency
bc990dab-11fb-4113-b4e1-a7d2362eb1ca.description: The number of times a light, sound or radio wave passes a fixed point in unit time; the SI unit used to measure frequency is the hertz.

73bdfca6-7555-40ec-a1b7-0e69343318ac.title: probability
73bdfca6-7555-40ec-a1b7-0e69343318ac.description: The chance of something happening shown on a scale from 0 and 1 (inclusive). For example, the probability that a fair coin toss will come up ‘heads’ is 0.5.

7dc9f786-c21e-4b67-b313-56f59e96942b.title: location
7dc9f786-c21e-4b67-b313-56f59e96942b.description: In measurement and geometry, the relative position of an object is referred to as its location. It can be expressed in terms of a description (such as ‘next to’, ‘behind’, ‘on top of’), a grid reference (such as ‘A5’), or a coordinate (such as ‘(−2,7)’).

6103074a-6570-49f0-ab4a-889e69a32e3f.title: material culture
6103074a-6570-49f0-ab4a-889e69a32e3f.description: Physical objects made or used by humans that provide evidence of how people lived, worked and thought in the past.

33e930c9-126f-46ab-a210-9db0f54ac32a.title: commemoration
33e930c9-126f-46ab-a210-9db0f54ac32a.description: The public remembrance and honouring of significant historical figures or events.

d0c11e36-1509-4a9d-a18c-8a86ae907b23.title: memorialisation
d0c11e36-1509-4a9d-a18c-8a86ae907b23.description: The preservation of the memory of historical figures or events.

a88b1cf3-6ba1-4025-ab2c-3116145172f9.title: diversity
a88b1cf3-6ba1-4025-ab2c-3116145172f9.description: Differences that exist within a group, for example, age, sex, gender, gender expression, sexuality, ethnicity, ability/disability, body shape and composition, culture, religion/spirituality, learning differences, socioeconomic background, values and experiences.

00e3915c-9c7b-4c5d-8669-9771973f9040.title: language revival
00e3915c-9c7b-4c5d-8669-9771973f9040.description: The process and range of strategies for increasing knowledge and use of a language that is no longer spoken fluently across all generations in the context of language loss or language dispossession caused by colonisation. Aboriginal Languages and Torres Strait Islander Languages are being revived through community initiatives, linguistic research and school programs. ‘Language revival’ may be used as an overarching term that could also include ‘reclamation’, ‘revitalisation’, ‘renewal’ and ‘reawakening’.

bca7ea23-00bf-4129-b6d4-1f06de7bed4e.title: language reclamation
bca7ea23-00bf-4129-b6d4-1f06de7bed4e.description: The process of restoring, preserving, recording and promoting Aboriginal Languages.

6950670c-3575-48fb-b7e8-ec27cf426445.title: language group
6950670c-3575-48fb-b7e8-ec27cf426445.description: An Aboriginal community identified with a common language, both verbal and nonverbal, and with a particular territory. Used in preference to the term ‘tribe’.

ef8946c1-d09d-42c0-8abc-75255db5745a.title: communication forms
ef8946c1-d09d-42c0-8abc-75255db5745a.description: The ways people communicate and the communicative behaviours they use. Communication forms can be non-symbolic and/or symbolic. Non-symbolic forms include sounds, gestures, facial expressions and eye movements. Symbolic forms can be aided or non-aided. Aided forms of symbolic communication include objects, symbols, photographs and drawings. Aided forms can be digital. Non-aided forms of symbolic communication include formal gestures; speech; and signs, such as Key Word Sign.

959c2a77-7faf-4287-b3b0-e3d6c2164462.title: decolonisation
959c2a77-7faf-4287-b3b0-e3d6c2164462.description: The process of colonised peoples reclaiming autonomy over governance, land and culture by dismantling colonial structures and restoring or revitalising sovereignty.

54c87c94-b520-4088-a7bf-d6f7de18f195.title: protocols
54c87c94-b520-4088-a7bf-d6f7de18f195.description: The appropriate ways of behaving, communicating and showing respect for diversity of history and culture. This involves appreciation of the knowledge, standing and status of people within the local Aboriginal community and the school community. Protocols inevitably vary between communities, and between people within a community. In establishing a partnership between schools and Aboriginal communities, it is especially important that protocols are acknowledged and respected.

1ba30598-e48d-4a21-8bb5-307c72af1222.title: Country/Place
1ba30598-e48d-4a21-8bb5-307c72af1222.description:
Country is used to describe a specific area of a nation or clan including physical, linguistic and spiritual features. Aboriginal communities’ cultural associations with their Country may include or relate to languages, cultural practices, knowledge, songs, stories, art, paths, landforms, flora, fauna and minerals. These cultural associations may include custodial relationships with particular landscapes such as land, sea, sky, rivers as well as the intangible places associated with the Dreaming(s). Custodial relationships are extremely important in determining who may have the capacity to authentically speak for their Country. 

Place is a space mapped out by physical or intangible boundaries that individuals or groups of Torres Strait Islander Peoples occupy and regard as their own. It is a space with varying degrees of spirituality.

2218dbcf-7e39-48ec-8cde-9b4a4cb283b6.title: ancestral remains
2218dbcf-7e39-48ec-8cde-9b4a4cb283b6.description: The physical remains of deceased individuals, culturally significant to descendant communities and central to reparations efforts.

97808aaf-c7c2-4c8c-ab07-11245303b97b.title: Story sharing
97808aaf-c7c2-4c8c-ab07-11245303b97b.description: The practice of handing down Stories that embody cultural Lore, values and teachings.

5b64cfa8-f494-4de1-a5cf-c7060d4124a1.title: copyright
5b64cfa8-f494-4de1-a5cf-c7060d4124a1.description: The protection provided to the creators of original works and makers of sound recordings and films, that offers a legal framework for the control and reproduction or transmission of their literary, dramatic, artistic or musical works.

f6740482-7c17-4238-bed3-e09d0f863337.title: self-determination
f6740482-7c17-4238-bed3-e09d0f863337.description: Involves the effective participation of Aboriginal Peoples in all decision-making that affects them.

7c569dd0-0c54-4c8e-aecc-b65f04511c10.title: jigs
7c569dd0-0c54-4c8e-aecc-b65f04511c10.description: A custom-made tool or piece of equipment used to control the positioning and/or motion of another tool to go into a work piece.

e006c859-f4e6-4c32-9b13-9b575aef966b.title: project
e006c859-f4e6-4c32-9b13-9b575aef966b.description: An individual or collaborative problem-solving activity undertaken by students that is planned to achieve an articulated aim.

c12318b2-21c6-4445-a247-aba0c4aab67d.title: sustainability
c12318b2-21c6-4445-a247-aba0c4aab67d.description: The patterns of activities that meet the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

bfa2e609-d671-4e12-89a5-b3687f92db3c.title: signage
bfa2e609-d671-4e12-89a5-b3687f92db3c.description: The use of words, graphic designs and/or symbols used to communicate a message, eg information signs, plaques, warning signs, road signs, signs that show direction.

9c859a00-f159-49b8-8a77-3d5fd017a6b2.title: project management
9c859a00-f159-49b8-8a77-3d5fd017a6b2.description: The process of planning, organising, controlling resources, monitoring timelines and activities, and completing a project to achieve a goal that meets identified criteria.

62649b05-1cf8-42d6-b5c1-ebadf797f3b6.title: disability
62649b05-1cf8-42d6-b5c1-ebadf797f3b6.description:
An umbrella term for any or all of the following components: 

  • impairments: challenges in body function or structure
  • activity limitations: difficulties in executing activities
  • participation restrictions: challenges an individual may experience in involvement in life situations. (World Health Organization)

d1be360f-41f6-4b07-9a77-6ae3209c5976.title: microcontroller
d1be360f-41f6-4b07-9a77-6ae3209c5976.description: A small computer built for the purpose of dealing with specific tasks, such as managing the engine in a car, displaying information in a microwave control panel or receiving information from a television remote control. Microcontrollers process data inputted by users (e.g. keypad) or sensors (e.g. light).

0a188687-157c-4ec5-b183-e993fa5b1989.title: on-Country
0a188687-157c-4ec5-b183-e993fa5b1989.description:
Taking place on Aboriginal land or Country of origin.

See Country/Place

82730240-bd85-49d7-a034-fe032446ad79.title: historical inquiry
82730240-bd85-49d7-a034-fe032446ad79.description: The process of developing knowledge and understanding by posing questions about the past, and applying skills associated with locating, analysing, evaluating and using sources as evidence to develop an informed argument or interpretation.

07b82337-bf30-4e26-aee3-f81dcad684f3.title: legacy
07b82337-bf30-4e26-aee3-f81dcad684f3.description: The long-lasting impact, influence or significance of a person, action or event from the past.

f0251b70-16ac-464c-980a-1f52fb0be084.title: terms
f0251b70-16ac-464c-980a-1f52fb0be084.description: A word or phrase used to describe abstract aspects or features of the past, e.g. imperialism, democracy or republic; and more specific features, such as trench warfare, or a dictator, gladiator or vizier.

69b9a2e9-c41d-4611-8cdc-b83f83a1ff7c.title: chronology
69b9a2e9-c41d-4611-8cdc-b83f83a1ff7c.description: The order in which a series of events happened, or a list of these events in the order in which they happened.

6aaf0e18-8410-41e9-9b29-2165607baeaa.title: source
6aaf0e18-8410-41e9-9b29-2165607baeaa.description: Any written or non-written materials that can be used to investigate the past.

a61296ae-0b61-446e-83a0-8911446eac0a.title: artefact
a61296ae-0b61-446e-83a0-8911446eac0a.description: An object made by a person, e.g. a tool, weapon, or ornament.

b62939ed-736c-4e4f-b875-228f7fd438fe.title: reliability
b62939ed-736c-4e4f-b875-228f7fd438fe.description: An extent to which repeated observations and/or measurements taken under identical circumstances will yield similar results.

1a2052da-c1e4-44fd-9efe-60c3986b69db.title: concepts
1a2052da-c1e4-44fd-9efe-60c3986b69db.description: The key ideas that shape the practice of the discipline of history, e.g. causation, continuity and change, contestability, perspectives and significance. They provide the scope for judgement, interpretation and argument and are the major means by which knowledge is constructed, analysed, questioned and represented.

15ecb651-6c60-4046-a352-687f6121d58e.title: causation
15ecb651-6c60-4046-a352-687f6121d58e.description: The link between a person accused of a crime and the end result. The actions that led to the crime.

87cfccd4-9419-478c-9a3b-d128e97bb4c8.title: continuity and change
87cfccd4-9419-478c-9a3b-d128e97bb4c8.description: Aspects of the past that have remained the same over a period of time or have changed over time. Change can be understood as a 'process'.

2a6a8f2a-e983-453d-a434-d4f80ad42165.title: perspective
2a6a8f2a-e983-453d-a434-d4f80ad42165.description: A way of regarding situations, facts and texts, and evaluating their relative significance.

8d9d69f0-eef8-4f7d-a329-e1ad58e310f7.title: significance
8d9d69f0-eef8-4f7d-a329-e1ad58e310f7.description: The importance attributed to a particular aspect of the past such as an individual or event. Significance involves an understanding of the various considerations which cause different groups at different times to judge aspects of the past more or less historically significant.

8326dc6c-911d-4a0c-b487-cf929dc33215.title: contestability
8326dc6c-911d-4a0c-b487-cf929dc33215.description: An examination of how interpretations and representations of the past differ, e.g. as a result of using differing evidence or resulting from different perspectives.

42f66bf6-e768-4573-85aa-b9e872f436fa.title: modern
42f66bf6-e768-4573-85aa-b9e872f436fa.description: In the study of Modern History in Stage 6, the period of time in the modern world – generally between 1750 and the present.

bac9db3c-b9a6-49e6-b55d-ec03a9b89420.title: ideology
bac9db3c-b9a6-49e6-b55d-ec03a9b89420.description: A framework of beliefs that guides actions, e.g. fascism and communism.

96170433-b04a-4796-9138-4e1db23b74ac.title: interpretation
96170433-b04a-4796-9138-4e1db23b74ac.description: The individual choices made by a performer, choreographer or viewer that establish a personal perspective relative to the communication of the intent in dance works.

3aa0995a-d69a-4b89-883a-f7e389812405.title: site
3aa0995a-d69a-4b89-883a-f7e389812405.description: A location, building or structure of historical significance.

b8fa443f-1237-452d-aa90-d40b7d611195.title: reconstruction
b8fa443f-1237-452d-aa90-d40b7d611195.description: A process of piecing together evidence from sources to develop an understanding or picture of the past. It may include the physical reconstruction of ancient sites.

1b68caf1-967b-4623-8a00-0629c269bfb3.title: dictatorship
1b68caf1-967b-4623-8a00-0629c269bfb3.description: A form of government in which one person, or group of people, holds absolute power.

73e93b6a-0673-431d-b6c2-f2842dd56859.title: archaeology/archaeological
73e93b6a-0673-431d-b6c2-f2842dd56859.description: The practice of excavation and the study of the material remains of past human life and activities, e.g. pottery, jewellery, tools, monuments and human remains.

da299888-1982-4f52-b6c7-f68cda382b06.title: accessibility
da299888-1982-4f52-b6c7-f68cda382b06.description: The extent to which a system, environment or object may be used irrespective of a user’s capabilities or abilities. For example, the use of assistive technologies (AT) to allow people with disability to use computer systems, or the use of icons in place of words to allow young children to use a system.

bad90c15-fd94-4984-8642-f29a8280e294.title: food security
bad90c15-fd94-4984-8642-f29a8280e294.description: Assurances that food supplies are reliable and of a sufficient quality and quantity to maintain human life.

6e0e8327-ec9a-42c4-aa9d-6cc900c50df3.title: food systems
6e0e8327-ec9a-42c4-aa9d-6cc900c50df3.description: The network of activities and resources that deal with the supply, distribution and sustainability of food, from its production and consumption to the disposal of surplus or waste.

1daa73f3-5f9e-4099-a31c-432f74cdf086.title: food design
1daa73f3-5f9e-4099-a31c-432f74cdf086.description:
The creative process involved in the designing of food products, packaging, preparation methods, presentation and the spaces where food is consumed, with the aim of meeting human needs and enhancing the consumer experience.

See food systems

0eb1806d-0145-46e2-b8c5-cb20ac10e558.title: food practices
0eb1806d-0145-46e2-b8c5-cb20ac10e558.description: The patterns and behaviours involved in the selection, preparation, consumption and disposal of food, shaped by culture, religion, nutritional choices, food preparation techniques, environmental sustainability, resource availability and individual preferences.

16ab43f9-9d83-4837-85af-aa6759875e5d.title: independent variable
16ab43f9-9d83-4837-85af-aa6759875e5d.description: The variable that is deliberately changed, often through a series of pre-set values.

373c5f05-3ce6-49bc-abab-588bb8ab4aca.title: controlled variable
373c5f05-3ce6-49bc-abab-588bb8ab4aca.description: A variable that is kept constant (or changed in constant ways) during an investigation. For example, the same amount of water would be a controlled variable in an investigation comparing solubility.

ca093aea-342e-4301-b963-a65b9db5a54e.title: experimental control
ca093aea-342e-4301-b963-a65b9db5a54e.description:
The sample in an experiment to which all the other samples are compared.

Extended in Science 11–12: The sample in an experiment that does not receive the independent variable.

add65a46-e030-40a3-aee4-403325d45775.title: hazard
add65a46-e030-40a3-aee4-403325d45775.description: A source that poses a potential risk of harm or injury.

3d14c0e3-3ed5-489d-a25b-7a16b107bb4f.title: observation
3d14c0e3-3ed5-489d-a25b-7a16b107bb4f.description: To see, watch, perceive or notice. Observations can be made using all 5 senses as well as digital and non-digital tools that extend our senses.

2ead9a52-8a0d-47fa-90d1-f7c35063dc8a.title: percentage error
2ead9a52-8a0d-47fa-90d1-f7c35063dc8a.description: The absolute error of a measurement expressed as a percentage of the recorded measurement.

0bc59483-5782-4404-a138-8788ec08ee5b.title: qualitative
0bc59483-5782-4404-a138-8788ec08ee5b.description: To use descriptive explanations involving features, characteristics or properties to identify important components. Data and information that is not numerical in nature.

87359809-aa33-4988-a83a-f0209f43ae94.title: quantitative
87359809-aa33-4988-a83a-f0209f43ae94.description: Data or components that can be expressed or measured numerically, including chemical formulae or numbers.

f3e803d3-5b37-47ee-bd29-c377fa185903.title: validity
f3e803d3-5b37-47ee-bd29-c377fa185903.description: The extent to which the processes and resultant data measure what was intended.

3f64693f-fc7a-4567-8719-5786121ac4e9.title: precision
3f64693f-fc7a-4567-8719-5786121ac4e9.description: The extent to which repeated measurements of the same item are close to each other.

05202dce-3f5c-4dbc-9015-3c39d2de8ed0.title: model
05202dce-3f5c-4dbc-9015-3c39d2de8ed0.description: A mathematical, conceptual or physical representation that describes, simplifies, clarifies or provides an explanation of the structure, workings or relationships within an object, system or idea. Models can provide a means of testing and predicting behaviour within limited conditions. Models may be physical or exist in digital form.

0d1597a5-f870-4622-a415-e6f4e9c2ea64.title: scientific investigation
0d1597a5-f870-4622-a415-e6f4e9c2ea64.description: A scientific process of answering a question, exploring an idea or solving a problem, which requires activities such as planning a course of action, collecting data, interpreting data, reaching a conclusion and communicating these activities. Investigations can include practical and/or secondary-source data or information.

610b446d-ac77-43a5-b88c-c4375528ba3f.title: trend
610b446d-ac77-43a5-b88c-c4375528ba3f.description: A general direction or pattern in data or observations that shows how something changes over time or under different conditions.

6a6ab029-a99d-4c39-a9b6-83d43a4cdd63.title: prediction
6a6ab029-a99d-4c39-a9b6-83d43a4cdd63.description: A statement or estimate about what will happen in the future, often based on available evidence, past experiences or statistical analysis.

e90993ac-5bc1-4067-850f-cde77b9a1181.title: ecosystem
e90993ac-5bc1-4067-850f-cde77b9a1181.description:
A system formed by the interaction of biotic organisms with each other and with the abiotic components of the environment in which they live.

While an ecosystem may be synonymous with a specific environment, the ‘system’ approach enables a focus on the various components and their interconnected nature.

dda69fd2-bf58-4f59-9888-af1cc4d24904.title: invasive species
dda69fd2-bf58-4f59-9888-af1cc4d24904.description: A species which thrives in a habitat it is not native to and threatens the environment, economy or human health.

dd048846-0670-4fe1-8e20-716777e7e4a6.title: mutation
dd048846-0670-4fe1-8e20-716777e7e4a6.description:
A change in genetic material (DNA).

Extended in Biology 11–12: Occurs due to an error during DNA replication.

9627d8aa-910a-451a-9b98-f7569938d9b8.title: natural selection
9627d8aa-910a-451a-9b98-f7569938d9b8.description: The process by which organisms with traits that are better suited to their environment survive and reproduce more successfully than those with less favourable traits. This leads to the gradual change or adaptation of a population over time.

72666108-4e60-4fd9-8efa-3c30ae82ede9.title: budding
72666108-4e60-4fd9-8efa-3c30ae82ede9.description: An asexual reproduction method where part of the adult organism divides through mitosis to produce a small genetically identical bud.

f8ad74e3-3528-45d8-b69e-0773c8ee99e1.title: parthenogenesis
f8ad74e3-3528-45d8-b69e-0773c8ee99e1.description: A form of asexual reproduction in which an embryo develops from an unfertilised egg without the need for fertilisation by a male sperm or pollen.

e895249d-8928-4bfa-8d5a-d54aff22aaef.title: binary fission
e895249d-8928-4bfa-8d5a-d54aff22aaef.description: An asexual reproduction method of division into 2 identical daughter cells.

727bcbe5-364e-403a-b156-01c063b72636.title: asexual reproduction
727bcbe5-364e-403a-b156-01c063b72636.description: Reproduction involving only one parent and no sex cells.

66d3a5a6-07b3-4ff8-ba8f-da6f3373319d.title: sedimentary (rock)
66d3a5a6-07b3-4ff8-ba8f-da6f3373319d.description: Relating to rocks formed by the deposition and compaction of sediments – particles of minerals, organic matter or fragments of other rocks – that are deposited by water, wind, ice or biological activity.

75a290b8-9c96-4e32-9af2-3d52a53511bd.title: cool burning
75a290b8-9c96-4e32-9af2-3d52a53511bd.description: A land management Practice used by Aboriginal Peoples using small, low-temperature fires to promote the regeneration of bushland and reduce the risk of intense, uncontrolled bushfires.

4f3a5acf-1305-41d8-a46c-c88c56c2742d.title: gene pool
4f3a5acf-1305-41d8-a46c-c88c56c2742d.description: The total number of different alleles within all genes in a breeding population.

84360c73-13a1-4f64-8f45-3781f3bf76df.title: genetic drift
84360c73-13a1-4f64-8f45-3781f3bf76df.description: A change in allele frequency within a population due to random chance/causes.

de0c786f-21f8-4691-a179-60063961c9cb.title: gene flow
de0c786f-21f8-4691-a179-60063961c9cb.description: The natural transfer of genes between populations of the same species, affecting the allele frequency within a population.

09a5f581-7640-49a0-963e-0fc9643f67a7.title: selection pressures
09a5f581-7640-49a0-963e-0fc9643f67a7.description: Environmental factors that influence which traits are advantageous for the survival and reproduction of organisms that drive evolution.

187c9c4e-b882-4757-a617-265f7ae7e94f.title: allele frequency
187c9c4e-b882-4757-a617-265f7ae7e94f.description: A percentage measure of the allele composition within a population’s gene pool.

b97fbdf1-c254-4272-aab0-92e4258791d8.title: biodiversity
b97fbdf1-c254-4272-aab0-92e4258791d8.description: The variety of living organisms within a particular habitat, ecosystem, biome, or globally.

92265ab1-af3b-49b1-8608-5c62c55737a7.title: fossil
92265ab1-af3b-49b1-8608-5c62c55737a7.description: The preserved remains or traces of an organism, such as a skeleton, or a footprint, from a past geological age, typically found in sedimentary rock layers.

5b06a96e-ebf8-4c73-ba6f-3740446541ea.title: transpiration
5b06a96e-ebf8-4c73-ba6f-3740446541ea.description: The process by which plants evaporate water into the atmosphere, usually via the stomata found within the leaves of a plant.

1e93ae57-a19f-4b22-8806-6cf7c56e3626.title: homeostasis
1e93ae57-a19f-4b22-8806-6cf7c56e3626.description: The ability of an organism to maintain stable internal conditions despite external changes.

5c1bc0ef-7315-49d7-8116-679d7a4807bf.title: bush tucker
5c1bc0ef-7315-49d7-8116-679d7a4807bf.description: Edible bush foods, including meat, fish, seafood, nuts, seeds, spices and fruits consumed by Aboriginal Peoples.

f105d4f3-abe7-431c-bc8f-b1bebbf952a0.title: tubules (kidney)
f105d4f3-abe7-431c-bc8f-b1bebbf952a0.description: Tiny tubes within the kidney that filter blood to form urine, including the proximal convoluted tubule, the Loop of Henle, the distal convoluted tubule and the collecting duct.

c336c125-55bd-4efc-9a0f-a3f402a0e916.title: selective reabsorption
c336c125-55bd-4efc-9a0f-a3f402a0e916.description: The process in which substances required by the body move from the renal tubules back into the blood in the capillaries by diffusion or active transport.

39872ed8-4b29-4fb8-ad4c-97f812d0638b.title: secretion (within the nephron)
39872ed8-4b29-4fb8-ad4c-97f812d0638b.description: Part of a process within the nephron of moving unwanted substances from the blood capillaries into the renal tubules, mostly via active transport.

a070ec5f-3215-45ef-8198-f4207d9f473c.title: photosynthesis
a070ec5f-3215-45ef-8198-f4207d9f473c.description: A chemical process that uses sunlight and chlorophyll to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose, oxygen and water.

dbb4366b-2a0b-4ce4-9465-91ade673e0bf.title: stimulus
dbb4366b-2a0b-4ce4-9465-91ade673e0bf.description: The motivation that provides the initial inspiration for the choreographer to make a dance work.

8b5ed33a-627c-4644-bdbc-d1f9cc490abb.title: receptor
8b5ed33a-627c-4644-bdbc-d1f9cc490abb.description: A group of sensory cells within the body that detects a change in a particular component of the internal and/or external environment.

429a89ad-a778-40fa-a604-2a21c6261389.title: control centre
429a89ad-a778-40fa-a604-2a21c6261389.description: A region of the brain that maintains homeostasis by processing messages received from receptors and sending responses to effectors to counteract a stimulus.

a414d9e9-455c-44fa-8d69-aadfbccf0390.title: effector
a414d9e9-455c-44fa-8d69-aadfbccf0390.description: A muscle or gland that carries out a response.

20aee21e-3353-4595-b048-f53e5a28f6d5.title: phloem
20aee21e-3353-4595-b048-f53e5a28f6d5.description: A tissue in vascular plants that transports organic nutrients, particularly sugars, from leaves to other parts of the plant, including roots, stems and developing fruits.

05664c2e-fba9-489d-b684-fc21e612393b.title: epigenetics
05664c2e-fba9-489d-b684-fc21e612393b.description: Changes in the way a gene functions within an organism that are heritable but do not alter the genetic code itself; changes that affect the phenotype without changing the genotype.

dcf2acbc-eb29-4a69-aae4-aed9ecc09a6c.title: mutagen
dcf2acbc-eb29-4a69-aae4-aed9ecc09a6c.description: A chemical, biological or physical agent capable of causing changes in DNA.

a624aafc-6ec9-4df9-b61b-de9b352f57a9.title: chromosome
a624aafc-6ec9-4df9-b61b-de9b352f57a9.description: Chromosomes are tiny structures found in all living cells. They are made up of DNA and proteins, which contain the genetic information that determine how an organism develops and functions.

9d1499fb-4617-4bb0-b241-b88ebd01b52b.title: intron
9d1499fb-4617-4bb0-b241-b88ebd01b52b.description: The sequence of bases that are spliced out from the mRNA molecule also known as the non-coding section of DNA.

c1de0c01-136b-4784-a595-71008fe429de.title: exon
c1de0c01-136b-4784-a595-71008fe429de.description: The coding section of DNA that remains in a mature mRNA molecule to be translated to form a protein.

841f401b-fe1d-488c-81ab-cc41902ab204.title: protein
841f401b-fe1d-488c-81ab-cc41902ab204.description: A large molecule made up of polypeptide chains found within cells.

3000a497-dd58-4fd2-ab8c-76d80ec2d9c3.title: somatic variant
3000a497-dd58-4fd2-ab8c-76d80ec2d9c3.description: A change in a DNA sequence that occurs in body cells.

73c351c5-9be9-4baa-9521-a942fb435345.title: germline variant
73c351c5-9be9-4baa-9521-a942fb435345.description: A DNA variation that occurs in the sexual reproductive cells (eggs and sperm) which can be passed on to the offspring.

8fe78b9f-3f01-4886-acbd-456947fa39c5.title: single nucleotide polymorphism
8fe78b9f-3f01-4886-acbd-456947fa39c5.description: A single nucleotide base change at a particular locus on DNA in the genome of at least one per cent of individuals within a population.

1f58aabd-6334-4e7c-88e7-6c17703d7d03.title: allele
1f58aabd-6334-4e7c-88e7-6c17703d7d03.description: The alternative form of a gene at identical loci of homologous chromosomes.

459eefd9-d0a9-4bdd-bb51-3d71bf0b678f.title: meiosis
459eefd9-d0a9-4bdd-bb51-3d71bf0b678f.description: A cell division process that halves the chromosome numbers to become haploid and results in gametes.

6c4ba153-c535-4a31-93a4-62cca504b2a0.title: random segregation
6c4ba153-c535-4a31-93a4-62cca504b2a0.description: The separation of allele pairs by chance during the formation of gametes.

7469688c-e0e3-44a8-aabc-967c1e4b2b14.title: genetic variation
7469688c-e0e3-44a8-aabc-967c1e4b2b14.description: The diversity in genetic makeup within a population or species, resulting from differences in the genetic information carried by individuals.

e727409f-6498-41f5-a31a-2b8b3dbdd8e7.title: DNA
e727409f-6498-41f5-a31a-2b8b3dbdd8e7.description: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is a molecule found in cells that carries the genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all living organisms including viruses.

70c7245e-5092-420f-af87-f6f8cd42c721.title: tRNA (transfer ribonucleic acid)
70c7245e-5092-420f-af87-f6f8cd42c721.description: A small RNA molecule containing an anticodon that corresponds to the specific amino acid being carried used in translation.

2a85a79d-34e0-4656-af10-07e7a360ba44.title: dominant
2a85a79d-34e0-4656-af10-07e7a360ba44.description: A trait expressed in a heterozygous organism or a homozygous-dominant organism.

1e1c6c1d-df32-4bdd-a61d-32eea1e6ffde.title: gene expression
1e1c6c1d-df32-4bdd-a61d-32eea1e6ffde.description: The process by which the information encoded in a gene is turned into a function.

4101594f-2687-4ea7-a896-01e2fbc10413.title: base substitution
4101594f-2687-4ea7-a896-01e2fbc10413.description: The replacement of one nucleotide base with a different one.

40505f4b-def6-47cb-9e94-59bb69961684.title: point mutation
40505f4b-def6-47cb-9e94-59bb69961684.description: A single nucleotide base change in the DNA or RNA sequence.

456a1421-7c1b-493f-9f6d-073f082a66c5.title: codon
