456a1421-7c1b-493f-9f6d-073f082a66c5.description: A triplet sequence of nucleotides in mRNA that codes for a specific amino acid.

62dc41fe-35fa-4444-b7c5-f19f8b5a0c38.title: amino acid
62dc41fe-35fa-4444-b7c5-f19f8b5a0c38.description: An organic compound considered the building block from which proteins are formed.

0d97ceb8-4b63-4219-98e5-29eaaf453cf7.title: transcription
0d97ceb8-4b63-4219-98e5-29eaaf453cf7.description: A process within polypeptide synthesis in which a segment (gene) of DNA is copied into mRNA within the nucleus.

2eb02cd0-dbf2-4247-be47-2d833c09aff2.title: silent mutation
2eb02cd0-dbf2-4247-be47-2d833c09aff2.description: A point mutation which includes a change in the DNA sequence that does not change the amino acid produced during protein synthesis.

c7825eca-853b-4d0a-b1ca-89fe979fe0c4.title: nonsense mutation
c7825eca-853b-4d0a-b1ca-89fe979fe0c4.description: A mutation that occurs in DNA when a sequence change gives rise to a stop codon rather than a codon specifying an amino acid.

20356afd-3103-4bd8-beec-7f31552e7680.title: frameshift mutation
20356afd-3103-4bd8-beec-7f31552e7680.description: A type of genetic mutation in which one or more nucleotides are inserted into or deleted from the DNA sequence, causing a shift in the reading frame of the genetic code during protein synthesis.

8f240a3d-22b4-46e8-b6d4-0f1398ddcf70.title: cytokinesis
8f240a3d-22b4-46e8-b6d4-0f1398ddcf70.description: The process following mitotic and meiotic division in which the cytoplasm divides, separating into daughter cells.

87c0af35-c69e-402f-abfe-4573fc485a76.title: mitosis
87c0af35-c69e-402f-abfe-4573fc485a76.description: The process that takes place as part of the cell cycle in which cellular division takes place, resulting in 2 genetically identical daughter cells.

5ac55cae-8cec-44d0-b8e2-225f9abfccab.title: enzyme
5ac55cae-8cec-44d0-b8e2-225f9abfccab.description: A biological catalyst that increases the rate of a chemical reaction.

2110a12a-4be7-4543-8170-50d741ca6542.title: eukaryotic cell
2110a12a-4be7-4543-8170-50d741ca6542.description: A cell which has DNA in its clearly defined nucleus, and also contains membrane-bound organelles.

f1b6922b-d84b-4a11-b4b4-bde48bd7fed8.title: prokaryotic cell
f1b6922b-d84b-4a11-b4b4-bde48bd7fed8.description: A simple, single-celled organism containing single-strand DNA and without a distinct nucleus or membrane-bound organelles.

efd24fb7-fa67-47c3-99e3-e06f228ec310.title: active transport
efd24fb7-fa67-47c3-99e3-e06f228ec310.description: The process of transporting molecules or ions across a cell membrane from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration using energy.

372925b8-6273-4e98-86eb-0849742edb14.title: exocytosis
372925b8-6273-4e98-86eb-0849742edb14.description: The process of expelling unwanted molecules from a cell through the cell membrane to the outside space by vesicles.

ea4cb562-f543-4d39-bc73-2bcc90deeb71.title: endocytosis
ea4cb562-f543-4d39-bc73-2bcc90deeb71.description: The process by which material is ingested into a cell by the folding of the cell membrane to form a vesicle.

44239cdf-9f8c-4c45-8656-401b93cb8194.title: hypertonic
44239cdf-9f8c-4c45-8656-401b93cb8194.description: Denoting a solution that has a higher concentration of solutes compared to another solution.

b4f41724-464b-4c88-8add-edb98352b267.title: hypotonic
b4f41724-464b-4c88-8add-edb98352b267.description: Denoting a solution that has a lower concentration of solutes compared to another solution.

3bfee798-8440-4a63-9193-aef923539f40.title: isotonic
3bfee798-8440-4a63-9193-aef923539f40.description: A solution which has the same concentration of solutes as another solution.

77f38dcf-7449-49c9-b8c1-dbbb233a6da5.title: fluid mosaic model
77f38dcf-7449-49c9-b8c1-dbbb233a6da5.description: A model used to describe the structure and function of the cell membrane.

a0500ad3-04d1-4e77-a61f-1ef773210eed.title: replication fork
a0500ad3-04d1-4e77-a61f-1ef773210eed.description: The Y-shaped region formed by the unwinding and partial separation of the DNA double helix during replication.

8781f984-0dae-4aa1-b103-0a47656d13e3.title: prevalence
8781f984-0dae-4aa1-b103-0a47656d13e3.description: The number or proportion (of cases, instances, and so forth) in a population at a given time. For example, in relation to cancer, refers to the number of people alive who had been diagnosed with cancer in a prescribed period (usually 1, 5, 10 or 26 years).

3c9f794e-5367-4211-8f5b-15aa3137fbb3.title: recombinant DNA
3c9f794e-5367-4211-8f5b-15aa3137fbb3.description: DNA that has been artificially constructed by combining genetic material from 2 or more different genomes.

8b3a3bd7-0c85-4a81-8156-70ed13489d88.title: genetic trait
8b3a3bd7-0c85-4a81-8156-70ed13489d88.description: Characteristics and qualities that offspring inherit from their parents.

694901c2-3fae-4618-bb1b-e12b204f5b6e.title: bioinformatics
694901c2-3fae-4618-bb1b-e12b204f5b6e.description: The science of collecting and analysing biological data using computer technology.

84a3363e-71d7-4c82-8a82-ebc26dcfae1d.title: biotechnology
84a3363e-71d7-4c82-8a82-ebc26dcfae1d.description: The development or creation of products from biological systems, processes or living organisms.

923d3496-7fc0-4e97-bb98-8228a5c2dcea.title: transgenic organisms
923d3496-7fc0-4e97-bb98-8228a5c2dcea.description: A species that has artificially inserted genes from another species into their genome using genetic engineering techniques.

8686f11a-7c03-4049-9499-423fbe2b3e4c.title: biotic
8686f11a-7c03-4049-9499-423fbe2b3e4c.description: Involving the living components of the environment.

c391fa23-c6ef-463f-8531-829396bcf663.title: predation
c391fa23-c6ef-463f-8531-829396bcf663.description: A biological interaction where a predator hunts and kills prey, usually for nutrition.

3254830b-b3c0-406a-a13d-3c5fb07ce9a2.title: mutualism
3254830b-b3c0-406a-a13d-3c5fb07ce9a2.description: A symbiotic relationship between organisms of 2 different species where each benefit from the interaction.

4d819741-a0dc-4487-aa88-e55d0663f2ca.title: commensalism
4d819741-a0dc-4487-aa88-e55d0663f2ca.description: A type of symbiotic relationship in which one organism benefits from living with, on or in another one without affecting the other organism.

8eae16db-ca59-472d-ac35-c39d589bbaa4.title: allelopathy
8eae16db-ca59-472d-ac35-c39d589bbaa4.description: The adverse effect one plant causes another through the release of chemicals into the soil.

e0890ea1-73fc-44ea-a5b7-b511c8aaf18f.title: parasitism
e0890ea1-73fc-44ea-a5b7-b511c8aaf18f.description: A symbiotic relationship in which a parasite lives on or within a host and benefits at the host’s expense.

83e1fb9b-1dcd-4185-ae94-8cd1a38d5edf.title: ectotherm
83e1fb9b-1dcd-4185-ae94-8cd1a38d5edf.description: An organism that has a variable body temperature which is dependent on the ambient temperature.

15c84ecd-7e0e-4f00-bbfb-5fb137c2fb3b.title: endotherm
15c84ecd-7e0e-4f00-bbfb-5fb137c2fb3b.description: An organism that maintains body temperature within a narrow range of tolerance despite any variation in the ambient temperature.

e0ac58e2-1d34-452b-be11-7ee67685d50a.title: comparative anatomy
e0ac58e2-1d34-452b-be11-7ee67685d50a.description: The scientific study of the similarities and differences in the anatomical structures of different species of animals.

2505bda5-589f-4518-9930-a563404a8436.title: transect
2505bda5-589f-4518-9930-a563404a8436.description: A straight line drawn on a map between 2 points, used to represent changes in elevation, landforms and other geographical features along the path.

5b840fe0-91ab-473d-857e-904b736fd09e.title: quadrat
5b840fe0-91ab-473d-857e-904b736fd09e.description: A square or rectangular area used within a larger habitat to identify and count species, used as sampling technique.

b81212dc-98a1-4110-a034-78457b1f8695.title: carrying capacity
b81212dc-98a1-4110-a034-78457b1f8695.description: The largest amount of individuals of a species that can be supported by an environment. The number is based on resources, such as food, water and shelter, and how accessible they are.

b379e454-7b3f-46af-b930-64bf5b3e6792.title: phylogenetic tree
b379e454-7b3f-46af-b930-64bf5b3e6792.description: A branching diagram that visually represents the evolutionary relationships between different species or groups of organisms.

f8353508-6b03-4844-ba1f-8177d08ecf3e.title: gradualism
f8353508-6b03-4844-ba1f-8177d08ecf3e.description: The theory that species evolve slowly from existing ones over long periods of time.

5d5dec5f-2687-49a9-a234-5a66e8678baa.title: punctuated equilibrium
5d5dec5f-2687-49a9-a234-5a66e8678baa.description: A theory of evolution stating that species experience long periods of little or no evolutionary change, interrupted by brief periods of rapid change that lead to the formation of new species.

de5afe2b-eb40-4956-b3a9-1ec66b733221.title: bush medicine
de5afe2b-eb40-4956-b3a9-1ec66b733221.description: Medicines developed and used by Aboriginal Peoples in healing illness and infection.

a113fc4b-ec0a-4942-8ba2-31b6a8672c80.title: immune response
a113fc4b-ec0a-4942-8ba2-31b6a8672c80.description: The body’s co-ordinated defence mechanism characterised by both the innate immune system and the adaptive immune system.

2ff19d5f-144d-4a40-a7db-d0a352f6661e.title: incidence
2ff19d5f-144d-4a40-a7db-d0a352f6661e.description: The number of new cases (of an illness or event, and so on) occurring during a given period.

69d8856d-9723-4708-a369-cbb421f56bc9.title: morbidity
69d8856d-9723-4708-a369-cbb421f56bc9.description: The ill health of an individual and levels of ill health in a population or group.

61ed3b12-a1cc-42d0-8675-cd90ca2500b5.title: mortality
61ed3b12-a1cc-42d0-8675-cd90ca2500b5.description: Number or rate of deaths in a population during a given time period.

aa1d7f85-7769-4c8c-9395-f5f2a9625c77.title: phagocytic leukocyte
aa1d7f85-7769-4c8c-9395-f5f2a9625c77.description: A type of white blood cell that ingests and digests foreign particles, microorganisms and cellular debris.

e49b8721-7d54-4c6e-b078-ea172ea647c7.title: T cell
e49b8721-7d54-4c6e-b078-ea172ea647c7.description: A white blood cell, produced in bone marrow and matured in the thymus, which is responsible for the identification and killing of infected cells, the activation of other immune cells and the regulation of immune responses.

15962b81-d57b-46dc-81ff-b8d53a633e74.title: cell-mediated response
15962b81-d57b-46dc-81ff-b8d53a633e74.description: An immune response involving macrophages and T cells that eliminate intracellular pathogens.

742e371b-a207-4976-8bbb-23ba3085d990.title: interleukin
742e371b-a207-4976-8bbb-23ba3085d990.description: A group of proteins, mainly secreted by leukocytes, responsible for the activation and differentiation of immune cells during an immune response.

ab5279df-2726-489c-80d7-bebed82d7d71.title: correlation
ab5279df-2726-489c-80d7-bebed82d7d71.description: A measure of the strength of the linear relationship between 2 variables.

2931f934-af08-43b5-93f5-e4aa48d7e10c.title: B cell
2931f934-af08-43b5-93f5-e4aa48d7e10c.description: Lymphocytes produced in the bone marrow that develop into plasma cells responsible for making antibodies.

460175b1-f9ff-4d71-8d63-ea52af1fb6b1.title: antibody
460175b1-f9ff-4d71-8d63-ea52af1fb6b1.description: A type of blood protein produced in response to a specific antigen in order to counteract it. Also known as immunoglobin.

152b1b04-1215-44e1-bb4a-415ee2f6e4d3.title: advocate
152b1b04-1215-44e1-bb4a-415ee2f6e4d3.description: The process of arguing in support of a cause or position, or acting on behalf of yourself or another individual, to ensure that your or others’ best interests are taken into account.

e10f6cd6-55fc-4aec-b61e-6d592cb53f0a.title: health promotion
e10f6cd6-55fc-4aec-b61e-6d592cb53f0a.description: The process of enabling people to increase control over, and to improve, their health.

a9a157ad-f588-44bf-bca1-0872aff287d7.title: World Health Organization (WHO)
a9a157ad-f588-44bf-bca1-0872aff287d7.description: A specialised agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health. It aims to ensure there is universal health coverage, protect people from health emergencies and provide people with better health and wellbeing.

5246e4a3-38c2-4a6a-989d-b48903a49093.title: dimensions of health
5246e4a3-38c2-4a6a-989d-b48903a49093.description: There are 5 dimensions of health. These include physical, mental, emotional, spiritual and social. These dimensions are interrelated.

e66ddedb-bed8-4e9a-8a28-8c0cb88a211b.title: concept
e66ddedb-bed8-4e9a-8a28-8c0cb88a211b.description: Key ideas that shape practice, e.g. equity, fitness.

0abb6307-7d81-48fd-8e36-f9e2bd9efb69.title: epidemiology
0abb6307-7d81-48fd-8e36-f9e2bd9efb69.description: The study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events (including disease), and the application of this study to the control of diseases and other health problems.

51cac40e-1719-4f7a-bd6c-e595844d8182.title: infant mortality
51cac40e-1719-4f7a-bd6c-e595844d8182.description: The number of deaths among children aged under one in a given period, per 1,000 live births in the same period.

bdcedf47-3db7-482c-9164-276213b6c668.title: health status
bdcedf47-3db7-482c-9164-276213b6c668.description: The health of an individual or population measured against an identifiable standard.

aa81d0ee-f52a-47e1-a340-f3326b961858.title: social justice principles
aa81d0ee-f52a-47e1-a340-f3326b961858.description: Principles aimed at decreasing or eliminating inequity; promoting inclusiveness of diversity; and establishing environments that are supportive of all people. The principles include: participation, equity, access and rights.

c2c7f3a2-9b46-4675-bb96-94d03decf2bc.title: equity
c2c7f3a2-9b46-4675-bb96-94d03decf2bc.description: Resources are allocated in accordance with the needs of individuals and populations with the desired goal of equality of health outcomes.

37c40e6b-0ab4-4d80-a11f-dc40423e0bea.title: community
37c40e6b-0ab4-4d80-a11f-dc40423e0bea.description: A group of people linked by a common social structure and sense of belonging. This may be based on location, education, gender, interests, cultural background, political or religious beliefs. It may also refer to an online community.

b255ea15-ae82-44fa-8416-4d5079753eca.title: environmental factors
b255ea15-ae82-44fa-8416-4d5079753eca.description: Factors in the built and natural environments that impact on health, e.g. geographical location, remoteness.

6b065900-1053-45c5-81ac-fb075a087e29.title: health behaviours
6b065900-1053-45c5-81ac-fb075a087e29.description: Refers to a person’s beliefs and actions regarding their health and wellbeing. For example, tobacco use, alcohol consumption, physical activity, dietary behaviour.

ba8df0b5-6acc-4ff1-aa24-47c0c8f3f22a.title: wellbeing
ba8df0b5-6acc-4ff1-aa24-47c0c8f3f22a.description: A sustainable state characterised by predominantly positive feelings, attitudes and relationships. It involves resilience, self-efficacy and a high level of satisfaction with self.

67084702-8777-40f2-a369-4e535a2a03c9.title: personal care
67084702-8777-40f2-a369-4e535a2a03c9.description: Personal care is a broad term used to refer to supporting personal hygiene and toileting, along with dressing and maintaining personal appearance.

4f60547c-f25d-4d96-9ca0-143f80c8f462.title: privacy
4f60547c-f25d-4d96-9ca0-143f80c8f462.description: The right to be left alone, be free from interference or intrusion, and to have some control over your personal information and how it is accessed, used and shared.

8f1eac44-8858-48cc-b98a-c169cea4d4ed.title: interrelationship
8f1eac44-8858-48cc-b98a-c169cea4d4ed.description: The way in which 2 or more things or people are connected and affect one another.

aa2389cb-9485-4368-822b-03eb92cb3e13.title: strategies
aa2389cb-9485-4368-822b-03eb92cb3e13.description: A plan of action developed before beginning a task or activity to successfully achieve a goal or outcome.

49298187-38f1-4625-bfc6-5c17d6210eba.title: access
49298187-38f1-4625-bfc6-5c17d6210eba.description: To gather information from a variety of sources, services and facilities.

3d52bbf2-ae66-429c-a828-c1b0a9b49952.title: community health
3d52bbf2-ae66-429c-a828-c1b0a9b49952.description: Focuses on work within defined communities to maintain and improve the health and wellbeing of all people in that community through collective action.

e86eb910-65bb-4623-bbcf-754ece73688a.title: older people
e86eb910-65bb-4623-bbcf-754ece73688a.description: In Australia, this includes people aged 65 and over.

721dddd6-65f0-4739-a734-05bb1f7287f6.title: digital health
721dddd6-65f0-4739-a734-05bb1f7287f6.description: The electronic management of health information. This includes using technology to collect and share a person’s health information, e.g. a person wearing a device to record how much exercise they do each day, or healthcare providers sharing clinical notes about an individual.

ef017d1f-a2d6-4e56-a62a-eba4ea2802e2.title: big data
ef017d1f-a2d6-4e56-a62a-eba4ea2802e2.description: Extremely large datasets that may be analysed computationally to reveal patterns, trends and associations.

702f68c7-57bf-41b6-9d4d-01e142ccb2aa.title: sociocultural
702f68c7-57bf-41b6-9d4d-01e142ccb2aa.description: Related to social and cultural factors that influence people and communities.

204c3fa3-12ad-45be-9e68-c0a5f29c817b.title: life expectancy
204c3fa3-12ad-45be-9e68-c0a5f29c817b.description: Measures how long, on average, a person is expected to live, based on current age and sex-specific death rates. It is often expressed as the number of years a person born today is expected to live.

7ad25140-c78f-4b73-b740-30a186fdbf65.title: micronutrients
7ad25140-c78f-4b73-b740-30a186fdbf65.description: One of the major groups of nutrients needed by the body for energy production, immune function, blood clotting, growth, bone health and fluid balance, among other functions. Also known as vitamins and minerals.

9c17ab2a-8c06-48ad-acf1-3b1dcf6ea924.title: fitness
9c17ab2a-8c06-48ad-acf1-3b1dcf6ea924.description: A measure of the body’s ability to function efficiently, effectively and without injury in everyday activities, to pursue recreational activities and to cope with emergency situations.

6d2a8db7-13a2-4c65-aced-83cd1a70b1cb.title: biomechanics
6d2a8db7-13a2-4c65-aced-83cd1a70b1cb.description: The area of study with a focus on how and why we move. By applying the fundamental principles of physics to human movement, biomechanists describe and measure movement, and study the causes of such movement. Biomechanics in sports involves a detailed analysis of sports movements in order to minimise the risk of injury and improve performance.

386e664a-9260-4cb7-b346-58d9608341b9.title: sport
386e664a-9260-4cb7-b346-58d9608341b9.description: The term sport is broadened to include physical activity as well as organised and high-performance sport, reflecting ever-increasing opportunities for Australians to engage in physical activity throughout life.

7d0c7fb1-0ffc-4bcb-bfcf-da85a6f20350.title: physical fitness
7d0c7fb1-0ffc-4bcb-bfcf-da85a6f20350.description: A set of attributes (health and skill components) that enable an individual to be physically active.

b72a0333-3880-4374-9c08-c488d2733e07.title: TOTAPS
b72a0333-3880-4374-9c08-c488d2733e07.description: A way of assessing sports injuries in athletes and recreational players before allowing a player to return to the field. TOTAPS stands for Talk, Observe, Touch, Active movement, Passive movement and Skills test.

e7af06d5-01e0-4dd5-b4cc-09b5c07d3069.title: drugs
e7af06d5-01e0-4dd5-b4cc-09b5c07d3069.description: Any substance (excluding food, water and oxygen) that, when taken into a body, alters its function physically or psychologically.

f615b76c-ee19-4925-9dd5-ce1545549bb9.title: first aid
f615b76c-ee19-4925-9dd5-ce1545549bb9.description: The initial care of the ill or injured, usually given by someone who is on the scene when a person becomes ill or injured.

a109ec32-b8ca-4c72-9546-07041a77b97f.title: aerobic
a109ec32-b8ca-4c72-9546-07041a77b97f.description: When referring to exercise, aerobic refers to any physical activity typically performed at a moderate level of intensity for extended periods of time, requiring oxygen to generate energy.

44a0fb74-f8ca-470d-bceb-cfced85ed22d.title: interplay
44a0fb74-f8ca-470d-bceb-cfced85ed22d.description: The way in which 2 or more things have an effect on each other.

94e3e0f6-f328-49f5-9f8b-47dbd2f9e748.title: anaerobic
94e3e0f6-f328-49f5-9f8b-47dbd2f9e748.description: When referring to exercise, anaerobic refers to any physical activity that is performed at a high intensity for a short duration. A limited supply of stored glycogen is used as energy, not requiring oxygen.

a06efcaa-770f-411b-911f-9f4f46007282.title: FITT principle
a06efcaa-770f-411b-911f-9f4f46007282.description: A framework for developing fitness programs that emphasises the variables – Frequency, Intensity, Type of exercise and Time or duration of exercise.

2d3c1707-47e9-4966-98b0-924d23b130d1.title: biomechanical principles
2d3c1707-47e9-4966-98b0-924d23b130d1.description: Scientific principles of mechanical physics concerned with describing movement and understanding the forces that cause movement. Understanding biomechanics helps to minimise the risk of injury, reduce rehabilitation time, improve sports performance and promote sport mastery.

3d1f27f3-954f-4e45-8c8c-6f09d1c7617b.title: values
3d1f27f3-954f-4e45-8c8c-6f09d1c7617b.description: These are ideas and beliefs in a text. They may be reflected in characters, through what they do and say; through the setting of the text, reflecting particular social views; and through the narrative voice of the text, perhaps through authorial comment. Values are specific to individuals and groups, and a text may contain a number of conflicting values.

e62467ea-dfcd-4f3f-9178-8fe7b76d97dc.title: compose
e62467ea-dfcd-4f3f-9178-8fe7b76d97dc.description:
Develop and/or produce signed, spoken, written or multimodal texts in print, visual, oral or digital forms.

See create

fb4811b7-c94c-4ed0-9e9a-b7ee3ec13527.title: conventions
fb4811b7-c94c-4ed0-9e9a-b7ee3ec13527.description: Accepted practices or features that help define textual forms, creative forms, styles and meaning.

2ca15160-063a-4097-8d4a-d430e62798b8.title: audience
2ca15160-063a-4097-8d4a-d430e62798b8.description: Readers, listeners or viewers who engage with a text.

b4c39ca8-c656-4fd4-bd65-4e58bec04036.title: context
b4c39ca8-c656-4fd4-bd65-4e58bec04036.description: An environment or situation (social, cultural or historical) in which a text is responded to or created. Or wording surrounding an unfamiliar word, which a reader or listener uses to understand its meaning.

d394de2d-0772-4669-bb7f-518032fff4ec.title: language forms and features
d394de2d-0772-4669-bb7f-518032fff4ec.description: The symbolic patterns and conventions that shape meaning in texts. These vary according to the particular mode or media of production and can include written, spoken, nonverbal or visual communication of meaning.

3953c626-97bc-4923-ab4d-3c24cf3c8e8d.title: create
3953c626-97bc-4923-ab4d-3c24cf3c8e8d.description:
Develop and/or produce signed, spoken, written or multimodal texts in print, visual, oral or digital forms.

See compose

feddb035-42fa-437d-9f8c-d2dbe7235b60.title: model text
feddb035-42fa-437d-9f8c-d2dbe7235b60.description: A text that is studied as an example to show how specific textual features are crafted. Also known as a mentor text.

e1d9fac1-62b3-47f7-88d4-e270197c2812.title: perspective
e1d9fac1-62b3-47f7-88d4-e270197c2812.description: A way of regarding situations, facts and texts, and evaluating their relative significance.

5ad6016e-bb3f-4521-8d93-ee6e54105e5f.title: language
5ad6016e-bb3f-4521-8d93-ee6e54105e5f.description: A structured system of communication. The structure of a language is its grammar and the free components are its vocabulary. Languages are the primary means of communication of humans, and can be conveyed through speech (spoken language), sign or writing.

58d91b00-13e7-4f26-b7b1-86611c0aa34c.title: form
58d91b00-13e7-4f26-b7b1-86611c0aa34c.description: The category into which a text can be classified based on its arrangement, structure and style, e.g. novel, autobiography, essay, sonnet, haiku, documentary.

d487925c-03cf-4140-a655-08adce5c69a1.title: critical
d487925c-03cf-4140-a655-08adce5c69a1.description: Involving the assessment of the quality of argument, content, analysis, information or persuasion in oral, visual or written text, to assess the way in which themes, issues or ideas are presented for the audience and purposes intended.

27caa0b2-2327-4f27-8ee9-b1f71677542a.title: reflection
27caa0b2-2327-4f27-8ee9-b1f71677542a.description: A transformation of a shape formed by creating a mirror image on the other side of a given line.

a5d3dd08-32cc-4fc6-812d-6364ce91cf44.title: narrative
a5d3dd08-32cc-4fc6-812d-6364ce91cf44.description: An account of events or experiences, which are real or imagined. In English literary theory, narrative includes a story (what is narrated) and a discourse (how it is narrated). Narrative can present as an explicit sequencing of events (type of text) or it can be an implied or inferred component in a text.

56b5557a-2a23-4efc-b61a-0f3927750aa6.title: tone
56b5557a-2a23-4efc-b61a-0f3927750aa6.description: The attitude or feeling the writer expresses through choice of words and/or literary devices, e.g. solemn, playful, defensive or sinister.

2c74b25f-4fe6-4a7d-94cb-668d92685e55.title: preferred communication form(s)
2c74b25f-4fe6-4a7d-94cb-668d92685e55.description: The ways people communicate (i.e. the communicative method(s) or strategies they use) including augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems, eye gaze, objects, gestures, visuals, Key Word Sign or technology.

a93b0470-261f-4b10-8c8e-11bf81f47812.title: critique
a93b0470-261f-4b10-8c8e-11bf81f47812.description: Comprehensive analysis and assessment of a thing, especially a literary, philosophical or political theory, which usually offers a judgement.

1c0f3b94-103e-442b-9ed7-ec6ac2b99386.title: style
1c0f3b94-103e-442b-9ed7-ec6ac2b99386.description: Related creative works and/or practices that share distinctive conventions and/or characteristics.

c8e94f63-7f1e-42b4-b519-04266d8ad7d6.title: representation
c8e94f63-7f1e-42b4-b519-04266d8ad7d6.description: The way ideas are portrayed and represented in texts, using language devices, forms, features and structures of texts to create specific views about characters, events and ideas. Representation applies to all modes: spoken, written, visual and multimodal.

89e30f95-f55e-4125-a5ac-216df2599a26.title: writing
89e30f95-f55e-4125-a5ac-216df2599a26.description:
The planning, composition, editing and publishing of texts in print or digital forms. Various methods of transcription may be used, including communication form(s) and systems.

See communication forms

5a642ef7-4687-47ec-b16a-8fb6856d0f5e.title: mode
5a642ef7-4687-47ec-b16a-8fb6856d0f5e.description:
The most frequently occurring value in a set of data.

Extended in 7–10: There can be more than one mode. When there are 2 modes, the dataset is said to be bimodal.

8a29ed65-a5f8-4564-9aab-bcaa8d24db4c.title: aesthetic
8a29ed65-a5f8-4564-9aab-bcaa8d24db4c.description: Relating to a sense of beauty or an appreciation of artistic expression.

c37ce230-ff3a-4650-a8a5-5d3d25198fc6.title: sustained
c37ce230-ff3a-4650-a8a5-5d3d25198fc6.description: When referring to texts, maintaining consistency of style, form, language features, argument and other unifying characteristics across the entire text.

8bcb4935-6d0d-4710-b561-c064e2aa027f.title: register
8bcb4935-6d0d-4710-b561-c064e2aa027f.description: The degree of formality or informality of language used for a particular purpose or in a particular social setting.

70850e77-38f0-4bf5-92a7-b8b5505d0180.title: composer
70850e77-38f0-4bf5-92a7-b8b5505d0180.description: A noun used to (collectively) describe an author, poet, playwright, director, designer and so on.

3d90b41e-01f7-418c-b854-dc1395cfbc85.title: adaptations
3d90b41e-01f7-418c-b854-dc1395cfbc85.description: A literary work that has been rewritten for presentation in a different medium.

fd805fb8-d276-4804-b3c4-9d92368e27e8.title: appropriation
fd805fb8-d276-4804-b3c4-9d92368e27e8.description: Taking a text or component of a text (such as a character or plot) from one context and using it in another context.

f8b74954-4821-4aad-9e0d-7118168c27f8.title: genre
f8b74954-4821-4aad-9e0d-7118168c27f8.description:
The categories into which texts are grouped based on similarities in premise, structure and function. The ‘genre’ of a text describes larger recurring patterns of subject matter and textual structures observable between texts, such as typical plots, characters and setting.

‘Genre’ can also describe categories of form and structure in texts.

f99f7667-0e33-4140-9ad6-bd7260876a54.title: syntax
f99f7667-0e33-4140-9ad6-bd7260876a54.description: The specific grammatical arrangement of words and phrases into sentences in order to make meaning.

06a51313-6140-41ac-bbf4-baea75680534.title: literacy
06a51313-6140-41ac-bbf4-baea75680534.description: A synthesis of language, thinking and contextual practices through which meaning is shaped. 'Effective literacy is intrinsically purposeful, flexible and dynamic' (J Dawkins 1991, Australia's Language: The Australian Literacy and Language Policy, AGPS, Canberra) and involves interactions in a range of modes and through a variety of media.

86a4c10e-67a0-4280-8e35-9195f0b9a7b0.title: characterisation
86a4c10e-67a0-4280-8e35-9195f0b9a7b0.description: The technical construction and representation of any personality or person-like figure in text, including features such as their appearance, actions, words or thoughts.

07b98739-cfad-4a18-be56-5137b94c6564.title: subject matter
07b98739-cfad-4a18-be56-5137b94c6564.description: The topic or content of a text. For example, an information report on marine vessels may include content about construction materials, and different types of boats and engines.

452f2ee3-9866-408f-992d-4d748ac3c429.title: elements of art and design
452f2ee3-9866-408f-992d-4d748ac3c429.description: Visual and multisensory conventions, including colour, line, shape, space, texture, tone.

5487d56e-1eaa-4e4e-a26a-671b90806c1a.title: art form
5487d56e-1eaa-4e4e-a26a-671b90806c1a.description: A category of artistic representation in Visual Arts distinguished by specific techniques and mediums, encompassing 2D, 3D and 4D creations.

2d8c32f3-dd72-4a9d-a4c5-228bc9bb1c2d.title: multimodal text/presentation
2d8c32f3-dd72-4a9d-a4c5-228bc9bb1c2d.description: A text that combines 2 or more expressive modes to communicate.

267b00b3-1ee0-49c7-a566-dc3808175eaa.title: Cultural identity
267b00b3-1ee0-49c7-a566-dc3808175eaa.description:
Central to Aboriginal ways of knowing, being and doing. Cultural identity includes values and Practices, connections to Country, family, Community, Dreaming, Lore, customs, art, dance and shared experiences.

See culture, Country/Place, Cultural Practices and language group

d1d483a0-75c4-43e9-9047-09221fb03790.title: Cultural Knowledges
d1d483a0-75c4-43e9-9047-09221fb03790.description: Information and technical Knowledge about Country/Place, Customs, Lore, ecologies, environmental management Practices, medicinal and scientific Knowledge, connected to a specific Language Group.

2fa885bd-899a-4161-aa88-cbfcc3da437a.title: improvise
2fa885bd-899a-4161-aa88-cbfcc3da437a.description: Generate spontaneous actions, movement or sounds in response to a stimulus.

91989b62-a52c-4e41-9537-fb7925deaf97.title: timbre
91989b62-a52c-4e41-9537-fb7925deaf97.description: The distinctive and identifiable quality of a sound.

dd0e2e69-3213-4078-b98f-f883305dca49.title: intent
dd0e2e69-3213-4078-b98f-f883305dca49.description: The purpose or message a choreographer or performer aims to communicate.

63186fae-a87f-4b0a-8f9e-77a5269e8a8c.title: elements of music
63186fae-a87f-4b0a-8f9e-77a5269e8a8c.description: Duration, pitch, texture, performing media, timbre, dynamics, expression, structure.

b4f220f5-5ca6-4898-b547-2a9e58209d78.title: listening skills
b4f220f5-5ca6-4898-b547-2a9e58209d78.description:
Skills used to receive sound and understand the message conveyed.

This may include accessing music through other senses and/or the use of assistive technology.

421ebff5-4719-4f70-8d42-04aa136d83d0.title: alignment
421ebff5-4719-4f70-8d42-04aa136d83d0.description: An aspect of safe dance practice. The relationship of the skeleton to the line of gravity and the base of support, which makes movement more efficient and reduces the chance of injury.

bb8065a6-50d6-43dc-978b-406dae39a3a8.title: level
bb8065a6-50d6-43dc-978b-406dae39a3a8.description: The height at which a dancer moves in a space, which may include high, medium or low levels.

ac3bd165-6ce3-455b-9159-bbdb1dcc7adb.title: role
ac3bd165-6ce3-455b-9159-bbdb1dcc7adb.description:
Points of view, objects or personas presented through embodiment.

See character

c0990bcc-8f6f-4d78-abc1-0d4cc359d729.title: character
c0990bcc-8f6f-4d78-abc1-0d4cc359d729.description:
A dramatic role built with complexity, personality and/or background.

See role

5fad2b12-6d7c-42b7-b646-061cf4734504.title: gesture
5fad2b12-6d7c-42b7-b646-061cf4734504.description: A way of communicating with the hands that uses largely unconventional forms (except for conventional gestures such as the thumbs up for good), and that represents more imagistic thought of a speaker or signer. In spoken languages, gestures co-occur with speech, and in signed languages they form gestural overlays.

117aec8f-e622-43ca-9759-5a69e2044470.title: elements of production
117aec8f-e622-43ca-9759-5a69e2044470.description: Set, costume, lighting, props, sound and technologies.

065919f5-15ad-444f-a5e8-45683d0c319e.title: enact
065919f5-15ad-444f-a5e8-45683d0c319e.description: Represent or act the part of an idea or character.

75169a68-cbe6-4515-997d-256796eb0e9c.title: tension
75169a68-cbe6-4515-997d-256796eb0e9c.description: The energy which drives drama. Tension can be developed through embodiment, structure, problems, tasks, conflict and manipulation of audience expectations.

819018b3-8070-4a40-828b-4924a417976d.title: dramatic elements
819018b3-8070-4a40-828b-4924a417976d.description: Role, character, tension, situation, space, time, structure, language, symbol, atmosphere.

f38baaba-5e4a-4679-af3d-1af9cd5eee56.title: still image
f38baaba-5e4a-4679-af3d-1af9cd5eee56.description: A freeze frame, frozen image or tableau that performers make with their bodies, facial expressions and gestures to communicate an idea or a moment in time.

ca22fa97-29d8-4ca9-b825-7f61853f84af.title: pitch
ca22fa97-29d8-4ca9-b825-7f61853f84af.description: The relative highness and lowness of sounds. Can be heard or felt through vibrations.

ee524077-a57b-4878-9082-9935b76171fa.title: rounds
ee524077-a57b-4878-9082-9935b76171fa.description: A part-song in which the voices sing the same melody but enter one after the other.

06d3dc6a-d714-4947-bcbc-b0dfa5ff3684.title: duration
06d3dc6a-d714-4947-bcbc-b0dfa5ff3684.description: The lengths of sounds and silences in music.

f8f09fd8-252d-470d-a9de-0f3df24acba7.title: dramatic play
f8f09fd8-252d-470d-a9de-0f3df24acba7.description: Using imagination to explore and enact ideas, actions, roles and situations.

768e40b3-5d7e-49ac-a9d0-e300832d3a3b.title: sign
768e40b3-5d7e-49ac-a9d0-e300832d3a3b.description: Hand signs (or hand talk) used to supplement or replace oral language. Signs form part of nonverbal communication for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and may be used by people who are hearing, or d/Deaf or hard of hearing. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Sign Languages may be used in some areas. Some Sign Languages may be associated with sacred ceremonial practices.

a88da540-5433-4640-b753-431e20da6ca7.title: Aboriginal Dreaming Stories
a88da540-5433-4640-b753-431e20da6ca7.description:
Stories associated with the beginning of everything, passed down through oral traditions, songs and ceremonies over millennia. Central to Aboriginal Peoples' beliefs about creation, spiritual and physical existence.

See Dreaming

692f7ae0-4549-41f7-b839-f7e3718dd7a2.title: Legends of the Torres Strait
692f7ae0-4549-41f7-b839-f7e3718dd7a2.description: Central to Torres Strait Islander Peoples' beliefs about creation and spiritual and physical existence. Stories about the beginning of all things, passed down through oral traditions, songs and ceremonies for millennia.

0f1f1424-13f3-40c1-af45-f3c3dc2cfc76.title: access content points
0f1f1424-13f3-40c1-af45-f3c3dc2cfc76.description: Content for students with significant intellectual disability who are working towards the Early Stage 1 outcomes. Teachers can use the access content points on their own, or in combination with the content for each outcome.

64a1d8d1-8625-48b5-a659-99a345eff45f.title: performing media
64a1d8d1-8625-48b5-a659-99a345eff45f.description: The instruments, voices or sound sources used in a piece of music.

1a8ba4f7-bcd2-4c1d-8209-3d9fbeb2ab7d.title: collaborate
1a8ba4f7-bcd2-4c1d-8209-3d9fbeb2ab7d.description: Working with others towards a shared goal, through a variety of modes of communication. This may be achieved using a range of technologies, tools and processes.

03f73e3e-7115-416f-ac5b-b27bcc5699a5.title: sequence
03f73e3e-7115-416f-ac5b-b27bcc5699a5.description: A series of kinaesthetically linked dance movements not necessarily based on a compositional idea and intent.

3cc20f67-3d87-47cb-ae5b-92671e4c40c3.title: generating movement
3cc20f67-3d87-47cb-ae5b-92671e4c40c3.description: A process that begins with stimulus, idea and intent, and is developed through improvisation, abstraction, selection and refinement.

e2e1c0fd-99e5-4241-a626-bf1d82f07556.title: expression
e2e1c0fd-99e5-4241-a626-bf1d82f07556.description: The communication of ideas, images and emotions by the performer.

a2cd3818-2885-42c7-bbd4-28e5ee112c18.title: abstraction
a2cd3818-2885-42c7-bbd4-28e5ee112c18.description: The process of generating movement that is symbolic, or changing movement from being representational to symbolic.

ed398a77-c0d2-49c1-99ab-032e30de17b8.title: performance quality
ed398a77-c0d2-49c1-99ab-032e30de17b8.description: The dancer’s skill in applying projection, focus, musicality, quality of line, kinaesthetic awareness, commitment and confidence in order to communicate the desired intent.

0476feff-d1e8-43ac-9688-414f7d333741.title: dance technique
0476feff-d1e8-43ac-9688-414f7d333741.description: Training that physically prepares the body to dance. It is based on safe dance practices and anatomical principles to build strength, coordination and endurance.

d833c310-30a1-4be3-968a-65a53307bdcd.title: warm-up
d833c310-30a1-4be3-968a-65a53307bdcd.description: Movements and/or movement phrases designed to raise the core body temperature and bring the mind into focus for the dance activities to follow.

2eda663e-6ecd-486e-86cb-ac87e0f4407b.title: cool-down
2eda663e-6ecd-486e-86cb-ac87e0f4407b.description: To bring the body back to its normal physiological level after fast, vigorous exercise or activity by gradually slowing the pace of activity or by doing gentle exercises or stretches.

5563de33-c73f-4642-aec5-2f8d26256347.title: dance work
5563de33-c73f-4642-aec5-2f8d26256347.description: A coherent organisation of phrases and sections driven by thematic considerations that create a unified whole.

a542f84e-9ac7-463a-9bf3-0f4855200b3e.title: ancient
a542f84e-9ac7-463a-9bf3-0f4855200b3e.description: In the study of Ancient History in Stage 6, the ancient period covers history from the development of early human communities to the end of late antiquity (around AD 650).

0ae63cb4-594c-41c2-95b2-1e7a96054ff1.title: Dreaming
0ae63cb4-594c-41c2-95b2-1e7a96054ff1.description: The Dreaming has different meanings for different Aboriginal groups. The Dreaming can be seen as the embodiment of Aboriginal creation which gives meaning to everything; the essence of Aboriginal beliefs about creation and spiritual and physical existence. It establishes the rules governing relationships between the people, the land and all things for Aboriginal Peoples. The Dreaming is linked to the past, the present and the future. Where appropriate, refer to Aboriginal names for the Dreaming.

c3d783a4-1e18-454e-adad-dbd930bbe719.title: Elders
c3d783a4-1e18-454e-adad-dbd930bbe719.description: The custodians of knowledge and lore. They are chosen and accepted by their own communities as people who have the permission to disclose cultural knowledge and beliefs. Recognised Elders are highly respected people within Aboriginal communities. Proper consultation with local Aboriginal communities will often direct schools to recognised Elders.

fc4a4c3a-c21d-44e6-a8fa-14630ddf5a9c.title: conservation
fc4a4c3a-c21d-44e6-a8fa-14630ddf5a9c.description: The management and preservation of the natural environment and resources to ensure they are not destroyed in the process of development. The preservation of areas which are culturally or scientifically significant in their natural state.

ab6be143-76d0-454b-8093-6ef2b8f937be.title: local Aboriginal community
ab6be143-76d0-454b-8093-6ef2b8f937be.description:
A local Aboriginal community is constituted by those people who are Aboriginal and who reside in the near locality. Aboriginal communities will have a rich and diverse history that has been seriously affected by dispossession and relations, which sees families with spiritual connection to Country residing beside those who have been forced to move from other locations. The notion of locality is complex and multilayered: schools should seek advice from a range of people and/or organisations representing local interests. 

See community(ies)

0a5ba4c4-e7a9-4324-8478-8e8b399f3926.title: mechanical wave
0a5ba4c4-e7a9-4324-8478-8e8b399f3926.description: A type of wave that requires a medium, such as air, water or a solid material, to travel through.

d1199077-b9b1-42bb-97d8-8dbf1a8af9b4.title: frequency shift phenomenon
d1199077-b9b1-42bb-97d8-8dbf1a8af9b4.description: The observed change in the frequency of a wave when there is relative motion between the source and the observer.

7b8ffea8-c25d-4763-ba6c-afbf8d62e40c.title: blueshift
7b8ffea8-c25d-4763-ba6c-afbf8d62e40c.description: A phenomenon where light from a distant object in the universe shifts to shorter (bluer) wavelengths, indicating it is moving toward the observer.

dd828b4d-bb1f-424c-a94e-7ad473d8e14c.title: redshift
dd828b4d-bb1f-424c-a94e-7ad473d8e14c.description: A phenomenon where light from a distant object in the universe shifts to longer (redder) wavelengths, indicating it is moving away from the observer.

fcdea710-0a2d-49b0-a7e0-5d710aa6246e.title: node
fcdea710-0a2d-49b0-a7e0-5d710aa6246e.description: A point of intersection or connection within a data communication network.

3bcd0910-176c-4a84-9070-af55820b18c5.title: antinode
3bcd0910-176c-4a84-9070-af55820b18c5.description: A point in a standing wave where the amplitude of oscillation is at its maximum, which occurs halfway between 2 nodes.

2e74d920-355f-4d33-9275-ce23dce3ee67.title: refraction
2e74d920-355f-4d33-9275-ce23dce3ee67.description: The changed direction (bending) of a wave when it passes through one transparent substance into another.

e7ceaf93-a4f0-4b5a-ab58-b536f9496d2f.title: constructive interference
e7ceaf93-a4f0-4b5a-ab58-b536f9496d2f.description: Occurs when 2 or more waves combine in phase, causing their amplitudes to add together to produce a wave with a larger amplitude than the original waves.

e7e7a52c-938c-4bf7-bc61-1a9ae4c4fc87.title: destructive interference
e7e7a52c-938c-4bf7-bc61-1a9ae4c4fc87.description: Occurs when the crests and troughs of 2 interfering waves of equal frequency and opposite phase meet, and their amplitudes cancel out.

2e635714-2cba-4d80-bebf-b1fa006194b2.title: rarefactions
2e635714-2cba-4d80-bebf-b1fa006194b2.description: Regions in a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are spread apart, resulting in decreased density and pressure compared to the surrounding areas.

13b1b911-914d-4723-b0a4-b98cc017b196.title: transverse (wave)
13b1b911-914d-4723-b0a4-b98cc017b196.description: A wave motion in which all points of the wave oscillate along paths perpendicular to the direction of the wave's movement, e.g. surface ripples on water, seismic S (secondary) waves, and electromagnetic waves like radio and light.

9e866bb4-a1f3-49c5-aae5-866a5b812bd0.title: longitudinal (wave)
9e866bb4-a1f3-49c5-aae5-866a5b812bd0.description: A type of wave in which the disturbance or oscillation of the medium occurs in the same direction as the direction of propagation of the wave.

7a8ee195-2f25-4fe2-8ab6-672011f50030.title: superposition
7a8ee195-2f25-4fe2-8ab6-672011f50030.description: Two or more waves meet at a point, the total displacement of which is equal to the algebraic sum of the displacements of the individual waves.

99e45eb5-ce7a-406c-9ad2-9bf92dcf7b09.title: standing wave
99e45eb5-ce7a-406c-9ad2-9bf92dcf7b09.description: A wave in which the nodes appear to remain stationary, while the antinodes oscillate with maximum amplitude.

723f82da-0100-4b30-8802-66bed9dbcde8.title: centripetal acceleration
723f82da-0100-4b30-8802-66bed9dbcde8.description: The acceleration directed toward the centre of a circular path that keeps an object moving in a uniform circular motion.

809c9577-e5da-417c-bcb0-cf8713eb5fca.title: work
809c9577-e5da-417c-bcb0-cf8713eb5fca.description: The transfer of energy that occurs when an external force is applied to an object, causing it to move in the direction of the force.

6459c5a6-9a72-4503-8a82-bbe831585661.title: force
6459c5a6-9a72-4503-8a82-bbe831585661.description: A push or pull between objects, which may cause one or both objects to change speed, and/or direction of their motion, and/or their shape.

5c83b1b6-16c6-49d5-b3d6-79d277032765.title: friction
5c83b1b6-16c6-49d5-b3d6-79d277032765.description: The resistance to motion that occurs when 2 surfaces rub against each other.

a2f83a50-a60f-4b68-9cb2-b0ef6e5e1b69.title: attraction (electrical)
a2f83a50-a60f-4b68-9cb2-b0ef6e5e1b69.description: The force that pulls opposite electric charges toward each other.

5aeffcf0-d6df-40cf-8e62-532c7c4488e5.title: repulsion (electrical)
5aeffcf0-d6df-40cf-8e62-532c7c4488e5.description: The force that pushes 2 like electric charges away from each other.

7309a120-3058-4c91-bc71-442d29ebc225.title: electric potential energy
7309a120-3058-4c91-bc71-442d29ebc225.description: The energy in charged objects as a result of their position in an electric field.

f6e058d6-0d82-4f33-96ad-7d8497c8415f.title: conventional current
f6e058d6-0d82-4f33-96ad-7d8497c8415f.description: The flow of positive charge from the positive terminal to the negative terminal of a power source in a circuit.

fb4760f1-414a-4e88-b2f4-e50093f442c9.title: electric circuit
fb4760f1-414a-4e88-b2f4-e50093f442c9.description: A closed path through which electric current flows. It typically consists of a power source, conductive wires, and electrical components.

75eb5368-7a27-408b-958a-e69eda387f43.title: simultaneity
75eb5368-7a27-408b-958a-e69eda387f43.description: The concept that 2 events that occur at the same for one observer may not appear to do so for another observer, depending on their relative motion.

6f792781-c984-4271-b1f1-fd5c3e90ac80.title: time dilation
6f792781-c984-4271-b1f1-fd5c3e90ac80.description: The relativistic effect where time passes at different rates for observers in relative motion.

86090156-7385-4b2d-87a0-56bd2aa3a62a.title: photoelectric effect
86090156-7385-4b2d-87a0-56bd2aa3a62a.description: The process in which a photon ejects an electron from an atom so that all the energy of the photon is absorbed in separating the electron and imparting kinetic energy to it.

6ab0d411-2f5e-44fb-8340-27c81053a6bc.title: diffraction
6ab0d411-2f5e-44fb-8340-27c81053a6bc.description: The bending and spreading of waves when they encounter an obstacle or pass through a narrow opening.

54730572-6546-4e28-a4b9-2033ef319088.title: monochromatic light
54730572-6546-4e28-a4b9-2033ef319088.description: Light that consists of a single wavelength or frequency – meaning it is pure light of one colour of one specific energy.

ced7db29-244b-4ccc-a471-fee3b63de248.title: wavelength
ced7db29-244b-4ccc-a471-fee3b63de248.description: The distance between successive peaks (or troughs) of a wave, measured in metres (m) in the International System of Units (SI).

70f5c49d-8935-4683-8b3d-c6891aab2374.title: inertial frame of reference
70f5c49d-8935-4683-8b3d-c6891aab2374.description: A viewpoint in which Newton’s First Law (the law of inertia) holds true.

d111d1d2-b812-4802-8fdd-aeddc0a6b333.title: non-inertial frame of reference
d111d1d2-b812-4802-8fdd-aeddc0a6b333.description: A viewpoint that is accelerating relative to an inertial frame and to which Newton’s laws of motion do not apply directly.

a2beb139-5537-4c21-a6f0-6428dd0de007.title: muon
a2beb139-5537-4c21-a6f0-6428dd0de007.description: Part of the lepton group which are a type of fundamental particle.

c9351655-68a8-4694-bc22-9b1339e92ad5.title: black body (ideal)
c9351655-68a8-4694-bc22-9b1339e92ad5.description: An object that absorbs all incident electromagnetic radiation, regardless of wavelength or angle, and emits radiation with a characteristic spectrum that depends only on its temperature, not its material or surface.

c4b3320a-bc9f-4498-b391-71b6d6b430eb.title: length contraction
c4b3320a-bc9f-4498-b391-71b6d6b430eb.description: A relativistic phenomenon where an object moving at a high velocity appears shorter along the direction of motion to a stationary observer.

28369a52-dcd2-4f38-aea1-89d9fd9a71fe.title: relativistic momentum
28369a52-dcd2-4f38-aea1-89d9fd9a71fe.description: The momentum of an object moving close to the speed of light, where classical momentum formulas no longer apply: momentum increases more rapidly than classical momentum as an object’s speed approaches c.

d6bc1d85-9c57-4bbb-8ebb-b645a9ad8ef5.title: photon
d6bc1d85-9c57-4bbb-8ebb-b645a9ad8ef5.description: A massless, chargeless particle that represents a quantum with its energy being proportional to the frequency of the radiation.

383e305f-02ea-44d8-a740-1df6797046c2.title: reflection
383e305f-02ea-44d8-a740-1df6797046c2.description: A transformation of a shape formed by creating a mirror image on the other side of a given line.

ba063c75-f6f3-4de2-8553-f8de7c592a03.title: back emf (back electromotive force)
ba063c75-f6f3-4de2-8553-f8de7c592a03.description: The voltage that is induced in a motor's coil when the motor is running. It opposes the applied voltage and is a direct consequence of the Law of Electromagnetic Induction.

a7cead67-aabb-4872-97fa-cbd74f59d456.title: wasted energy
a7cead67-aabb-4872-97fa-cbd74f59d456.description: The energy that is lost during a process or energy conversion usually as heat.

8f849b44-9b45-4b44-b135-b62fa5e67b61.title: conservative forces
8f849b44-9b45-4b44-b135-b62fa5e67b61.description: Forces where work done on an object depends only on initial and final positions, not the path taken.

184c0548-6b9b-4cd8-8882-68ce693bc7e9.title: non-conservative forces
184c0548-6b9b-4cd8-8882-68ce693bc7e9.description: Forces that dissipate mechanical energy from a system, usually by converting it into other forms like heat, sound or deformation; the work done by non-conservative forces depends on the path taken.

97034c20-69b1-46f3-b9b1-9d96f0e94df7.title: elastic collision
97034c20-69b1-46f3-b9b1-9d96f0e94df7.description: A type of collision where both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

a9bb46b8-b4af-4f99-9695-51c5d4b894a3.title: inelastic collision
a9bb46b8-b4af-4f99-9695-51c5d4b894a3.description: A type of collision where momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not, as some of the kinetic energy is converted into other forms of energy.

b591dbd4-025d-466e-b05b-e0ffbb3b53bb.title: mechanical energy
b591dbd4-025d-466e-b05b-e0ffbb3b53bb.description: Is the energy of an object due to its kinetic energy and potential energy.

49282da6-1637-4669-b299-b03a853d27a3.title: electromagnetic spectrum
49282da6-1637-4669-b299-b03a853d27a3.description: The complete range of electromagnetic waves arranged by frequency or wavelength, spanning from low-frequency radio waves to high-frequency gamma rays.

eda40dff-7242-4742-9f5b-b245475407cb.title: translational velocity
eda40dff-7242-4742-9f5b-b245475407cb.description: The rate at which an astronomical object changes position in space.

13476f75-f495-42f7-a558-14ceb174255a.title: fusion (nuclear)
13476f75-f495-42f7-a558-14ceb174255a.description: A process in which 2 or more atomic nuclei combine to form a single, heavier nucleus, releasing a large amount of energy in the process.

7e932553-0b92-4a0e-b1e4-4a03e5a0335e.title: boson
7e932553-0b92-4a0e-b1e4-4a03e5a0335e.description: A type of fundamental particle that carries forces in nature.

4f097570-2e43-4bbd-a91a-76a3290c8b9c.title: binding energy
4f097570-2e43-4bbd-a91a-76a3290c8b9c.description: The energy required to split a nucleus of an atom into its individual protons and neutrons.

a9be5beb-8eab-4f1e-959b-b09815e60d94.title: echolocation
a9be5beb-8eab-4f1e-959b-b09815e60d94.description: A biological sonar system used by some animals to navigate, hunt, and understand their surroundings by emitting sounds and listening to the echoes that bounce back from objects.

5c82bba1-05ba-4354-8790-a808829352ba.title: half-life
5c82bba1-05ba-4354-8790-a808829352ba.description: The time it takes for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.

518fd071-65b9-4e1a-bbab-428711d4cf43.title: transmutation
518fd071-65b9-4e1a-bbab-428711d4cf43.description: The process by which one chemical element or isotope is converted into another when the number of protons in a nucleus changes.

e820739f-75ed-4df9-9de5-4fcacb675b52.title: cathode ray
e820739f-75ed-4df9-9de5-4fcacb675b52.description: A stream of electrons observed in vacuum tubes which are emitted from the cathode (the negatively charged electrode) and travel toward the anode (the positively charged electrode).

be2b3515-0162-4456-a9c9-91d477404f41.title: nucleosynthesis
be2b3515-0162-4456-a9c9-91d477404f41.description: The process by which new atomic nuclei are formed from pre-existing protons and neutrons.

61767b00-2856-43ab-9ff4-1216add76d2d.title: lepton
61767b00-2856-43ab-9ff4-1216add76d2d.description: A type of fundamental particle that does not experience the strong nuclear force.

5c90deb2-da89-44d9-aa63-1205b46bd907.title: weak force
5c90deb2-da89-44d9-aa63-1205b46bd907.description: One of the 4 fundamental forces of nature responsible for processes that change one type of particle into another, particularly within the nuclei of atoms.

d2e4841b-f201-4cdf-91f6-3b35ebe2ae68.title: beta-minus decay
d2e4841b-f201-4cdf-91f6-3b35ebe2ae68.description: A type of radioactive decay in which a neutron inside an unstable atomic nucleus transforms into a proton and, in the process, emits a beta particle (which is an electron) and an electron antineutrino.

af9c9125-ba28-4765-ac15-378ceff1014c.title: beta-plus transformation
af9c9125-ba28-4765-ac15-378ceff1014c.description: A type of radioactive decay where a proton in an unstable nucleus is transformed into a neutron and emits a positron and an electron neutrino.

06cce959-a52e-4735-bee8-d63bd0b504d8.title: radioactivity
06cce959-a52e-4735-bee8-d63bd0b504d8.description: The spontaneous emission of particles or energy from the unstable nucleus of certain atoms as they decay into more stable forms.

cfd5deff-e8c3-44f9-9f87-d3d31379f090.title: baryon
cfd5deff-e8c3-44f9-9f87-d3d31379f090.description: A type of subatomic particle made up of 3 quarks and are part of the hadron family – particles that experience the strong nuclear force.

482c3e48-340c-4541-83a8-192cff4150fb.title: quark
482c3e48-340c-4541-83a8-192cff4150fb.description: A fundamental subatomic particle that experiences all 4 fundamental forces (including the strong nuclear force) and combines to form hadrons.

9df3b817-3af8-4819-93c2-e4ed95615487.title: alpha (decay)
9df3b817-3af8-4819-93c2-e4ed95615487.description: Radioactive disintegration in which positively charged particles composed of 2 protons and 2 neutrons (and therefore equivalent to the nucleus of a helium atom) are emitted.

19b7b0fb-b7f8-4285-ac2a-13578b7b09e5.title: beta (decay)
19b7b0fb-b7f8-4285-ac2a-13578b7b09e5.description: A radioactive transformation in which high-energy, high-speed electrons are emitted.

969b02c2-bee3-4f0c-8ba7-49ed6960fc9f.title: skill-related components of fitness
969b02c2-bee3-4f0c-8ba7-49ed6960fc9f.description: Includes agility, balance, coordination, reactions, power and speed.

a1e9b0cb-a960-407c-b8c3-ee0cf2b4d1b2.title: tactic
a1e9b0cb-a960-407c-b8c3-ee0cf2b4d1b2.description: A specific action or response to a particular situation, designed to implement or support a strategy.

c87bacc1-1893-4110-bb09-ab5490cd12b5.title: movement concepts
c87bacc1-1893-4110-bb09-ab5490cd12b5.description: Movement concepts (or elements of movement) explored in the content include body awareness; spatial awareness; effort awareness; and the relationship to or with objects, people and space.

62520aef-420d-428f-a972-575abce709cf.title: specialised movement skills
62520aef-420d-428f-a972-575abce709cf.description: Movement skills that are task-specific and are required in more organised games and activities.

a5bcb909-a246-45d4-92c7-df85a28db2ff.title: ethical practices
a5bcb909-a246-45d4-92c7-df85a28db2ff.description:
The application of fundamental ethical principles when undertaking research and collecting information, e.g. confidentiality, informed consent, citation and integrity of data. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • respecting confidentiality and anonymity
  • avoiding use of deception or misleading information
  • preventing physical and/or emotional risk or harm
  • obtaining permission to access private property or restricted areas
  • minimising damage to the natural environment
  • observing referencing conventions to avoid plagiarism
  • storing data appropriately, e.g. securely, depersonalising data collected
  • acknowledging the provenance of sources, e.g. information, data, visual materials.

47a247b3-211b-46b0-bd8f-75d4c0e3a247.title: secondary sources/information
47a247b3-211b-46b0-bd8f-75d4c0e3a247.description: Sources of information that have been collected, processed, interpreted and published by others, e.g. census data, newspaper articles and images or information in a published report.

f1fea18a-eebd-4147-9fe6-3b531c3c3368.title: land cover
f1fea18a-eebd-4147-9fe6-3b531c3c3368.description: The natural and artificial features and structures that cover the land’s surface, e.g. trees, grass, crops, wetlands, water, ice, buildings and pavement.

edba77d7-ba9c-4a1b-bb13-0c5d841628d4.title: natural system
edba77d7-ba9c-4a1b-bb13-0c5d841628d4.description: A combination of physical and/or biological elements, and their interconnected processes, that form an integrated whole.

7dcd1204-6a56-4454-a67b-96e4ca10efd3.title: biophysical
7dcd1204-6a56-4454-a67b-96e4ca10efd3.description: Biological and physical elements of the environment. It includes various life forms, both plant and animal, and elements such as temperature, light, humidity and soil nutrients.

0e149239-b8f1-4c7d-a003-4cd0672d8797.title: change
0e149239-b8f1-4c7d-a003-4cd0672d8797.description: The concept of change involves both time and space. Places, environments and geographical phenomena can often be best understood by investigating how they have developed over time periods ranging from a few years to thousands of years. This is important in helping students to understand what is happening around them and to see their world as dynamic.

d26bb655-7f5d-4341-929b-bb1b6a62370b.title: inspirational landscape
d26bb655-7f5d-4341-929b-bb1b6a62370b.description: Landscapes that stimulate emotional responses based on aesthetic elements, e.g. their dramatic physical form, vibrant colour, arrangement of physical features, diversity of plant species. An inspirational landscape may be experienced directly or through soundscapes and tactile representations, e.g. physical models.

71bb1e3b-e39f-437c-bdd1-da87c9156cf4.title: students investigate
71bb1e3b-e39f-437c-bdd1-da87c9156cf4.description: In the context of Geography 11–12, this encompasses a broad range of learning approaches and activities, facilitated by a variety of teaching strategies.

beb45b47-4fc6-46b3-b57c-312b45069cb0.title: human diversity
beb45b47-4fc6-46b3-b57c-312b45069cb0.description: Variations in how people use the places and spaces they occupy, including the nature of their settlements, economies, cultures and societies.

f1311d9f-1ee0-4b72-b272-e35f9214d967.title: economic integration
f1311d9f-1ee0-4b72-b272-e35f9214d967.description: The process by which places become increasingly linked and interdependent economically. This involves the reduction or elimination of the barriers to the flow of goods, services and factors of production between places and nations.

2c769fa6-5f07-4626-aaf2-f62357dd2cad.title: Indigenous
2c769fa6-5f07-4626-aaf2-f62357dd2cad.description:
An internationally recognised term for the first peoples of a land. In NSW the term Aboriginal person/Peoples is preferred.

See Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

532454b8-9e9d-4880-863d-9258ea60ad73.title: geopolitical
532454b8-9e9d-4880-863d-9258ea60ad73.description: Politics and international relations as influenced by geographical factors, e.g. related to space, place and environment.

040ceb1b-5a25-4d28-8551-e20ee8f3e599.title: economic activity
040ceb1b-5a25-4d28-8551-e20ee8f3e599.description: The production, distribution or consumption of goods or services at all levels of society.

d65a0560-7bec-4415-bbaf-5340fd31ee04.title: enterprise
d65a0560-7bec-4415-bbaf-5340fd31ee04.description: An activity that produces goods and/or services. Enterprises are run for the benefit of an individual or a group of individuals. They can range in scale from a transnational corporation to home-based economic activities.

9c3b0468-7589-48a4-a1fa-8178692e64dc.title: range of scales
9c3b0468-7589-48a4-a1fa-8178692e64dc.description: The varying frames of reference used for viewing and analysing the world in spatial terms. These are commonly described as local, national, regional and global. These scales can be used to develop an understanding of places, environments, natural and human phenomena, geographical patterns and processes, and management. They represent the geographical way of investigating the world.

ccc64900-6282-44f1-950f-46b5e6abb343.title: resilience
ccc64900-6282-44f1-950f-46b5e6abb343.description: The ability of an ecosystem to tolerate and recover from natural and/or human-induced disturbance.

b9efca30-1ce4-4e5c-a56c-72998aa2a39d.title: urban place
b9efca30-1ce4-4e5c-a56c-72998aa2a39d.description: A reference to a permanent settlement or built-up area with a relatively dense population.

907c3f15-9198-4f98-97af-de84aff957cd.title: geographical processes
907c3f15-9198-4f98-97af-de84aff957cd.description: The physical and human processes that form and transform the world, e.g. the water cycle, erosion, migration and urbanisation. Geographical processes can work in combination and operate within and between places.

771643b6-eee9-4d1e-9328-7a91f4654438.title: spheres of influence
771643b6-eee9-4d1e-9328-7a91f4654438.description: The geographical area over which the services and functions of an urban settlement extend. Larger settlements typically have a greater sphere of influence than smaller settlements and attract people from a wider geographical area.

0d9eab4c-4643-427e-8875-c0cad890eba6.title: urbanisation
0d9eab4c-4643-427e-8875-c0cad890eba6.description: The process of demographic, economic and/or social change in which an increasing proportion of the population of a country or region live in urban areas. The size and rate of urbanisation is influenced by push-pull factors.

799eb10c-aa26-4c58-9fb9-9381053accb7.title: demography
799eb10c-aa26-4c58-9fb9-9381053accb7.description: The science of vital and social statistics such as the births, deaths, diseases, and/or marriages of human populations. It is the range of different groups existing in a particular population, as distinguished by factors such as age, ethnicity, social background and other statistics.

a5131aec-af37-474b-86ae-d5bf3b677590.title: megacity
a5131aec-af37-474b-86ae-d5bf3b677590.description: In the context of Geography 11–12 and Geography 11–12 Life Skills, a megacity is a metropolitan area with a total population in excess of 10 million.

6e6305a8-9a41-47e3-964f-6da3c4ce48bf.title: geographic region
6e6305a8-9a41-47e3-964f-6da3c4ce48bf.description: A region exhibits shared natural or human characteristics, e.g. political, economic, social, cultural, climate, land/water cover, vegetation, that distinguishes the region from neighbouring regions. Regions can be divisions of a nation, or larger than a nation.

080a55f9-b3a4-4410-b086-c6c3f571d18b.title: ecological hazard
080a55f9-b3a4-4410-b086-c6c3f571d18b.description: A biological hazard that has the potential to impact adversely on the wellbeing of people or the environment more generally. Examples of ecological hazards include malaria, coronavirus, Dengue fever, rabies, cholera, locust plagues, invasive species.

3eda7e97-c0ce-4350-9a82-7ebe60a2fc55.title: natural hazard
3eda7e97-c0ce-4350-9a82-7ebe60a2fc55.description: Atmospheric, hydrological and geomorphic processes and events in the environment that have the potential to damage the environment and endanger communities, e.g. bushfires, tropical cyclones, floods, earthquakes.

b8a99bbd-4096-4627-b904-29002b9ebafb.title: ecological integrity
b8a99bbd-4096-4627-b904-29002b9ebafb.description: The ability of an ecosystem to support and naturally maintain ecological processes, species, a diverse community of organisms, and other important characteristics, with minimal or no intervention through human management.

f40a35fc-9a94-4225-b9cf-335bcc4a5891.title: primary data
f40a35fc-9a94-4225-b9cf-335bcc4a5891.description: Original material collected e.g. field notes, measurements, responses to a survey or questionnaire.

8e3a4412-fd14-4f55-ab20-f4ef55f60777.title: vulnerability
8e3a4412-fd14-4f55-ab20-f4ef55f60777.description: In the context of this syllabus, the term vulnerability refers to an ecosystem’s risk of exposure or susceptibility to stress.

c9293575-b67e-4036-82be-f1a2e9e8aa1a.title: biocapacity
c9293575-b67e-4036-82be-f1a2e9e8aa1a.description: The capacity of nature/ecosystems to produce and renew the resources that people use and to absorb and filter the waste generated by human activities, within a limited period of time.

b3885529-7975-4850-bd4e-79beb1250d16.title: ecological disturbance
b3885529-7975-4850-bd4e-79beb1250d16.description: Temporary changes or events in an ecosystem that cause disturbance to its functioning, e.g. increased mortality of organisms, changes in spatial patterning. Ecosystems are typically resilient to ecological disturbance.

b7ee6069-8443-49ce-9bca-b931f68213bb.title: load
b7ee6069-8443-49ce-9bca-b931f68213bb.description: Any external force or weight that is applied to a structure or component.

e08c0375-c9d4-42d1-94fb-b8bdfc70ab3a.title: mechanical advantage
e08c0375-c9d4-42d1-94fb-b8bdfc70ab3a.description: The ratio of the output force to the input force in a mechanical system.

9b935258-d77d-4701-9af4-4c2948c1a912.title: control system
9b935258-d77d-4701-9af4-4c2948c1a912.description: A system designed to manage, command or regulate the behaviour of other devices or systems using electronic, hydraulic, pneumatic or mechanical methods.

e435897f-8db7-45a9-a2b3-f18c3d31b8af.title: hydraulic
e435897f-8db7-45a9-a2b3-f18c3d31b8af.description: The use of liquids, such as water or oil, to create movement or apply force, usually through pipes or cylinders.

0afed6f2-a821-4aba-b581-46e7d82d94b4.title: pneumatic
0afed6f2-a821-4aba-b581-46e7d82d94b4.description: The use of compressed air or gas, to create movement or apply force, usually through pipes or cylinders. Pressure is often controlled by a regulator.

ec7c0537-d74b-4c4d-81d9-ed4f012cac8a.title: open-loop control system
ec7c0537-d74b-4c4d-81d9-ed4f012cac8a.description: A system that works without using feedback. It follows a set of instructions to produce an outcome but does not check or adjust its performance.

4ec8c0d1-adbb-46bc-8a64-f232e1d92863.title: efficiency
4ec8c0d1-adbb-46bc-8a64-f232e1d92863.description: The ratio of the work done, or energy developed by a machine or engine, to the energy supplied to it.

db4ce491-ee40-4f5f-9d51-1a9abd67739d.title: simple machine
db4ce491-ee40-4f5f-9d51-1a9abd67739d.description: A basic mechanical device that changes the direction or magnitude of a force, making work easier.

87807f3d-41e4-4d1f-8353-a67fde6531de.title: gear
87807f3d-41e4-4d1f-8353-a67fde6531de.description: A toothed wheel that engages with other wheels or parts to transfer motion. This engagement allows motion to be transferred in the same or a different direction.

8f138f00-7273-4551-8b26-fa9bba453928.title: mechanism
8f138f00-7273-4551-8b26-fa9bba453928.description: A system of moving parts that work together to perform a function, often by transforming the direction, speed, or size of a force.

79d5df87-e0c0-48f2-b9d7-0888516bf8bc.title: structure
79d5df87-e0c0-48f2-b9d7-0888516bf8bc.description: Part of the forming process in composition and choreography. There are 2 main parts; organising the movement; and organising the dance.

c3c2b537-7177-4e28-9e0b-71c49e6e56e4.title: live load
c3c2b537-7177-4e28-9e0b-71c49e6e56e4.description: Temporary or changing weight on a structure such as people, furniture, or vehicles. These loads can move or change over time.

5bc79f77-dce5-41fd-ae58-91ec79fb244b.title: dead load
5bc79f77-dce5-41fd-ae58-91ec79fb244b.description: A permanent and immovable load, such as the weight of a structure itself.

aeeab801-99c4-4643-9d7b-01c8b78e450f.title: notions
aeeab801-99c4-4643-9d7b-01c8b78e450f.description: The small objects or accessories, including items that are sewn or otherwise attached to a textiles article, such as buttons, ribbon, zippers, hooks and eyes.

4d9f8e6c-48a3-4e14-9266-ebb700b6bfea.title: aesthetics
4d9f8e6c-48a3-4e14-9266-ebb700b6bfea.description: Concerned with the appearance and visual impact or appeal of a product, system or environment and influenced by social, emotional and demographic factors.

3242273c-44c2-478d-a37c-2400f35b027e.title: innovation
3242273c-44c2-478d-a37c-2400f35b027e.description: The action or process of developing new items or changing existing products, systems or environment in order to improve their function, aesthetics or environmental impact.

00ff5fd3-7fb0-420a-bd98-b3159e4d2463.title: product
00ff5fd3-7fb0-420a-bd98-b3159e4d2463.description: The tangible end results of natural, human, mechanical, manufacturing, electronic or digital production and processes.

5a746551-3b8c-4192-8927-58345bee4425.title: branching
5a746551-3b8c-4192-8927-58345bee4425.description: An instruction in a computer program or algorithm that causes different actions to be performed depending on specified conditions.

92569360-9b9d-43f4-bb1c-b806e0e81339.title: iteration
92569360-9b9d-43f4-bb1c-b806e0e81339.description: A repetition of a process in computer programming where each repeated cycle builds towards a desired result.

b21e5987-d364-48dd-8e2f-0597f507eba1.title: digital technologies
b21e5987-d364-48dd-8e2f-0597f507eba1.description: Refers to electronic tools, systems, devices and resources that generate, process or store data, and may include applications, games, microcontrollers, mobile devices, multimedia, networks, robotics.

78536d55-360e-45e1-a96b-d71b1066460e.title: algorithm
78536d55-360e-45e1-a96b-d71b1066460e.description: A step-by-step procedure required to solve a problem. Algorithms may be presented in many ways, e.g. written instructions, flow charts or using a computer programming language.

ee6526ed-46f4-43b0-af86-e686a7bc22d8.title: user interface (UI)
ee6526ed-46f4-43b0-af86-e686a7bc22d8.description: The means by which users interact with computer hardware or software. In software, this usually comprises fields for text and number entry, mouse pointers, buttons and other graphical elements. In hardware, switches, dials and light-emitting diodes (LEDs) provide information about the interactions between a user and a machine.

adb39aa5-6420-432f-a229-71dde601ab85.title: artificial intelligence (AI)
adb39aa5-6420-432f-a229-71dde601ab85.description: Intelligence demonstrated by machines. Sometimes called machine intelligence.

cd59c161-1903-4d88-97b6-659b75ef1d96.title: computational thinking
cd59c161-1903-4d88-97b6-659b75ef1d96.description: A process in which a problem is analysed and solved so that a human, machine or computer can effectively implement the solution. It involves using strategies to organise data logically, break down problems into parts, interpret patterns and design, and implement algorithms to solve problems.

d424d842-a858-4023-8d6a-222ed3c3e456.title: systems thinking
d424d842-a858-4023-8d6a-222ed3c3e456.description: An understanding of how related objects or components interact to influence how systems function. Students are provided with opportunities to recognise the connectedness of, and interactions between phenomena, people, places and events in local and wider contexts and consider the impact of their decisions. Understanding the complexity of systems and the interdependence of components is important for scientific research and for the creation of solutions to technical, economic and social issues.

7ec8fc89-3a19-420e-b1fa-e610dba4658e.title: user experience (UX)
7ec8fc89-3a19-420e-b1fa-e610dba4658e.description: The usability, ease of use, and enjoyment provided in the interaction between the customer and the product.

1ee5c038-cf4e-48a6-9d08-c7853652606f.title: cybersecurity
1ee5c038-cf4e-48a6-9d08-c7853652606f.description: The protection of information technology elements, including hardware and software, data or network services.

91017140-1948-41b4-98c6-5751ccefa9c9.title: design thinking
91017140-1948-41b4-98c6-5751ccefa9c9.description: A process where a need or opportunity is identified and a design solution is developed. The consideration of economic, environmental and social impacts that result from designed solutions are core to design thinking. Design thinking methods can be used when trying to understand a problem, generate ideas and refine a design based on evaluation and testing.

f133c98b-68cf-475b-bea7-e53867ea7ec0.title: design and production
f133c98b-68cf-475b-bea7-e53867ea7ec0.description: A process that typically involves identifying and defining, researching and planning, producing and implementing, and testing and evaluating to create a designed solution that considers social, cultural and environmental factors.

5a1184ff-8fce-4758-b983-fddabe3f0c2f.title: prototype
5a1184ff-8fce-4758-b983-fddabe3f0c2f.description:
A trial product or model built to test an idea or process to inform further design development. Its purpose is to see if and how well the design works and is tested by users and systems analysts. A prototype can be either a physical object or exist in digital form.

See model

ff79e2e4-cc20-48dd-89da-ff58876db8e6.title: app
ff79e2e4-cc20-48dd-89da-ff58876db8e6.description: A software program designed for a specific purpose to run on mobile devices or on a personal computer. An abbreviation of the word ‘application’.

9124e62c-e812-4b6b-b4c6-ca6c3241ae12.title: assistive technology (AT)
9124e62c-e812-4b6b-b4c6-ca6c3241ae12.description: A device or system whose primary purpose is to maintain or improve an individual's functioning and independence to facilitate participation and enhance overall wellbeing. This includes technologies specifically designed to meet an individual's needs, eg eye gaze technology, as well as more general technologies that can be used by anyone, eg speech-to-text applications. Assistive technology can also be referred to as inclusive technology.

5024e843-34e4-4385-8b7d-cda9a0a1eab7.title: interactive media
5024e843-34e4-4385-8b7d-cda9a0a1eab7.description: The use of digital technologies to present combinations of text, graphics, video, animation and/or sound in an integrated way. For example, include interactive games, media-rich websites and electronic books (eBooks).

f98101cd-2df2-4fc7-811e-fc0ae2f016f3.title: information
f98101cd-2df2-4fc7-811e-fc0ae2f016f3.description: The presentation of data in a manner that is readily understood.

410bc277-6674-41ec-a4f1-3a4c443c9cbb.title: hardware
410bc277-6674-41ec-a4f1-3a4c443c9cbb.description: The collection of physical components that constitute a computer system, all of which are tangible objects. Hardware includes both internal and external components of the system, as well as any peripheral devices that can be connected.

de924b36-24cd-4a40-9c42-30ecca3f6277.title: assets
de924b36-24cd-4a40-9c42-30ecca3f6277.description: Assets are the digital elements that can be used or incorporated into a multimedia presentation or production. They include graphics, photographs, videos, audio, animations or other artistic data.

27181b8c-34e2-4db7-bfb7-5e513852bfa8.title: lossless compression
27181b8c-34e2-4db7-bfb7-5e513852bfa8.description: A type of compression algorithm that retains sufficient information to allow the original data to be perfectly reconstructed from the compressed data. It is used when it is important for the original data to be accurately preserved, e.g. in text documents, programming source code, application files or for archival purposes.

7f1cae53-18a3-457e-8fa2-8bf7e515b742.title: interactive media systems
7f1cae53-18a3-457e-8fa2-8bf7e515b742.description: Where there is facility for a user to interact with multimedia, the term ‘interactive media’ may be used. The use of digital technologies to present combinations of text, graphics, video, animation and/or sound in an integrated way. For example, interactive games, media-rich websites and electronic books (e-books).

8f6638e2-3abc-43be-825b-6d578eb3ff88.title: evaluate
8f6638e2-3abc-43be-825b-6d578eb3ff88.description: Make a judgement based on criteria; determine the value of.

0abedeb4-af67-4efe-8554-db41780713fa.title: data types
0abedeb4-af67-4efe-8554-db41780713fa.description:
Data types used in computing are expressed as either:

  • string/text
  • character
  • integer
  • floating point or real
  • date and time
  • Boolean.

9e50f7a1-90b3-4cf3-97c6-d12a20834400.title: visualisation
9e50f7a1-90b3-4cf3-97c6-d12a20834400.description: The presentation of data or information through pictures or graphics to help the intended audience understand its significance.

b26b9607-6937-4a34-a3fb-bc7f14e8736b.title: data sampling
b26b9607-6937-4a34-a3fb-bc7f14e8736b.description: The practice of analysing a subset of a larger dataset in order to determine meaningful information such as patterns and trends.

e8106068-0e64-41ab-ae6b-c57d0343e2b2.title: informatics
