e8106068-0e64-41ab-ae6b-c57d0343e2b2.description: The science of processing data for storage and retrieval.

bccaddf1-8333-4f0d-a010-30100d4abee2.title: structured data
bccaddf1-8333-4f0d-a010-30100d4abee2.description: Data with a high degree of organisation, such that it can easily be analysed and processed using algorithms. The organisation of the data takes on a form that captures the properties and behaviours of the source the data represents.

4ebd40d7-d9e3-4d68-8665-05f49e6a039c.title: blockchain
4ebd40d7-d9e3-4d68-8665-05f49e6a039c.description: A growing list of records, known as blocks, which are linked using cryptography. It can be used to record transactions between 2 parties efficiently and in a verifiable and permanent way.

3a24583b-9f58-4fb9-8c15-328d32bb61ca.title: database
3a24583b-9f58-4fb9-8c15-328d32bb61ca.description: A collection of data organised by records and fields that can be easily stored, accessed, managed and updated.

869cb91f-24b3-4b51-9e8f-ae6f7cb2ba88.title: enterprise system
869cb91f-24b3-4b51-9e8f-ae6f7cb2ba88.description: The combination of digital systems, people and processes that collect, manage and analyse data.

6f01b632-ced6-442d-8018-c98e06f83c6f.title: enterprise computing
6f01b632-ced6-442d-8018-c98e06f83c6f.description: Refers to business-oriented information technology that is critical to a company’s operations. Enterprise computing encompasses types of information technology tools that businesses use for resource management, efficient production operations, relationship management and back office support.

97ec5bf1-1add-46d3-afce-ac4acee5d390.title: social network
97ec5bf1-1add-46d3-afce-ac4acee5d390.description: A structure that describes the relationships that exist between individuals and/or organisations. Social networking services and tools provide a mechanism for people who share common interests or personal ties to communicate, share and interact using a range of media such as text, images and video.

31c37a8e-9fd8-41c1-9b24-784d2f45915b.title: block-based
31c37a8e-9fd8-41c1-9b24-784d2f45915b.description: A type of programming that uses colourful, draggable shapes that represent code. Blocks are arranged and connected to write programs.

40aea08d-1b82-41b5-a7da-310c35d92e1a.title: node
40aea08d-1b82-41b5-a7da-310c35d92e1a.description: A point of intersection or connection within a data communication network.

9c72895d-846d-4352-ae86-cc43b948d4e2.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
9c72895d-846d-4352-ae86-cc43b948d4e2.description: Internet of Things (IoT) encompasses smart devices and smart objects that send and receive information using the internet and communication infrastructure.

ee056031-0a38-4c6f-93b7-c05738861391.title: Internet of Me (IoMe)
ee056031-0a38-4c6f-93b7-c05738861391.description: The internet of me (IoMe) loosely refers to technology which connects our minds and bodies with the online world. It transforms our biological and cognitive life into streams of data which can be monitored, shared and shaped.

fc70c85b-16f8-4e37-a291-a2bb441b1ad8.title: metadata
fc70c85b-16f8-4e37-a291-a2bb441b1ad8.description: A set of data that describes and gives information about other data. For example, the metadata of a photograph is the set of data providing information about copyright.

11ad7976-619b-4beb-9589-9c59ec2e4fef.title: social media
11ad7976-619b-4beb-9589-9c59ec2e4fef.description: Websites and applications that enable users to create and share content or to participate in social networking.

8e789057-f99f-4b23-aae3-7f7aa49d6fad.title: intelligent system
8e789057-f99f-4b23-aae3-7f7aa49d6fad.description: A collective term for enterprise-based information systems that have the capacity to gather and/or analyse data and communicate with other systems, learn and produce targeted output to respond to the world around them.

53e53160-11b4-4861-9c50-ed661411b521.title: encryption
53e53160-11b4-4861-9c50-ed661411b521.description: A process in cryptography of encoding (converting) data, using mathematical formulas, into a form that only an intended recipient can decode, often including a personal digital signature.

70ba2547-ce2f-4f93-821e-b4ab49ba8185.title: transmission media
70ba2547-ce2f-4f93-821e-b4ab49ba8185.description: The means through which data is sent from one system to another on a network.

fec347c9-288b-457c-9940-290772a28373.title: workflow
fec347c9-288b-457c-9940-290772a28373.description: A sequence of processes and/or activities that a document or artefact transitions through in order to reach completion.

9af61f61-b3fa-4baa-8577-143f19a4d03f.title: cloud computing
9af61f61-b3fa-4baa-8577-143f19a4d03f.description: Distributing computing over a network where storage of files, processing of data and/or access to software occurs automatically on interconnected server computers to which the user’s device is connected. The term refers to accessing files, software and services over the internet.

00d20516-b7ab-4bf9-9603-a6b7710df61d.title: expert system
00d20516-b7ab-4bf9-9603-a6b7710df61d.description: A computer program that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to solve complex problems and emulate the decision-making ability of a human expert.

88d300ef-878d-4490-b43e-a57d86df9961.title: automate
88d300ef-878d-4490-b43e-a57d86df9961.description: The process of transforming and manipulating data that does not require user intervention. For example, through the use of formulae in a spreadsheet, new sets of data can be processed and the results recalculated automatically, or a webcam can be turned on as a result of movement sensor input.

a48516f7-48e5-4ca2-a54c-d87ecec4943a.title: producing
a48516f7-48e5-4ca2-a54c-d87ecec4943a.description: Actively realising (making) designed solutions, using appropriate resources and means of production.

5c34503e-3378-49eb-babc-741ff25b71c7.title: cyber safety
5c34503e-3378-49eb-babc-741ff25b71c7.description: A term that refers to behaviour and the precautions that may be exercised when providing personal information in an online or digital environment.

2aad2114-2999-40ee-a6b8-c1ff6676b1a2.title: digital citizenship
2aad2114-2999-40ee-a6b8-c1ff6676b1a2.description: An acceptance and upholding of the norms of appropriate, responsible behaviour with regard to the use of digital technologies.

44225606-831f-49fb-b425-6f8a8947e649.title: digital footprint
44225606-831f-49fb-b425-6f8a8947e649.description: Traces of data left behind by a person using a digital system. A person’s digital footprint includes all information actively provided by that person, such as interactions on social networks, online purchases, emails and instant messages. It also includes passive information, such as logs of software installed and used on a computer, metadata associated with files, a user’s internet protocol (IP) address, a device being used to access a webpage, and a user’s browsing history stored as cookies or by internet service providers.

0684c6e0-fdde-41cb-88df-ca1984224a82.title: threat actor
0684c6e0-fdde-41cb-88df-ca1984224a82.description: An individual or group that poses a security threat to an individual or organisation.

4901de61-359a-419d-a58a-9dfc2e292fa8.title: polyprotic acid
4901de61-359a-419d-a58a-9dfc2e292fa8.description: An acid that can donate more than one proton (H+) per molecule.

3f960835-5a48-4bf8-862f-b031c8259c8b.title: limiting reagents
3f960835-5a48-4bf8-862f-b031c8259c8b.description: The reactant that is completely used up first in a chemical reaction, limiting the amount of product produced.

12d06fdc-9a3b-4939-b02f-7b925dcb31e2.title: back titration
12d06fdc-9a3b-4939-b02f-7b925dcb31e2.description: An analytical technique used to determine the concentration of a substance that is not able to be determined directly.

991e6ba1-5f81-4040-a8ab-1312bd6db93c.title: neutralisation reaction
991e6ba1-5f81-4040-a8ab-1312bd6db93c.description: The act of making a substance chemically neutral, so it is not an acid or a base.

ded8a746-b365-4181-a297-aa37b64eb199.title: primary standard solution
ded8a746-b365-4181-a297-aa37b64eb199.description: A solution made from a highly pure, stable and accurately weighable substance used to determine the concentration of another solution in titration.

7eef53b7-4a36-41bb-8a05-8676a3d6b0b8.title: buffer
7eef53b7-4a36-41bb-8a05-8676a3d6b0b8.description: A solution that remains unchanged in its pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.

3c29fb2a-305c-4e12-be60-fe3f6b457879.title: equivalence point
3c29fb2a-305c-4e12-be60-fe3f6b457879.description: The point in a titration when equal amounts of acid and base have reacted, meaning the moles of acid equals moles of base.

949871a5-56fa-452d-8a4d-2cdb5d7869e9.title: endpoint (of titration)
949871a5-56fa-452d-8a4d-2cdb5d7869e9.description: The point at which the indicator changes colour to show the equivalence point has been reached.

483783c9-6fbf-41c2-b841-901c84861da1.title: acid–base indicator
483783c9-6fbf-41c2-b841-901c84861da1.description: A substance used to indicate an acidic or basic solution.

abe5d75d-c4da-4c83-9034-d533748eda32.title: conjugate acid–base pairs
abe5d75d-c4da-4c83-9034-d533748eda32.description: Two substances that differ by one proton where the acid donates a proton and becomes its conjugate base or the base accepts a proton and becomes its conjugate acid.

a16c551a-7d1a-4dfc-99fd-79ee116de96b.title: amphiprotic
a16c551a-7d1a-4dfc-99fd-79ee116de96b.description: A substance capable of accepting or donating a proton to act like either an acid or base.

8a9095b9-c969-4790-bc04-96c4c4d6673e.title: substance
8a9095b9-c969-4790-bc04-96c4c4d6673e.description: Matter in the form of elements, compounds, or mixtures.

0974ea0e-0282-4e91-bc46-cc3336903137.title: monoprotic acid
0974ea0e-0282-4e91-bc46-cc3336903137.description: An acid that can donate only 1 proton (H+) per molecule to a base

3abaa4c2-dc2a-44d1-9560-19b27e30504a.title: diprotic acid
3abaa4c2-dc2a-44d1-9560-19b27e30504a.description: An acid substance that can donate 2 protons per molecule in an aqueous solution.

715a019d-1147-4936-9aeb-b2bbdf1d464f.title: triprotic acid
715a019d-1147-4936-9aeb-b2bbdf1d464f.description: An acid that can donate 3 protons (H+) per molecule in a reaction.

25aae243-f496-43ec-9c11-043ddd1c1c92.title: titration curves
25aae243-f496-43ec-9c11-043ddd1c1c92.description: A graph that represents the change in pH of a solution as a titrant is gradually added during a titration process.

3df88940-311c-4363-a818-1b70ca79f964.title: dissociation constant
3df88940-311c-4363-a818-1b70ca79f964.description: An equilibrium constant that describes the separation of a weak acid (Ka) or weak base with water (Kb).

6a1c4789-c567-4f6c-9547-dc4450922a83.title: acid dissociation constant (Ka)
6a1c4789-c567-4f6c-9547-dc4450922a83.description: The measure of the strength of an acid in solution.

c9bcdeea-3525-4f35-abb1-819f7801aeca.title: base dissociation constant (Kb)
c9bcdeea-3525-4f35-abb1-819f7801aeca.description: The measure of the strength of a base in solution.

02019bb4-403f-4a5e-a628-4801f6a41076.title: electron configuration
02019bb4-403f-4a5e-a628-4801f6a41076.description: The arrangement of electrons in an atom’s orbitals, showing how electrons fill shells and subshells (s, p, d, f) according to energy levels.

d3665778-6c88-494d-8fb8-c9186bb886c3.title: galvanic cell
d3665778-6c88-494d-8fb8-c9186bb886c3.description: An electrochemical cell that generates electrical energy from a spontaneous redox reaction occurring within it.

7c1a5346-7ec4-40c5-aaac-2ff43ece104a.title: proton (1H) NMR spectroscopy
7c1a5346-7ec4-40c5-aaac-2ff43ece104a.description: An analytical technique used to determine the structure of organic compounds by studying how hydrogen nuclei (¹H) in a molecule absorb radiofrequency energy in a magnetic field.

0a369198-e014-473d-9cc1-1135c9954988.title: atomic emission spectroscopy (AES)
0a369198-e014-473d-9cc1-1135c9954988.description: An analytical technique to determine and measure the unknown concentration of metal ions in a sample based on the amount of light it emits.

1b87554a-4df3-47eb-abc1-8fe293a0e58f.title: infrared spectroscopy
1b87554a-4df3-47eb-abc1-8fe293a0e58f.description: An analytical technique that uses the interaction of infrared light with a sample to identify and characterise molecules.

49f513bf-3753-4a97-b5eb-1021dbd04dfa.title: standard reduction potentials
49f513bf-3753-4a97-b5eb-1021dbd04dfa.description: The measure of the tendency of a chemical species to be reduced by gaining electrons measured under standard conditions.

d186bdb3-f7c3-4f6d-8870-506cc63cf4b0.title: cell potential
d186bdb3-f7c3-4f6d-8870-506cc63cf4b0.description: The voltage difference between the 2 electrodes of an electrochemical cell.

76151aee-7d3b-4d70-8924-635b20244e35.title: carbon (13C) NMR spectroscopy
76151aee-7d3b-4d70-8924-635b20244e35.description: An analytical technique used to determine the structure of organic compounds by observing the behaviour of carbon-13 nuclei in a magnetic field.

e4f41bd6-0e30-4276-aa5f-943d4d1f0874.title: redox reactions
e4f41bd6-0e30-4276-aa5f-943d4d1f0874.description: A reaction in which oxidation and reduction is occurring.

15f79ecb-6f90-4dfb-9d91-f4b6f85179c2.title: homologous series
15f79ecb-6f90-4dfb-9d91-f4b6f85179c2.description: A family of organic compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties and general formula, where each successive member differs by a CH2 unit.

c7ce260d-526e-4c71-b4fb-3683eff1a5a7.title: chemical reaction
c7ce260d-526e-4c71-b4fb-3683eff1a5a7.description: A process in which the breaking and forming of chemical bonds transforms one or more reactants into different products and includes the release or absorption of energy.

0ff65102-31ce-4146-a1fa-d1e30f830ab0.title: electronegativity
0ff65102-31ce-4146-a1fa-d1e30f830ab0.description: The ability of an atom to attract bonding electrons toward itself to form a chemical bond.

491d3fdf-e454-4d7c-a1f6-11a2d9780c22.title: decomposition
491d3fdf-e454-4d7c-a1f6-11a2d9780c22.description: A chemical reaction in which a complex reactant (that consists of multiple components or molecules) breaks down into 2 or more simpler products.

b623f712-ef5f-4afb-898b-d851f0991ca1.title: closed system
b623f712-ef5f-4afb-898b-d851f0991ca1.description: A chemical system in which no substances are able to enter or leave.

5cc3f3d2-7f9e-403a-9cad-cdcf704ec902.title: solution
5cc3f3d2-7f9e-403a-9cad-cdcf704ec902.description: A mixture made up of a solvent and a dissolved solute.

8a9640f3-99c4-4788-b945-b1ec69f88d3a.title: dynamic equilibrium
8a9640f3-99c4-4788-b945-b1ec69f88d3a.description: In the context of Geography 11–12, when an ecosystem is able to maintain its natural balance and remain relatively stable, subject to gradual changes through natural succession. An ecosystem that is in a state of dynamic equilibrium is able to return to its balanced state in response to natural and/or human stresses.

ed11bcdc-cb5c-459e-958c-d7c3751a3581.title: dissolution
ed11bcdc-cb5c-459e-958c-d7c3751a3581.description: The dissolving of a gas, liquid or solid in a solvent to form a homogenous solution (gas or liquid).

1348e03e-47ef-448a-9f49-e80e77f3a754.title: solute
1348e03e-47ef-448a-9f49-e80e77f3a754.description: A substance that is dissolved by a solvent.

de40e214-b8be-4061-8272-b48daf0a567a.title: ideal gases
de40e214-b8be-4061-8272-b48daf0a567a.description: A theoretical gas that perfectly follows the ideal gas law and assumes no interactions between particles and in which the particles occupy no volume.

423e6de4-cb0c-450b-a09a-e0b6e175ef3c.title: solvent
423e6de4-cb0c-450b-a09a-e0b6e175ef3c.description: A substance, especially a liquid, that can dissolve other substances.

53a10e53-3760-416c-be1c-48bf953d4ca1.title: open system
53a10e53-3760-416c-be1c-48bf953d4ca1.description: A chemical system in which substances are able to enter or leave.

583329b2-2275-41fb-87b4-cf509cc8c2b6.title: percentage composition
583329b2-2275-41fb-87b4-cf509cc8c2b6.description: Ratio by mass in which elements are present.

8d7cb457-64b5-4189-8621-6951b059f404.title: empirical formulae
8d7cb457-64b5-4189-8621-6951b059f404.description: The chemical formula of a compound that gives the simplest whole-number ratio by atoms of each element in a compound.

1e01877f-a0c6-4abb-965f-c836e2e4ce8e.title: stoichiometry
1e01877f-a0c6-4abb-965f-c836e2e4ce8e.description: Study of quantitative relationships in chemical formulae and equations.

469636c6-fb19-41df-8fe3-e49926ae2d58.title: radioisotope
469636c6-fb19-41df-8fe3-e49926ae2d58.description: An element that has the same atomic number and similar chemical properties, but different atomic masses.

42b0ec33-3099-419d-89ca-44bac557199a.title: ionic (bond)
42b0ec33-3099-419d-89ca-44bac557199a.description: A very strong chemical bond formed by the transfer of one or more electrons from one atom to another atom; the ions are held together by electrostatic attraction.

cb05f8aa-23fd-4f0e-bcb4-df31d8130f6f.title: first ionisation energy
cb05f8aa-23fd-4f0e-bcb4-df31d8130f6f.description: The amount of energy required to remove one electron from a neutral atom in the gaseous state to form a +1 ion.

90be08c7-5835-4dc7-8f37-e2b72ec7c6a9.title: matter
90be08c7-5835-4dc7-8f37-e2b72ec7c6a9.description: A physical substance; anything that has mass and occupies space.

0e6127f9-0784-4b9a-bc41-4e2a0fbafa30.title: metallic bond
0e6127f9-0784-4b9a-bc41-4e2a0fbafa30.description: A type of chemical bond formed between positively charged metal ions and the delocalised electrons surrounding them.

689761d5-66a3-4ef4-88bb-041c7da7e147.title: groups (within the periodic table)
689761d5-66a3-4ef4-88bb-041c7da7e147.description: A vertical column of the periodic table.

1ad84fad-2e81-4c93-bede-da88d71e8c38.title: covalent bond
1ad84fad-2e81-4c93-bede-da88d71e8c38.description: A chemical bond made when 2 atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

1b788415-1037-4357-8fd0-336b2d0dc36b.title: periodic table
1b788415-1037-4357-8fd0-336b2d0dc36b.description: A table in which all the known chemical elements are arranged in rows and columns so that elements with similar chemical properties lie in the same column.

37f6e3d3-5ba8-4428-8aa0-4d7336973823.title: element
37f6e3d3-5ba8-4428-8aa0-4d7336973823.description: One of a class of substances which consists entirely of atoms of the same atomic number, and which cannot be further divided by chemical methods.

f44c9f23-26b7-4fb4-8d1d-fe238fcc42c8.title: isotope
f44c9f23-26b7-4fb4-8d1d-fe238fcc42c8.description: Variants of a chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.

4dc65418-aeec-42e2-ae66-621341ff4e82.title: electrostatic
4dc65418-aeec-42e2-ae66-621341ff4e82.description: Relating to electricity or fields that do not move in a current but are instead attracted to the surface of an object, as opposed to electric currents.

565526a8-ff37-48ee-b22b-01626084b978.title: orbital
565526a8-ff37-48ee-b22b-01626084b978.description: A region around an atom’s nucleus where there is a high probability of finding an electron.

b31cb2c4-073f-4a36-b83d-49f35a1c1cd0.title: hydrogen bonding
b31cb2c4-073f-4a36-b83d-49f35a1c1cd0.description: A type of strong dipole–dipole interaction that occurs when a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom (N, O, or F) is attracted to the lone pair of electrons on another nearby electronegative atom.

4c737975-c8e8-46d1-a649-b9b3b978d02f.title: intermolecular force
4c737975-c8e8-46d1-a649-b9b3b978d02f.description: The attractions or repulsions between adjacent molecules.

4cf364e0-1c89-4714-8275-f6b90a6dee6c.title: chain isomer
4cf364e0-1c89-4714-8275-f6b90a6dee6c.description: Compounds with different arrangements of the substituents on the carbon chain and the same molecular formula.

636e8efb-1351-4cee-a4df-7c11285a23b8.title: crude oil
636e8efb-1351-4cee-a4df-7c11285a23b8.description: Oil as it is found naturally in underground reservoirs; a raw natural resource made from hydrocarbons that formed over millions of years from the remains of animals and plants.

cad12b33-5b02-4631-ad55-e12234c732cf.title: polymerisation
cad12b33-5b02-4631-ad55-e12234c732cf.description: A chemical process where small molecules join together to form a large molecule.

968b9ebb-b20b-4b2e-b4b3-7e08f6982685.title: aliphatic hydrocarbon
968b9ebb-b20b-4b2e-b4b3-7e08f6982685.description: An organic compound arranged in straight chains, branched chains or non-aromatic rings (not benzene rings).

70fa5bd1-4cd3-488a-80ed-7788557be58f.title: complete combustion
70fa5bd1-4cd3-488a-80ed-7788557be58f.description: A chemical reaction in which a fuel reacts with unlimited oxygen gas (O2) resulting in the production of carbon dioxide (CO2), water (H2O), and heat.

a6ba1468-9425-47eb-ac04-1fcba0ef6a98.title: enthalpy
a6ba1468-9425-47eb-ac04-1fcba0ef6a98.description: A measure of the total heat content of a substance or system at a constant pressure.

b801896e-1d9a-4848-b11b-b0035c7e2ab5.title: addition reaction
b801896e-1d9a-4848-b11b-b0035c7e2ab5.description: A chemical reaction in which atoms are added to a molecule usually by the breaking of double or triple bonds.

fdf1134b-47f6-4498-a320-123815b7c8ff.title: incomplete combustion
fdf1134b-47f6-4498-a320-123815b7c8ff.description: A chemical reaction in which a fuel reacts with limited oxygen gas (O2). Can lead to the formation of carbon, as soot (C), or carbon monoxide (CO).

9f1c2a23-8357-4f52-87bd-a544397b6997.title: substitution reaction
9f1c2a23-8357-4f52-87bd-a544397b6997.description: A chemical reaction where an atom or functional group in a molecule is replaced by a different atom or group.

e755d58b-770f-47b8-9446-56e3bc61059b.title: hydrocarbons
e755d58b-770f-47b8-9446-56e3bc61059b.description: A group of compounds containing only hydrogen and carbon, such as methane (CH4), ethene (C2H4) and but-1-yne (C4H6).

1dd5bb09-4192-4d50-ab63-bda5d67e3352.title: augmented reality (AR)
1dd5bb09-4192-4d50-ab63-bda5d67e3352.description: A technology that replicates, enhances or overlays extra information about the real-world environment, using computer-generated data such as global positioning systems (GPS), sound, videos and images. Common examples include a car windshield with a heads-up display (HUD) that projects three-dimensional navigation information and virtual lanes, or a swimming telecast using a line to indicate the position of the record holder in relation to the actual swimmers in the race.

50ae4737-ace3-459d-bb2b-e394e205e34d.title: virtual reality (VR)
50ae4737-ace3-459d-bb2b-e394e205e34d.description: The use of computing technology to create a simulated environment. Unlike traditional user interfaces, VR places the user inside an experience. Instead of viewing a screen in front of them, users are immersed and able to interact with three-dimensional worlds.

e5831772-0960-482f-bcba-551d0f40604a.title: sensor
e5831772-0960-482f-bcba-551d0f40604a.description: A device that detects and responds to some type of input from the physical environment.

7a7379fb-da3e-4c4e-ad4a-8bd67971e10e.title: general-purpose programming language
7a7379fb-da3e-4c4e-ad4a-8bd67971e10e.description: A coding or programming language used to write computer software. It uses letters, numbers and symbols arranged in a prescribed format (language) to instruct a computer how to carry out specific tasks. Also known as text-based programming.

33aa4884-dabd-459d-a973-49d2375ce113.title: desk check
33aa4884-dabd-459d-a973-49d2375ce113.description: A method used by a human to check the logic of a computer program's algorithm to reduce the likelihood of errors occurring. This may be done on paper, using a diagram, or mentally trying a sample of typical inputs to see what the outputs would be.

80d6ed34-3855-4330-9456-fe6969b6e75f.title: structured English/pseudocode
80d6ed34-3855-4330-9456-fe6969b6e75f.description: An informal high-level description of a computer program, process or algorithm. It is intended for humans to understand the flow of operations without necessarily needing to understand a programming language.

7806fe6d-2021-4889-b6ae-b1c3f78b9a04.title: network
7806fe6d-2021-4889-b6ae-b1c3f78b9a04.description:
A system of interconnected digital devices and/or people.

See social network

6dfd7355-66b9-4466-817b-43e9fcfd8c03.title: sociogram
6dfd7355-66b9-4466-817b-43e9fcfd8c03.description: A diagram that describes the social links or relationships that one person has with other people.

d410b253-99f5-439d-b4a9-a34b8ef97a14.title: html
d410b253-99f5-439d-b4a9-a34b8ef97a14.description: Hypertext mark-up language (html) is one of the first coding systems (or languages) designed to be used for web­page files so that an internet browser can efficiently display a page and elements for that page such as text, links and media in the intended position.

0d8e672c-04c6-4df6-8b77-1779333f7ba1.title: multisensory
0d8e672c-04c6-4df6-8b77-1779333f7ba1.description: The process of engaging at least 2 senses to communicate or experience the same thing simultaneously.

a15af24b-3c22-4403-8b73-6a554474e323.title: perspective
a15af24b-3c22-4403-8b73-6a554474e323.description: A way of regarding situations, facts and texts, and evaluating their relative significance.

64152cc6-7928-4fa8-9685-9d4a59779977.title: material
64152cc6-7928-4fa8-9685-9d4a59779977.description: Encompasses physical forms, such as paint, clay, a printed photograph or ready-made objects. Virtual forms include digital projections, virtual reality and interactive installations.

207f1119-a952-4c39-a7a4-21622e02c9ae.title: design form
207f1119-a952-4c39-a7a4-21622e02c9ae.description: A category of artistic representation in Visual and Motion Design distinguished by specific techniques and mediums.

0bb26b67-ec9d-45f7-8ee3-6cace99976f0.title: expressive
0bb26b67-ec9d-45f7-8ee3-6cace99976f0.description: The use of artistic methods and techniques to convey emotions, intentions and meanings in a personal, imaginative and intuitive manner.

20d90ac7-ddba-4c77-8090-16e331ce1f79.title: code(s)
20d90ac7-ddba-4c77-8090-16e331ce1f79.description: Agreed systems of making, communicating and interpreting meaning through signs and symbols.

6ad172b3-aeb0-4df1-be8f-610c868e93c3.title: design practice
6ad172b3-aeb0-4df1-be8f-610c868e93c3.description: The application of skills and knowledge to make, represent, respond to and interpret design artworks.

ae8dcfd6-dc27-4592-acca-438f09e42df4.title: text
ae8dcfd6-dc27-4592-acca-438f09e42df4.description: Any written, spoken/signed, nonverbal, visual, auditory or multimodal communication. Texts may be extended unified works, a series of related pieces or a single, simple piece of communication.

98dda34f-03c4-44da-9cbe-4a9037caaa65.title: haptic
98dda34f-03c4-44da-9cbe-4a9037caaa65.description: Refers to the sense of touch. Often used to describe a method of output from a device that can be measured by feel or touch.

4080dafc-b26c-4205-93ac-5653556c42cb.title: iconography
4080dafc-b26c-4205-93ac-5653556c42cb.description: A visual code used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples that connects art to ancestral Cultural Knowledge systems, Country and Cultural identity.

cb6bb2ab-9f28-49f1-ac9c-5c58a5598d63.title: identity
cb6bb2ab-9f28-49f1-ac9c-5c58a5598d63.description: A person’s conception and expression of individuality or group affiliation, self-concept and self-representation. It is closely connected to culture and language.

705bd9b1-408b-43d8-9e57-b3d13873c7b7.title: hybrid form
705bd9b1-408b-43d8-9e57-b3d13873c7b7.description: The combination of multiple art forms, genres or media to create innovative and interdisciplinary artworks.

d9999716-c1ff-406c-aab9-c4160614cb72.title: art movement
d9999716-c1ff-406c-aab9-c4160614cb72.description: A group of artists with a shared style or philosophy, typically emerged during a specific time period.

ebc6b933-85fd-491a-896b-2bf46cb21a48.title: art period
ebc6b933-85fd-491a-896b-2bf46cb21a48.description: A span of time characterised by distinctive styles, techniques and conventions in Visual Arts, often aligned with broader historical and cultural contexts.

20eabbce-9e0b-4115-a930-f9d4477703fd.title: artist
20eabbce-9e0b-4115-a930-f9d4477703fd.description: A person that makes artworks individually, as a group, at a school, as part of a movement or by enlisting others to produce their artwork.

25572292-3656-4cd5-afba-542337968529.title: representation
25572292-3656-4cd5-afba-542337968529.description: The way ideas are portrayed and represented in texts, using language devices, forms, features and structures of texts to create specific views about characters, events and ideas. Representation applies to all modes: spoken, written, visual and multimodal.

7808cbaa-e02a-403b-b36f-894440d5ea08.title: art form
7808cbaa-e02a-403b-b36f-894440d5ea08.description: A category of artistic representation in Visual Arts distinguished by specific techniques and mediums, encompassing 2D, 3D and 4D creations.

92adfea1-d724-4555-bdb3-bbcb5039a74d.title: signs
92adfea1-d724-4555-bdb3-bbcb5039a74d.description: A visual or multimodal element in an artwork that directly represents or points to a specific meaning or idea, often understood immediately and literally, or through cultural and contextual knowledge.

52447e56-edc3-43f5-920c-bd6f6629e786.title: decode
52447e56-edc3-43f5-920c-bd6f6629e786.description: A process of efficient word recognition in which readers use knowledge of the relationship between letters (graphemes) and sounds (phonemes) to work out how to say and read written words.

426986c8-29f6-43fe-9d3d-ca6b3ef42ffe.title: artworld
426986c8-29f6-43fe-9d3d-ca6b3ef42ffe.description: The community and system that encompasses artists, artworks, audiences, galleries, museums, collectors, and the practices and theories of producing, promoting and distributing art.

628c6178-306a-45af-8c80-93268162d4c3.title: conventions
628c6178-306a-45af-8c80-93268162d4c3.description: Accepted practices or features that help define textual forms, creative forms, styles and meaning.

065628a9-b0aa-4051-a191-6e373997d46e.title: symbolic
065628a9-b0aa-4051-a191-6e373997d46e.description: Pertaining to the use of symbols in artworks to represent ideas, beliefs or concepts. Communicates deeper meanings to audiences through material, physical and visual elements.

1ddfbba7-765c-4ca6-9e5d-a038ffa811fc.title: viewpoints
1ddfbba7-765c-4ca6-9e5d-a038ffa811fc.description: Represents the different perspectives, values and beliefs about visual arts. Viewpoints, including Structural, Subjective, Cultural and Contemporary, function as means for generating alternative interpretations of the artworld.

f638e8e3-0ff5-4cf5-81ce-0cf0f59a0a9d.title: artworld practitioner
f638e8e3-0ff5-4cf5-81ce-0cf0f59a0a9d.description: Individuals, such as artists, curators, critics and historians, who engage in the making, curation, critique and/or historical explanations of artworks.

9ae4eef8-ea55-4951-9b6d-0e00e504cada.title: Cultural Practices
9ae4eef8-ea55-4951-9b6d-0e00e504cada.description: Rules or behaviours and standards that guide Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ worldview. Cultural Practices guide spiritual beliefs, Customs, Lore, history and Tradition.

dc6021d6-6e28-4fec-b55e-346ba54650b7.title: Artworld concepts
dc6021d6-6e28-4fec-b55e-346ba54650b7.description: A framework for understanding the functions and roles in the artworld, through the interrelated concepts of artist, artwork, world and audience.

d58416bc-9277-4880-a990-e4d9bf27f7e7.title: curatorial
d58416bc-9277-4880-a990-e4d9bf27f7e7.description: A way to select, organise and present material and artworks for exhibition or informal sharing.

d807e62b-b016-4dfe-8eb1-e2de184e9212.title: practice
d807e62b-b016-4dfe-8eb1-e2de184e9212.description: The application of skills and knowledge to make, represent, respond to and interpret artworks.

59b3e9fa-ce36-46ca-b4e1-743331abdfc3.title: stylistic conventions
59b3e9fa-ce36-46ca-b4e1-743331abdfc3.description: Established rules, methods and techniques used in the artworld that create a recognisable style.

feb5d8b6-e7d7-4057-a771-927cc4d57178.title: virtual properties
feb5d8b6-e7d7-4057-a771-927cc4d57178.description: Characteristics of an artwork that exist in virtual or digital environments.

15cb2241-4e66-4dc1-9d83-27e61d44096a.title: body of work
15cb2241-4e66-4dc1-9d83-27e61d44096a.description: A collection of artworks produced by an artist over time, which reflects their evolving artistic practice.

e469899f-4108-4f52-a08c-034574629806.title: rectangle
e469899f-4108-4f52-a08c-034574629806.description: A four-sided shape (quadrilateral) with opposite sides of equal length and all 4 interior angles equal (right angles).

8da1caff-101f-47bf-a460-4bbf60a7b308.title: reflection
8da1caff-101f-47bf-a460-4bbf60a7b308.description: A transformation of a shape formed by creating a mirror image on the other side of a given line.

30aaee2b-25f3-4ad5-bc45-2661a5c73ef4.title: triangle
30aaee2b-25f3-4ad5-bc45-2661a5c73ef4.description: A closed shape with exactly 3 straight sides and 3 interior angles.

b381a7d0-1d8a-4e39-bf39-0ba251da9870.title: base
b381a7d0-1d8a-4e39-bf39-0ba251da9870.description: Has different meanings for different mathematical contexts. A base is a number that is raised to a power and the base of a solid is the face the object rests on.

e0d38231-babb-4ec4-99c1-7a359d4a7c11.title: point
e0d38231-babb-4ec4-99c1-7a359d4a7c11.description: Representation of a location in space that has zero dimensions. Lines, curves, shapes, surfaces and objects are constructed from sets of points. Points in the Cartesian plane are specified by coordinates.

24889ba6-2457-4c18-8403-ff755baeb8f7.title: line
24889ba6-2457-4c18-8403-ff755baeb8f7.description: A one-dimensional figure that is straight, has no thickness and extends endlessly.

a4866bb2-c957-4519-b764-1530baf93aa7.title: coordinates
a4866bb2-c957-4519-b764-1530baf93aa7.description: A set of values that define the position of a point or an object in a space. The coordinate system being used will govern the nature of the coordinates.

05838e7d-68d5-446a-baa8-d387d071441e.title: vertex
05838e7d-68d5-446a-baa8-d387d071441e.description:
Where 2 straight sides of a two-dimensional shape meet.

Extended in 7–12: A vertex is a point in the plane where lines meet and do not extend beyond, or a point in space where several edges meet. A vertex can also refer to a node in a network. It is also the turning point of a parabola.

6c201036-e45a-47db-b6c7-f515def1aa14.title: square
6c201036-e45a-47db-b6c7-f515def1aa14.description: A four-sided shape (quadrilateral and a parallelogram) with all sides of equal length and all 4 interior angles equal (right angles).

13b2cf01-d851-4659-9075-a99c62ead09c.title: side
13b2cf01-d851-4659-9075-a99c62ead09c.description: A side is the line segment joining 2 vertices of a two-dimensional shape.

1eede9dd-755e-48a8-8a9e-cb1de6c820b7.title: reflex angle
1eede9dd-755e-48a8-8a9e-cb1de6c820b7.description: An angle that measures between 180 and 360 degrees, i.e. between 2 and 4 right angles.

96d085a5-be32-473b-87b5-fb9d7460c203.title: place value system
96d085a5-be32-473b-87b5-fb9d7460c203.description:
The place value system has 4 properties: positional, base-ten, additive and multiplicative.

The value of a digit is determined by its position in a number relative to the ones (or units) place. For example, in the number 924, the 4 denotes 4 ones, the 2 denotes 2 tens or 20 ones, and the 9 denotes 9 hundreds, 90 tens or 900 ones.

6405a8a9-f55e-40e8-97d5-59fe5a27c589.title: perpendicular
6405a8a9-f55e-40e8-97d5-59fe5a27c589.description: Two lines, rays, line segments, vectors, planes or other objects that intersect at a 90° angle (a right angle).

92585db9-074e-48b1-8e40-d48f9391caae.title: adjacent angles
92585db9-074e-48b1-8e40-d48f9391caae.description:
Angles that share a vertex and an arm. They do not overlap.

Extended in 7–10: Two angles at a point are called adjacent if they share a common ray and a common vertex and lie on opposite sides of the common ray.

afdcc8eb-4c74-4ecc-9876-35f33c72cf7a.title: cubic
afdcc8eb-4c74-4ecc-9876-35f33c72cf7a.description: Having the form of a cube or being of the third power or degree.

fb4634c3-0b5f-4ab5-bf95-0749554f0fc7.title: cube
fb4634c3-0b5f-4ab5-bf95-0749554f0fc7.description: An object with 6 equal square faces and 12 edges.

b44852bd-f8dd-4968-9699-922be6cd85b3.title: constant difference
b44852bd-f8dd-4968-9699-922be6cd85b3.description: Constant difference refers to a common difference between pairs of numbers. For example, the difference between 3 and 7 is 4, and another pair of numbers that has a difference of 4 is 2 and 6.

93867960-e890-4424-92d1-df0f48b6219f.title: rounding
93867960-e890-4424-92d1-df0f48b6219f.description: The process for approximating a value that lies between 2 known values. It is used to specify a number correct to a given accuracy. For example, 4.027 becomes 4.03 when rounded to 2 decimal places.

663b4839-286b-455e-ac14-f5b4fb4c48fc.title: integer
663b4839-286b-455e-ac14-f5b4fb4c48fc.description:
A whole number, positive, negative or zero, e.g. −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 …

Extended in Advanced, Extension 1, Extension 2: The set of integers is usually denoted by ℤ.

1c706aa2-05c0-4e97-9f71-e40eb20eb079.title: container
1c706aa2-05c0-4e97-9f71-e40eb20eb079.description: Objects such as bottles, jars and tubs.

0a79f144-83ee-4df3-b7f4-6e3e0e511511.title: net
0a79f144-83ee-4df3-b7f4-6e3e0e511511.description:
A diagram showing the pattern of connected faces and the edges of an unfolded polyhedron (a solid with all faces polygons).

One possible net for a cube is shown below.

f7010110-5cc6-4dd0-b65d-6b5186d14226.title: polygon
f7010110-5cc6-4dd0-b65d-6b5186d14226.description: Plane shape bounded by 3 or more line segments.

1d2611d0-f9af-4203-baf0-68a900275bef.title: table
1d2611d0-f9af-4203-baf0-68a900275bef.description: An arrangement of information in rows and columns.

412eec7b-3de0-4197-9016-9f1a2f7578d5.title: number sentence
412eec7b-3de0-4197-9016-9f1a2f7578d5.description: A number sentence uses numerals and mathematical symbols. A number sentence may be used instead of the word equation. For example, instead of writing 6 apples plus 7 apples equals 13 apples, the number sentence would be 6 + 7 = 13.

686e9af7-a8b2-443a-95ff-29d5eed2a633.title: inverse operation
686e9af7-a8b2-443a-95ff-29d5eed2a633.description:
The operation that reverses the effect of another operation. 

Examples:

  • Addition and subtraction are inverse operations. When you add 3 to 7 you get 10. If you then subtract 3, you get back to 7.
  • Multiplication and division are inverse operations. When you multiply 6 by 2 you get 12. If you then divide by 2 you get back to 6.

2b2016c5-9781-4732-aa64-2e59076ddcdc.title: partition
2b2016c5-9781-4732-aa64-2e59076ddcdc.description:
Partitioning is dividing a quantity into parts.

In the early years, it commonly refers to treating whole numbers as made up of 2 parts (number bonds), e.g. 10 is 8 and 2.

In later years, it refers to dividing both continuous and discrete quantities into equal parts (equi-partitioning) when learning about fraction and division concepts.

66927ccc-6d71-4c67-8315-c76d94bc82ee.title: composite number
66927ccc-6d71-4c67-8315-c76d94bc82ee.description: A non-zero natural number that has a factor other than 1 and itself. For example, all even numbers besides 2 are composite numbers. Some odd numbers are composite (e.g. 21) but not all are composite (e.g. 11).

9c38ae91-4ed6-4f23-8c52-17b0404b075f.title: quotient
9c38ae91-4ed6-4f23-8c52-17b0404b075f.description: The result of dividing one number or algebraic expression by another.

ea04a825-f3d7-4d6c-8ba1-50d2130b3470.title: average
ea04a825-f3d7-4d6c-8ba1-50d2130b3470.description: A number expressing a central or typical value in a set of data. While it usually refers to the arithmetic mean, that is, the sum of a set of numbers divided by the number of numbers in the set, it may also refer to other measures of centre.

43d8487a-6b6b-478d-8f2f-5cf0fb7d9fe9.title: skewness
43d8487a-6b6b-478d-8f2f-5cf0fb7d9fe9.description: A measure of asymmetry (non-symmetry) in a distribution of values about the mean of a set of data.

74956753-9f6b-4c23-8e87-84324ed2b303.title: inference
74956753-9f6b-4c23-8e87-84324ed2b303.description: A conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning.

ff8dd933-e596-4dcf-b89f-f7c42e6c5aa4.title: simple interest
ff8dd933-e596-4dcf-b89f-f7c42e6c5aa4.description: The interest accumulated when the interest payment in each period is a fixed percentage of the principal (the initial lump sum of money).

737ca905-7594-4e9e-9d16-e8c69cb761bd.title: depreciation
737ca905-7594-4e9e-9d16-e8c69cb761bd.description: A decrease in value due to wear and tear, decay, decline in price etc.

df09cc6e-0f3d-490b-a96d-e2723be7bbc3.title: algebraic fraction
df09cc6e-0f3d-490b-a96d-e2723be7bbc3.description: A fraction in which the numerator and/or the denominator are algebraic expressions.

8d5ddf8e-cf10-4966-9d04-4f063adf328f.title: variable
8d5ddf8e-cf10-4966-9d04-4f063adf328f.description: A factor that can be changed, kept the same or measured in an investigation.

097d642d-58b0-4c64-bc14-b017344d8dec.title: expression
097d642d-58b0-4c64-bc14-b017344d8dec.description: The communication of ideas, images and emotions by the performer.

07b53b67-f97b-4283-8409-3129a6e92da3.title: factor
07b53b67-f97b-4283-8409-3129a6e92da3.description: A number that divides another number without a remainder. For example, 1, 2, 3 and 6 are factors of 6 but 4 and 5 are not.

fa72cdf8-31df-45fb-98a1-5c52fb97f96b.title: attribute
fa72cdf8-31df-45fb-98a1-5c52fb97f96b.description: A quality, feature or characteristic of an object or shape.

bb5dc906-d939-4eae-afef-c03c1857077b.title: interior angle
bb5dc906-d939-4eae-afef-c03c1857077b.description:
When referring to polygons, the inner angles formed by 2 adjacent sides.

When referring to a transversal cutting through a pair of straight lines, the 4 angles formed are called interior angles.

2953c81c-ecd6-441b-83bc-bb5d6538e54c.title: uniform
2953c81c-ecd6-441b-83bc-bb5d6538e54c.description: Means ‘the same as’. Used to refer to units of the same size used for measuring.

d87acba3-c583-47dc-b8bb-0d31c2007fe8.title: cross-section
d87acba3-c583-47dc-b8bb-0d31c2007fe8.description: The intersection of a solid with a plane. May differ for a given solid depending on the orientation of the slicing plane. For example, the cross-section of a sphere will be a circle (of different radius depending on the slicing plane), while the cross-section of a cube could be a square or other polygon (e.g. triangle, hexagon) depending on the orientation of the slicing plane.

adb1adfe-acbb-4b7e-ab11-530030165cb0.title: combinations
adb1adfe-acbb-4b7e-ab11-530030165cb0.description: The various ways a group of items can be arranged without regard to order.

51ff6d9b-7fee-4c93-bbed-fd809d22140d.title: corresponding angles
51ff6d9b-7fee-4c93-bbed-fd809d22140d.description:
Angles that lie in the same relative position at the points of intersection where a pair of lines is cut by a transversal.

If the lines are parallel, then each pair of corresponding angles is equal.

Conversely, if a pair of corresponding angles is equal, then the lines are parallel.

fbae9ef6-5ae3-45f0-b229-6a27797fae5d.title: index
fbae9ef6-5ae3-45f0-b229-6a27797fae5d.description: Also called ‘exponent’. The power to which a number or algebraic expression is to be raised. The index or exponent is written as a superscript. Positive integral exponents indicate the number of times a term is to be multiplied by itself.

5801758f-fab5-45de-99b3-e869f0bec99c.title: repeated addition
5801758f-fab5-45de-99b3-e869f0bec99c.description: An early strategy for solving multiplication problems used to add groups of the same quantity. For example, 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 to solve 4 groups of 3.

19432bfb-91cd-4a8a-b944-6461214f9463.title: sample space
19432bfb-91cd-4a8a-b944-6461214f9463.description: The set of all possible outcomes of a chance experiment. For example, the set of outcomes (also called sample points) from tossing 2 identical coins at the same time is {HH, HT, TT}, where H represents a ‘head’ and T a ‘tail’.

d29316a7-eda6-4f9f-b80a-4a84ebdc379d.title: simulation
d29316a7-eda6-4f9f-b80a-4a84ebdc379d.description: A recreation of random phenomena used to collect probability data through either physical or virtual manipulatives such as spinners, coins and cards or computer-generated simulations that can be performed a large number of times.

b56ac875-75a4-4cf2-81dc-2e65de4a3d4e.title: random number
b56ac875-75a4-4cf2-81dc-2e65de4a3d4e.description: A number whose value is governed by chance. For example, the number of dots showing when a fair die is tossed. The value of a random number cannot be predicted in advance.

512e8cfc-8baf-44f1-b45c-0313b6a42609.title: interval
512e8cfc-8baf-44f1-b45c-0313b6a42609.description: A continuous subset of the real number line. For example, ‘the set of all real numbers greater than or equal to 10’.

07cb1a4a-1752-4733-9e12-adfe115f4eea.title: hypotenuse
07cb1a4a-1752-4733-9e12-adfe115f4eea.description: The longest side in a right-angled triangle that is opposite the right angle.

5945ada3-b4f3-4f60-8445-1b034a5ccfb9.title: midpoint
5945ada3-b4f3-4f60-8445-1b034a5ccfb9.description: A point on a line segment or interval that divides the segment into 2 equal parts.

370d8bf4-3538-415b-ba50-2e595fd8d68f.title: radius
370d8bf4-3538-415b-ba50-2e595fd8d68f.description: The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on its perimeter. It is equal to half of the circle’s diameter.

0ab4388a-ef72-48d7-b1f7-b514a431e68c.title: diameter
0ab4388a-ef72-48d7-b1f7-b514a431e68c.description: A chord passing through the centre of a circle. The word is also used for the length of the diameter.

1ee42100-985c-497a-a5f2-91bd2f0896b0.title: arc
1ee42100-985c-497a-a5f2-91bd2f0896b0.description:
A part of a circle’s circumference.

Extended in Mathematics Extension 1: A part of a curve.

c0cd13c7-08fa-42df-b0af-4de15ec94032.title: chord
c0cd13c7-08fa-42df-b0af-4de15ec94032.description: A line segment (interval) joining 2 points on a circle.

e7b9ae3c-23bb-412a-b35c-2dafbd00f0b9.title: segment
e7b9ae3c-23bb-412a-b35c-2dafbd00f0b9.description: The act of separating a spoken word into its syllables and/or phonemes.

b0380cb8-0ae4-4cab-8dfa-dc78d105351c.title: tangent
b0380cb8-0ae4-4cab-8dfa-dc78d105351c.description: A line that intersects a circle at just one point. It touches the circle at that point of contact but does not pass inside it.

52bbb726-2a2d-497f-a8d2-1dd0246e85e2.title: highest common factor (HCF)
52bbb726-2a2d-497f-a8d2-1dd0246e85e2.description: The common divisor of a given set of natural numbers that is greater than each of the other common divisors. For example, 1, 2, 3 and 6 are common factors of 24, 54, and 66, and 6 is the highest common factor.

1c96eb2a-ec12-42e2-b5ee-98f1a55026db.title: terminating decimal
1c96eb2a-ec12-42e2-b5ee-98f1a55026db.description: A decimal expansion of a number that has a finite number of non-zero digits, e.g. 3.125. Every terminating decimal represents a rational number where the denominator is a power of 10.

d34830c4-be9c-485f-984e-4461723d9544.title: dependent events
d34830c4-be9c-485f-984e-4461723d9544.description: An event that relies on another event to happen first. One event influences the probability of another event.

6a90e8d1-faab-42d8-ba5b-d609e9971822.title: independent events
6a90e8d1-faab-42d8-ba5b-d609e9971822.description: Two events are independent if knowing the outcome of one event tells us nothing about the outcome of the other event.

cdf8f801-76b3-4fef-ab31-1dedca344996.title: curved surface
cdf8f801-76b3-4fef-ab31-1dedca344996.description: Surface of an object that is not flat, e.g. a cylinder has one curved surface.

28ea1558-6c72-4566-bb04-85d54fbc8ce7.title: ray
28ea1558-6c72-4566-bb04-85d54fbc8ce7.description: The part of a line that starts at a point and continues in a particular direction to infinity.

ee17a7d6-992c-49c7-a7d8-f121e5e5794c.title: transversal
ee17a7d6-992c-49c7-a7d8-f121e5e5794c.description: A line that intersects 2 other lines obliquely.

6269e894-92bd-4a67-9dec-959668a71b05.title: alternate angle
6269e894-92bd-4a67-9dec-959668a71b05.description: In each diagram below, the 2 marked angles are called alternate angles (since they are on alternate sides of the transversal).

7d4cda75-7538-421f-9f95-a0bbe06f3b88.title: co-interior angles
7d4cda75-7538-421f-9f95-a0bbe06f3b88.description:
A pair of angles that lie between a pair of parallel lines cut by a transversal and have a sum of 180 degrees or 2 right angles.

In each diagram the 2 marked angles are called co-interior angles.

If the 2 lines are parallel, then co-interior angles add to give 180° and so are supplementary.

Conversely, if a pair of angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel.

f1ff220a-2d04-4e8a-9620-983f99e641e0.title: supplementary angles
f1ff220a-2d04-4e8a-9620-983f99e641e0.description: Two adjacent angles that form a straight angle and whose sum is 180 degrees (a straight angle). For example, 45° and 135° are supplementary angles.

9b65cbce-9baa-4a71-ad39-06d2abc5f4a8.title: vertically opposite angles
9b65cbce-9baa-4a71-ad39-06d2abc5f4a8.description: Two pairs of vertically opposite angles formed at the point of intersection of 2 lines in a plane. Vertically opposite angles are equal.

ec3f1def-0447-4dbc-9db9-84ec5014bd3a.title: direct variation
ec3f1def-0447-4dbc-9db9-84ec5014bd3a.description: A proportional relationship where one quantity directly varies with respect to a change in another quantity. This implies that if there is an increase (or decrease) in one quantity then the other quantity will experience a proportionate increase (or decrease).

9c2d8862-8f9b-49f5-9008-a2206ad07fc8.title: curve
9c2d8862-8f9b-49f5-9008-a2206ad07fc8.description: A one-dimensional figure that is not straight.

8d637b9b-5649-4fd7-bd2f-1881bea4c52a.title: congruent
8d637b9b-5649-4fd7-bd2f-1881bea4c52a.description: An exact match between every part of one figure with the corresponding part of another figure, i.e. congruent figures can be exactly superimposed on each other.

e00673c6-ef2e-4377-8d34-de205510d5b8.title: similarity
e00673c6-ef2e-4377-8d34-de205510d5b8.description: When the enlargement of one figure is congruent to another figure. Similar figures have corresponding lengths in the same proportion, are the same shape and have equal corresponding angles.

ed6d75f3-35d7-4f48-8da8-fd41e83ee8bd.title: non-linear
ed6d75f3-35d7-4f48-8da8-fd41e83ee8bd.description: Functions or graphs that cannot be represented by a straight line or a linear function.

8995d731-49b8-4359-81cb-ee7b8ebfde02.title: logarithmic scale
8995d731-49b8-4359-81cb-ee7b8ebfde02.description: A scale where successive endpoint values of intervals increase by a constant factor (multiplicatively). Contrast with linear scales in which the increase is a constant amount.

bcc65170-71a1-4802-8da6-740ac33f78a3.title: mutually exclusive events
bcc65170-71a1-4802-8da6-740ac33f78a3.description:
Two events that cannot have simultaneous outcomes in the same chance experiment. For example, when a fair coin is tossed twice, the events 'HH' and 'TT' cannot occur at the same time and are, therefore, mutually exclusive.

In a Venn diagram, as shown below, mutually exclusive events do not overlap.

eb0c0134-c679-42a6-9a83-7591a4edb6f8.title: monic
eb0c0134-c679-42a6-9a83-7591a4edb6f8.description: A polynomial in which the coefficient of the leading term is 1.

00a93433-fb5d-4fcf-905a-6e31d7603163.title: range (function)
00a93433-fb5d-4fcf-905a-6e31d7603163.description: The set of values of the dependent variable for which a function is defined.

02d1493e-e0f4-45d2-910b-18fb75534e9e.title: vertical line test
02d1493e-e0f4-45d2-910b-18fb75534e9e.description: Determines whether a relation or graph is also a function. If a vertical line intersects or touches a graph at more than one point, then the graph is not a function.

ed86dff6-f1d7-483c-8445-fbb1f79af599.title: planar graph
ed86dff6-f1d7-483c-8445-fbb1f79af599.description: A connected graph that is drawn within a plane whose edges do not cross.

ad7703ef-4c13-4a49-98ae-b9d63188fcc6.title: face
ad7703ef-4c13-4a49-98ae-b9d63188fcc6.description: A flat surface of a 3-dimensional geometric object (polyhedron) with only straight edges.

cd9516a7-ea95-43f3-b1f5-53a6784834de.title: edge
cd9516a7-ea95-43f3-b1f5-53a6784834de.description: The line segment formed by the intersection of two faces of a polyhedron, e.g. a cube has 6 faces and 12 edges.

3ab92a3f-9d81-43c6-96a0-9717b366e1bd.title: connected
3ab92a3f-9d81-43c6-96a0-9717b366e1bd.description:
In the Cartesian plane, 2 points are connected if there is a line or curve that joins them. In a network, a set of points is connected if every point can be reached from another point. A set of points that is not connected is called disconnected.

Examples of a connected network and a disconnected network respectively are shown below:

1547a1e5-5611-4b49-992d-304b01bfafa8.title: walk (networks)
1547a1e5-5611-4b49-992d-304b01bfafa8.description: A sequence of edges and vertices in a network.

98f29577-aee2-4016-bf67-466cb01bf475.title: trail (networks)
98f29577-aee2-4016-bf67-466cb01bf475.description: A walk where no edges are repeated.

7d729316-775d-4e66-bbcc-097a1504c1d2.title: circuit (networks)
7d729316-775d-4e66-bbcc-097a1504c1d2.description: A trail that begins and ends on the same vertex. Vertices can be repeated.

c90737db-20e1-4038-b032-6ed895468a40.title: cycle (networks)
c90737db-20e1-4038-b032-6ed895468a40.description: A closed path that starts and finishes on the same vertex. No vertex is repeated.

aa7ea236-b6cd-4584-aa4e-b1875264f704.title: polynomial
aa7ea236-b6cd-4584-aa4e-b1875264f704.description: An expression made up of non-negative integer powers of the same variable and coefficients combined using addition, subtraction and multiplication.

4f9acd0e-218a-44c8-b7ea-a759f03268ef.title: secant
4f9acd0e-218a-44c8-b7ea-a759f03268ef.description: The straight line passing through 2 points on the graph of a function.

a4e63fde-497d-46c8-bdb5-90e934662551.title: adjacent
a4e63fde-497d-46c8-bdb5-90e934662551.description: Has different meanings for different mathematical contexts. For example, adjacent vertices in a network are joined by an edge and adjacent faces in a solid have a common edge. In trigonometry, the adjacent side of a right-angled triangle is the side next to the angle to which the trigonometric ratio is referring.

5a27e1e9-455e-4361-afdd-a7890ebdae58.title: unit circle
5a27e1e9-455e-4361-afdd-a7890ebdae58.description: A circle with a radius of 1 unit.

3867b2ec-d562-4f61-b5d8-095b8ea6e217.title: bearing
3867b2ec-d562-4f61-b5d8-095b8ea6e217.description:
A direction from one point on the Earth’s surface to another. Two types of bearings may be used: compass bearing and true bearing.

See compass bearing and true bearing

37f4ca26-d301-46a7-b66d-12a972eafc35.title: list
37f4ca26-d301-46a7-b66d-12a972eafc35.description: A number of items, typically presented one after the other.

7c779cd5-320b-44e5-9ab7-dcc346de7468.title: face
7c779cd5-320b-44e5-9ab7-dcc346de7468.description: A flat surface of a 3-dimensional geometric object (polyhedron) with only straight edges.

ce0a2272-9e8c-41a4-bdcf-d944888a36c6.title: surface
ce0a2272-9e8c-41a4-bdcf-d944888a36c6.description:
The flat or curved area of an object. A surface with straight edges is called a face, a surface with a curved boundary is called a curved surface.

See face

e87dae09-2e1a-44d9-b11f-e3ca471c990d.title: equals sign
e87dae09-2e1a-44d9-b11f-e3ca471c990d.description:
In mathematics, the equals sign is used to indicate equivalence, e.g. 5 + 1 = 2 + 4 and to show that two or more amounts have the same value.

See equivalent

cbfa9ad5-4af6-4bbb-bae4-f0b46ef5174c.title: quantity value
cbfa9ad5-4af6-4bbb-bae4-f0b46ef5174c.description: The amount a digit represents in a number. For example, the quantity value of the five in 546 is 500, and the quantity value of the four is 40.

a56fc966-841f-4c76-9d35-ad03c2cfdc19.title: closed shape
a56fc966-841f-4c76-9d35-ad03c2cfdc19.description: A shape enclosed by all its sides with no gaps.

f4392fba-f121-4c3d-a688-071db2fec07d.title: hefting
f4392fba-f121-4c3d-a688-071db2fec07d.description: Testing the weight of an object by lifting and/or balancing it.

3f72feb4-a6b1-4b88-9bea-bf0c8f1d6f1b.title: weight
3f72feb4-a6b1-4b88-9bea-bf0c8f1d6f1b.description: The measure of the force of gravity acting on a body with a given mass. An object can be weightless without its mass being zero. The term ‘weight’ is used as a synonym for mass when the concept of gravitational force has not been introduced.

5dd6c5d7-ec62-4236-a480-49cb3f6611a0.title: internal volume (capacity)
5dd6c5d7-ec62-4236-a480-49cb3f6611a0.description: A measure of how much a container can hold.

6df14388-d749-433e-9c73-51e0b98a3223.title: equal-arm balance
6df14388-d749-433e-9c73-51e0b98a3223.description: A balance where the distance from the support point (middle) to the arms at each end is equal.

988780cd-6774-4791-b965-b967b80e8555.title: one-to-one data display
988780cd-6774-4791-b965-b967b80e8555.description: Display of data using objects and pictures where one object or picture represents one data value.

da323f9f-2c5a-4582-98d4-17bfae1f28f7.title: number bonds
da323f9f-2c5a-4582-98d4-17bfae1f28f7.description: Combinations (pairs) of numbers that add to a given number, e.g. 8 + 2, 6 + 4, and 7 + 3 all bond to form 10.

e9ebf96b-d15b-45d8-beee-27f1e5972107.title: picture graph
e9ebf96b-d15b-45d8-beee-27f1e5972107.description: Display of data using images, symbols or pictures to represent data in categories.

41bcb38a-aa8e-42ff-a4ef-1df6954d6261.title: superimposed
41bcb38a-aa8e-42ff-a4ef-1df6954d6261.description: To place or lay on top of.

ad6d1998-28cd-41be-8b74-97857ac7e4bb.title: linear pattern
ad6d1998-28cd-41be-8b74-97857ac7e4bb.description: A pattern created by the regular repetition of units with the same difference between terms.

b6518c91-fdfc-4cfc-9888-3991117b58f6.title: number chart
b6518c91-fdfc-4cfc-9888-3991117b58f6.description:
A table that lists numbers in numerical order. There are different types of number charts.

For example:

  • a 1–120 or 0–99 chart
  • a calendar display for a month.

ab42145a-1385-4256-8379-7d4c7e47cd7a.title: rhythmic counting
ab42145a-1385-4256-8379-7d4c7e47cd7a.description: Rhythmic counting refers to the repeated sound pattern that students may use to vocalise the count – creating a beat to emphasise the pattern.

5ef2ae5e-fe10-4a28-9264-105ba12687ec.title: skip counting
5ef2ae5e-fe10-4a28-9264-105ba12687ec.description: Skip counting is counting forwards or backwards in groups or multiples of a particular number, e.g. 5, 10, 15, 20 ...

4142e48d-1309-4824-928c-865bfaedf45b.title: grouping division
4142e48d-1309-4824-928c-865bfaedf45b.description:
Grouping (quotitive) division requires finding how many groups are formed, e.g. if I have 12 marbles and each child gets 4, how many children will get marbles?

When grouping, the quotient represents the number of groups within the shared quantity.

9f912798-8d5d-4efe-8356-9cd3b23c468a.title: sharing division
9f912798-8d5d-4efe-8356-9cd3b23c468a.description:
Sharing (partitive) division requires finding how many are in each group, eg if 12 marbles are shared between 3 students, how many does each student get?

When sharing, the quotient represents the quantity of shared objects in each group.

b89ee774-98ed-44a6-915f-ba25fabee580.title: doubling and halving
b89ee774-98ed-44a6-915f-ba25fabee580.description:
Doubling and halving is a strategy that can make solving multiplication problems easier, e.g. solving 4 x 12 is the same as solving 2 x 24.

Doubling and halving is also a strategy used to find factors of a number. For example, to find the factors of 24, start with 1 x 24 then double and halve, 2 x 12, 4 x 6, 8 x 3.

71b48f47-5d52-4d75-9cb3-20ba6ce9b74c.title: dramatic action
71b48f47-5d52-4d75-9cb3-20ba6ce9b74c.description: The combined moments and experiences that create meaning, tension and audience engagement.

e17dd866-1f2b-429e-8a7d-7d2d90a643bb.title: movement
e17dd866-1f2b-429e-8a7d-7d2d90a643bb.description: The processes or results of moving performers, objects, set, lighting and/or audiences in dramatic works and experiences.

fc8445aa-05e4-4487-b6b8-930dfdb2aeaf.title: interpret
fc8445aa-05e4-4487-b6b8-930dfdb2aeaf.description: The act of translation from one language to another, the process of understanding and explaining.

194f5f05-1996-4400-99bf-9b981ecaef7b.title: artistic
194f5f05-1996-4400-99bf-9b981ecaef7b.description: Relating to the construction, deconstruction and/or expression of creative works.

d6d1aeb6-0031-44d5-affb-07671c16c6b1.title: elements of drama
d6d1aeb6-0031-44d5-affb-07671c16c6b1.description: Role, character, focus, tension, situation, space, time, structure, language, moment, atmosphere, belief and symbol.

b07491de-a969-4933-8138-8f6870d52766.title: devise
b07491de-a969-4933-8138-8f6870d52766.description: Create through researching, experimenting, structuring and refining.

8c4053f5-59b0-41fa-9034-0eddf50ab11a.title: scripted
8c4053f5-59b0-41fa-9034-0eddf50ab11a.description: Drama developed or interpreted from a working text.

9119f7fa-6dc2-4a2e-a981-d9a85ff9a94a.title: dramatic meaning
9119f7fa-6dc2-4a2e-a981-d9a85ff9a94a.description: Ideas, feelings, images and stories communicated with an audience.

95fe9407-1a86-48cc-9fd3-12a3138aa5d9.title: moment
95fe9407-1a86-48cc-9fd3-12a3138aa5d9.description: A point in time within a dramatic work or experience that creates meaning, engagement and impact in itself and in relation to the dramatic journey.

eaa3bc4e-3743-446f-a266-5e24b402447c.title: transition
eaa3bc4e-3743-446f-a266-5e24b402447c.description: A change from one scene, moment or idea to another.

fcf8b95d-ceba-4041-b7d2-76e42d7ec0e2.title: rehearse
fcf8b95d-ceba-4041-b7d2-76e42d7ec0e2.description: To train, practise or refine a work before sharing it with an audience.

cf0ba38b-8139-48c1-988a-14ca891089df.title: elements of performance
cf0ba38b-8139-48c1-988a-14ca891089df.description:
Voice and movement refined through the elements of dynamics, clarity, energy and expression. 

See voice and movement

13eebf02-53de-4237-bad4-7bd0293db4de.title: dramatic works
13eebf02-53de-4237-bad4-7bd0293db4de.description: Dramatic performances and experiences, or materials such as scripts and designs.

71ba263f-7a95-48d3-b41b-2f8261118aca.title: dramatic practices
71ba263f-7a95-48d3-b41b-2f8261118aca.description: The ways in which dramatic practitioners engage in making, performing and appreciating.

e4aa78f4-0fc0-4a4e-82e7-04477df6ff3a.title: dramatic practitioner
e4aa78f4-0fc0-4a4e-82e7-04477df6ff3a.description: Someone engaged in the practices of drama, such as an actor, playwright, director, designer, stage manager, deviser or drama student.

594cb24e-ae51-405a-9629-c4964df31596.title: dramatic forms
594cb24e-ae51-405a-9629-c4964df31596.description: Recognisable types of drama developed, performed or staged for specific mediums, such as theatre, audio, video or multidisciplinary drama.

8ecdf26e-fce4-4f34-aa51-047366ebf003.title: consent
8ecdf26e-fce4-4f34-aa51-047366ebf003.description:
Informed and freely given agreement to engage in an activity, or for a specific thing to happen. Consent is denied when someone does not have the capacity to give consent.

According to the Commonwealth Consent policy Framework, sexual consent is a free, voluntary and informed agreement between people to participate in a sexual act. This agreement is only present when these people mutually and genuinely want to engage in that sexual act and actively make sure their partner does too.

In NSW, consent is a fundamental part of sexual offence law.

e0a03c16-9e11-450c-9d30-5e7221198a50.title: improvisation
e0a03c16-9e11-450c-9d30-5e7221198a50.description: Spontaneous performance used as a key method of making drama, or as a rehearsal or live performance technique to communicate ideas and construct drama.

25084400-421d-4a55-af75-12ab0838b94f.title: offers
25084400-421d-4a55-af75-12ab0838b94f.description: Ideas or dramatic action that dramatic practitioners and/or audiences initiate and/or respond to.

a4d78d4d-6369-4ab7-96a0-fe2a36881b6b.title: stage
a4d78d4d-6369-4ab7-96a0-fe2a36881b6b.description: To produce or perform a dramatic work for an audience.

539a9f67-b1ff-41d2-ae7c-6489a0c12dd3.title: explain
539a9f67-b1ff-41d2-ae7c-6489a0c12dd3.description: Relate cause and effect; make the relationships between things evident; or provide why and/or how.

8b10d803-40ac-4361-8c34-dec71966d162.title: ensemble
8b10d803-40ac-4361-8c34-dec71966d162.description: A group of people who perform together to produce a unified creative work.

032b8a72-2b62-4495-ad96-e44f2a759505.title: argument
032b8a72-2b62-4495-ad96-e44f2a759505.description:
A stated position about an idea.

The way in which various dimensions of a text (such as theme, perspective and style) can be understood to represent a particular position on an issue.

70199610-035e-424c-b6cc-ec4349ef2558.title: authority
70199610-035e-424c-b6cc-ec4349ef2558.description:
Authority of a text – How trustworthy, authentic or valid an audience may find the representation of ideas, experiences, perspectives and arguments in a text.

Authority over a text – The varying degrees to which the meaning of a text is controlled or constructed by its creator(s) and by its audience.

f4fbec94-64dc-4e5e-a310-96862a81646d.title: compare
f4fbec94-64dc-4e5e-a310-96862a81646d.description: Show how things are similar or different.

608a41ea-9ead-446a-a92a-523e94c35ba6.title: analyse
608a41ea-9ead-446a-a92a-523e94c35ba6.description: Identify components and the relationship between them; draw out and relate implications.

c9ae0477-560a-49c4-9f28-ef2c2ad54ad6.title: character
c9ae0477-560a-49c4-9f28-ef2c2ad54ad6.description:
A dramatic role built with complexity, personality and/or background.

See role

1cf6389e-8396-4939-8dd7-02035cc5ee9c.title: literature
1cf6389e-8396-4939-8dd7-02035cc5ee9c.description: An evolving category of text that is broadly seen by its audience to hold enduring personal, social, cultural or aesthetic value. Literature comprises a dynamic range of fiction and nonfiction texts from diverse historical and cultural contexts.

e9aafa82-0259-42f8-9876-88db02821ca7.title: code and convention
e9aafa82-0259-42f8-9876-88db02821ca7.description: Agreed systems of making, communicating and interpreting meaning.

718564f3-942f-4ce7-aec1-8eb0b2f2b955.title: figurative language
718564f3-942f-4ce7-aec1-8eb0b2f2b955.description: Word groups/phrases used differently from the expected or everyday usage to express an idea in a non-literal way for a particular effect.

b2763805-75d9-42dd-9a43-ac8522fc1305.title: symbol
b2763805-75d9-42dd-9a43-ac8522fc1305.description: A letter, figure or other character or mark, or a combination of letters, used to represent something.

bf5aa2a6-b785-4a1d-93d9-20b9d3eed6f0.title: imagery
bf5aa2a6-b785-4a1d-93d9-20b9d3eed6f0.description: Use of figurative language to represent objects, characters, actions or ideas in such a way that they appeal to the senses of the reader or viewer.

c7ac42b3-6d13-42c3-a7fa-63ba03e1f84a.title: subvert
c7ac42b3-6d13-42c3-a7fa-63ba03e1f84a.description: To compose or respond to a text in ways that are different from the widely accepted reading or different from the conventional genre. For example, Roald Dahl's Revolting Rhymes provides a subverted reading of Cinderella. The purpose of producing a subverted reading of a text might be to entertain or to raise questions about the meaning or inherent values in the original text.

74770002-e6eb-4be0-ad17-265ff29a191b.title: purpose
74770002-e6eb-4be0-ad17-265ff29a191b.description: To entertain, to inform or to persuade different audiences in different contexts. Composers use a number of ways to achieve these purposes: persuading through emotive language, analysis or factual recount; entertaining through description, imaginative writing or humour, and so on.

1511aa39-425a-4145-81e9-14517e309c23.title: Aboriginal Songline(s)
1511aa39-425a-4145-81e9-14517e309c23.description: Texts that describe landscapes and directions of the tracks forged in lands, waters and skies by Creator Spirits during the Dreaming.

d0016a0d-d05d-4a44-bc87-f6e299ce3930.title: Tier 2 words
d0016a0d-d05d-4a44-bc87-f6e299ce3930.description:
General academic words that can be used across a variety of domains. They are of high utility for mature language users and are commonly used in written language.

Tier 2 words add power and precision to written and spoken language, but many Tier 2 words are most commonly found in written language, e.g. contradict, precede, stale, awful, snuggle.

859e31ab-30e0-4424-aced-0c99640076d1.title: Tier 3 words
859e31ab-30e0-4424-aced-0c99640076d1.description: Words that are used rarely (low frequency) and only in highly specific situations, e.g. decibel, cataclysm, atom.

7a0809a1-ce82-4df5-8a21-f1b2c2647fd3.title: synonym
7a0809a1-ce82-4df5-8a21-f1b2c2647fd3.description: A word or phrase that has the same or a similar meaning to another word or phrase. For example, sick and ill.

ead95893-53f4-4375-855e-1eda8632e6a8.title: reading
ead95893-53f4-4375-855e-1eda8632e6a8.description: To process written words, to derive and/or construct meaning. It is the product of word reading and language comprehension.

edb1e37d-57de-4637-8da3-458d747e6879.title: metalanguage
edb1e37d-57de-4637-8da3-458d747e6879.description: Technical terms used to describe and discuss how language and texts function.

b877307c-2f06-4a13-afcb-a37740310990.title: discuss
b877307c-2f06-4a13-afcb-a37740310990.description: Identify issues and provide points for and/or against.

f872ed9a-7463-4657-a17f-b4f5cbed8a58.title: idiom
f872ed9a-7463-4657-a17f-b4f5cbed8a58.description: A commonly used phrase or expression, usually figurative or non-literal, that has an understood meaning specific to a language or dialect, e.g. over the moon, half asleep, pull your socks up.

b76bd67f-8bb1-4772-9158-69b0e47bd1cc.title: metaphor
b76bd67f-8bb1-4772-9158-69b0e47bd1cc.description:
Linguistic – a figure of speech used for effect that implies one thing by referring to another.

Literary – an object, entity or situation that can be regarded as representing something else.

73e967ac-6d3e-480e-a87a-deecf374cd38.title: Aboriginal English
73e967ac-6d3e-480e-a87a-deecf374cd38.description: A recognised dialect of English which is the first, or home language, of many Aboriginal people. It differs from other dialects of English, such as Standard Australian English, in systematic ways including sounds, grammar, words and their meanings, and language use. Aboriginal English is a powerful vehicle for the expression of Aboriginal identity. Aboriginal English is not a target language study option for NSW Aboriginal Languages syllabuses.

97456c0d-75ff-43b2-b0b4-1c802d4f2dfb.title: spoken text
97456c0d-75ff-43b2-b0b4-1c802d4f2dfb.description: Communication produced using spoken words and delivered either face-to-face or digitally.

1cd4d8d1-5118-4ebf-b2f9-2d1b71759ac9.title: etymology
1cd4d8d1-5118-4ebf-b2f9-2d1b71759ac9.description:
The origins of, and changes to, words in relation to meaning.

Words derived from earlier or other languages, place names, words derived from people's names, coinages.

8ffee150-b623-497b-8177-d26a128a676b.title: suffix
8ffee150-b623-497b-8177-d26a128a676b.description:
A bound morpheme comprising a letter or group of letters that attach to a base word to make a new word.

For example:

  • The -s in dogs is an inflected suffix that marks plurality.
  • The derivational suffix, -ion can be added to the end of the verb, protect, to form the noun, protection.

See derivational word form and inflected word forms

18bf4315-f8ec-4914-9bb8-4c2e1dc8ddc4.title: root
18bf4315-f8ec-4914-9bb8-4c2e1dc8ddc4.description: A morpheme that gives the word its core meaning. A root may or may not stand alone as a word. Many roots in Standard Australian English derive from Latin and Greek.

3cdeabef-3821-44a8-b283-caeccbe0021c.title: assimilated prefix
3cdeabef-3821-44a8-b283-caeccbe0021c.description: A bound morpheme that is added before a base word and where its last letter changes to match the first letter of the base word. For example, in + mature = immature.

fb9ab1c6-1b94-48b0-a759-aa51bc04677a.title: homophone
fb9ab1c6-1b94-48b0-a759-aa51bc04677a.description: A word having the same sound as another but different spelling and meaning.

ac44ab35-54fe-46ed-a59f-457f85f6c0c9.title: grapheme
ac44ab35-54fe-46ed-a59f-457f85f6c0c9.description:
The smallest unit of writing used to represent one phoneme. A letter or combination of letters corresponding to or representing a single phoneme.

Examples include:

  • the f in frog
  • the ph in phone
  • the gh in cough

be59d02d-0946-4451-8820-b4ce7cf2e27c.title: base word
be59d02d-0946-4451-8820-b4ce7cf2e27c.description:
A morpheme (meaningful unit) that stands freely on its own to make a word.

See morpheme

2c911cca-6f14-4fbc-bd88-6995006cf3cb.title: reference
2c911cca-6f14-4fbc-bd88-6995006cf3cb.description:
The use of a source of information in order to ascertain something.

The act of mentioning someone or something in speech or writing.

25e835dd-ced1-46e9-8d43-baf7044d8ea1.title: segment
25e835dd-ced1-46e9-8d43-baf7044d8ea1.description: The act of separating a spoken word into its syllables and/or phonemes.

732aa134-ba06-4b7e-8377-616dc55bb59b.title: syllable
732aa134-ba06-4b7e-8377-616dc55bb59b.description: A unit of sound within a word that contains a vowel phoneme and feels like one ‘beat’. For example, a word with 3 syllables is: won-der-ful.

2db143a2-8235-498e-9619-1b9690fa61b3.title: phoneme
2db143a2-8235-498e-9619-1b9690fa61b3.description:
The smallest unit of speech sound.

Examples include:

  • Cat has 3 phonemes: c/a/t
  • Truck has 4 phonemes: t/r/u/ck.

a4f84f7a-9895-4b57-842e-803b932ad60e.title: mental model
a4f84f7a-9895-4b57-842e-803b932ad60e.description: A mental representation of the information in a real or an imaginary world. A student develops a mental model as the text progresses. It may include information derived from inferences and from background knowledge as well as from what is explicitly stated in the text itself.

5e31e3f0-3a9f-4f72-97a9-6c8875fa7396.title: modality
5e31e3f0-3a9f-4f72-97a9-6c8875fa7396.description: Referring to visual–gestural languages as opposed to auditory–verbal languages.

433ad83d-1072-4095-a6a1-91617b464cee.title: cohesive devices
433ad83d-1072-4095-a6a1-91617b464cee.description: Words or phrases that indicate a relationship with other words, phrases, clauses or paragraphs across a text.

43be6078-52f7-4b40-abe2-e65d14e4f014.title: anaphor(a)
43be6078-52f7-4b40-abe2-e65d14e4f014.description:
Grammar – a word or phrase that references an earlier word or phrase.

Rhetoric – the intentional repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of several clauses, sentences, stanzas or paragraphs.

5bb8a029-d380-4118-aab8-2e9dd1d06427.title: pronoun
5bb8a029-d380-4118-aab8-2e9dd1d06427.description: A word that is used in place of a noun. A pronoun may be personal (he, she, we, they), demonstrative (that, this) or relative (who).

60897755-b89e-43ca-a663-1fb7273c7a22.title: verb group
60897755-b89e-43ca-a663-1fb7273c7a22.description:
A group of words built around a verb.

Verb groups:

  • may include auxiliary verbs (‘helping’ verbs used to indicate tense or modality), e.g. I am going soon. I must leave before dark.
  • are sometimes referred to as a complex verb or compound verb.

422818be-a8b6-481b-8827-b4bbee69daf7.title: causal connective
422818be-a8b6-481b-8827-b4bbee69daf7.description: A word or groups of words used as a cohesive device between sentences, when explaining how something works or why something happens.

82efcedc-2eb1-4a48-9ee7-468035680162.title: sentence
82efcedc-2eb1-4a48-9ee7-468035680162.description:
A collection of words that conveys a complete thought, typically containing a subject and predicate. A sentence:

  • may express a statement, exclamation, command or question
  • comprises a main clause and sometimes one or more subordinate clauses
  • begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, exclamation mark or question mark.

See clause (main), simple sentence, compound sentence and complex sentence

757f4932-23d6-4a7a-8e09-5f2aebe3b013.title: phrase
757f4932-23d6-4a7a-8e09-5f2aebe3b013.description: A group of related words that form part of a sentence and do not include both a verb and its subject.

58037e77-87b7-4b66-a4ca-65f7a241bfbd.title: inferencing
58037e77-87b7-4b66-a4ca-65f7a241bfbd.description:
Local inferencing requires the reader to comprehend implied information from within relatively small sections of text, such as 2 adjacent sentences.

Global inferencing requires the reader to comprehend implied information from across relatively larger sections of text and is supported by the reader’s depth of vocabulary and background knowledge.

851aeda4-551e-429d-9f10-4b0a69a35f75.title: subjective language
851aeda4-551e-429d-9f10-4b0a69a35f75.description: Words used to communicate based on opinion, feelings or personal biases.

2cbbcd77-6ade-4b03-948c-18c40e2be4c9.title: objective language
2cbbcd77-6ade-4b03-948c-18c40e2be4c9.description: Language that is fact-based, measurable and observable, verifiable and unbiased. It does not include a speaker or writer’s point of view, interpretation or judgement.

a1d78929-5a07-44cf-bd7d-faac636509d3.title: tense
a1d78929-5a07-44cf-bd7d-faac636509d3.description:
The form of the verb that indicates when something is happening in relation to the speaker’s time: past, present or future.

For example:

  • I ate bananas (past).
  • I am eating bananas (present).
  • I will eat bananas (future).

086314dc-a217-4e14-bd96-0a37969a77c8.title: question
086314dc-a217-4e14-bd96-0a37969a77c8.description: A sentence that seeks information by asking or requesting to elicit a response.

f9b4a543-b976-47f9-9f68-66b3ad69ca47.title: gist statements
f9b4a543-b976-47f9-9f68-66b3ad69ca47.description: Succinct thoughts and information that capture the generalisations gleaned from what has been read, heard or viewed.

550a624c-c9a3-43fd-bd7f-1acef3e644c4.title: contrast
550a624c-c9a3-43fd-bd7f-1acef3e644c4.description: Show how things are different or opposite.

11082eb1-804d-4114-8603-6c9c886feb05.title: fluency
11082eb1-804d-4114-8603-6c9c886feb05.description: Reading, speaking, encoding and spelling with appropriate pace and accuracy.

68346357-f869-48ed-bcfe-d873a5eeaee2.title: blend
68346357-f869-48ed-bcfe-d873a5eeaee2.description: The act of synthesising phonemes smoothly from left to right, to read words.

d3a2ddf8-4a24-4686-aba2-1db254e32b6e.title: digital text
d3a2ddf8-4a24-4686-aba2-1db254e32b6e.description: An audio, visual or multimodal text produced by electronic technology. A digital text may be interactive and include still and/or dynamic images, animations and/or hyperlinks.

27b958d7-8ef5-4f44-b688-284dab706b21.title: background knowledge
27b958d7-8ef5-4f44-b688-284dab706b21.description: Information that is important for understanding a subject.

c1f26943-8884-4e61-a88b-1e9f2f1d454e.title: theme
