c1f26943-8884-4e61-a88b-1e9f2f1d454e.description: An overarching or recurring idea that describes attitudes or values that are perceived in a text. A theme may range from the understood ‘moral’ of a text to philosophical observations that the audience makes about the events, characters and experiences depicted in a text. A text may have more than one theme.

2ed7138f-7c0e-4caa-ba6e-8ced7bd76c8b.title: synthesise
2ed7138f-7c0e-4caa-ba6e-8ced7bd76c8b.description: Put together various elements to make a whole.

ed9c722f-c248-48dd-b05a-97ad199d4f2c.title: rhetorical question
ed9c722f-c248-48dd-b05a-97ad199d4f2c.description: A question that is asked to provoke thought rather than require an answer.

12b9aea7-4af4-4226-8817-c47f360b3839.title: verb
12b9aea7-4af4-4226-8817-c47f360b3839.description:
A word that tells what is happening. Different types of verbs include:

  • action verbs: They danced ...
  • thinking verbs: I forgot ...
  • feeling verbs: We like ...
  • saying verbs: He whispered ...
  • relating verbs: They are ....

c727d184-4b29-4727-855f-b4388d66999e.title: intonation
c727d184-4b29-4727-855f-b4388d66999e.description: The pattern or melody of pitch changes in connected speech, especially the pitch pattern of a sentence.

fd8444b8-375b-4722-9c47-ada14197d82e.title: reciting
fd8444b8-375b-4722-9c47-ada14197d82e.description: Repeating a prepared text aloud, such as a published poem, to an audience. Reading should be prosodic and may occur from memory.

b5c775a9-f968-4bbd-bb76-7c4fd6d7111e.title: expanded noun group
b5c775a9-f968-4bbd-bb76-7c4fd6d7111e.description: An extended group of words that provide rich or detailed information about the noun.

795b73c5-e90c-4d7e-91f1-b8485471c68e.title: expanded verb group
795b73c5-e90c-4d7e-91f1-b8485471c68e.description: A main verb that is preceded by one or more auxiliary or modal verbs to provide detail or precision.

43cf4ff2-e424-4ec7-9b84-3f53abe2eafd.title: voice
43cf4ff2-e424-4ec7-9b84-3f53abe2eafd.description:
The way in which language is used and/or interpreted to represent particular thoughts, opinions or perspectives. This includes the authorial voice or the voice of a narrator, character or persona within a text.

Describes the relationship between the action expressed by the verb and the subject/object of the sentence. For example, ‘active voice’ is where the subject performs the action, ‘The cat broke the vase’; ‘passive voice' is where the object is acted upon, ‘The vase was broken by the cat’.

In speaking, a description of the oral production of text.

See point of view for ‘narrative voice’

5974c1b6-225c-4d0e-a88a-814b8e250449.title: poetic forms
5974c1b6-225c-4d0e-a88a-814b8e250449.description: Fixed forms within poetry that follow specific rules, such as ballad, sonnet, elegy, ode, dramatic monologue. The form will often be determined by the tone and subject matter. Note that some poets may deliberately subvert the fixed form.

0f31f1f3-7ccc-47a1-a241-0eccefddc451.title: informative text
0f31f1f3-7ccc-47a1-a241-0eccefddc451.description: Texts whose primary purpose is to provide information through explanation, description, argument, analysis, ordering and presentation of evidence and procedures.

4330783c-5c52-4bf7-b0b2-9a994ed8cefe.title: paragraph
4330783c-5c52-4bf7-b0b2-9a994ed8cefe.description: A sequence of sentences, grouped together and focused on a specific theme. A distinct section of writing indicated by a new line.

4f4de5c7-450b-4c44-85cb-2f0641a67fe8.title: topic sentence
4f4de5c7-450b-4c44-85cb-2f0641a67fe8.description: A sentence that usually occurs at the start of a paragraph and outlines the main idea of that paragraph.

a37c894d-75e2-41a6-b80c-8fcb0ba3ebaa.title: rhetorical devices
a37c894d-75e2-41a6-b80c-8fcb0ba3ebaa.description: Strategies used by writers and speakers to achieve particular effects, such as, to stimulate the audience’s imagination or thought processes, to draw attention to a particular idea, or simply to display wit and ingenuity in composition.

ad2ff4bc-1939-4fd1-808f-90085bc26d37.title: hybrid text
ad2ff4bc-1939-4fd1-808f-90085bc26d37.description: Composite texts resulting from combining elements from different genres, styles and modes.

32d74b2b-fddb-4d23-a8e1-e40d25715420.title: assess
32d74b2b-fddb-4d23-a8e1-e40d25715420.description: Make a judgement of value, quality, outcomes, results or size.

1ea8e0f3-a39b-45f2-85cb-3f569c0e5bb0.title: grammar
1ea8e0f3-a39b-45f2-85cb-3f569c0e5bb0.description: A description of a language’s system, in regard to both structure (form) and meaning (function), at the level of a word, sentence and/or text.

44aa1977-bdc3-480f-ade6-5a8d3204cb8c.title: comma (,)
44aa1977-bdc3-480f-ade6-5a8d3204cb8c.description: A punctuation marker used to show separation between parts of a sentence, such as clauses or phrases, where separation is important to the meaning. Commas are also used to separate words, phrases or numbers in a series.

9bfaa6a3-bde5-46dd-af2e-ee41e9c6e304.title: clause (main)
9bfaa6a3-bde5-46dd-af2e-ee41e9c6e304.description:
A main clause (also known as principal or independent clause) is a clause that can stand alone as a complete sentence.

See adjectival clause and adverbial clause

a34483ff-873a-4cb5-a358-e11d1fbd5f2e.title: quotation marks
a34483ff-873a-4cb5-a358-e11d1fbd5f2e.description: Punctuation markers used to indicate: quoted or direct speech; the actual words quoted from another source in formal writing; the titles of poems, songs, short stories or articles; or, to draw attention to an unusual or particular sense or usage of a word.

ad371143-452e-4ede-8499-95532765b2d1.title: dialogue
ad371143-452e-4ede-8499-95532765b2d1.description: A conversation between 2 or more people: the conversation between characters in a text, an exchange of ideas or opinions on a particular issue, or a literary work in the form of a conversation.

7c38f254-3017-4f5f-a59a-48a3be1b8e89.title: parenthesis
7c38f254-3017-4f5f-a59a-48a3be1b8e89.description:
A punctuation marker used to indicate an interjected explanatory or qualifying remark.

Plural: parentheses

e4954a53-3f2f-4297-adcf-75014aeee503.title: hyphenation
e4954a53-3f2f-4297-adcf-75014aeee503.description: Used at the end of a line, to break a word between syllables or morphemes.

6055d9ff-732d-4a67-9245-4061ed9feebc.title: adverbial clause
6055d9ff-732d-4a67-9245-4061ed9feebc.description: A dependent clause that modifies a verb, adjective, adverb or a main clause in a sentence.

651af016-99d8-4ea0-86dc-835a670a0cc6.title: adjectival clause
651af016-99d8-4ea0-86dc-835a670a0cc6.description: A type of dependent clause that operates as an adjective to give more information to a noun or pronoun in a sentence.

60ee74cb-038d-4bf6-815b-9b315ababd53.title: subject
60ee74cb-038d-4bf6-815b-9b315ababd53.description: The noun (or noun group) in a sentence that conveys who or what the clause is about.

760277bf-8514-4a91-93ed-fd43929c9279.title: appositive
760277bf-8514-4a91-93ed-fd43929c9279.description:
A noun or pronoun that is positioned beside another noun or pronoun to explain or identify it. An appositive often includes modifiers.

See modifier

0a05712c-ec84-4bc3-8d68-4ac507879e1c.title: nominalisation
0a05712c-ec84-4bc3-8d68-4ac507879e1c.description: A process of transforming actions or events (verbs) or descriptions of nouns and pronouns (adjectives) into things, concepts or people (nouns). It can also refer to the process of forming noun groups from clauses. Nominalisation is often a feature of texts that contain abstract ideas and concepts.

5c4b83a2-0fd5-46e6-9a4f-d9688a4ef380.title: declarative sentence
5c4b83a2-0fd5-46e6-9a4f-d9688a4ef380.description: A statement presented as a complete sentence to provide fact, evidence or detail. For example: Drinking water is important for your health.

a66dd758-f53b-4000-9313-f6f006fbdf35.title: exclamatory sentence
a66dd758-f53b-4000-9313-f6f006fbdf35.description: A statement expressing a strong emotion, formed as a complete sentence, and often ending with an exclamation mark.

06f8f4d1-ff86-457e-a15f-6321bb072695.title: interrogative sentence
06f8f4d1-ff86-457e-a15f-6321bb072695.description: A sentence that asks a direct or indirect question.

b4cb0c2f-a5fc-4672-9712-776fa79ea5c1.title: imperative sentence
b4cb0c2f-a5fc-4672-9712-776fa79ea5c1.description: A complete sentence conveying a direct command, request, invitation, warning or instruction, typically directed to an implied person.

9661187c-6840-4778-b28f-4179891708d9.title: compound sentence
9661187c-6840-4778-b28f-4179891708d9.description: A sentence comprising 2 or more independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction.

605b3d57-c9f9-400a-a0f0-f7b745370fed.title: complex sentence
605b3d57-c9f9-400a-a0f0-f7b745370fed.description: Formed by adding one or more dependent (subordinate) clauses to a main (independent) clause using subordinating conjunctions and/or relative pronouns.

e3e43a03-11e0-4359-93d2-26608597fa1a.title: noun
e3e43a03-11e0-4359-93d2-26608597fa1a.description:
A word used to represent people, places, ideas and things.

  • Common nouns: nouns used to name any one of a class of things, e.g. girl, classroom, egg.
  • Proper nouns: nouns used to name a place, a person or the title of something and are signalled by a capital letter, e.g. Wagga Wagga, Sam, Olympic Games.
  • Collective nouns: nouns used to name a group of things, e.g. crowd, swarm, team.
  • Abstract nouns: nouns used to name things that we cannot see but which exist in thoughts and feelings, e.g. sadness, love, wonder.

See pronoun

717ebd62-53c1-46d1-a23b-11965631db1e.title: subject–verb agreement
717ebd62-53c1-46d1-a23b-11965631db1e.description: Occurs when the writer or speaker selects the correct verb for the noun or noun group to which it is referring. For example: The bike was here (not: The bike were here).

c0186e99-f0a9-4cad-8cf9-119b7af9148b.title: conditional connective
c0186e99-f0a9-4cad-8cf9-119b7af9148b.description: A word, or groups of words, that describes the condition that needs to be met for something to happen. This may be in the form of a word ‘if’ or phrase ‘in this case’.

ce5c9f79-76b0-4ce6-ae1d-63b34d117903.title: word association
ce5c9f79-76b0-4ce6-ae1d-63b34d117903.description: The relationship between a word and other words that are semantically related in a text.

3fd36e54-3eb8-493a-9ece-fffa42822ea7.title: hyperbole
3fd36e54-3eb8-493a-9ece-fffa42822ea7.description: An exaggerated statement not intended to be taken literally; may be used as a rhetorical device or figure of speech.

a218c25e-da17-440a-9ffd-ce3091ad3270.title: media
a218c25e-da17-440a-9ffd-ce3091ad3270.description:
Means of communication, such as publishing, broadcasting or the internet.

Plural of medium.

016ad9a6-c57d-47dc-8acd-a256f54c129a.title: visual texts
016ad9a6-c57d-47dc-8acd-a256f54c129a.description: Texts that consist of or include images. Visual elements in texts may contribute to meaning. Visual design elements in a text may include choices of lines, symbols, vectors, size and colour.

9ec38a3a-6988-4cf8-b8fe-613e075adae5.title: persuasive text
9ec38a3a-6988-4cf8-b8fe-613e075adae5.description: A text designed to convince a reader of a particular opinion or way of thinking on an issue. A persuasive text may express an opinion while discussing, analysing and/or evaluating an issue.

96aee557-2ce5-4b00-a460-5c497f9c0b89.title: imaginative text
96aee557-2ce5-4b00-a460-5c497f9c0b89.description: Texts that represent ideas, feelings and mental images in words or visual images. Imaginative texts entertain or provoke thought through their creative use of literary elements and make connections between ideas and experiences.

4d63aa49-2f9e-49f5-9e4b-2cafc9ef80a3.title: preposition
4d63aa49-2f9e-49f5-9e4b-2cafc9ef80a3.description: A word that is used before a noun, noun group or pronoun that connects it to another word in the sentence, e.g. in, on, after, before, by, under, over, of.

af8e3c6e-8cb9-4190-8371-8cbe4dedfffc.title: modifier
af8e3c6e-8cb9-4190-8371-8cbe4dedfffc.description: Words, phrases and clauses that affect and often enhance the meaning of a sentence.

786685fc-6e04-4683-91a0-f74f9fb3ec5c.title: adverbial phrase
786685fc-6e04-4683-91a0-f74f9fb3ec5c.description:
A group of words that provides information about where, when, with what, how far, how long, with whom, about what or as what.

For example:

  • He swept the floor with an old broom.
  • Throughout time people have attempted to halt old age.

01abd8ba-930d-49ca-8860-68801f5db5dc.title: decode
01abd8ba-930d-49ca-8860-68801f5db5dc.description: A process of efficient word recognition in which readers use knowledge of the relationship between letters (graphemes) and sounds (phonemes) to work out how to say and read written words.

8a541d2a-597f-4a56-961a-34b6a22080ae.title: automaticity
8a541d2a-597f-4a56-961a-34b6a22080ae.description: The fast, accurate and effortless word recognition that comes with practice. NESA acknowledges that reading aloud may include the use of Auslan, assistive technology or AACs.

88221dca-5f90-4117-bb88-e89b824c0308.title: prosody
88221dca-5f90-4117-bb88-e89b824c0308.description: Reading with expression using correct phrasing, intonation and attention to punctuation.

81b3274d-cc89-4c69-9db3-0f18eb9a830c.title: sustained reading
81b3274d-cc89-4c69-9db3-0f18eb9a830c.description: Independently reading texts to expand and maintain comprehension.

991b1f27-d97e-41e7-a223-467578af1e9d.title: prior knowledge
991b1f27-d97e-41e7-a223-467578af1e9d.description: The knowledge a person already has before encountering a particular topic.

a2d1c129-4f17-4ace-ad9f-67990ff2cd01.title: investigate
a2d1c129-4f17-4ace-ad9f-67990ff2cd01.description: Plan, inquire into and draw conclusions about.

964c55aa-306e-461f-9afe-eef86d65dc90.title: salience
964c55aa-306e-461f-9afe-eef86d65dc90.description:
A strategy used to highlight what is important in a text.

In an image, salience may be created through framing an object in the foreground, and/or by its size or distinct colour.

In written text, salience may be conveyed by positioning the most important idea at the beginning of a sentence, or through font styling such as the use of bold, underlined or italicised text.

f903136b-e94b-4da5-b58e-29ee54074e31.title: home language
f903136b-e94b-4da5-b58e-29ee54074e31.description: A language acquired and used in the home or community.

341e247f-fd75-4191-9bed-40ec0c5d2eff.title: Standard Australian English
341e247f-fd75-4191-9bed-40ec0c5d2eff.description: A system of standard English language, characterised by the perceived consistent usage of words and syntax across Australian political, business, media and education contexts. While it is always dynamic and evolving, it is recognised as the ‘common language’ of Australians.

109d9706-6c22-413b-a919-bc88238b51af.title: point of view
109d9706-6c22-413b-a919-bc88238b51af.description:
The position from which the information and events of a text are intended to be perceived by its audience. Point of view is constructed through the narrator, voice or images of the text and by characters or voices presented within it.

Point of view should not be confused with the term ‘perspective’ or with notions of opinion.

07317690-737c-4ea9-8981-6cabfe6d35d7.title: noun group
07317690-737c-4ea9-8981-6cabfe6d35d7.description:
A group of words built around a noun.

Noun groups:

  • include a noun and any words that modify it
  • may include articles, adjectives and other modifiers
  • operate the same way as a single noun in the structure of a sentence.

431b43b6-0471-4890-8eb0-29a02945225b.title: discursive text
431b43b6-0471-4890-8eb0-29a02945225b.description: Texts whose primary focus is to explore an idea or variety of topics. These texts involve the discussion of an idea(s) or opinion(s) without the direct intention of persuading the reader, listener or viewer to adopt any single point of view.

7789f5d5-b6b6-46e6-9ac1-772659a24e43.title: connotation
7789f5d5-b6b6-46e6-9ac1-772659a24e43.description: The nuances or implied meaning attached to language, beyond that of its literal or dictionary meanings. Connotations may be positive, negative, or neutral.

6d8038a9-b045-4fa6-93ae-9ad22ce66278.title: construct
6d8038a9-b045-4fa6-93ae-9ad22ce66278.description: Make; build; put together items or arguments.

e5979d86-b3d1-4eeb-ae4e-69fc680760fd.title: appreciate
e5979d86-b3d1-4eeb-ae4e-69fc680760fd.description: Make a judgement about the value of.

db532848-c047-4b81-80aa-4e3ac30e1339.title: medium
db532848-c047-4b81-80aa-4e3ac30e1339.description:
Means of communication, such as publishing, broadcasting or the internet.

Singular of media.

6835cf9d-ba9e-439e-a675-1b7c1e5cc966.title: visualise
6835cf9d-ba9e-439e-a675-1b7c1e5cc966.description: A comprehension strategy used to create a mental image from a text read, viewed or heard. To visualise is to bring the text to life, engage the imagination, and use a person’s senses.

76860d6e-344c-43c1-b69b-b14548ab4d3a.title: adverb
76860d6e-344c-43c1-b69b-b14548ab4d3a.description: A word that tells something about a verb, adjective, another adverb or a whole clause. They usually indicate manner (commonly ending in -ly) or degree.

aa6b36dc-e03c-4a42-9442-c314e320e93d.title: contraction
aa6b36dc-e03c-4a42-9442-c314e320e93d.description: A shortened form of one or 2 words (one of which is usually a verb). In a contraction, an apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter or letters.

fe8deb23-d387-4cbf-9446-198d59eeb1ed.title: apostrophe (’)
fe8deb23-d387-4cbf-9446-198d59eeb1ed.description: A punctuation marker used to indicate possession or missing letters or numbers in a contracted expression.

9e733efc-4154-4b0b-8274-75ebe9fc8ab4.title: homonym
9e733efc-4154-4b0b-8274-75ebe9fc8ab4.description: A word having the same sound and the same spelling as another, but a different meaning.

d1043fda-4881-468e-813f-b700b424948b.title: quoted speech
d1043fda-4881-468e-813f-b700b424948b.description: The exact words expressed by a person, reproduced in quotation marks. For example: ‘You'll never guess what I've just seen!’ exclaimed Loreta.

4cf934bd-5afb-4aad-a342-c9d8b059a01f.title: reported speech
4cf934bd-5afb-4aad-a342-c9d8b059a01f.description:
Speech in a text used to communicate what someone else said, but without using the exact words. In reported speech the tense of the verbs is often changed.

For example:

  • She said that she was going to leave (indirect speech).
  • ‘I am going to leave', she said (direct speech).

9598d439-c5f8-455b-8a78-859be2d44a21.title: word play
9598d439-c5f8-455b-8a78-859be2d44a21.description:
Experimenting with and manipulating language.

See pun and spoonerism

82989e2f-a02c-47c2-b527-941f82ab7dcf.title: pun
82989e2f-a02c-47c2-b527-941f82ab7dcf.description: A figure of speech where there is a play on words, usually created through the use of a homonym or homophone. Puns rely on more than one meaning of a word to emphasise the point.

637c4853-8892-4734-a79a-d79767332dc9.title: spoonerism
637c4853-8892-4734-a79a-d79767332dc9.description:
A language device, sometimes a slip of the tongue, by which corresponding phonemes or morphemes are switched between 2 words or within a word.

For example:

  • butterfly becomes flutterby
  • It's pouring with rain becomes it’s roaring with pain.

See word play

4ecfbaa8-c3ee-4144-b6f8-265e749fbbf1.title: prefix
4ecfbaa8-c3ee-4144-b6f8-265e749fbbf1.description: A bound morpheme made up of letters that appear before a base word to make a new word. For example, un- in ‘unhappy’ means ‘not’ (un + happy = not happy).

7e76a5cc-ca59-47fb-9253-cc0fee404716.title: Tier 1 words
7e76a5cc-ca59-47fb-9253-cc0fee404716.description: Basic-level, everyday words, e.g. dog, baby, happy, pretty, was, come, said.

08337272-4efc-43c3-b101-a75c566855af.title: antonym
08337272-4efc-43c3-b101-a75c566855af.description: A word or phrase that has the opposite meaning of another word or phrase.

ac0077e1-c54b-4b39-975f-ebcb989e39d8.title: navigation pathway
ac0077e1-c54b-4b39-975f-ebcb989e39d8.description: A possible way to move around and locate content on a digital platform.

6270c0c5-bf25-4a82-bed8-cf76c5ff664e.title: monitoring
6270c0c5-bf25-4a82-bed8-cf76c5ff664e.description: Considering meaning and/or purpose when reading and/or writing.

aa0442ea-f589-408c-a862-54218d6114d8.title: clause (dependent)
aa0442ea-f589-408c-a862-54218d6114d8.description: A dependent clause (also known as subordinate clause) is a group of words that cannot stand alone as a sentence.

7843637d-6345-4a21-8894-a024b7a1a190.title: coordinating conjunction
7843637d-6345-4a21-8894-a024b7a1a190.description:
A word or group of words that functions to link:

  • 2 words or phrases within a sentence, e.g. shoes and socks
  • 2 independent clauses within a sentence.

043d03ec-8a45-4e53-9e6e-8bf8bc53d88b.title: subordinating conjunction
043d03ec-8a45-4e53-9e6e-8bf8bc53d88b.description: A word or group of words that function to link a dependent clause to an independent clause.

6d237b77-86e6-4d59-bc2c-9019e7cca66f.title: simile
6d237b77-86e6-4d59-bc2c-9019e7cca66f.description:
A figure of speech that compares the similar qualities of 2 different things. The comparison usually includes like, as or as if.

See figurative language

e1a57b86-e433-4cea-890b-a57fff39e453.title: personification
e1a57b86-e433-4cea-890b-a57fff39e453.description:
Attributing human characteristics to abstractions such as love, things or animals.

See figurative language

9f0fdd50-16f2-4364-8dda-7224e9002ae5.title: paraphrase
9f0fdd50-16f2-4364-8dda-7224e9002ae5.description: A rewording of something that has been written or spoken.

f2cc7c55-bb91-42ad-95c6-509e9b7b3171.title: temporal connective
f2cc7c55-bb91-42ad-95c6-509e9b7b3171.description: A word or group of words that indicates when something is happening, e.g. first, next, finally, before, after, then.

6182b4d8-3190-46e0-a585-c7f86fd91bb8.title: adjectival phrase
6182b4d8-3190-46e0-a585-c7f86fd91bb8.description:
A group of words (usually beginning with a preposition) that gives more information about a noun.

For example:

  • The girl with brown curly hair sat at the front.
  • The flowers in the vase were wilting.

25285085-5359-402e-9036-639666adf80c.title: irregular plural word
25285085-5359-402e-9036-639666adf80c.description:
A noun that indicates more than one thing without requiring a plural marking suffix, -s or -es.

Mouse is a singular noun and mice is an irregular noun.

38d6df75-3d4d-4dbf-aaee-66ec53d83920.title: vowel
38d6df75-3d4d-4dbf-aaee-66ec53d83920.description:
A sound that is voiced with the mouth open and not obstructed by the lips, teeth or tongue. For example: the short /o/ phoneme in the word ‘dog’.

Often represented by the graphemes: a, e, i, o, u.

70e0b997-f2fb-44aa-b26f-e90423c7c451.title: diphthong
70e0b997-f2fb-44aa-b26f-e90423c7c451.description: A type of vowel phoneme, also known as a glide vowel, formed by combining 2 vowel sounds within a single syllable. For example, /oi/ in join, /ou/ in proud.

5ad8f722-905b-491a-9f9c-ec278cbfcf5d.title: schwa
5ad8f722-905b-491a-9f9c-ec278cbfcf5d.description: A reduced vowel phoneme occurring in an unaccented (unstressed) syllable of a multisyllabic word. For example, in the word ‘problem’ the final vowel phoneme is unstressed and is said quickly and quietly, and with less emphasis.

ccdb89f3-ada1-409d-b7d8-02188b6ecc3d.title: onset
ccdb89f3-ada1-409d-b7d8-02188b6ecc3d.description:
The consonant speech sound(s) that appear at the start of a syllable and before the vowel phoneme. For example, /b/ represents the onset in the word ‘big’.

See rime

72aca422-0700-4d36-8818-80bc123d4759.title: rime
72aca422-0700-4d36-8818-80bc123d4759.description: The vowel and other speech sounds that occur at the end of a syllable. For example, the /-ig/ represents the rime in the word ‘big’.

69558ad1-9f59-413a-931d-51334f3fff03.title: rhyme
69558ad1-9f59-413a-931d-51334f3fff03.description: A repetition of similar speech sounds in 2 or more words, beginning from the last stressed vowel sound and carrying through any remaining syllables.

1b5fb88d-3dbc-481b-8ffe-c1dbe59ed2c1.title: vowel digraph
1b5fb88d-3dbc-481b-8ffe-c1dbe59ed2c1.description:
Two vowel graphemes that represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • ea in cream
  • ai in snail
  • oo in chook.

e905bc55-75cd-48b1-a582-9ea9219e5c0b.title: split digraph
e905bc55-75cd-48b1-a582-9ea9219e5c0b.description:
Two graphemes that are split by a consonant to represent a long vowel phoneme.

For example:

  • a-e in cake
  • i-e in side
  • o-e in rope.

bd37a92c-d4a9-4ee2-b215-0b7c35338d8e.title: high-frequency words
bd37a92c-d4a9-4ee2-b215-0b7c35338d8e.description: Words that appear often in written texts.

a30a0720-1d1d-41d9-a2b8-ac8e98a0bce8.title: digraph
a30a0720-1d1d-41d9-a2b8-ac8e98a0bce8.description:
Two graphemes used to represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • consonant digraphs – sh, ck, th
  • split digraphs – a-e, i-e, o-e
  • vowel digraphs – ee, oo, ea.

5f0d05dd-a4c8-4793-977e-f60ee1683b48.title: CVC words
5f0d05dd-a4c8-4793-977e-f60ee1683b48.description: Words formed by a consonant-vowel-consonant. For example, cat, bag, pen.

4e6ae283-3101-47a0-afd6-bdd3dc4e9436.title: decodable texts
4e6ae283-3101-47a0-afd6-bdd3dc4e9436.description:
Texts that are made up of grapheme–phoneme correspondences (GPCs) that students have learnt. These texts are used by beginning readers to practise segmenting and blending skills to read words, quickly and effortlessly.

See automaticity

755d5925-ee53-40f6-9822-fbee8e2768a2.title: single-letter grapheme
755d5925-ee53-40f6-9822-fbee8e2768a2.description:
One letter used to represent one phoneme (speech sound).

See phoneme

adc75432-8ea2-4798-8fe9-b3b66683a42e.title: encode
adc75432-8ea2-4798-8fe9-b3b66683a42e.description: Spell words in their visible written form.

96c03464-e494-4e50-bd6c-856107c90930.title: predict
96c03464-e494-4e50-bd6c-856107c90930.description: Suggest what may happen based on available information.

78320747-a493-4845-971b-1251fd2713ee.title: phonic knowledge
78320747-a493-4845-971b-1251fd2713ee.description: The ability to decode and encode words using knowledge of grapheme–phoneme relationships.

7a8bfd6c-4e90-426c-9969-41d5132733c8.title: adjective
7a8bfd6c-4e90-426c-9969-41d5132733c8.description: A word class that describes, classifies or qualifies a noun or a pronoun.

e6f50f8c-75e4-43c2-a90e-01a5d9ab34a6.title: upper/lower-case letters
e6f50f8c-75e4-43c2-a90e-01a5d9ab34a6.description:
Two visible forms of alphabetic letters. Lower-case letters are generally used, except when it is necessary to:

  • indicate specific names (proper nouns) such as those of people, organisations, titles or countries
  • indicate the beginning of a sentence or the initial letter of a proper noun
  • write headings
  • achieve a particular effect, such as to indicate shouting.

ba2ab313-07ca-4dce-99e4-64834c0066b9.title: fluent reading
ba2ab313-07ca-4dce-99e4-64834c0066b9.description: The act of identifying words accurately, effortlessly, at a contextually appropriate rate, and with phrasing and expression that reflects the meaning of the passage.

d65d609f-5909-4db7-8c52-ccd3b2ae2695.title: question mark (?)
d65d609f-5909-4db7-8c52-ccd3b2ae2695.description: A punctuation marker used at the end of a sentence to indicate that a question is being asked.

294cc6d6-ea64-4ade-942c-a15f7321cf15.title: full stop (.)
294cc6d6-ea64-4ade-942c-a15f7321cf15.description: A punctuation marker used to indicate the end of a sentence that is a statement or command.

d8f646d8-0ced-46f0-a512-5e9d52e1ac10.title: simple sentence
d8f646d8-0ced-46f0-a512-5e9d52e1ac10.description: A complete message that contains a subject and predicate, forming a single independent clause.

ca017e32-e40c-4239-aece-f5a6ada553e7.title: mentor text
ca017e32-e40c-4239-aece-f5a6ada553e7.description: A text that is studied as an example to show how specific textual features are crafted. Also known as a model text.

984c05ee-80ee-48b5-a05c-cb26a661fbe3.title: return sweep
984c05ee-80ee-48b5-a05c-cb26a661fbe3.description: The eye movement that takes the reader’s eyes from one end of the line of text to the start of the next line.

7bd77874-063e-4f5d-8132-3b5f11d077bb.title: oral language
7bd77874-063e-4f5d-8132-3b5f11d077bb.description: A system through which spoken words can be used to express, receive and understand information, ideas and feelings.

bf8d57ca-90d3-48dd-9bb7-ef8de2c51b5b.title: inflected word forms
bf8d57ca-90d3-48dd-9bb7-ef8de2c51b5b.description:
A word form that marks a distinction in tense (jump-jumps-jumping-jumped), plurality (cat-cats), and comparatives and superlatives (big-bigger-biggest).

See suffix

bc53a0c2-f418-4e9b-ac48-c2ab7c03772b.title: double consonant
bc53a0c2-f418-4e9b-ac48-c2ab7c03772b.description: Two of the same consecutive letters. Also referred to as a consonant doublet.

277dfeda-5ccd-43c1-99f4-fb78ddf982eb.title: trigraph
277dfeda-5ccd-43c1-99f4-fb78ddf982eb.description:
Three letters used to represent one phoneme.

For example:

  • the tch in catch.
  • the igh in flight.

c71a2ab5-ece1-42ed-a874-0cef0c813eb6.title: extended phonic code
c71a2ab5-ece1-42ed-a874-0cef0c813eb6.description: The vowel and consonant phonemes which are represented by less frequently occurring and alternative spellings.

2d96334f-d10f-4fe1-8e11-c6cd50a8587e.title: consonant phoneme
2d96334f-d10f-4fe1-8e11-c6cd50a8587e.description: A speech sound produced with a complete or partial obstruction of the flow of air by the teeth, lips, tongue and/or voice.

3b78445b-816d-40a9-b325-a2871e472e41.title: hyperlink
3b78445b-816d-40a9-b325-a2871e472e41.description: A hyperlink is a text, image, frame or button that when clicked or tapped will open another webpage, website, image, sound, document or application, such as email. Hyperlinks are often used within documents to link to other pages or sections.

f7a36d25-0bdd-4d2f-a83c-e85bab693be4.title: belonging
f7a36d25-0bdd-4d2f-a83c-e85bab693be4.description: A strong feeling of being happy or comfortable as part of a group, place or experience.

a78f1468-b08f-4f70-b723-5ff437458b66.title: contextual factors
a78f1468-b08f-4f70-b723-5ff437458b66.description: Factors that can influence health, safety, wellbeing and participation in physical activity including personal, social, cultural, economic, environmental and political factors that exist in differing ways and have varying impacts across population groups.

5490abdd-3173-4fae-acdd-6fbcce98c448.title: bullying
5490abdd-3173-4fae-acdd-6fbcce98c448.description: Ongoing misuse of power through repeated behaviour that causes harm to a person or group of people.

8f1e129b-eabe-46c0-ab99-6461c8d5c145.title: discrimination
8f1e129b-eabe-46c0-ab99-6461c8d5c145.description: An unjust or prejudicial treatment of someone because they belong to a particular group of people or have a particular characteristic.

a82af7f8-c755-44fb-ae54-39687f867ac9.title: dynamic movement environments
a82af7f8-c755-44fb-ae54-39687f867ac9.description: Situations that are constantly changing and are more unpredictable.

a2359868-2f26-45da-acb0-2eb201882765.title: initiative games
a2359868-2f26-45da-acb0-2eb201882765.description: Physical activities designed to challenge individuals that require critical and creative thinking, promote cooperation or encourage the solving of problems or movement challenges.

4acdd7f5-2282-4114-bb0e-7e5d1fec712d.title: movement challenges
4acdd7f5-2282-4114-bb0e-7e5d1fec712d.description: Tasks that require individual students or groups of students to use a problem-solving approach to successfully complete the task.

b9974d6b-c8cf-43e6-9372-051d4ee274b6.title: rhythmic movement sequences
b9974d6b-c8cf-43e6-9372-051d4ee274b6.description: Movement that is composed and performed in response to stimuli such as equipment, beats and sounds, images, words or themes. It includes creative movement, movement exploration, dance styles and dance elements.

f5d6213a-87c6-4e57-823a-f8a6d14ebd7a.title: movement sequences
f5d6213a-87c6-4e57-823a-f8a6d14ebd7a.description: A combination of movement skills and movement concepts to enable a body and/or objects to move in response to a stimulus; or a planned order of movements.

db6984e2-42f4-4bc3-95a8-b6e34b8deae1.title: fundamental movement skills
db6984e2-42f4-4bc3-95a8-b6e34b8deae1.description: A specific set of gross motor skills.

14175f2a-3cc3-4008-9059-ca9a6f4237cd.title: health literacy
14175f2a-3cc3-4008-9059-ca9a6f4237cd.description: The ability to selectively access and critically analyse information, navigate community services and resources, and take action to promote personal health and the health of others.

3129fe0c-819b-49d0-a64f-c5b8c5cf08d8.title: consent
3129fe0c-819b-49d0-a64f-c5b8c5cf08d8.description:
Informed and freely given agreement to engage in an activity, or for a specific thing to happen. Consent is denied when someone does not have the capacity to give consent.

According to the Commonwealth Consent policy Framework, sexual consent is a free, voluntary and informed agreement between people to participate in a sexual act. This agreement is only present when these people mutually and genuinely want to engage in that sexual act and actively make sure their partner does too.

In NSW, consent is a fundamental part of sexual offence law.

2eac64a8-734d-496a-b5b3-1129a1ba17ca.title: cyberbullying
2eac64a8-734d-496a-b5b3-1129a1ba17ca.description: The use of electronic communication and technology to bully or harass a person.

0c11980d-6d74-452e-a12e-7f153d82acd8.title: grooming
0c11980d-6d74-452e-a12e-7f153d82acd8.description: The process of someone building a relationship with a child or vulnerable person with the intention of manipulating, exploiting and/or abusing them, typically for sexual purposes.

d6707c93-9b72-4c47-a46a-deaad0aab445.title: image-based abuse
d6707c93-9b72-4c47-a46a-deaad0aab445.description: The act of sharing or threatening to share sexual or intimate images or videos of a person without their consent, often with the intention of causing distress or harm.

c21904ac-20c7-4247-8d0b-30bfaa396f73.title: sexual relationship
c21904ac-20c7-4247-8d0b-30bfaa396f73.description: Involves interactions between individuals that include sexual activities or behaviours.

91c09f20-43fe-4ad2-af8e-ce8427353751.title: upstander behaviour
91c09f20-43fe-4ad2-af8e-ce8427353751.description: An individual and/or group standing up to take safe actions to support themselves and/or others.

afd97e33-3f13-465b-8ac2-b094c0daf217.title: coercion
afd97e33-3f13-465b-8ac2-b094c0daf217.description: The act of persuading or compelling someone to do something through the use of intimidation or force.

3753de1d-a92c-46f1-a54b-b63b816bddce.title: intimate relationships
3753de1d-a92c-46f1-a54b-b63b816bddce.description: Close, personal connections between individuals characterised by deep affection and emotional closeness.

6ca4b8e2-5084-46b9-a340-b7e4550a00f4.title: Deaf culture
6ca4b8e2-5084-46b9-a340-b7e4550a00f4.description:
The beliefs, values, traditions, history, social norms, literary traditions and art shared by d/Deaf people who belong to the Deaf community. Culture is understood as a framework in which things come to be seen as having meaning. It involves the lens through which people:

  • see, think, interpret the world and experience
  • make assumptions about self and others
  • understand and represent individual and community identity.

See culture

6220bba3-5694-4c83-b018-2a18dfcf8364.title: Deaf community
6220bba3-5694-4c83-b018-2a18dfcf8364.description: A local, national or transnational network of people who share the language and culture of Deaf people and a history of common experiences. A primary unifying factor in Deaf communities is the use of sign language.

6d825633-b71c-4d58-9f30-e2f9118905ce.title: interpret
6d825633-b71c-4d58-9f30-e2f9118905ce.description: The act of translation from one language to another, the process of understanding and explaining.

f2c59897-e17c-4e0c-bf24-c3312c5a8360.title: language
f2c59897-e17c-4e0c-bf24-c3312c5a8360.description: A structured system of communication. The structure of a language is its grammar and the free components are its vocabulary. Languages are the primary means of communication of humans, and can be conveyed through speech (spoken language), sign or writing.

d38463ac-543a-460f-a3b9-504c322546ce.title: first language(s)
d38463ac-543a-460f-a3b9-504c322546ce.description: The first language(s) that a person learns to speak.

02ef6182-214e-4bd8-bc8b-3be831276055.title: depicting signs
02ef6182-214e-4bd8-bc8b-3be831276055.description:
A partly-lexical sign that is highly iconic and can be modified in a gradient way by a signer. Depicting signs can act as verbs or nouns depending on their use in context.

See entity depicting signs, handling depicting signs, size and shape specifier depicting signs

0966b58c-8701-4b37-b9f7-4ae3753a6c1a.title: non-manual features
0966b58c-8701-4b37-b9f7-4ae3753a6c1a.description: Elements of a sign that contribute to the meaning but are not made with the hands, e.g. eyebrow position or mouth gestures.

da81065e-34bb-446c-a962-6df5dd731146.title: spatial locations
da81065e-34bb-446c-a962-6df5dd731146.description: Locations in the signing space that are associated with particular absent referents so that they can be referred back to in place of naming a referent.

913c2936-a61b-498d-90de-5940f45dfa6b.title: constructed action
913c2936-a61b-498d-90de-5940f45dfa6b.description: A discourse strategy used in signed languages when signers use their own face and body to represent actions, signs, thoughts or feelings of a referent in a text. The referent can be themselves at another time, a different character, or something thought of as an animate entity.

524c6f97-b0e9-4555-922c-3a2454779e68.title: cohesion
524c6f97-b0e9-4555-922c-3a2454779e68.description: The use of a range of language features to link parts of a signed text to make it easy to follow and understand referents in the text.

d37d6a9e-db6a-48bf-9e59-a380fbb189e5.title: communication
d37d6a9e-db6a-48bf-9e59-a380fbb189e5.description: The purposeful interpretation and expression of meaning.

73f1560b-0600-426b-b6f3-8ef5156fe799.title: fingerspelling
73f1560b-0600-426b-b6f3-8ef5156fe799.description: The manual representation of the letters of the alphabet of a spoken language. In Australia, a 2-handed fingerspelling system is used to fingerspell English letters.

0439eab4-100e-4885-a97a-674da89a05e1.title: handshape
0439eab4-100e-4885-a97a-674da89a05e1.description: The held position of the hand and fingers in producing a particular sign.

fc19a169-a0ca-4619-961c-91ede9f289b3.title: indicating verbs
fc19a169-a0ca-4619-961c-91ede9f289b3.description: A subset of verbs which can have their start or end location modified or be moved around in space to show who, what or where is involved in the verb. Directional indicating verbs can be moved meaningfully in space. Locatable indicating verbs cannot change direction, but can be meaningfully signed in a non-neutral location.

e7ac49b2-00f8-4100-abd3-e0f1a39764b5.title: referent
e7ac49b2-00f8-4100-abd3-e0f1a39764b5.description: The person or thing being talked about with a sign or phrase.

d6147b59-6832-4ad3-a9a7-ce1a8a12c8d0.title: entity depicting signs
d6147b59-6832-4ad3-a9a7-ce1a8a12c8d0.description:
Signs in which the handshape represents an object, and the object can move around or be located in space mirroring real-world movement and location.

See depicting signs

4684b434-0be9-4766-978a-dd1f7757c74c.title: orientation
4684b434-0be9-4766-978a-dd1f7757c74c.description: The direction the palm or fingers of a handshape point in a given sign.

bcbd6316-6f06-41e0-bcbf-b0f239c4f329.title: visual vernacular
bcbd6316-6f06-41e0-bcbf-b0f239c4f329.description: A highly visual form of performance often incorporated into storytelling which uses features of mime, gesture, non-manual features and specific cinematic techniques in the production of signs. Techniques include close and distant focus, dissolving of visual images and cutting between scenes, objects and characters, and time distortion in the 3-dimensional delivery of visually presented information.

cbcb352f-a9e4-4a8c-b45f-1cc7d0a96d07.title: responding
cbcb352f-a9e4-4a8c-b45f-1cc7d0a96d07.description: Engaging with a text. ‘Responding’ involves identifying, selecting, describing, comprehending, imagining, interpreting, explaining, analysing and/or evaluating.

7a178cd9-9cfe-4c31-94c0-c3793f40896e.title: d/Deaf
7a178cd9-9cfe-4c31-94c0-c3793f40896e.description: When referring to deaf people who belong to a linguistic and cultural minority known as the Deaf community, the 'D' may be capitalised in reference to the individual, the group, or the culture in order to accord respect and deference, for example, the Deaf community. When referring simply to audiological status or when cultural affiliation is not known, as in the case of a person with a hearing loss in general, the lowercase 'd', as in 'deaf' is the more common usage.

1d8f46e7-d5b3-44f0-af87-4971eb0a23c3.title: Deaf gain
1d8f46e7-d5b3-44f0-af87-4971eb0a23c3.description: Used to reframe the term ‘deaf’, from the traditional pathological perspective of ‘hearing loss’ often held by wider society to a view of deafness through the lens of bicultural diversity. Being deaf is seen as an individual and social gain and as a positive form of diversity that involves cognitive and sensory changes that have the potential to contribute to the greater good of humanity.

041f64a5-0bf3-4ceb-9572-7920413ee74d.title: sign languages
041f64a5-0bf3-4ceb-9572-7920413ee74d.description:
Visual–gestural languages which evolve naturally in Deaf communities, such as Auslan. They are neither universal nor based on the spoken language of the country or region. Sign languages have their own lexicon and grammar and are equally complex and sophisticated as spoken languages. Adapted forms of sign language can be used for people who are deafblind.

See adapted forms

dbfae055-3124-48a1-8167-0331fc62bb2c.title: Deaf
dbfae055-3124-48a1-8167-0331fc62bb2c.description: A cultural identity for people with hearing loss who share a common culture and who usually have a shared sign language.

8c0d4705-c522-43d5-859c-34de3890d3f0.title: non-body-anchored signs
8c0d4705-c522-43d5-859c-34de3890d3f0.description: Signs that are made in neutral space and do not make contact with a location on the body. These signs can easily be moved around in space.

18c825fe-2b83-42af-87ae-8ba1b4a9d592.title: signing space
18c825fe-2b83-42af-87ae-8ba1b4a9d592.description: The area around a signer in which signs are articulated and can be modified.

e419d98a-be72-4ba6-a609-b30f115683a6.title: fully-lexical signs
e419d98a-be72-4ba6-a609-b30f115683a6.description: Signs with a form that is fully specified, that is, the handshape, movement and location are conventional. Lexical signs make up a large proportion of the signs in a sign language dictionary.

d35bb60c-3a49-4309-9182-641f195d4e2e.title: partly-lexical signs
d35bb60c-3a49-4309-9182-641f195d4e2e.description: Signs with a form that is not fully specified. The handshape, movement and/or location can change, e.g. in pointing signs (direction or handshape can be modified), or depicting signs (movement and location are often created on the spot).

269111b2-a27e-4a2c-82f9-19034e67b6a0.title: non-lexical signs
269111b2-a27e-4a2c-82f9-19034e67b6a0.description: Symbolic units of meaning that are created on the spot in a particular context, particularly in constructed action but also gesturing. These signs cannot be listed in a dictionary.

b0e9614e-5164-41f5-9069-448a485ef003.title: gesture
b0e9614e-5164-41f5-9069-448a485ef003.description: A way of communicating with the hands that uses largely unconventional forms (except for conventional gestures such as the thumbs up for good), and that represents more imagistic thought of a speaker or signer. In spoken languages, gestures co-occur with speech, and in signed languages they form gestural overlays.

4ad52348-3ab5-4587-a3f9-93c2c61f30af.title: iconicity
4ad52348-3ab5-4587-a3f9-93c2c61f30af.description: See arbitrary signs, translucent signs and transparent signs

8c1adb99-1425-4f42-b4f8-18f66981966e.title: linguistic features/structures
8c1adb99-1425-4f42-b4f8-18f66981966e.description: Grammatical, lexical, phonological or structural characteristics of a language or a text.

c58a798b-797b-44dd-8098-95610df7a2c3.title: handling depicting signs
c58a798b-797b-44dd-8098-95610df7a2c3.description:
Signs where the handshape represents how a human hand holds or touches an object and the movement shows how something is moved around or located in space.

See depicting signs

c4bb055c-7dfa-4a2e-a5c7-231f132703dd.title: path movements
c4bb055c-7dfa-4a2e-a5c7-231f132703dd.description: Movement of the hands from one location in space to another while producing a sign.

d285c3ed-4fac-4e6e-9e44-42598a847ee8.title: backchannel
d285c3ed-4fac-4e6e-9e44-42598a847ee8.description: Responses given by the receiver of a message in a conversation that serve a social function, such as showing attention or nodding without interrupting the signer or giver of the message.

b38a596c-90a1-458d-9837-592b7487dc5a.title: simple text
b38a596c-90a1-458d-9837-592b7487dc5a.description: A text in which the vocabulary and language structures are very familiar and straightforward, with mostly simple sentences. Comprehension may be supported by the use of visuals and/or word lists.

77b8f515-4f47-4193-81bb-7c1f4726ffd9.title: access
77b8f515-4f47-4193-81bb-7c1f4726ffd9.description: To gather information from a variety of sources, services and facilities.

b930b606-d061-4d13-87dc-c24c66286c95.title: translation
b930b606-d061-4d13-87dc-c24c66286c95.description: A type of transformation that moves a shape (or all the points in a plane) by the same amount to the left or right, or up or down.

de09b12f-856a-4535-a423-9814063c02c7.title: modality
de09b12f-856a-4535-a423-9814063c02c7.description: Referring to visual–gestural languages as opposed to auditory–verbal languages.

6d9dbe39-ae79-426d-a872-3b27edd6ffb7.title: enacting
6d9dbe39-ae79-426d-a872-3b27edd6ffb7.description: Showing or constructing the action, thoughts or language of a referent using the whole body or part of the body. Enactments are context-dependent for meaning.

16c242f8-6139-4938-99db-17386a2e437c.title: eye gaze
16c242f8-6139-4938-99db-17386a2e437c.description: The direction in which a signer is looking, which can have conventional associated meanings in Auslan, such as marking a shift into character in constructed action.

80d57994-ad47-4234-adc4-449393a66476.title: visual–gestural languages
80d57994-ad47-4234-adc4-449393a66476.description: Signed languages are described as visual–gestural because they are received through vision and signed with hands, compared to spoken languages which are described as auditory–oral languages, as they are received through hearing and spoken with the mouth. The term does not equate signed languages with gesture in general.

c8ba6506-bc5c-4f8a-bc57-cfcd5854c9b2.title: dialect
c8ba6506-bc5c-4f8a-bc57-cfcd5854c9b2.description: A variant of a language that is characteristic of a region or social group.

9ada49b2-4864-40a9-8ef2-97af0a697aae.title: modelled language
9ada49b2-4864-40a9-8ef2-97af0a697aae.description: Language that has been modelled or previously taught by the teacher. It can be used by students as a scaffold in structured situations.

0b88c9c1-f944-41d4-ba08-ceb86aaefd10.title: switch
0b88c9c1-f944-41d4-ba08-ceb86aaefd10.description:
A type of assistive technology that enables people with cognitive and/or physical disability to access a range of devices, including computers and communication devices. Switches can be activated by touch, or triggered without contact, such as through eye gaze, sound or blowing.

See assistive technology (AT)

ee00f4c9-ded3-45c0-b98b-1d02c6c0160a.title: formulaic phrases or expressions
ee00f4c9-ded3-45c0-b98b-1d02c6c0160a.description: Words or expressions which are commonly used in fixed patterns and learnt as such without grammatical analysis. For example: Once upon a time (story-starter).

a863de96-7453-4587-a24e-461982a59ab2.title: list buoys
a863de96-7453-4587-a24e-461982a59ab2.description: A sign where the fingers on the non-dominant hand are used to represent the items in a list while the dominant hand signs something about those items.

e74886ed-50a0-4496-88a5-d184037e8369.title: planetary health
e74886ed-50a0-4496-88a5-d184037e8369.description: The relationship between the health of the planet and the health of humans.

1eb90e46-0838-4000-8ee0-364dd958c62e.title: risky play
1eb90e46-0838-4000-8ee0-364dd958c62e.description: Play activities that involve a degree of challenge and allow children to test limits and explore boundaries.

178ff06d-c6ae-4992-8beb-a41be48e328b.title: mental health
178ff06d-c6ae-4992-8beb-a41be48e328b.description: A state of mental wellbeing in which a person can function and manage ordinary stresses.

6e213295-9b21-45b2-8636-05c6de0888de.title: milestones
6e213295-9b21-45b2-8636-05c6de0888de.description: Behaviours or physical skills demonstrated by infants and children as they grow and develop.

67d932b1-f389-47d3-b4a5-2e922acef9ed.title: kinship
67d932b1-f389-47d3-b4a5-2e922acef9ed.description: A key aspect of Aboriginal cultures and values. It includes the importance of all relationships and of being related to and belonging to the land.

4d543dd0-4abb-4e04-b7e1-6e235d12206c.title: otitis media
4d543dd0-4abb-4e04-b7e1-6e235d12206c.description: Infection of the middle ear. Otitis media is a leading cause of ear disease in Aboriginal children.

f33ce25d-a7cc-461b-a5ac-d5378d0fce06.title: weather
f33ce25d-a7cc-461b-a5ac-d5378d0fce06.description: The state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, with respect to wind, precipitation, temperature, cloud cover, humidity and air pressure.

7d1a1ccc-3c1a-4dee-b939-642d60e2ba1f.title: primary production
7d1a1ccc-3c1a-4dee-b939-642d60e2ba1f.description: The harvesting or extraction of natural resources from the environment to produce raw materials in industries such as agriculture, mining, fishing and forestry.

a5c63e0c-16a7-4fa6-9b72-bd7638c4a0ad.title: spatial variation
a5c63e0c-16a7-4fa6-9b72-bd7638c4a0ad.description: The difference or variation in natural and human-made features over an area of the Earth’s surface.

3070d22b-daac-4a27-9d86-edfa958b1dcf.title: topography
3070d22b-daac-4a27-9d86-edfa958b1dcf.description: The relief and configuration of a landscape, including its natural and man-made features.

569e47b1-dd74-4aab-972e-faedec9c8063.title: vegetation zones
569e47b1-dd74-4aab-972e-faedec9c8063.description: Large areas of land classified by dominant plant types and climate conditions.

7ce84656-fd4c-482c-afed-0818858e93a9.title: transect
7ce84656-fd4c-482c-afed-0818858e93a9.description: A straight line drawn on a map between 2 points, used to represent changes in elevation, landforms and other geographical features along the path.

82d6d1b7-1573-4926-8dcf-24b76e27618b.title: maritime choke points
82d6d1b7-1573-4926-8dcf-24b76e27618b.description: A narrow maritime passage critical for global shipping and trade where congestion or disruption can significantly affect transport routes and security.

372fec20-b7b4-4513-8118-e10dc1f99b78.title: geomorphic
372fec20-b7b4-4513-8118-e10dc1f99b78.description: Relating to the form of the landscape and other features on the Earth’s surface.

d0367dde-9177-4c22-99b6-2b7daecaddfe.title: natural disaster
d0367dde-9177-4c22-99b6-2b7daecaddfe.description: When a natural hazard results in extensive damage to people, places and environments.

2fb8e4b4-54ce-41f2-87f2-f3b3282814f8.title: nation-state
2fb8e4b4-54ce-41f2-87f2-f3b3282814f8.description: A country with defined borders, a recognised government and common nationality.

e8a46fcc-9881-4f60-8a6c-33b553d19c73.title: sovereignty
e8a46fcc-9881-4f60-8a6c-33b553d19c73.description: The authority of a state, community or political unit to govern itself and exercise control over its territory, population, resources and internal affairs without external interference.

879a5401-d026-447d-80c2-5bd7a8154a6c.title: spatial patterns
879a5401-d026-447d-80c2-5bd7a8154a6c.description: The positioning or organisation of phenomena or features in a geographic space.

9dd8f0ab-f5c7-4399-9833-d083cb720adc.title: geothermal zones
9dd8f0ab-f5c7-4399-9833-d083cb720adc.description: Areas on Earth’s surface, or underground where heat from the Earth’s interior rises to the surface, often characterised by volcanic activity, hot springs or geysers.

40efd28c-bae8-4332-9894-0dc7b61b3e78.title: extreme environmental events
40efd28c-bae8-4332-9894-0dc7b61b3e78.description: Hazardous and often unpredictable occurrences, such as floods, bushfire or cyclones, that can cause major environmental, social and economic impacts.

9d79e40f-511b-48d2-9a55-3b01091c2fc2.title: productivity
9d79e40f-511b-48d2-9a55-3b01091c2fc2.description: The amount of biomass or living plant material produced through photosynthesis that influences ecosystems and food chain dynamics.

5bfea59a-54ef-4309-8d46-83144947114b.title: insolation
5bfea59a-54ef-4309-8d46-83144947114b.description: The amount of solar energy reaching the Earth over a specific period, influenced by the planet’s tilt, orbit and atmospheric scattering and absorption.

9314c8fd-1f53-4525-b3dc-66ca6c26e851.title: ecological
9314c8fd-1f53-4525-b3dc-66ca6c26e851.description: Relating to the interactions between living organisms and their environment, including how species depend on and affect one another within ecosystems.

08b615ee-f77b-4cf2-8ad9-8c137e788cfd.title: weathering
08b615ee-f77b-4cf2-8ad9-8c137e788cfd.description: The breaking down of rock and surface materials that have been exposed to the natural processes of weather, chemical reactions, and actions of plants and animals.

ceaca514-01a4-4ec1-bd86-bb62c7029dfd.title: global air circulation
ceaca514-01a4-4ec1-bd86-bb62c7029dfd.description: The large-scale movement of air that redistributes heat and moisture around the Earth, forming wind belts, pressure zones and influencing climate patterns.

d84db9c3-08ab-4382-8bb7-fe0708927d03.title: pressure patterns
d84db9c3-08ab-4382-8bb7-fe0708927d03.description: The distribution and movement of high-pressure and low-pressure systems on a weather map.

a5290dcc-dc8f-41d9-96b5-800fd650bb56.title: tectonic plate
a5290dcc-dc8f-41d9-96b5-800fd650bb56.description: A massive, irregularly shaped slab of solid rock, generally composed of both continental and oceanic lithosphere (also called ‘lithospheric plate’).

829ce8f6-f31f-4b19-a836-555ab0125334.title: temporal scale
829ce8f6-f31f-4b19-a836-555ab0125334.description: The timeframe over which a geographical process, pattern or event occurs ranging from short-term to long-term.

213df7d3-03b4-4572-bed7-70b4556fe5bd.title: erosion
213df7d3-03b4-4572-bed7-70b4556fe5bd.description: The process by which soil, rocks and other surface materials are carried away, by the actions of water, wind or ice.

053906c3-84d0-4e07-bc68-de9686db39e8.title: deposition
053906c3-84d0-4e07-bc68-de9686db39e8.description: The process by which eroded materials are laid down in a new location.

ba8f4740-87b6-487e-9a12-295c3652a1c6.title: environmental stewardship
ba8f4740-87b6-487e-9a12-295c3652a1c6.description: Caring for the environment in a responsible and respectful way so that it remains healthy for future generations. In Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Cultures, environmental stewardship is guided by Cultural connections to Country and Place, where caring for the environment also means caring for Community.

06710481-9ba6-4071-8ca9-4b8b21bfc9d2.title: navigational rights
06710481-9ba6-4071-8ca9-4b8b21bfc9d2.description: Legal freedoms under international law that allow ships to pass through oceans, such as territorial seas, straits and exclusive economic zones.

e4913be1-b683-4f0b-9efd-57c9cb64073d.title: maritime boundaries
e4913be1-b683-4f0b-9efd-57c9cb64073d.description: Divisions of maritime space where different countries have rights to use and control the water, seabed and natural resources.

21ff894c-0e3d-4e5b-9e40-e859210e685f.title: tactile graphics and models
21ff894c-0e3d-4e5b-9e40-e859210e685f.description: Diagrams and 3D representations produced with raised lines, shapes and textured surfaces that can be explored visually and/or tactually.

be54f481-081c-4874-a257-b347a9c8f472.title: Cultural mapping
be54f481-081c-4874-a257-b347a9c8f472.description: Creating a record of a landscape that is alive with activity, including Culture, Lore, language and ethics.

f133cea1-de75-4497-b72d-4053d2af12c7.title: Oral histories
f133cea1-de75-4497-b72d-4053d2af12c7.description:
An account of the past shared through Oral traditions such as song and story.

See Oral traditions

f283203e-846c-48b4-b0c9-394b050e839e.title: field sketches
f283203e-846c-48b4-b0c9-394b050e839e.description: A type of visual representation created during fieldwork activities used to record the main geographical features observed.

afc7e073-e2b0-40d6-be39-6d99fe33c670.title: line drawings
afc7e073-e2b0-40d6-be39-6d99fe33c670.description: A type of black-and-white illustration that uses lines to represent the main features of a geographical area without detailed shading or colour.

92546cca-7b9c-47ce-b3e4-6088b5d0fd4d.title: photo sketches
92546cca-7b9c-47ce-b3e4-6088b5d0fd4d.description: A type of sketch based on a photograph used to highlight key features or elements of the landscape or area of study.

ed909186-c985-4a3b-8591-000115866a0b.title: large-scale maps
ed909186-c985-4a3b-8591-000115866a0b.description: A map that covers a small area with a comprehensive amount of detail.

065a66dc-e18e-408c-a8ce-c017f41b90ff.title: small-scale maps
065a66dc-e18e-408c-a8ce-c017f41b90ff.description: A map that covers a large area with limited amount of detail.

04cfc4dd-2d82-4d37-87d7-0cf811b32008.title: special-purpose maps
04cfc4dd-2d82-4d37-87d7-0cf811b32008.description: A map designed to be used for a particular purpose or by a group of users.

b2148454-d91b-4307-93cb-11f9a3c04f8f.title: physical maps
b2148454-d91b-4307-93cb-11f9a3c04f8f.description: A map that displays natural features of the Earth’s surface.

024bbb52-5caa-4301-a814-ad6edc04aca8.title: political maps
024bbb52-5caa-4301-a814-ad6edc04aca8.description: A map displaying the boundaries of countries, states and cities, and which highlights political divisions.

e2607f07-b52d-45d8-b88c-aa78f38abb71.title: topographic maps
e2607f07-b52d-45d8-b88c-aa78f38abb71.description: A detailed, large-scale map of part of the Earth’s surface which illustrates the shape of the land and selected natural and human features.

6b001073-0ae2-4bb7-aae3-d022b1353ec8.title: thematic maps
6b001073-0ae2-4bb7-aae3-d022b1353ec8.description: Maps that feature one theme or topic and that use colour, shading, dots, symbols or lines joining places of equal value, e.g. a choropleth map or isoline map.

ec8b7ae8-8dcb-450b-8521-013e87819678.title: cartogram maps
ec8b7ae8-8dcb-450b-8521-013e87819678.description: A map in which the size of the countries are adjusted to illustrate the distribution of a feature or statistic.

44e3d20d-039d-41d8-8076-0bb2ee0b1c33.title: weather map or synoptic chart
44e3d20d-039d-41d8-8076-0bb2ee0b1c33.description: A map showing atmospheric conditions at the Earth’s surface at a point in time.

66336aff-2e5b-4485-94de-886c3951a44c.title: sector graphs
66336aff-2e5b-4485-94de-886c3951a44c.description: A graph that divides a circle into segments or sectors, each representing a portion of a whole.

366fccad-f565-4731-ae7a-935fb1e791f5.title: population profiles
366fccad-f565-4731-ae7a-935fb1e791f5.description: A graph showing the age and gender composition of a population.

9c90e8c4-9260-4205-a0d8-846b7d85ab38.title: bubble charts
9c90e8c4-9260-4205-a0d8-846b7d85ab38.description: Type of graph that displays data points as bubbles on a 2-dimensional axis. The size, colour and position of a bubble can represent different variables.

cad0c45c-6a91-42a8-af36-bf87e36c4911.title: virtual or digital map
cad0c45c-6a91-42a8-af36-bf87e36c4911.description: Maps that are interactive and can include zooming, panning, layering and search functionality.

c4de5ac5-5b70-46ac-91bf-76872ba57fa2.title: remote sensing data
c4de5ac5-5b70-46ac-91bf-76872ba57fa2.description: Information collected from satellites or aircraft about Earth’s geographical features from a distance.

dd2d84b3-e2d4-4de6-8816-eefaea20e3d7.title: fieldwork transects
dd2d84b3-e2d4-4de6-8816-eefaea20e3d7.description: A straight measured line between 2 points along which environmental features are observed and recorded. Often measured with a tape measure or rope.

0bc4ebc7-7ec0-4e3d-ad6b-543318de4d48.title: global positioning systems (GPS)
0bc4ebc7-7ec0-4e3d-ad6b-543318de4d48.description: Navigation systems that provide location and time information when there is a line of sight to GPS satellites.

442cfa7a-b458-4587-85a0-51d5444eb2fa.title: relief maps
442cfa7a-b458-4587-85a0-51d5444eb2fa.description: A 3-dimensional map showing the shape of the land and distinctive landforms (terrain) or a 2-dimensional map representing 3D terrain.

45357931-2a93-4d01-ac02-8d907a545ad3.title: sketch maps
45357931-2a93-4d01-ac02-8d907a545ad3.description: A simplified map or illustration outlining the main geographical features of an area.

0df41632-1f5e-40ad-9038-f7e46e3aff2a.title: précis maps
0df41632-1f5e-40ad-9038-f7e46e3aff2a.description: A simple sketch map, drawn from a topographic map or photograph, showing the key patterns and features of an area by omitting minor details.

69191dd6-9abc-40c4-bd54-a8bd09977f1d.title: land use maps
69191dd6-9abc-40c4-bd54-a8bd09977f1d.description: A map showing how land is used, e.g. for infrastructure, settlements or agriculture.

02b6026c-0467-43ce-b560-7fe18a944089.title: isoline maps
02b6026c-0467-43ce-b560-7fe18a944089.description: A thematic map which has lines joining places that have the same value of any selected element, e.g. rainfall, temperature or ocean depth.

250dd48a-77b8-4556-a785-f9e7e0bf51a4.title: dot maps
250dd48a-77b8-4556-a785-f9e7e0bf51a4.description: A thematic map that uses dots to mark locations where a phenomenon occurs.

79d46b94-9367-465d-8913-0fe133f1003d.title: flowline maps
79d46b94-9367-465d-8913-0fe133f1003d.description: Map showing the flows of people, goods, information or ideas between places.

ff0e8184-31f5-45e1-9a74-a07da0a8c06a.title: latitude and longitude
ff0e8184-31f5-45e1-9a74-a07da0a8c06a.description: Lines on a map used to find broad locations in degrees or precise locations in degrees and minutes, north/south of the equator and east/west of the Greenwich meridian.

e3dfd32f-fce2-4cc8-b899-8f6dc8411fec.title: contour lines
e3dfd32f-fce2-4cc8-b899-8f6dc8411fec.description: Lines on a map that indicate altitude.

1677dd7e-c594-4974-93bc-7691aa3cab0f.title: density
1677dd7e-c594-4974-93bc-7691aa3cab0f.description: A measure of how tightly packed the particles in a substance are. Density is calculated by dividing the mass of the substance by its volume (measured as grams per centimetre cubed, or g/cm3).

ffc6a985-43c8-45c8-a019-aa663d59f21b.title: cross-section
ffc6a985-43c8-45c8-a019-aa663d59f21b.description: The intersection of a solid with a plane. May differ for a given solid depending on the orientation of the slicing plane. For example, the cross-section of a sphere will be a circle (of different radius depending on the slicing plane), while the cross-section of a cube could be a square or other polygon (e.g. triangle, hexagon) depending on the orientation of the slicing plane.

ed5a4e7b-b029-4cbd-a065-77d03b74c28c.title: physical features (on a map)
ed5a4e7b-b029-4cbd-a065-77d03b74c28c.description: Physical or natural features located in an environment.

9eefc76b-704e-4f0c-91fb-eb6d800bea13.title: propagation
9eefc76b-704e-4f0c-91fb-eb6d800bea13.description: The process of breeding and growing new plants or animals.

55d95891-7c5b-4c23-82d5-062857286c57.title: species
55d95891-7c5b-4c23-82d5-062857286c57.description: A single, specific type of living organism.

62036f62-d48c-42b2-9851-c302cce60c85.title: Agtech
62036f62-d48c-42b2-9851-c302cce60c85.description: The collective term for innovation in agricultural practice through new and improved tools, technologies and processes, including devices, networks, sensors, robotics, automation and artificial intelligence.

c72c1666-5bef-4928-9088-ae906cccfb1f.title: biosecurity
c72c1666-5bef-4928-9088-ae906cccfb1f.description: Measures taken to prevent the spread of disease to plants or animals in a specific region.

4f4d3aa9-1c61-42d7-af71-bfacdb7a337d.title: intensive (production system)
4f4d3aa9-1c61-42d7-af71-bfacdb7a337d.description: Agricultural production using small areas of land or spaces. Carrying capacity and crop capability require greater inputs, including labour and resources, to increase income and yield.

f5c861ef-def8-4a38-8716-959ffa36907e.title: dramatic journey
f5c861ef-def8-4a38-8716-959ffa36907e.description: The way an audience, character or narrative changes through a work or experience.

40e18cb5-a25f-4c24-b087-35bf721cde8c.title: dramatic processes
40e18cb5-a25f-4c24-b087-35bf721cde8c.description: The ways in which dramatic practitioners shape meaning and experiences.

4c75ecc5-0c93-44ed-9918-8badff01b95a.title: structure
4c75ecc5-0c93-44ed-9918-8badff01b95a.description: Part of the forming process in composition and choreography. There are 2 main parts; organising the movement; and organising the dance.

23424aa8-a482-48df-99fe-8f26c91d127d.title: audience engagement
23424aa8-a482-48df-99fe-8f26c91d127d.description: The level and type of audience response developed in relation to intention and context.

61cd4336-2d93-4d81-95aa-5bd8c97ab400.title: directorial concept
61cd4336-2d93-4d81-95aa-5bd8c97ab400.description: The central idea or interpretation that shapes how a dramatic work is structured, staged or performed.

cefea35d-f27e-4203-9250-922a16029f8e.title: proxemics
cefea35d-f27e-4203-9250-922a16029f8e.description: The conscious use of space between actors, objects and the stage to indicate relationships, emotion and meaning.

86f1b390-d1c4-4f18-8c7d-6e9f155f5857.title: making
86f1b390-d1c4-4f18-8c7d-6e9f155f5857.description: The ways in which makers create dramatic works, including their roles, responsibilities and approaches.

5f351d62-92a7-40ce-9344-e250bdd18e15.title: aesthetic style
5f351d62-92a7-40ce-9344-e250bdd18e15.description: The visual or sensory qualities of a performance communicated though set, costume, sound, lighting and other design or performance choices.

078ce808-6fc2-47f2-8fd1-ad3376c87466.title: directorial vision
078ce808-6fc2-47f2-8fd1-ad3376c87466.description: The director’s artistic perspective that guides the style, mood and overall audience experience of a performance.

63edce94-a074-4a6d-af98-cb066ad695f2.title: craft
63edce94-a074-4a6d-af98-cb066ad695f2.description: To create and shape a dramatic work using skills and intention.

064243b0-e4d3-4888-8bee-8db79586941e.title: anatomical structure
064243b0-e4d3-4888-8bee-8db79586941e.description: A specific identifiable part of the human body, such as the spinal cord, muscle tissue or skeletal system.

fcc3ce0d-7205-45f0-81d1-8de0badbfb22.title: accompaniment
fcc3ce0d-7205-45f0-81d1-8de0badbfb22.description: The choreographer’s use of music, sounds, silence, vocalisations, the spoken word, percussion and body percussion as stimulus, or to accompany dance works to support the intent.

e22458a4-c3fc-4b26-8d9c-288af575f3fb.title: auditory elements
e22458a4-c3fc-4b26-8d9c-288af575f3fb.description: The auditory components of an accompaniment that include structure, temporal, dynamic and musical qualities, thematic material and lyrics.

24a63728-5acb-4811-b343-e03802449444.title: musicality
24a63728-5acb-4811-b343-e03802449444.description: The attention and sensitivity to the musical elements of dance while creating or performing.

54d3cbbb-207a-4403-ae10-b637b1e5a257.title: dancers
54d3cbbb-207a-4403-ae10-b637b1e5a257.description: In the Appreciation focus area ‘dancers’ refers to the person/ people dancing, their number, role, arrangement and contribution to the dance work.

cf9d661f-52e0-45d8-8f81-ba3c3fe2ca97.title: abstract symbolic movement
cf9d661f-52e0-45d8-8f81-ba3c3fe2ca97.description: Shapes, motifs and phrases created by a choreographer to represent ideas, emotions and intent through symbols.

72a2182f-87c8-470b-a895-6e8d4d132d46.title: sequencing
72a2182f-87c8-470b-a895-6e8d4d132d46.description: The ordering of movements and structural devices in a dance work to effectively communicate the intent.

7b3439cd-f002-49b6-a485-4f738c74f22c.title: repetition
7b3439cd-f002-49b6-a485-4f738c74f22c.description: A choreographic device where thematically significant motifs and/or phrases are repeated to reinforce their importance in the effective communication of the intent.

04f69b4e-5a9b-4f02-9c71-d3c6e449d82f.title: variation
04f69b4e-5a9b-4f02-9c71-d3c6e449d82f.description: A choreographic device for generating new movement based on the manipulation of existing movement.

027d03aa-afc4-47db-aee4-3f615e0bc4d0.title: contrast
027d03aa-afc4-47db-aee4-3f615e0bc4d0.description: Show how things are different or opposite.

a4c96c64-0852-4822-b4ac-3a3182992b43.title: components of performance
a4c96c64-0852-4822-b4ac-3a3182992b43.description: Includes dance technique, kinaesthetic awareness, elements of dance, auditory elements, structure and interpretation.

81f4bcf0-d194-48b7-bf0a-dd6131a675c4.title: components of choreography
81f4bcf0-d194-48b7-bf0a-dd6131a675c4.description: Includes stimulus, idea, intent, elements of dance, auditory elements, abstract symbolic movement and structure.

b136ddc5-fc32-48e4-b2c0-1d2c72a0892f.title: components of appreciation
b136ddc5-fc32-48e4-b2c0-1d2c72a0892f.description: Includes stimulus, idea, intent, elements of dance, auditory elements, abstract symbolic movement, structure, dancers and theatrical elements.

7ab54f6f-8e13-42a0-a179-4f0a1a6b2a6b.title: adaptive radiation
7ab54f6f-8e13-42a0-a179-4f0a1a6b2a6b.description: The rapid evolutionary diversification of a single ancestral line into species which evolve different morphological features (adaptations) in response to different environmental selection pressures.

91f93900-6096-4b73-b754-536ecd7e92a7.title: biosphere
91f93900-6096-4b73-b754-536ecd7e92a7.description: The part of the earth that includes all plant and animal life forms.

108257f7-ac1e-41e3-b5d1-995a25e54cde.title: hydrosphere
108257f7-ac1e-41e3-b5d1-995a25e54cde.description: All water on the surface of the globe, including underground water and water in lakes, rivers and oceans.

a0efc551-1c95-46ac-bd73-ce5277430d8b.title: geosphere
a0efc551-1c95-46ac-bd73-ce5277430d8b.description: The solid parts of the Earth, encompassing the crust, mantle, and core.

d280f39c-c388-4cff-ae23-c15f56c874e2.title: uniformitarianism
d280f39c-c388-4cff-ae23-c15f56c874e2.description: The theory that the geological processes observed on Earth today (such as erosion, sedimentation, and volcanic activity) have operated in the same way throughout Earth’s history.

44786f7a-a207-4c27-8223-773217bab314.title: event conjunctions
44786f7a-a207-4c27-8223-773217bab314.description: The simultaneous occurrence of multiple geophysical or environmental events, related or independent, that combined, produce greater environmental impacts than each would alone.

450aa2c9-1b98-4d07-b8b3-9d846e4e0aa6.title: index fossils
450aa2c9-1b98-4d07-b8b3-9d846e4e0aa6.description: Fossils of organisms that were abundant, widespread, and existed for a short geological timeframe, making them useful for dating and correlating rock layers.

93eed0c5-8f76-4d29-81b7-a1e4bb3e5983.title: banded iron formation (BIF)
93eed0c5-8f76-4d29-81b7-a1e4bb3e5983.description: A distinctive formation found in sedimentary rocks made of alternating layers of iron-rich minerals and silica-rich minerals.

225c07f8-6645-49b4-bc71-47937795471d.title: absolute dating
225c07f8-6645-49b4-bc71-47937795471d.description: The process of establishing an actual date, or date range, in numbers of years of a geological sample usually using radiometric methods.

d6abcf1b-199b-46c5-ac13-6d7d58dedd51.title: relative dating
d6abcf1b-199b-46c5-ac13-6d7d58dedd51.description: Determines the age order of rocks, fossils, or geological events by comparing their positions or relationships, to determine which are older or younger without knowing their exact age in years.

c2e89ac0-cb73-440d-b24f-638e9559b676.title: stratigraphic dating
c2e89ac0-cb73-440d-b24f-638e9559b676.description: A method for determining the relative age of rock layers and fossils by examining their position within a sequence of strata, using principles like superposition and faunal succession to establish an age order of geological events without knowing their exact age.

b1cacc55-04c6-4236-ba8b-87068211de73.title: Cambrian event
b1cacc55-04c6-4236-ba8b-87068211de73.description: The unparalleled emergence of organisms including most ancestral lineages of present-day animal species at the beginning of the Cambrian period.

c2d279e6-701a-4aa8-a4bd-b9125b23c944.title: conquest of land
c2d279e6-701a-4aa8-a4bd-b9125b23c944.description: The evolutionary transition of plants and animals from aquatic to terrestrial environments over hundreds of millions of years.

b872a465-3c41-4e3f-9578-b80e8663babe.title: Cambrian metazoans
b872a465-3c41-4e3f-9578-b80e8663babe.description: Complex multicellular animals that lived during the Cambrian period.

d8da84ab-83b3-4861-aa67-1398fc60fcfe.title: original horizontality
d8da84ab-83b3-4861-aa67-1398fc60fcfe.description: The principle which states that layers of sediment are originally deposited in a horizontal or nearly horizontal position.

a6c82e69-6d16-4fb6-be5a-542463a466d5.title: lateral continuity
a6c82e69-6d16-4fb6-be5a-542463a466d5.description: A geological concept that sediment layers originally spread out horizontally in all directions until they gradually thin or reach a boundary, meaning rock layers now separated by erosion or other factors were once connected.

905d9923-5335-40b5-b378-5cf9151b5fd1.title: cross-cutting relationships
905d9923-5335-40b5-b378-5cf9151b5fd1.description: A geological feature, such as a fault, intrusion, or erosion surface that disrupts or intersects another feature must be younger than the feature it alters or cuts across.

d3c6dd92-2d26-4afc-abc3-a77449a27823.title: faunal succession
d3c6dd92-2d26-4afc-abc3-a77449a27823.description: The principle that fossils appear in a consistent, recognisable order through geological layers over time allowing scientists to use fossil assemblages to relative date rock layers across different geographic regions.

840dfdd0-354b-4737-b698-1b47d68a42b7.title: inclusions
840dfdd0-354b-4737-b698-1b47d68a42b7.description: Any rock fragments found within another rock which are older than the rock they are enclosed in.

a12672cf-f9ca-474a-a6e9-0894f7e684f9.title: unconformity
a12672cf-f9ca-474a-a6e9-0894f7e684f9.description: A surface in rock layers that represents a break or gap in the geologic record, caused by erosion or a period without deposition.

7dbf637e-1d6c-44ec-a5cb-44209f0bd5be.title: radioisotope decay
7dbf637e-1d6c-44ec-a5cb-44209f0bd5be.description: The spontaneous decay of an unstable atomic nucleus into a more stable one, releasing energy or particles, and is the fundamental process behind radiometric dating.

4583a65d-d78e-43f1-bb21-00fc12989b97.title: plate tectonic supercycle
4583a65d-d78e-43f1-bb21-00fc12989b97.description: The long-term repeating cycle of supercontinents forming, breaking apart and reassembling due to plate tectonics.

1c264c42-2a71-4432-8fc5-1b8833a72ef8.title: Cultural burning
1c264c42-2a71-4432-8fc5-1b8833a72ef8.description: Cultural burning is a Cultural Practice that draws upon the use of fire by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples to improve the health of Country and Place.

711cd996-ecc8-4031-acde-89bd3d99f916.title: seismic wave
711cd996-ecc8-4031-acde-89bd3d99f916.description: A vibration, typically generated by earthquakes or volcanic eruptions, that carries energy away from the source through the Earth.

cd184a7f-3860-4608-b2d9-4152e7f5c43f.title: effusive eruption
cd184a7f-3860-4608-b2d9-4152e7f5c43f.description: A type of volcanic eruption in which lava steadily flows out of a volcano onto the ground.

3417f0d0-222c-4578-aba7-cb523a4483bf.title: Oral traditions
3417f0d0-222c-4578-aba7-cb523a4483bf.description:
The Customs and beliefs shared through Storytelling and song.

See Oral histories

883c9069-d5b7-496f-a33a-6134474fb438.title: earthquake foci
883c9069-d5b7-496f-a33a-6134474fb438.description: The place inside Earth’s crust where an earthquake originates.

736af2a6-af46-4484-8e66-62ac3a6031bc.title: convergent boundary
736af2a6-af46-4484-8e66-62ac3a6031bc.description: A geographic location where tectonic plates are moving towards one another.

4ae4fe17-1622-43fa-b3e4-387f9a416a05.title: subduction zone
4ae4fe17-1622-43fa-b3e4-387f9a416a05.description: A region of the Earth’s crust where one tectonic plate is forced beneath another.

2084554d-b231-4695-9632-b0d16a63ea75.title: divergent boundary
2084554d-b231-4695-9632-b0d16a63ea75.description: A geographic location where tectonic plates are moving away from one another.

217b9580-ea18-4c92-bb70-a6af0eb6ffc0.title: transform boundary
217b9580-ea18-4c92-bb70-a6af0eb6ffc0.description: A plate boundary where 2 tectonic plates slide horizontally past each other without creating or destroying crust.

911946e5-7a17-4ef2-9a23-a2221ba05c6f.title: pyroclastic flow
911946e5-7a17-4ef2-9a23-a2221ba05c6f.description: A fast-moving current of hot gas, ash, and volcanic rock fragments that flows down the slopes of a volcano during explosive eruptions.

5519fb96-5cc2-4797-be81-5bc8ddd61835.title: lahar
5519fb96-5cc2-4797-be81-5bc8ddd61835.description: A fast-moving volcanic debris flow made of mud and/or volcanic materials, such as ash, pumice and rock fragments, that flows down the slopes of a volcano.

5f5e6c3c-c3f7-4919-bfd6-e1e27bb68222.title: renew/renewable
5f5e6c3c-c3f7-4919-bfd6-e1e27bb68222.description: A resource that cannot be exhausted. A resource that can be restored in a human lifetime.

8ff15862-47ee-4c2d-b5ed-99acd6fa429d.title: non-renewable (resource)
8ff15862-47ee-4c2d-b5ed-99acd6fa429d.description: A resource that becomes depleted or takes longer than a human life span to be restored.

52e64cc6-4ac2-4dda-882e-d8b7f9c15461.title: problem waste
52e64cc6-4ac2-4dda-882e-d8b7f9c15461.description: A product that is hazardous, difficult to recycle, or harmful to the environment and human health and which requires special handling as it cannot be disposed of in regular landfill.

21354ccd-084e-4767-bb80-091d075b2a67.title: critical minerals
21354ccd-084e-4767-bb80-091d075b2a67.description: An element which plays a vital role in the operation of modern technologies, economic systems or national security and whose supply chain is vulnerable to potential disruptions.

d27dc857-57f2-4cca-8501-64ce720cfdc8.title: sustainable
d27dc857-57f2-4cca-8501-64ce720cfdc8.description: Supporting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to support their needs.

095abc06-f7cb-4169-b6bf-d8587c38e28e.title: non-renewable energy economy
