095abc06-f7cb-4169-b6bf-d8587c38e28e.description: An economic system that relies primarily on finite energy sources.

eec66a3b-3a45-4049-9164-3640b1a712fb.title: dispatchability
eec66a3b-3a45-4049-9164-3640b1a712fb.description: A measure of how quickly and predictably a power plant or energy source can activated to maintain grid stability and meet both peak and off-peak demand efficiently.

1a005a5b-4f88-44b8-a632-550f692f8933.title: photovoltaic
1a005a5b-4f88-44b8-a632-550f692f8933.description: Providing electric current using electromagnetic radiation from the Sun.

58576538-d350-485c-a7ae-48f26c0666dc.title: feedback loops
58576538-d350-485c-a7ae-48f26c0666dc.description: Feedback loops are reactions in response to environmental change. Positive feedback loops cause one or more components to increase overall, creating a negative impact on the ecosystem. A negative feedback loop has a positive impact on the ecosystem because it decreases the impact of change, bringing it closer to dynamic equilibrium.

899aa5b8-941b-48cb-972f-f853b8a47487.title: dendrochronology
899aa5b8-941b-48cb-972f-f853b8a47487.description: A scientific method used to study Earth’s past climate by analysing growth rings in trees which vary in width, density and structure depending on environmental conditions.

ff3a8929-3fd4-41a4-9acd-2864acdc3f0a.title: global warming potential (GWP)
ff3a8929-3fd4-41a4-9acd-2864acdc3f0a.description: A measure of a greenhouse gas’s heat-trapping ability compared to carbon dioxide (assigned a value of 1).

036f2b10-a415-439a-80c3-a6a8009b28c0.title: carbon footprint
036f2b10-a415-439a-80c3-a6a8009b28c0.description: The total amount of greenhouse gases, primarily carbon dioxide for which humans and/or organisations are responsible for.

66a2ee14-3464-4f7f-908f-20f117ce7b06.title: greenhouse gases
66a2ee14-3464-4f7f-908f-20f117ce7b06.description: Gases found in the atmosphere that let sunlight in but prevent some heat from escaping back into space.

4854334c-1cf6-460c-a873-c69c2d38e40f.title: isotope ratio
4854334c-1cf6-460c-a873-c69c2d38e40f.description: The quantitative relationship between 2 isotopes of the same element, typically expressed as a ratio.

aac7a9e7-cc77-4a2b-9e2b-0dc641400e73.title: proxy data
aac7a9e7-cc77-4a2b-9e2b-0dc641400e73.description: Indirect evidence from natural recorders, or ‘proxies’, used to reconstruct past climates and environmental conditions before direct measurements existed.

e005d319-69ce-4450-946f-3fac9b754b58.title: thermohaline circulation
e005d319-69ce-4450-946f-3fac9b754b58.description: The global ocean circulation driven by differences in water temperature and salinity which affect water density and help regulate Earth’s climate.

4289a391-f972-4c8a-8545-f7faa9b7768c.title: orbital eccentricity
4289a391-f972-4c8a-8545-f7faa9b7768c.description: The degree of elongation of a planet’s elliptical orbit around the Sun, ranging from 0 (circular) to 1 (highly elliptical).

f675649d-7dc9-4f34-b1fc-63b3b5d4a8c1.title: orbital obliquity
f675649d-7dc9-4f34-b1fc-63b3b5d4a8c1.description: The angle between Earth’s rotational axis and a line perpendicular to the orbital plane.

0a3bca3c-2e30-4381-877d-ae6812e243e2.title: orbital precession
0a3bca3c-2e30-4381-877d-ae6812e243e2.description: A cyclical change in the orientation of the Earth’s rotational axis causing it to trace a cone-shaped path over time, resulting in a gradual wobble of its axis.

3b1ee733-1a80-4709-9c4c-1d98594403fa.title: icehouse climate
3b1ee733-1a80-4709-9c4c-1d98594403fa.description: A long-term period in Earth’s history when global temperatures are relatively low and polar ice sheets and glaciers are extensive or permanent.

1b027c9a-30d7-4afe-bcc2-baa94ff3c5a4.title: pollen microfossils
1b027c9a-30d7-4afe-bcc2-baa94ff3c5a4.description: Microscopic fossilised pollen grains and spores from plants.

67bea327-887a-4db1-934f-64866af00609.title: El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO)
67bea327-887a-4db1-934f-64866af00609.description: A natural climate pattern marked by variations in sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, along with associated changes in atmospheric pressure and wind patterns.

b41c32d8-5b1c-497c-acc8-446585fdd912.title: albedo (surface)
b41c32d8-5b1c-497c-acc8-446585fdd912.description: The proportion of incoming solar radiation that snow and ice reflect from Earth back into space.

de916655-4a54-4b85-bbd6-19184966a664.title: custodians
de916655-4a54-4b85-bbd6-19184966a664.description: In Aboriginal communities, an individual charged with maintaining and passing on particular elements of cultural significance, eg language, stories, songs, rituals and imagery.

bce946b9-f3f5-487c-92fa-a9de43ba7d6d.title: cementation
bce946b9-f3f5-487c-92fa-a9de43ba7d6d.description: A process in which sediment is chemically bonded together when minerals precipitate from the water they are dissolved in and fill the pore space between compressed sediment.

1a0e6bf3-9c87-46aa-a5cf-3b9d815609b1.title: clastic
1a0e6bf3-9c87-46aa-a5cf-3b9d815609b1.description: Describes rocks composed of fragments of pre-existing rocks.

97fc6c30-987a-4505-a49b-a8e0b2482577.title: non-clastic sedimentary rocks
97fc6c30-987a-4505-a49b-a8e0b2482577.description: Rocks formed by chemical precipitation or biological accumulation, not from fragments (clasts) of pre-existing rocks.

5360e517-db6a-4a93-8401-6b262dc350ad.title: extrusive igneous rocks
5360e517-db6a-4a93-8401-6b262dc350ad.description: Rocks that form when lava rapidly cools on the Earth’s surface resulting in fine-grained or glassy textures with microscopic crystals. Also known as volcanic rocks.

d1aa4371-a6a7-4b5f-a471-fb47a6eda347.title: renewable energy economy
d1aa4371-a6a7-4b5f-a471-fb47a6eda347.description: An economic system primarily powered by renewable energy sources such as hydroelectric, solar and wind farms.

8d552237-34bf-4e43-8978-6523aa77599b.title: igneous (rock)
8d552237-34bf-4e43-8978-6523aa77599b.description: Rock formed from magma, either erupted from a volcano or cooled below ground in an intrusion.

61ba9243-300a-482a-a857-fb81f299a410.title: metamorphic (rock)
61ba9243-300a-482a-a857-fb81f299a410.description: Describes a type of rock that has been changed from its original form by heat and/or pressure.

ea7a3f38-a414-4792-8e17-8f3ad68d06da.title: mafic
ea7a3f38-a414-4792-8e17-8f3ad68d06da.description: Describes igneous rocks or minerals rich in magnesium and iron, typically dark-coloured and denser than felsic rocks.

370e8415-5734-4fc3-b4a6-c40e49ed014d.title: felsic
370e8415-5734-4fc3-b4a6-c40e49ed014d.description: A group of light-coloured rocks or minerals rich in silica, low in density, high in viscosity when molten, and common in continental crust.

2f2550a0-de04-4f6e-a489-5b922214a66c.title: soil salinity
2f2550a0-de04-4f6e-a489-5b922214a66c.description: The presence of dissolved salts in soil that occur naturally (primary) or as a result of human activities (secondary).

22a9578b-13ff-4c8b-998b-e904a93622b6.title: introduced species
22a9578b-13ff-4c8b-998b-e904a93622b6.description: Organisms that have been intentionally or accidentally moved by humans from their natural habitat to a new location.

07f8e916-9da4-4572-8ea7-4cd078e2f7ee.title: soil profile
07f8e916-9da4-4572-8ea7-4cd078e2f7ee.description: A vertical cross-section of soil that shows its layers (horizons) and reveals information about the composition, structure and formation of the soil over time.

aee9ce07-21ad-4f57-8ed9-c0ac4fa62ee6.title: water cycle
aee9ce07-21ad-4f57-8ed9-c0ac4fa62ee6.description: The biogeochemical cycle that involves the continuous movement of water on, above and below the surface of the Earth across different reservoirs.

c1d33228-6ff6-4ba4-8c81-48fb9584e033.title: seafloor spreading
c1d33228-6ff6-4ba4-8c81-48fb9584e033.description: The process by which new oceanic crust is formed at mid-ocean ridges and slowly moves away from the ridge, causing the ocean floor to spread.

7f958ed7-4303-4015-b73c-3e131cda51f1.title: mid-ocean ridges
7f958ed7-4303-4015-b73c-3e131cda51f1.description: Submarine mountain ranges or mountain ranges on the sea bed at divergent plate boundaries where spreading tectonic plates allow molten rock to rise, creating new ocean floor and basaltic mountain-forming eruptions.

017aeb60-0b8f-47f6-9345-0c92b6c9965e.title: asthenosphere
017aeb60-0b8f-47f6-9345-0c92b6c9965e.description: The layer underneath the lithosphere, extending between 80 to 150 km. It’s low-density and plastic.

c5ccab87-5ccf-4a58-9b79-bc3891bdc344.title: lithosphere
c5ccab87-5ccf-4a58-9b79-bc3891bdc344.description: The crust or solid part of the earth comprising the continental crust, oceanic crust and the brittle part of the upper mantle.

844a7739-b6dd-4330-9795-a3a58029e7f0.title: outer core
844a7739-b6dd-4330-9795-a3a58029e7f0.description: The liquid layer of the Earth located between the mantle and the inner core.

09dff256-741d-4f0d-8220-c78b87556fa0.title: inner core
09dff256-741d-4f0d-8220-c78b87556fa0.description: The solid centre of the Earth, which is its hottest and densest layer, made mainly of iron and nickel.

c7e7d1bd-9115-4249-a03b-656c203dd977.title: normal faults
c7e7d1bd-9115-4249-a03b-656c203dd977.description: Fractures in the Earth’s crust where one block (the hanging wall) moves downward relative to the other block (the footwall), due to tectonic tension.

1f3765f0-7449-4d92-8848-4b8b1400060a.title: reverse fault
1f3765f0-7449-4d92-8848-4b8b1400060a.description: A fracture in the Earth’s crust in which one block (the hanging wall) moves up and over the other block (the footwall) as a result of tectonic compression.

36deaf98-2589-4df3-8c69-66f800b53167.title: strike-slip faults
36deaf98-2589-4df3-8c69-66f800b53167.description: A type of fracture in the Earth’s crust where the dominant movement is horizontal and parallel to the fault line, rather than vertical.

72a087d1-85aa-4e1c-9499-6dbcdd219660.title: fold belt
72a087d1-85aa-4e1c-9499-6dbcdd219660.description: A large geological region where crustal compression at convergent plate boundaries creates deformed and folded rock layers.

b9bb086a-b753-4e0f-bda8-add0c3b129a9.title: thrust belt
b9bb086a-b753-4e0f-bda8-add0c3b129a9.description: A region of the Earth’s crust where rock layers are folded and pushed over each other along thrust faults by compressional forces.

65c2c8f9-4d4c-41d4-9203-baf54e4e833f.title: volcanic arc
65c2c8f9-4d4c-41d4-9203-baf54e4e833f.description: A curved chain of volcanoes that have formed above a subduction zone.

d8bb63f1-cefe-48dd-a3fa-162751c64baa.title: mantle
d8bb63f1-cefe-48dd-a3fa-162751c64baa.description: The layer of the Earth located between the crust and the outer core.

ad2b1fa4-776f-45ae-8e3e-0b018d044e30.title: slab pull
ad2b1fa4-776f-45ae-8e3e-0b018d044e30.description: A tectonic force in which a dense, sinking oceanic plate drags the rest of the plate into the mantle, which is a major driver of plate tectonics.

a8c1aecc-4e2d-4135-86d1-b1664ef7019c.title: ridge push
a8c1aecc-4e2d-4135-86d1-b1664ef7019c.description: The gravitational force exerted by the elevated mid-ocean ridge, causing the oceanic tectonic plates to slide away from the ridge towards lower elevation areas.

4db73455-4a2b-48d4-8d91-0ae67f55e478.title: basal drag
4db73455-4a2b-48d4-8d91-0ae67f55e478.description: The friction between convection currents in the asthenosphere and ridged overlying lithosphere which affect plate movement.

4d4e866b-ecb0-415e-8c82-7b1334ba7b99.title: relate
4d4e866b-ecb0-415e-8c82-7b1334ba7b99.description: To establish a connection or association between 2 or more things, often by identifying similarities, connections or shared characteristics.

316b9444-31ed-4da8-9f2f-ee66766aa254.title: data science
316b9444-31ed-4da8-9f2f-ee66766aa254.description: A field of study which involves collecting, analysing and interpreting large amounts of data to gain insights and make decisions.

3fb174ed-38c8-49e8-9a7a-3b08b9b747db.title: statistics
3fb174ed-38c8-49e8-9a7a-3b08b9b747db.description: A collection of numerical facts or other data.

fc48de01-4f9f-46eb-b1e2-8f5e96f336b0.title: phenomenon
fc48de01-4f9f-46eb-b1e2-8f5e96f336b0.description: An observable event or process that occurs in the natural world, such as weather patterns, geological events, astronomical events or biological processes.

fc5c766c-9bc3-424b-885d-68b72eeffb78.title: large dataset
fc5c766c-9bc3-424b-885d-68b72eeffb78.description: A dataset that must be of a size to be statistically reliable and require computational analysis to reveal patterns, trends and associations.

871cb253-20cd-4994-aaf3-816d7a39ca87.title: univariate
871cb253-20cd-4994-aaf3-816d7a39ca87.description: An analysis, study, or dataset that involves only one variable.

a551e062-0238-4ee9-b405-53a2d7a0b64e.title: bivariate analysis
a551e062-0238-4ee9-b405-53a2d7a0b64e.description: A type of statistical analysis involving 2 variables which aims to explain how changes in one variable affect the other.

853413a5-d82e-45f3-843d-c367c5e217e5.title: theory
853413a5-d82e-45f3-843d-c367c5e217e5.description: A formal explanation, based on evidence and reviewed by the scientific community. Predictions can be tested by comparing actual observations with the theory.

3626d0bb-3b03-4758-b5e5-5d8beaf133e3.title: variable
3626d0bb-3b03-4758-b5e5-5d8beaf133e3.description: A factor that can be changed, kept the same or measured in an investigation.

da44dd28-65df-4663-93b5-d64be851a33f.title: correlational relationship
da44dd28-65df-4663-93b5-d64be851a33f.description: A relationship that measures the strength of interdependence of 2 variables.

51ebd5fa-83bd-4bf4-af84-10216fa51dd2.title: hypothesis
51ebd5fa-83bd-4bf4-af84-10216fa51dd2.description: A supposition or proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation.

fcd4067b-af46-437d-95c9-ecbe335d31b9.title: peer review
fcd4067b-af46-437d-95c9-ecbe335d31b9.description: The process of other experts in a field reading, checking and giving their opinion on someone else’s research.

27380758-85bb-42bc-88d3-2a4ec8e2e19b.title: system
27380758-85bb-42bc-88d3-2a4ec8e2e19b.description: A set of components in the natural and made environments that interact. An understanding of natural complex systems requires the integration and application of concepts from more than one science discipline.

fe45eb54-dd6f-4fe8-863a-695a4a35a8cc.title: descriptive analysis
fe45eb54-dd6f-4fe8-863a-695a4a35a8cc.description: The analysis of statistics that quantitatively describe or summarise features of a collection of information.

d24c431b-0107-42a4-868c-a8791c892b9d.title: senses
d24c431b-0107-42a4-868c-a8791c892b9d.description: Perceptions that a living organism uses to take in information about its surroundings. The 5 main senses are hearing, sight, touch, taste and smell.

998da31c-d5ec-4b73-953e-6e9156d76d1d.title: transdisciplinary
998da31c-d5ec-4b73-953e-6e9156d76d1d.description: The integration of different disciplines with science.

ca6f5961-fd06-499a-9f12-d93a50345291.title: explanation
ca6f5961-fd06-499a-9f12-d93a50345291.description: A scientific explanation provides an account of a phenomenon through descriptive statements about how that phenomenon came to be.

5447cb9f-6c7e-40ed-8f51-1143b4bdd26a.title: law
5447cb9f-6c7e-40ed-8f51-1143b4bdd26a.description: A statement that describes a relationship or phenomena that does not change under the same conditions.

a581328a-f431-4a4d-a7f5-72a2c4f9d375.title: systematic observations
a581328a-f431-4a4d-a7f5-72a2c4f9d375.description: Following a valid scientific method to carry out observations.

2f5186f4-809e-49aa-8021-96b6c698da95.title: xylem
2f5186f4-809e-49aa-8021-96b6c698da95.description: A type of plant tissue responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the rest of the plant.

f5af6bed-b1f1-48db-ab05-7706f06baa40.title: disorder
f5af6bed-b1f1-48db-ab05-7706f06baa40.description: A disturbance of physical, mental or genetic health.

3d3c44d3-cb21-4159-adbb-bdc9f428490f.title: disease
3d3c44d3-cb21-4159-adbb-bdc9f428490f.description: An illness or condition of the body affecting the way an organism, or parts of an organism, or its organs, function.

d254e497-f7d8-43e4-bba3-b4bb5d63852b.title: food web
d254e497-f7d8-43e4-bba3-b4bb5d63852b.description: A series of interconnected food chains that outlines feeding relationships in an ecosystem.

b7afecf6-9cab-4cc2-9db3-2cf2274f6e0d.title: ecological energy pyramid
b7afecf6-9cab-4cc2-9db3-2cf2274f6e0d.description: A graphical representation of the flow of energy through different trophic levels in an ecosystem.

d77338f5-4f3e-4588-8434-2e7544cdfdfe.title: decomposers
d77338f5-4f3e-4588-8434-2e7544cdfdfe.description: Living things such as fungi and bacteria that break down dead organic material.

49f6a8b9-7fd2-474c-bf43-71ac8dedcc75.title: trophic level
49f6a8b9-7fd2-474c-bf43-71ac8dedcc75.description: The hierarchical position of organisms in a food chain or food web based on their feeding relationships and energy transfer.

3d417f2e-ffbc-4a2b-959e-736f509a2c61.title: interactions
3d417f2e-ffbc-4a2b-959e-736f509a2c61.description: Actions or influences between components and within and between systems.

7f6d29fe-dbc7-4764-a650-d10377123049.title: interdependency
7f6d29fe-dbc7-4764-a650-d10377123049.description: The condition of being dependent on each other. The state of being mutually dependent or dependent on each other.

3d0fa834-02bf-4613-a570-d10d9b1827fc.title: endangered (species)
3d0fa834-02bf-4613-a570-d10d9b1827fc.description: Facing a very high risk of extinction in the wild due to rapid population decline or loss of habitat.

aefbafed-b779-4328-ba14-5d2a0e669982.title: extinct
aefbafed-b779-4328-ba14-5d2a0e669982.description: No longer existing because all members of the species have died.

0c079716-4fc5-4187-a99f-064aee307c9b.title: chloroplast
0c079716-4fc5-4187-a99f-064aee307c9b.description: The chlorophyll-containing structures in the cells of plants and algae where photosynthesis occurs.

a9fadaa9-68d2-4aa6-a243-723c21044a2b.title: cellular respiration
a9fadaa9-68d2-4aa6-a243-723c21044a2b.description: The process by which a living organism or cells break down organic molecules to release energy. Cellular respiration can be aerobic (with oxygen) or anaerobic (without oxygen).

f59af6a6-0265-41fc-b3e9-add35d2c9740.title: characteristic
f59af6a6-0265-41fc-b3e9-add35d2c9740.description: A distinguishing aspect (including features and behaviours) of an object, material, living thing or event.

17381326-aff9-4668-a0a0-b81f0d57c488.title: habitat
17381326-aff9-4668-a0a0-b81f0d57c488.description: The place where an animal or plant can live.

22916c0c-7f46-48d9-8d6e-a574e317ddc4.title: adapted
22916c0c-7f46-48d9-8d6e-a574e317ddc4.description: Able to survive and reproduce in a changed environment because of modified physical, behavioural or physiological characteristics.

ac39c245-9173-4b6a-a22c-1f4dc16b7a2a.title: gravity/gravitational
ac39c245-9173-4b6a-a22c-1f4dc16b7a2a.description: The force of attraction that objects with mass exert on each other.

6e51e5b7-6ca4-46c1-9f7e-b044021091d1.title: properties
6e51e5b7-6ca4-46c1-9f7e-b044021091d1.description: Attributes of an object or material normally used to describe attributes common to a group.

4f175234-6528-4032-994f-f90cefca84e9.title: orbit
4f175234-6528-4032-994f-f90cefca84e9.description: Moving in a curved path around a body such as the Earth, an atom or the Sun.

283a1e33-9d11-49fd-bb67-3fa0d7b2e2d0.title: work health and safety (WHS)
283a1e33-9d11-49fd-bb67-3fa0d7b2e2d0.description: The requirements include safe practices in the laboratory and in the field.

9524bea5-d0ce-4298-bedb-1bd876890d64.title: physical quantities
9524bea5-d0ce-4298-bedb-1bd876890d64.description: Characteristics that can be seen or measured.

6a517239-20b9-4661-a809-349dc6cebbdc.title: subatomic
6a517239-20b9-4661-a809-349dc6cebbdc.description: Denoting a particle which is smaller than an atom.

05f6f678-b4d8-4ec8-8443-1d4fb4164578.title: atomic number
05f6f678-b4d8-4ec8-8443-1d4fb4164578.description: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom; used to order the chemical elements in the periodic table.

fa14f97d-553b-4a6a-a194-f788d54a7951.title: compound
fa14f97d-553b-4a6a-a194-f788d54a7951.description: A substance containing 2 or more atoms of different elements bonded together in a fixed ratio.

dde15916-fa28-46ea-9588-87d0e64529fa.title: alloy
dde15916-fa28-46ea-9588-87d0e64529fa.description: A substance composed of 2 or more metals (or, sometimes, a metal and a nonmetal) mixed together.

47152509-9d65-4e57-b0dc-bdb20e60adeb.title: metalloid
47152509-9d65-4e57-b0dc-bdb20e60adeb.description: An element that has properties intermediate between those of metals and nonmetals, such as arsenic, silicon or bismuth.

56395e03-85b5-45e7-bc95-907e700ef961.title: amplitude
56395e03-85b5-45e7-bc95-907e700ef961.description: The maximum value of an alternating quantity measured from its mean or base value.

7318b506-c186-415d-b5e0-086a0a5bb837.title: frequency
7318b506-c186-415d-b5e0-086a0a5bb837.description: The number of times a light, sound or radio wave passes a fixed point in unit time; the SI unit used to measure frequency is the hertz.

1a9b0f1b-d23a-4e98-9c76-d7ca71b76ea1.title: absorption
1a9b0f1b-d23a-4e98-9c76-d7ca71b76ea1.description: The process of the energy of a wave being taken in or assimilated by the medium it travels through, causing a decrease in the wave's intensity.

77fa80f3-3f27-4e9c-91f2-2cb735d6bb20.title: scattering
77fa80f3-3f27-4e9c-91f2-2cb735d6bb20.description: When any beam of radiation, electromagnetic or particle, is dispersed or redirected by particles or objects in its path, causing it to spread out in different directions.

38f94d19-7ab1-47c1-a899-8e1349e56784.title: vector analysis
38f94d19-7ab1-47c1-a899-8e1349e56784.description: The analysis of a quantity which possesses both magnitude and direction. Two such quantities acting on a point may be represented by the 2 sides of a parallelogram, so that their resultant (or sum of vectors) is represented in magnitude and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram.

1a4ca97a-c219-45ef-bf56-8e90180acaa6.title: acceleration
1a4ca97a-c219-45ef-bf56-8e90180acaa6.description: The rate at which velocity changes over time.

80ea7f5b-0221-4873-8d76-9f2bee65ef7f.title: evaporation
80ea7f5b-0221-4873-8d76-9f2bee65ef7f.description: The process by which a liquid, such as water, changes into a gas or vapor state, usually due to an increase in temperature.

8d0a8c25-21e6-43e9-a6b9-d09a29912c97.title: SI
8d0a8c25-21e6-43e9-a6b9-d09a29912c97.description: The International System of Units (SI) is a system of measurement based on agreed standards units, such as metre, second and gram.

735c2fa8-5c56-41a8-9c6e-b1e710f75432.title: solubility
735c2fa8-5c56-41a8-9c6e-b1e710f75432.description: The ability of a solute to dissolve.

ad8a7cdc-e111-481f-b69c-1b02bc2739f0.title: polluted
ad8a7cdc-e111-481f-b69c-1b02bc2739f0.description: Contaminated or made impure by harmful substances.

d4859bc9-14ec-496d-a86a-54497c01720e.title: saturated
d4859bc9-14ec-496d-a86a-54497c01720e.description: A chemical solution which contains the maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in a solution.

43081fc4-b156-4a12-b4f8-c107f35a8377.title: supersaturated
43081fc4-b156-4a12-b4f8-c107f35a8377.description: A chemical solution which contains more than the maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in a solution.

5c609350-7aae-4549-97ae-4d0e7d37ec89.title: density
5c609350-7aae-4549-97ae-4d0e7d37ec89.description: A measure of how tightly packed the particles in a substance are. Density is calculated by dividing the mass of the substance by its volume (measured as grams per centimetre cubed, or g/cm3).

61b517c1-ea17-400d-8b3b-25d40b4602f3.title: buoyancy
61b517c1-ea17-400d-8b3b-25d40b4602f3.description: The tendency of an object to rise upward or float in a fluid.

6776e68f-0a9a-4ea3-b155-1848a6b9eaf8.title: surface tension
6776e68f-0a9a-4ea3-b155-1848a6b9eaf8.description: The effect caused by molecular cohesion that makes a liquid seem as though it has a skin on its surface.

1c8c657c-d400-4c44-adf1-84b320085d2e.title: particle theory
1c8c657c-d400-4c44-adf1-84b320085d2e.description: The kinetic theory of matter that all matter consists of tiny indivisible particles that are constantly moving.

046a22dc-354e-4877-8626-0d85b771531c.title: vaccination
046a22dc-354e-4877-8626-0d85b771531c.description: The process of administering a vaccine with the aim of stimulating the immune system to develop immunity against a specific infectious disease, resulting in protection from future infections.

5763502e-3313-4e37-a085-ddc2d5e46c34.title: feedback loops
5763502e-3313-4e37-a085-ddc2d5e46c34.description: Feedback loops are reactions in response to environmental change. Positive feedback loops cause one or more components to increase overall, creating a negative impact on the ecosystem. A negative feedback loop has a positive impact on the ecosystem because it decreases the impact of change, bringing it closer to dynamic equilibrium.

92e1ed6b-62d0-419c-bf4d-af41f0fd3128.title: infectious (disease)
92e1ed6b-62d0-419c-bf4d-af41f0fd3128.description: Able to be passed from one living thing to another.

22f42b8c-f08f-437d-bdbf-5848faa7b1cf.title: non-infectious (disease)
22f42b8c-f08f-437d-bdbf-5848faa7b1cf.description: A medical condition that cannot be transmitted from one person to another. These diseases are typically caused by genetic factors, lifestyle choices, environmental factors, or a combination of these factors, e.g. heart disease, cancer, and asthma.

76f173f7-0ef3-40a3-aeb2-dcf809816957.title: epidemic
76f173f7-0ef3-40a3-aeb2-dcf809816957.description: A temporary occurrence of a disease which spreads rapidly and extensively within a specific population, community, or region, typically affecting a significantly higher number of individuals than expected.

12d5949e-82c1-4c9c-9484-2671b8587fb2.title: endemic
12d5949e-82c1-4c9c-9484-2671b8587fb2.description: Of a disease, commonly found in a particular community or locality.

7ce18a9d-041c-4faf-b466-875f7b0888f2.title: pandemic
7ce18a9d-041c-4faf-b466-875f7b0888f2.description: A disease prevalent throughout an entire country or continent, or the whole world.

d2a92974-ae1c-401b-ac7a-539affe3ec55.title: boiling (point)
d2a92974-ae1c-401b-ac7a-539affe3ec55.description: The temperature at which the vapour pressure of the liquid equals the pressure surrounding the liquid, and the liquid changes into a vapour.

e96ca59c-fd8e-4625-a145-22990e28c55a.title: conduction
e96ca59c-fd8e-4625-a145-22990e28c55a.description: The transfer of heat or electricity through a substance or between substances that are in direct contact with each other.

fa5f2745-7022-4604-a0ba-ff97abf92a6b.title: convection
fa5f2745-7022-4604-a0ba-ff97abf92a6b.description: The movement of a gas or fluid by the transfer of heat energy through the gas or fluid itself.

8d0f8997-eb45-4b64-b33c-91c5554d5af3.title: radiation
8d0f8997-eb45-4b64-b33c-91c5554d5af3.description:
The emission of energy as electromagnetic waves or as moving subatomic particles.

OR

The energy or particles that are released during radioactive decay.

b36f9e95-d802-4dc9-b0a2-d01e06da45a2.title: potential energy
b36f9e95-d802-4dc9-b0a2-d01e06da45a2.description: The energy that an object possesses due to its position in a force field or that is stored in a system by virtue of the configuration and interaction between bodies in that system, e.g. elastic potential energy.

69aef111-8b75-4314-814a-926a81528ecb.title: kinetic energy (KE)
69aef111-8b75-4314-814a-926a81528ecb.description: The energy that an object possesses by virtue of its motion; the energy an object gains by being in motion.

dfe21332-0c27-450b-bddd-44d7b01219cb.title: thermal
dfe21332-0c27-450b-bddd-44d7b01219cb.description: Properties or phenomena associated with heat, temperature, or the transfer of energy due to temperature differences.

0d4da7c6-183a-467f-834b-7c72900b5e51.title: law of conservation of energy
0d4da7c6-183a-467f-834b-7c72900b5e51.description: States that energy cannot be created or destroyed.

be36ea74-8134-40ed-b17e-8f764aaae999.title: geological processes
be36ea74-8134-40ed-b17e-8f764aaae999.description: Natural phenomena that shape and change the Earth's surface and interior over time. These processes include erosion, weathering, volcanic activity, the movement of tectonic plates, and sedimentation.

f96adaab-58c7-417d-841d-8b5cb8b03f8b.title: radioactive
f96adaab-58c7-417d-841d-8b5cb8b03f8b.description: A substance that emits radiation as its nucleus decays.

4389a131-dc97-44d2-bbdb-74bd1e7e74cd.title: synthesis
4389a131-dc97-44d2-bbdb-74bd1e7e74cd.description: A reaction in which a more complex compound is produced from simpler compounds (also called ‘combination reaction’).

b0ccb29c-729b-4c21-b49c-2a70c87d142d.title: displacement
b0ccb29c-729b-4c21-b49c-2a70c87d142d.description: The change in position of an object, after a period of time, from its original position. Displacement is a vector quantity. The displacement may be positive, negative or zero.

f8f67b9e-165d-4bd1-8c46-0a0da653be70.title: law of conservation of mass
f8f67b9e-165d-4bd1-8c46-0a0da653be70.description: States that matter cannot be created or destroyed.

fe635d64-525a-4097-9d99-50dac6fe1557.title: fission
fe635d64-525a-4097-9d99-50dac6fe1557.description: A process where the nucleus of an atom splits into two or more smaller nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy in the form of heat and radiation.

67857bfe-712b-4c58-93de-cd6f19ac3bdb.title: pH
67857bfe-712b-4c58-93de-cd6f19ac3bdb.description: A measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution.

3d3e91ac-a59f-4ba3-bdc0-481fe67c5f70.title: catalyst
3d3e91ac-a59f-4ba3-bdc0-481fe67c5f70.description: A substance that changes the speed of a chemical reaction but is itself unchanged at the end of the reaction.

0335f328-b8a9-4ff7-baef-4d1f3f9ca24f.title: IUPAC
0335f328-b8a9-4ff7-baef-4d1f3f9ca24f.description: Acronym for the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry, an authority on chemical terminology and nomenclature.

8a22a1a2-597d-4f92-8e83-53fa8f04ed36.title: covalent bond
8a22a1a2-597d-4f92-8e83-53fa8f04ed36.description: A chemical bond made when 2 atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.

18107def-c15e-4d37-8f73-952fb8b97ed5.title: descriptive statistics
18107def-c15e-4d37-8f73-952fb8b97ed5.description: Statistics that quantitatively describe or summarise features of a collection of information.

db4972fc-3284-4c3e-b267-e2f51f495967.title: first-hand (data)
db4972fc-3284-4c3e-b267-e2f51f495967.description: Information or data which has been directly observed or measured.

06288b2b-2090-44de-9d72-155677cd3ce6.title: error
06288b2b-2090-44de-9d72-155677cd3ce6.description: The difference between an observed result and an expected or theoretical result. Systematic errors are often due to limitations in equipment or procedure and will be consistently different from the expected result.

faecc2c6-4a62-46c2-bd6a-3d9f7889f475.title: voltage
faecc2c6-4a62-46c2-bd6a-3d9f7889f475.description: A measure of the electrical potential difference between 2 points. The SI unit for voltage is the volt (equivalent to joule/coulomb).

144a9f95-2c70-4d20-a010-081f13562939.title: current (electric)
144a9f95-2c70-4d20-a010-081f13562939.description: The flow of electric charge, usually through a conductor or resistor.

c2d3df14-6118-4311-91b0-2b8637598ec6.title: greenhouse effect
c2d3df14-6118-4311-91b0-2b8637598ec6.description: Heating effect due to heat rays from the ground being absorbed by some of the gases in the atmosphere.

4d2600c9-09ab-4871-afd1-91e130fe2fd1.title: phenotype
4d2600c9-09ab-4871-afd1-91e130fe2fd1.description: Observable traits produced by genes in a living thing.

fa9b6210-9951-4ad1-b669-017b71ee36b7.title: evolution
fa9b6210-9951-4ad1-b669-017b71ee36b7.description: The gradual process by which living things change over time.

4b96c2f6-27d5-4282-912c-5aff63d26828.title: isolation (geographic)
4b96c2f6-27d5-4282-912c-5aff63d26828.description: Populations that are separated by a physical barrier, such as a mountain range, river, or ocean so that interbreeding is no longer possible.

5ae69b91-4034-42b4-ba21-8c5e339080fd.title: pedigree
5ae69b91-4034-42b4-ba21-8c5e339080fd.description: A diagram or chart that shows the relationships between individuals in a family, typically across generations, and may include information about inherited traits or genetic conditions.

3e67d4f5-b735-4aa5-9f6c-97bab41551d7.title: Punnett square
3e67d4f5-b735-4aa5-9f6c-97bab41551d7.description: A graphical representation used to predict the possible genetic outcomes of a cross between 2 individuals.

c1d6e3e0-584d-489f-9830-e3c986f5cd5f.title: monogenic
c1d6e3e0-584d-489f-9830-e3c986f5cd5f.description: A trait or characteristic that is determined by a single gene.

d6000944-05a6-4d92-8475-e894259e4392.title: gene-trait relationship
d6000944-05a6-4d92-8475-e894259e4392.description: The relationship between specific genes and the observable characteristics, or traits, they control in an organism.

00812563-cf87-475c-8a71-fee2b5ad9f2c.title: gene
00812563-cf87-475c-8a71-fee2b5ad9f2c.description: A gene is a segment of DNA that contains the instructions for building and maintaining an organism. Genes determine the traits and characteristics of living organisms, and are passed from parents to their offspring during reproduction.

231b4b38-5174-42d2-9969-4714e1d252b9.title: genome
231b4b38-5174-42d2-9969-4714e1d252b9.description: The complete set of genetic material, including all of the genes and non-coding sequences, found within an organism's DNA.

64fc9e67-c25c-4882-9e5d-77cd5749f51b.title: geological timescales
64fc9e67-c25c-4882-9e5d-77cd5749f51b.description: The divisions of time used by geologists to describe the history of the Earth. These timescales are typically divided into different units, such as eons, eras, periods, and epochs, which help organise and understand the sequence of events in Earth's history spanning millions to billions of years.

2222a9f4-640d-43d9-ada0-662005030a3c.title: HeLa stem cell line
2222a9f4-640d-43d9-ada0-662005030a3c.description: A group of immortal cells derived from cervical cancer cells taken from Henrietta Lacks in 1951 without her consent. These cells have been used extensively in scientific research and have contributed to numerous medical advancements.

570ff95f-b681-4500-983e-a8a7549bbce1.title: megafauna
570ff95f-b681-4500-983e-a8a7549bbce1.description: A group of large or giant animals, typically vertebrates, that lived during prehistoric times or still exist today. Some examples of extinct megafauna include the woolly mammoth, sabre-toothed tiger, Irish elk, giant ground sloths and the dodo bird.

1478b061-327a-45ac-a71c-997669c438ee.title: noble gas configuration
1478b061-327a-45ac-a71c-997669c438ee.description: When an atom has a complement of electrons in its outer shell, such that it is completely filled and resembles one of the noble gases such as helium, neon or argon.

fe824b4e-f4d6-449d-93f4-4080b5ec47a9.title: biodegradability
fe824b4e-f4d6-449d-93f4-4080b5ec47a9.description: The ability of a material to decompose as a result of the action of living organisms, especially bacteria.

061efb99-324b-4019-a481-ab46c72d5304.title: bioaccumulation
061efb99-324b-4019-a481-ab46c72d5304.description: (Of a substance, especially a toxin) The build-up of substances (especially toxins) in an organism over time.

490358a4-ba23-4ba9-99bb-582b0aa6e4a7.title: microplastics
490358a4-ba23-4ba9-99bb-582b0aa6e4a7.description: Small particles of plastic in the environment, generally smaller than 5 millimetres in size.

26878d08-02fa-46eb-b568-ef874a008f71.title: valency
26878d08-02fa-46eb-b568-ef874a008f71.description: The number of chemical bonds that an atom can make with a univalent atom such as hydrogen.

ba88992d-cbe2-473d-b7e9-01c84a005e12.title: alkane
ba88992d-cbe2-473d-b7e9-01c84a005e12.description: An organic compound that consists entirely of single-bonded carbon and hydrogen atoms having the general formula CnH2n+2, as methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), and that lacks any other functional groups.

d9f71adf-168f-4138-9594-d026ca1a36fe.title: groove
d9f71adf-168f-4138-9594-d026ca1a36fe.description: Rhythmic quality that produces a strong sense of flow or physical response in music.

4b5d9143-fb9c-46f1-9b49-89b18c9b9273.title: dampen
4b5d9143-fb9c-46f1-9b49-89b18c9b9273.description: Muffle or deaden the sound of an instrument by reducing vibrations.

cb871f9f-8876-42c5-8354-869c65fd8700.title: piano roll
cb871f9f-8876-42c5-8354-869c65fd8700.description: A digital representation of musical notes on a grid against an image of piano keys or a keyboard. Pitch is shown vertically and time is shown horizontally.

912ef354-d8e4-47e9-b44c-7354001899ed.title: beat grid
912ef354-d8e4-47e9-b44c-7354001899ed.description: A framework of evenly spaced divisions that represents the pulse of music, against which the positions of other sounds are indicated.

dd49e6e9-3448-48ff-aca6-00144e9b526e.title: spectral visualisation
dd49e6e9-3448-48ff-aca6-00144e9b526e.description: A representation of the frequency spectrum of sound over time, often through visual displays such as spectrograms.

89543a3b-1c89-41f7-acc2-13d6b1e0e844.title: sharing economy
89543a3b-1c89-41f7-acc2-13d6b1e0e844.description: A system providing access to goods or services on a temporary basis as an alternative to purchasing, often through a digital platform.

12a3532a-9d2b-4be3-be97-7deb5190621f.title: job portfolio
12a3532a-9d2b-4be3-be97-7deb5190621f.description: A collection of materials presented to potential employers that serves as evidence of a person's knowledge, skills and work experience.

77ac1913-e5d2-418f-92b8-f0b2cdd9ef7a.title: technical skills
77ac1913-e5d2-418f-92b8-f0b2cdd9ef7a.description: Skills gained through education, training and/or experience that are directly linked to a specific job and required to perform specialised tasks.

34002a33-e6af-4862-bf5d-183c197f97ed.title: workplace code of conduct
34002a33-e6af-4862-bf5d-183c197f97ed.description: A set of guidelines and principles that outline the expected behaviours, responsibilities and ethical standards in an organisation.

ffec4e34-e978-415c-8ad9-eb40d03eb390.title: transferable skills
ffec4e34-e978-415c-8ad9-eb40d03eb390.description: Skills that are generic in nature, rather than job specific, and that can be applied across a variety of work roles, for example communication, teamwork and problem-solving.

426b5f3c-3923-4067-ad68-1e67b3f16297.title: social capital
426b5f3c-3923-4067-ad68-1e67b3f16297.description: Networks of relationships among people in a society that enable cooperation, trust and mutual support to help individuals and groups pursue their goals.

4995b12c-1b46-488e-8608-235b916835fd.title: employment contract
4995b12c-1b46-488e-8608-235b916835fd.description: An agreement between an employer and employee that sets out the terms and conditions of employment.

6c58ea2e-07a1-48d5-8771-45f696eef491.title: entrepreneurial mindset
6c58ea2e-07a1-48d5-8771-45f696eef491.description: A set of attributes that orient individuals and organisations toward recognising opportunities and approaching challenges with an innovative and solution-focused perspective.

bb976a52-1f1a-476f-a101-70addfa0f4ec.title: entrepreneurial behaviours
bb976a52-1f1a-476f-a101-70addfa0f4ec.description: Behaviours that are applicable in a range of contexts and demonstrate confidence, initiative, innovation and creativity, global competency, empathy, a willingness to take risks and the ability to act on identified opportunities.

48068f94-2c93-429a-94bd-ce0e40b6c6bc.title: entrepreneur
48068f94-2c93-429a-94bd-ce0e40b6c6bc.description: An innovative person who starts and grows a business by identifying and seizing market opportunities, and managing risks and rewards, with the aim of being successful and profitable.

b21a5560-6da4-43e1-8dcb-6e1da7c132ff.title: intellectual property
b21a5560-6da4-43e1-8dcb-6e1da7c132ff.description:
Non-material assets such as forms of cultural expression that belong to a particular individual or community. Intellectual property rights refer to the rights that the law grants to individuals for the protection of creative, intellectual, scientific and industrial activity, such as inventions. 

See Indigenous cultural and intellectual property (ICIP), and copyright

59cabf09-72d7-4f6a-8781-7bb5ed6d3f9b.title: lifelong learning
59cabf09-72d7-4f6a-8781-7bb5ed6d3f9b.description: Intentional and continuous learning throughout a person's life, aimed at enhancing knowledge, skills and abilities through education, training, professional development and life experience.

4f832600-8ef4-4233-beb4-48aaefaca973.title: open employment
4f832600-8ef4-4233-beb4-48aaefaca973.description: When people with and without disability work together in the same workplace.

dc594ff5-39e7-44df-a6a3-e9ca4c696d70.title: superannuation guarantee
dc594ff5-39e7-44df-a6a3-e9ca4c696d70.description: A mandatory system in which employers are legally required to contribute a percentage of an employee’s gross salary or wages into a superannuation fund.

fcbe88c8-1941-487c-9548-480ad4fb4e2e.title: sound–symbol correspondences
fcbe88c8-1941-487c-9548-480ad4fb4e2e.description: A relationship between letters or characters and the sounds they make when pronounced.

6817e71c-0770-4387-8e37-37e940ba9954.title: writing system
6817e71c-0770-4387-8e37-37e940ba9954.description: A method of visually representing verbal communication, based on an alphabet, characters and/or script.

5c2f017e-4d47-4aa0-ad70-a72d202a574c.title: lexical and grammatical chunks
5c2f017e-4d47-4aa0-ad70-a72d202a574c.description: A group of words that are commonly found together; a grammatical pattern, e.g. prepositional phrase, verb + infinitive.

b479f557-dfe6-47a7-94ff-a3bc41d60948.title: visual
b479f557-dfe6-47a7-94ff-a3bc41d60948.description: A visual item, such as a photograph or drawing; an image.

0947f97c-ead1-49e3-9f1a-c4ae35b8ef06.title: language systems
0947f97c-ead1-49e3-9f1a-c4ae35b8ef06.description: Includes the sounds, lexicon (vocabulary), grammar and alphabet/script of the language.

095f8d1c-6dad-4081-bdff-5fbc9ae3d2e1.title: text features
095f8d1c-6dad-4081-bdff-5fbc9ae3d2e1.description: Structural or stylistic components that combine to construct meaning and achieve purpose. Can be recognisable as characterising particular types of texts.

93a575b2-59fa-48bb-b48f-53d702c187f9.title: morphological features
93a575b2-59fa-48bb-b48f-53d702c187f9.description: The patterns of word formation in a particular language, including inflection, derivation and composition.

c2a2d788-13a0-4b57-a63a-116bf4f3638f.title: text types
c2a2d788-13a0-4b57-a63a-116bf4f3638f.description: Categories of text, classified according to the particular purposes they are designed to achieve, which influence the features the texts employ. For example, texts may be imaginative, informative or persuasive, or can belong to more than one category. Text types vary significantly in terms of structure and text features across different languages and cultural contexts.

75469949-1569-4354-8c08-05a29ffff665.title: pronunciation
75469949-1569-4354-8c08-05a29ffff665.description: A manner in which a syllable is uttered.

962ca965-c353-405a-a5ab-bdbf54a8cef3.title: predictable text
962ca965-c353-405a-a5ab-bdbf54a8cef3.description: A text in which the topic and/or type of text is very familiar; it contains mostly familiar language structures, but some unfamiliar language is present. Comprehension strategies may be used in conjunction with knowledge of language to understand the text.

872c2531-f79b-4b02-87f4-534f46132826.title: synthetic text
872c2531-f79b-4b02-87f4-534f46132826.description: Text in the target language written in modern times to assist reading comprehension for a diversity of learners.

10f8c4a9-8c42-4bc0-8a28-158d13f2d856.title: moderately complex text
10f8c4a9-8c42-4bc0-8a28-158d13f2d856.description: A text in which the topic and/or type of text is familiar; however, it may be structurally and/or conceptually more challenging, with greater complexity of language. The text may require students to understand stated and implied meanings.

fdd37525-8445-425d-93be-c80a886004b4.title: cues
fdd37525-8445-425d-93be-c80a886004b4.description: Sources of information used to facilitate comprehension of language that may be visual, grammatical, gestural or contextual.

e4acab8f-2e9c-4920-8675-d7b4e34a12e3.title: symbol
e4acab8f-2e9c-4920-8675-d7b4e34a12e3.description: A letter, figure or other character or mark, or a combination of letters, used to represent something.

9bf92c43-d978-43c7-993d-a8ef5fc48b9a.title: read
9bf92c43-d978-43c7-993d-a8ef5fc48b9a.description: Process visual or tactile symbols (e.g. braille), words or actions in order to derive and/or construct meaning. Reading includes elements of decoding (of sounds and symbols), interpreting, critically analysing and reflecting upon meaning in a wide range of written, visual, print and non-print texts.

f30eed80-78cc-402d-ba4c-2ee3fa67d2c7.title: cognate
f30eed80-78cc-402d-ba4c-2ee3fa67d2c7.description: A word which is directly related in origin to another; cognates have similar spellings and meanings.

70c4bf3d-87e7-45c7-993d-ee571d395040.title: derivation
70c4bf3d-87e7-45c7-993d-ee571d395040.description: A word which is formed from or based on another word.

dca236b8-12b0-4ce3-baec-89ae1e158603.title: photomedia practice
dca236b8-12b0-4ce3-baec-89ae1e158603.description: The application of skills and knowledge to make, represent, respond to and interpret photomedia artworks.

1cefdbce-654f-4293-81c1-69117ea2e366.title: photomedia artist
1cefdbce-654f-4293-81c1-69117ea2e366.description: A person who makes photomedia artworks as an individual, as part of a group, at a school, as part of a company, or by enlisting others to produce their photomedia artwork.

3d1f3159-a342-44da-b097-c7a78e867342.title: photomedia form
3d1f3159-a342-44da-b097-c7a78e867342.description: A category of artistic representation in Photography, Film and Digital Media distinguished by specific techniques and mediums in still, moving or emerging fields.

e121f031-1c6c-4c28-b20e-6f3084e8e27b.title: masking
e121f031-1c6c-4c28-b20e-6f3084e8e27b.description: Controlling what is visible or exposed by limiting light, or hiding parts of an image or layer.

9093895d-7571-40e6-b5d0-94a0a80330a4.title: retouching
9093895d-7571-40e6-b5d0-94a0a80330a4.description: Correcting or improving images, negatives or moving image footage by removing blemishes or distractions and fixing imperfections.

bf4c63c6-cef9-4619-a7bf-b95f63628151.title: layering
bf4c63c6-cef9-4619-a7bf-b95f63628151.description: The process of combining or stacking multiple images, videos, or graphic elements to build depth, texture, or meaning.

ce8df5d0-feb2-4552-a4a7-847a4d6af099.title: gimbal
ce8df5d0-feb2-4552-a4a7-847a4d6af099.description: A stabilising device that uses pivoted supports to keep a camera steady and level while filming, even when the operator or platform is moving.

1bc1d271-9915-4778-b83e-8f754cb44c93.title: title sequencing
1bc1d271-9915-4778-b83e-8f754cb44c93.description: The opening segment of a film or video that uses images, motion and sound to present the title and credits, and set the tone and mood.

2f64e92c-fd35-4aaf-afa7-63662fc0fd81.title: aperture
2f64e92c-fd35-4aaf-afa7-63662fc0fd81.description: The adjustable opening in a camera lens that controls how much light enters when taking a photograph, measured in f-stops.

a05c168f-4591-4272-8387-ee124b12a041.title: shutter speed
a05c168f-4591-4272-8387-ee124b12a041.description: The time the camera shutter stays open to light during an exposure which determines image brightness and whether motion appears sharp or blurred.

51c16518-63bc-4af1-b867-e885968abed1.title: frame rate
51c16518-63bc-4af1-b867-e885968abed1.description: The number of images, or frames, captured or displayed per second in film or video, measured in frames per second (FPS).

0cc90350-e12e-406a-9e47-69edfd88eb67.title: hyperlapse
0cc90350-e12e-406a-9e47-69edfd88eb67.description: A type of time-lapse video created by moving the camera through space between each shot, producing a dynamic sense of motion and accelerated time.

f2401374-fbec-4acd-a905-f10a8c9dc99b.title: analogue
f2401374-fbec-4acd-a905-f10a8c9dc99b.description: A method of capturing images using chemical processes on film, a hard plate, or paper.

6bea36cd-c449-4857-a76c-27124d7f2488.title: time lapse
6bea36cd-c449-4857-a76c-27124d7f2488.description: A photographic or filming technique that records frames at spaced intervals and plays them at normal speed to compress time and accelerate motion; the camera remains fixed.

a3dd5f32-dd56-42d2-a7a2-067ee05e045f.title: long exposure
a3dd5f32-dd56-42d2-a7a2-067ee05e045f.description: A photographic technique that keeps the camera’s shutter open for an extended time to capture motion, light trails, or low-light scenes.

98d1be35-9d29-4565-be62-9b085ec7b118.title: montage
98d1be35-9d29-4565-be62-9b085ec7b118.description: A technique that combines multiple photographic images or shots, placed side by side or layered, to convey a single idea, compress time, or create new meaning.

036efaa0-a6e5-4950-833e-6cb1ddc1490e.title: photogram
036efaa0-a6e5-4950-833e-6cb1ddc1490e.description: An image made without a camera by placing objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it to light to produce silhouettes and tonal shapes.

190deb47-21ee-420a-a81d-c84c1edcb2f2.title: cyanotype
190deb47-21ee-420a-a81d-c84c1edcb2f2.description: A photographic printing process using sensitised, precoated paper to create white forms on deep blue backgrounds; also the resulting print.

93bb6b6f-91ad-4515-9526-db2cd12c1dfc.title: photomedia practitioner
93bb6b6f-91ad-4515-9526-db2cd12c1dfc.description: Individuals, such as photomedia artists, curators, writers, critics and historians, who engage in the making, curation, critique and/or historical explanations of photomedia artworks.

a7f1fd6d-ba71-419c-a757-b5093b6d0d44.title: synthetic
a7f1fd6d-ba71-419c-a757-b5093b6d0d44.description: A style where images are created or shaped by computational digital processes, often including AI, rather than traditional or manual methods.

6f96c29a-fa7b-45a6-8487-ae5b84f64a87.title: stakeholder
6f96c29a-fa7b-45a6-8487-ae5b84f64a87.description: A person, group or organisation that has an interest in or concern about something.

7284fc5b-33df-447d-963f-134045f71696.title: supply
7284fc5b-33df-447d-963f-134045f71696.description: The quantity of a good or service that businesses are willing and able to offer for sale at a particular price at a given point in time.

e9cef6de-7711-4b10-add0-21ff6f8e0bff.title: demand
e9cef6de-7711-4b10-add0-21ff6f8e0bff.description: The quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to purchase at a particular price at a given point in time.

f98fa30f-378b-476a-a59c-473f773331fe.title: opportunity cost
f98fa30f-378b-476a-a59c-473f773331fe.description: What a person has to forgo if they choose to do A rather than B; the value of the next best alternative that is forgone whenever a choice is made.

222f402e-93dd-4af2-99f0-1ee1ebcfc2cf.title: consumer
222f402e-93dd-4af2-99f0-1ee1ebcfc2cf.description: A person or group who purchases goods and services to satisfy their needs and wants.

6605ce53-90de-4a18-b4b6-43d51fc953e5.title: non-legal rules
6605ce53-90de-4a18-b4b6-43d51fc953e5.description: Guidelines set by an individual or a group that are not enforceable by law but govern behaviour within a specific context.

8303088f-a6b5-4d23-a856-7cc90b4e28e2.title: public office
8303088f-a6b5-4d23-a856-7cc90b4e28e2.description: A position of authority within government filled through an election, where the elected individual represents the public and performs official duties.

62762778-9823-40c1-a0d7-bacc987db2fe.title: corporate social responsibility
62762778-9823-40c1-a0d7-bacc987db2fe.description: When businesses consider the impact of their decisions on people, communities and the environment, in addition to focusing on financial performance.

9fefe30d-59e0-4ca1-b81d-35c39af67a9f.title: target market
9fefe30d-59e0-4ca1-b81d-35c39af67a9f.description: The group of customers to whom a business intends to sell its goods and/or services.

65514f39-5125-43cd-b6a2-9693d91c9095.title: competitive advantage
65514f39-5125-43cd-b6a2-9693d91c9095.description: The ability of a business to outperform its rivals by differentiating its goods or services from those of its competitors or by operating at a lower cost.

2c1cdf1c-4f90-4c16-b937-624bcc7e5e5d.title: competition
2c1cdf1c-4f90-4c16-b937-624bcc7e5e5d.description: Rivalry between businesses that offer similar goods or services with each business aiming to gain a larger market share by attracting more customers.

41277d6b-e1a7-4b45-a5e2-e09cae052e40.title: scam
41277d6b-e1a7-4b45-a5e2-e09cae052e40.description: A fraudulent scheme that tricks people into giving away money or personal details by misleading them about the nature or benefits of the transaction.

dd1e2c5c-cc1a-4423-91e8-d081d77ad77c.title: consumer redress
dd1e2c5c-cc1a-4423-91e8-d081d77ad77c.description: Options available for purchasers of goods or services to resolve issues that may arise when consumer guarantees are not met.

76c7fd84-7ee1-4d50-a789-9a39160cae3d.title: risk mitigation
76c7fd84-7ee1-4d50-a789-9a39160cae3d.description: Action taken to reduce or manage potential negative impacts.

abe5c7b8-aa76-4053-b727-78adbc99462a.title: legal capacity
abe5c7b8-aa76-4053-b727-78adbc99462a.description: A person’s ability to make decisions that are recognised as valid and binding under the law.

7cd6149d-8db2-490a-b9ae-56a9a1718ed7.title: minor
7cd6149d-8db2-490a-b9ae-56a9a1718ed7.description: A person under the age of 18 years.

9b012220-a55b-4f60-bfbc-a136e9172bf1.title: investment portfolio
9b012220-a55b-4f60-bfbc-a136e9172bf1.description: A collection of assets owned by an individual or an organisation. It is managed to achieve financial goals.

e730d5ef-980a-4a7f-a6bf-afa85df3e416.title: living standards
e730d5ef-980a-4a7f-a6bf-afa85df3e416.description: The level of comfort, material wealth and wellbeing experienced by people, influenced by their income.

e71cc077-768a-45a3-bb4d-444cde47f42f.title: credit score
e71cc077-768a-45a3-bb4d-444cde47f42f.description: A numerical rating showing a person’s financial reliability based on their debt repayment history, helping lenders predict the likelihood of timely loan repayments.

1ea4433c-6795-4d10-9f87-fe8e20ac89e1.title: consent
1ea4433c-6795-4d10-9f87-fe8e20ac89e1.description:
Informed and freely given agreement to engage in an activity, or for a specific thing to happen. Consent is denied when someone does not have the capacity to give consent.

According to the Commonwealth Consent policy Framework, sexual consent is a free, voluntary and informed agreement between people to participate in a sexual act. This agreement is only present when these people mutually and genuinely want to engage in that sexual act and actively make sure their partner does too.

In NSW, consent is a fundamental part of sexual offence law.

744dc6dd-ff45-4c90-8193-1c2e0bb66253.title: fair play
744dc6dd-ff45-4c90-8193-1c2e0bb66253.description: Play that is free from any bias and includes the application of rules and/or etiquette.

b5c5583a-ff81-43a8-be17-a28c1b8330af.title: record
b5c5583a-ff81-43a8-be17-a28c1b8330af.description: Transfer sounds onto a recording medium for the purpose of reproduction.

33a619ab-4eee-4257-aff6-c36c71ec3925.title: repertoire
33a619ab-4eee-4257-aff6-c36c71ec3925.description: A collection of pieces of music within a particular social or cultural context, genre, style or tradition.

ec2ba36b-882e-4c55-bac3-7f7e62f405fa.title: score
ec2ba36b-882e-4c55-bac3-7f7e62f405fa.description:
A collection of notated representations of sound used to communicate musical information.

See notation

dabce50a-32d6-4947-a8f0-d05435822217.title: sensory score
dabce50a-32d6-4947-a8f0-d05435822217.description: The communication of musical information recorded through adapted media including modified stave notation, braille notation and graphic notation. It may also include sensory cues (such as visual, auditory, gestural and/or kinaesthetic stimuli) to assist the sequencing of musical material.

e4e052ac-252d-499a-89b3-4f0c215879c2.title: notation
e4e052ac-252d-499a-89b3-4f0c215879c2.description:
A written means of documenting musical thought through signs and symbols.

Notation forms may include staff notation, pre-notation, graphic notation, notations drawn from global music cultures, instrument-specific notations, braille, scores, charts, lead-sheets.

ba8e76dc-4009-4dd7-be55-605c502e6f02.title: improvisation
ba8e76dc-4009-4dd7-be55-605c502e6f02.description: Spontaneous performance used as a key method of making drama, or as a rehearsal or live performance technique to communicate ideas and construct drama.

b10dce72-3648-4cbf-a789-5dcfc8fd6e3f.title: structure
b10dce72-3648-4cbf-a789-5dcfc8fd6e3f.description: Part of the forming process in composition and choreography. There are 2 main parts; organising the movement; and organising the dance.

6e4e93d2-d624-41dc-a476-0296066edb06.title: notate
6e4e93d2-d624-41dc-a476-0296066edb06.description: Record a piece of music in written form.

e891de31-0429-460a-a449-c08a02193fb7.title: articulation
e891de31-0429-460a-a449-c08a02193fb7.description: The way a note is sung or played.

fa3cc878-9308-415f-bdc9-26643c3e695b.title: texture
fa3cc878-9308-415f-bdc9-26643c3e695b.description: The way layers of sound are combined in a piece of music.

b726cc78-2693-45c3-811e-d782917d30c3.title: source
b726cc78-2693-45c3-811e-d782917d30c3.description: Any written or non-written materials that can be used to investigate the past.

79200950-17bc-4de6-8b90-a63695ce54c0.title: Welcome to Country
79200950-17bc-4de6-8b90-a63695ce54c0.description: An ongoing protocol given by a Traditional Custodian of the Country.

f605b247-332a-41d6-91f7-1387e2e28195.title: tackle
f605b247-332a-41d6-91f7-1387e2e28195.description: The equipment used for fishing, such as rods, reels, lines and hooks. It includes all the tools and gear needed to catch fish.

0125c480-a3ef-4a54-ba6a-33bb8c5c343f.title: sounder
0125c480-a3ef-4a54-ba6a-33bb8c5c343f.description: An electronic device used on a boat to measure the depth of water beneath it. It sends sound waves to the bottom and calculates the distance based on how long it takes for the sound to bounce back.

17960bef-f985-47cc-9acd-b8fbb4b1e168.title: fish finder
17960bef-f985-47cc-9acd-b8fbb4b1e168.description: An electronic device used on a boat to detect and locate fish underwater. It uses sonar technology to send sound waves into the water and displays the results on a screen.

fd53ca3d-6d3e-4f69-bb51-9f9eaf9bfffe.title: watercraft
fd53ca3d-6d3e-4f69-bb51-9f9eaf9bfffe.description: Any vehicle used for traveling on water, including surfboards, kayaks, boats and ships.

8f903621-c00b-432a-8be4-d595e7fb8f97.title: carbon sink
8f903621-c00b-432a-8be4-d595e7fb8f97.description: A natural system, like forests, oceans, lakes or wetlands, that absorbs and stores carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. This process helps mitigate the effects of climate change.

763b17fc-904f-43fd-903c-1dd31b2aad74.title: turbidity
763b17fc-904f-43fd-903c-1dd31b2aad74.description: How cloudy or murky water is due to particles like dirt, algae or other materials floating in it. Higher turbidity means the water is less clear.

5ea18c40-cc7c-439e-ac53-3b6d1aadf88c.title: dissolved oxygen
5ea18c40-cc7c-439e-ac53-3b6d1aadf88c.description: The amount of oxygen present in water, essential for the survival of aquatic life. It enters the water from the air or through photosynthesis by aquatic plants.

36de3970-5173-4ab1-bc6d-d1eb92dd1f4d.title: propagation
36de3970-5173-4ab1-bc6d-d1eb92dd1f4d.description: The process of breeding and growing new plants or animals.

a3579c5a-90eb-40cc-a174-61e0d5af6b46.title: mariculture
a3579c5a-90eb-40cc-a174-61e0d5af6b46.description: A type of aquaculture involving farming marine organisms, such as fish, shellfish and seaweed in oceans, coastal areas and estuaries. Species are raised in either natural or controlled conditions for food, materials or other products.

f0beba49-013c-4c87-a203-4d287cbf3243.title: aquaculture
f0beba49-013c-4c87-a203-4d287cbf3243.description: The farming of aquatic animals and plants, especially fish, shellfish and seaweed, in natural or controlled marine or freshwater environments.

f954a156-271d-433f-a2b7-abf09a304b8e.title: riparian zones
f954a156-271d-433f-a2b7-abf09a304b8e.description: An area of land along the edge of a river, stream or other body of water. These zones are important for supporting diverse plant and animal life and help protect water quality.

24b515bb-480b-4262-affb-47cce983b5e7.title: biofouling
24b515bb-480b-4262-affb-47cce983b5e7.description: The accumulation of microorganisms, plants, algae, or small animals on surfaces, such as ships' hulls, pipes or underwater sensors, particularly in aquatic environments.

07af225a-da6b-45b9-8ef0-705b9253220c.title: brackish
07af225a-da6b-45b9-8ef0-705b9253220c.description: Describes a mixture of freshwater and saltwater. Brackish water has a higher salt content than freshwater but a lower salt content than seawater.

db6fcc39-79fe-4412-80f6-d2f517f70531.title: rigging
db6fcc39-79fe-4412-80f6-d2f517f70531.description: Creating the digital skeleton for a character or object inside a 3D model, so an animator can move, pose and control the character or object realistically.

d516c431-e852-43fc-934a-7a3ee22f3372.title: oblique projection
d516c431-e852-43fc-934a-7a3ee22f3372.description: A type of 3D drawing where the front face is shown straight on, and depth is represented with angled lines, usually 45°.

54bd39c2-d21e-4b57-9b22-047e89bf5b9f.title: rendering
54bd39c2-d21e-4b57-9b22-047e89bf5b9f.description: The process of creating realistic images by adding colour, shading and texturing to an image. Renderings can be generated using hand techniques or by using software.

4e548f4d-174e-43f1-b45d-c57469ac5ef7.title: axonometric projection
4e548f4d-174e-43f1-b45d-c57469ac5ef7.description: A drawing technique used to represent 3D objects using true scale, with one vertical axis and others angled, usually at 45° for architectural drawings.

e529644c-a888-4dbf-8d88-80c2b474192a.title: exploded view
e529644c-a888-4dbf-8d88-80c2b474192a.description: An image of an object with individual parts shown separately but arranged to show the relationship and position of how parts of a product fit together.

470bf010-d516-4e8f-b580-53ec8191b612.title: isometric projection
470bf010-d516-4e8f-b580-53ec8191b612.description: A type of pictorial drawing using vertical lines and lines drawn usually at a 30° angle to the horizontal.

b1eebf79-1559-49a7-bf14-d09ffa6ddbe0.title: cutaway view
b1eebf79-1559-49a7-bf14-d09ffa6ddbe0.description: A view represented in a drawing in which part of the exterior is removed to reveal selected internal parts or features of an object.

1bbac232-7d5b-4dc8-a439-19883259e51f.title: anthropometric data
1bbac232-7d5b-4dc8-a439-19883259e51f.description: Measurements of the human body collected for the purpose of assessing physical properties, including size, shape and proportions.

854e9a32-7b5f-4e25-b388-84508c9a968b.title: non-legal measures
854e9a32-7b5f-4e25-b388-84508c9a968b.description: A course of action used to address a situation without using the law.

c05c8552-b2d7-485a-8f7e-550aab0d2084.title: rule of law
c05c8552-b2d7-485a-8f7e-550aab0d2084.description: The principle that all citizens are equal before the law and that no one is above the law.

36ded7b4-c065-4f3d-898c-5bd664bdb58b.title: legal measures
36ded7b4-c065-4f3d-898c-5bd664bdb58b.description: Any act or process in law designed to regulate behaviour, prohibit actions or establish obligations.

924dc94a-f767-4a2e-a09f-3e65a5bc7c34.title: reform
924dc94a-f767-4a2e-a09f-3e65a5bc7c34.description: Changes made to the legal system to address outdated laws or reflect changing social values.

889a99b5-816c-44da-b75a-9de95f49474b.title: ad hoc tribunal
889a99b5-816c-44da-b75a-9de95f49474b.description: The temporary formation of a body or board of inquiry to investigate and rule on a particular event or fulfil a particular purpose.

c51892cd-99bd-4979-9877-1894c52d66cc.title: sanctions
c51892cd-99bd-4979-9877-1894c52d66cc.description: A measure used in international law to deter behaviour or restore peace and security.

1b527edc-ae3f-4f31-ae1d-ecfd9c531659.title: compliance
1b527edc-ae3f-4f31-ae1d-ecfd9c531659.description: Following the rules and laws in society.

c8a4e673-bd89-4519-b500-756725d73d6d.title: collective security
c8a4e673-bd89-4519-b500-756725d73d6d.description: A system of security where nation-states agree to commit to a united response against any threat or breach of peace.

e079c7d2-d074-46eb-bcf0-bc41e5fb4c4a.title: obligation
e079c7d2-d074-46eb-bcf0-bc41e5fb4c4a.description: A duty or responsibility that is binding on individuals, businesses or nation-states, and enforceable by law.

8a23b263-61a4-44e7-abff-e5064097fbde.title: non-state actors
8a23b263-61a4-44e7-abff-e5064097fbde.description: An organisation or entity that has influence in the global sphere but is independent and not affiliated with any nation-state or government.

7ddadd4b-33e8-4857-a958-40fd680c46f2.title: diplomacy
7ddadd4b-33e8-4857-a958-40fd680c46f2.description: The actions of maintaining relationships through discussions, negotiation and mediation between nations, groups or individuals to promote peace and prevent conflict.

354cea92-bc85-471e-a105-4af9280daeb9.title: peacebuilding
354cea92-bc85-471e-a105-4af9280daeb9.description: Assistance provided over the long term to countries impacted by conflict that addresses its root cause and which develops ways to prevent violence in the future.

716523ab-86eb-4c43-aeb2-db3000f2e5f0.title: peacekeeping
716523ab-86eb-4c43-aeb2-db3000f2e5f0.description: Actions undertaken by armed forces with the consent of all parties, to restore peace and security in areas impacted by conflict.

9e9e7e61-8f4e-4060-8f7d-0a90f0e6018e.title: displacement
9e9e7e61-8f4e-4060-8f7d-0a90f0e6018e.description: The change in position of an object, after a period of time, from its original position. Displacement is a vector quantity. The displacement may be positive, negative or zero.

d1f9879e-46dc-405d-8ee9-8fe939579395.title: tribunal
d1f9879e-46dc-405d-8ee9-8fe939579395.description: A body established to settle disputes, review administrative decisions and handle matters in a specialised area.

021128b8-6dc6-44e7-8bc3-951ebc2ec16e.title: intergovernmental organisation
021128b8-6dc6-44e7-8bc3-951ebc2ec16e.description: An international body established by treaty or agreement amongst nations to address common interests and goals.

de288b94-6e3c-49fc-b33e-d052f2b76f20.title: regulation
de288b94-6e3c-49fc-b33e-d052f2b76f20.description: The control of actions or processes in a certain area, usually maintained by an authority.

af955f63-1345-4788-8a5d-1acef9fbda1d.title: state sovereignty
af955f63-1345-4788-8a5d-1acef9fbda1d.description: A state’s authority to govern itself and its people without foreign interference.

36994325-1a22-447c-9e70-ae1234eeb23c.title: international relations
36994325-1a22-447c-9e70-ae1234eeb23c.description: When relationships exist between 2 or more countries with the prospect to cooperate through diplomacy, foreign policy and international law.

dab96a0b-1a16-4b32-b575-4a7d03721e57.title: human rights
dab96a0b-1a16-4b32-b575-4a7d03721e57.description: Universal freedoms and protections that belong to all individuals and groups by virtue of being human.

61c09728-e07e-41b5-838e-2fea8c4aece5.title: recognition
61c09728-e07e-41b5-838e-2fea8c4aece5.description: The formal acceptance of a claim, authority, achievement or fact as valid and existing.

61214904-946e-47b5-b21f-723f531b39de.title: equity
61214904-946e-47b5-b21f-723f531b39de.description: Resources are allocated in accordance with the needs of individuals and populations with the desired goal of equality of health outcomes.

17b5b2dc-23e5-4126-af39-34907cecae32.title: authorities
17b5b2dc-23e5-4126-af39-34907cecae32.description: Organisations that have the power to determine, adjudicate or settle issues or disputes in a specialised area or subject.

d22e269c-c6ff-44c9-8250-7c27d2d43c48.title: evolving capacity
d22e269c-c6ff-44c9-8250-7c27d2d43c48.description: The increasing ability for children and young people to make reasoned decisions for themselves as they grow and develop.

0e6a4482-1c86-41a9-a2d7-818ce4597c19.title: recidivism
0e6a4482-1c86-41a9-a2d7-818ce4597c19.description: Repeat offending by an individual convicted and punished for a crime.

13cdd406-a34e-4761-8af1-c655f24f40e6.title: justice reinvestment
13cdd406-a34e-4761-8af1-c655f24f40e6.description: A strategy to redirect funding from prisons towards community-based programs to address the underlying causes of crime.

b5960a89-238d-416f-be74-2b0e39031cc2.title: diversionary
b5960a89-238d-416f-be74-2b0e39031cc2.description: A process of moving an individual away from offending towards rehabilitation, to address the underlying causes of their behaviour and to avoid going to court.

45918f1f-02c0-4d51-bfe6-6a57bd43aac9.title: terra nullius
45918f1f-02c0-4d51-bfe6-6a57bd43aac9.description: A concept in international law meaning ‘a territory belonging to no-one’ or ‘over which no-one claims ownership’.

bc081ba4-56ea-40e4-bd23-21edcff0f393.title: judicial
bc081ba4-56ea-40e4-bd23-21edcff0f393.description: An action made by a judge or court.

7a95097c-7cbe-4d08-a732-52384d231f10.title: land rights
7a95097c-7cbe-4d08-a732-52384d231f10.description:
The evolving struggle of Aboriginal Peoples, Torres Strait Islander Peoples, and international Indigenous Peoples for the absolute legal and moral acknowledgement of prior ownership of their land and recognition of all accompanying rights and obligations which flow from this association. ‘Land Rights’ (capitalised) refers to the legislation.

See land

ed6ead86-7401-4b6c-977b-51c59c645601.title: Native Title
ed6ead86-7401-4b6c-977b-51c59c645601.description: Native Title in Australia recognises Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ rights to land and waters based on traditional laws and customs.

79ad27bf-ff35-4356-ae66-e7a26ebc4529.title: contract
79ad27bf-ff35-4356-ae66-e7a26ebc4529.description: An agreement between 2 or more individuals or organisations that is enforceable by law.

3aec4f00-af22-46cb-aaf7-fa271d78972a.title: non-compliance
3aec4f00-af22-46cb-aaf7-fa271d78972a.description: Failure to follow the rules or act within the law.

591b7f47-51b7-4608-8633-6f2c50769851.title: anti-competitive
591b7f47-51b7-4608-8633-6f2c50769851.description: Any business practice that limits or prevents competition.

f0e6d2be-2bed-41f7-850c-5b302356055a.title: civil law
f0e6d2be-2bed-41f7-850c-5b302356055a.description: A body of law relating to disputes between individuals such as negligence, defamation or contract law.

0ed9ceb9-5921-4c3a-bb87-c47e0a74bab3.title: burden of proof
0ed9ceb9-5921-4c3a-bb87-c47e0a74bab3.description: The responsibility of proving the case against the accused in a criminal matter or the defendant in a civil matter.

4ec9af73-e7df-4f16-bc57-ef15780c2f71.title: standard of proof
4ec9af73-e7df-4f16-bc57-ef15780c2f71.description: The level of certainty required for a court to find evidence to be a proven fact.

831a31b1-1534-4006-8b6c-7bab7c20b9ad.title: loss
831a31b1-1534-4006-8b6c-7bab7c20b9ad.description: The difference between the total cost and the total revenue of producing and selling goods or services where the cost is greater than the revenue.

aee1c9a1-dd77-4f2c-a2f5-144505db65f0.title: crime
aee1c9a1-dd77-4f2c-a2f5-144505db65f0.description: An act or omission that is harmful to society, violates the law and is punishable by the state.

fb8df3f2-74d0-4b37-a838-03ed8913325d.title: actus reus
fb8df3f2-74d0-4b37-a838-03ed8913325d.description:
Latin for ’the guilty act’. One of the 2 elements of a crime.

See mens rea

d6c86f25-6d91-49b8-b295-13401ba18647.title: mens rea
d6c86f25-6d91-49b8-b295-13401ba18647.description:
Latin for ‘the guilty mind’. One of the 2 elements of a crime.

See actus reus

f272a43c-cfab-415d-bce6-b92b4de870de.title: causation
f272a43c-cfab-415d-bce6-b92b4de870de.description: The link between a person accused of a crime and the end result. The actions that led to the crime.

dfd2a953-1ec8-462a-b923-1002e14cfb1d.title: strict liability
dfd2a953-1ec8-462a-b923-1002e14cfb1d.description: Actions where the law must only prove the person is responsible for the act, even without the intent to commit a crime.

e4c2b94e-b0f7-4adc-9327-a2ce49e64f5e.title: summary crime
e4c2b94e-b0f7-4adc-9327-a2ce49e64f5e.description: A minor criminal charge heard in a local court before a magistrate.

f0b3f8cc-5735-4225-a7e5-9d1c7e49dfe6.title: indictable crime
f0b3f8cc-5735-4225-a7e5-9d1c7e49dfe6.description: A serious criminal charge heard before a judge and jury.

13f5ad65-1d64-4db3-ba30-8597b3c29b81.title: exploitation
13f5ad65-1d64-4db3-ba30-8597b3c29b81.description: The act of using or treating someone unfairly for profit or gain.

d9fde408-1544-40df-b223-2daff63da480.title: award
d9fde408-1544-40df-b223-2daff63da480.description: The industry-specific terms and conditions of employment which are applied to employees.

4fca5155-0e1d-4687-b3bb-82672948cc11.title: enterprise agreement
4fca5155-0e1d-4687-b3bb-82672948cc11.description: An agreement that is legally binding and sets out the pay and working conditions between employees and employers in a specific workplace.

2906dccc-7e3e-49d4-a82a-368d60e8aff1.title: entitlement
2906dccc-7e3e-49d4-a82a-368d60e8aff1.description: The rights and benefits that employees are legally permitted to under law.

ce916efe-33e4-44b4-b70d-e0d503521977.title: adversarial system
ce916efe-33e4-44b4-b70d-e0d503521977.description: System of trial used in Australia where representatives act for opposing parties before an independent arbitrator who ensures the strict rules of evidence and procedure are maintained in the court.

2f7e3544-a367-4160-8145-15f83fa31646.title: custodial penalties
2f7e3544-a367-4160-8145-15f83fa31646.description: A penalty ordered by the court where an offender is confined to a prison or other correctional facility for a set period of time.

61aa7c7d-eda6-40fb-8689-0178255e44bd.title: plea
61aa7c7d-eda6-40fb-8689-0178255e44bd.description: A response to a criminal charge from the accused as either guilty or not guilty.

e67a12d6-6c2c-47a7-804a-fa0dc8d3a0ff.title: pre-trial processes
e67a12d6-6c2c-47a7-804a-fa0dc8d3a0ff.description: Steps taken before a trial to determine if the case is ready. This could include charges to be put forward, the entering of a plea or the disclosure of evidence.

1ae66bf6-ddbc-48ff-b46f-baffba7e9ca8.title: discretion
1ae66bf6-ddbc-48ff-b46f-baffba7e9ca8.description: The power of a judge or police officer to act or make a decision based on personal experience or judgement.

a7f667ad-b088-4b71-bcf5-25c0ad7b1117.title: community-based orders
a7f667ad-b088-4b71-bcf5-25c0ad7b1117.description: A non-custodial sentence that requires supervision of the offender who is subject to conditions while living in the community.

2ce38962-971d-4d1c-97c5-6886063d0527.title: de facto
2ce38962-971d-4d1c-97c5-6886063d0527.description: Two people living together in a genuine domestic relationship but who are not legally married.

fc1cf7c1-9044-4e8d-9e2e-7d8ed0d0dc83.title: procedural fairness
fc1cf7c1-9044-4e8d-9e2e-7d8ed0d0dc83.description: The steps taken by a decision-maker to ensure a fair and impartial process.

48a9a263-7bd4-4a62-b7c1-bfed438fb6bc.title: jurisdiction
48a9a263-7bd4-4a62-b7c1-bfed438fb6bc.description: The area or matter in which a court or parliament has authority.

474297f5-d74a-4027-b42f-b45a6ad8781d.title: fairness
474297f5-d74a-4027-b42f-b45a6ad8781d.description: The impartial and just treatment of individuals.

4e3ba92e-6e12-4dc1-b75d-781303238947.title: delegated legislation
4e3ba92e-6e12-4dc1-b75d-781303238947.description: Laws created by bodies other than parliament who derive their authority from an Act of parliament.

3879c563-7f37-4694-a943-9f654c1c4493.title: equality
3879c563-7f37-4694-a943-9f654c1c4493.description: To be equal, having the same rights or standing in society.

7f800852-19c1-4f42-af4f-170f2b01561d.title: referendum
7f800852-19c1-4f42-af4f-170f2b01561d.description: A national vote to propose a change to the Constitution.

ae9b2ad6-7e75-4ef7-b56b-d11ae740e0f2.title: Customary Lore
ae9b2ad6-7e75-4ef7-b56b-d11ae740e0f2.description:
The learning and transmission of Cultural heritage by observing Customs, ceremonies and songs. Customary Lore is connected to the Dreaming and provides protocols and Practices for how people interact with Country, Kinship and Community.

The term ‘Customary’ must be used with care. Some individuals and groups could find this term offensive, and may prefer to use Aboriginal Language terms or ‘law’. The term ‘folklore’ is not appropriate.

See Customary law

5ea9ba99-256f-4a85-ab4c-f62eedfc4446.title: precedent
5ea9ba99-256f-4a85-ab4c-f62eedfc4446.description: A legal decision made in a higher court that may be followed by that court or a lower court in a case with similar facts.

7cc6ed05-6568-4418-8927-2d671f083300.title: stress
7cc6ed05-6568-4418-8927-2d671f083300.description:
An emphasis in pronunciation that is placed on a particular syllable of a word.

For example:

  • She will conduct the orchestra.
  • Her conduct is exemplary.

30afcb4e-b3eb-4b17-96bd-62347e115704.title: written text
30afcb4e-b3eb-4b17-96bd-62347e115704.description: A text produced using written language. It is one-way information giving, such as a handwritten or digital text.

74cc7260-dd85-490e-8282-8d45d302ee10.title: sound system
74cc7260-dd85-490e-8282-8d45d302ee10.description: Phonological components of the language, including intonation, pronunciation and stress.

b87d7f00-b9ee-4873-bd9b-0b04935d6a0a.title: communication
b87d7f00-b9ee-4873-bd9b-0b04935d6a0a.description: The purposeful interpretation and expression of meaning.

861d60e6-1839-4fae-84c7-e4a7b588a1d3.title: manipulate
861d60e6-1839-4fae-84c7-e4a7b588a1d3.description: To change the vocabulary or syntax of a sentence to suit the purpose.

caf77933-dd34-4bb7-b410-c672859e756d.title: symbols
caf77933-dd34-4bb7-b410-c672859e756d.description: The written representations of a language such as letters, characters, marks, accents; identifiable aspects of culture such as flags, artefacts, costumes, landmarks.

717f3fa7-e792-4208-9134-bcdcdd4179f8.title: accent
717f3fa7-e792-4208-9134-bcdcdd4179f8.description:
A manner of pronunciation of a language which marks speakers as belonging to identifiable categories such as geographical or ethnic origin, social group or generation.

The stress placed on the syllable.

a4375426-f754-4187-aa57-6c335818ad39.title: binary code
a4375426-f754-4187-aa57-6c335818ad39.description: Binary digit (or bits) in digital technologies which describes a numbering scheme with either 0 or 1.
