5ead8c37-352d-4471-a24c-607f19c213d7.title: insulator
5ead8c37-352d-4471-a24c-607f19c213d7.description: A material which inhibits the transfer of heat, sound or electrical energy.

abe391bd-0976-4d06-a13c-6ecf02f9e418.title: galaxy
abe391bd-0976-4d06-a13c-6ecf02f9e418.description: A collection of gases, dust, and billions of stars and their solar systems, all held together by gravity.

327f043b-043b-44c7-9c02-15e390dd8f51.title: nebula/nebulae
327f043b-043b-44c7-9c02-15e390dd8f51.description: A giant cloud of dust and gas in space.

89507396-1802-426d-b1cb-bfa901f2d04f.title: exoplanet
89507396-1802-426d-b1cb-bfa901f2d04f.description: A planet found outside our solar system.

b8cd9cd9-ab7e-4892-b2fb-73d20a517a53.title: black hole
b8cd9cd9-ab7e-4892-b2fb-73d20a517a53.description: A region in space of such immense gravity that nothing – not even light – can escape from it.

1ce309c7-9dc1-4faa-a5e6-b14a251a67cb.title: convection
1ce309c7-9dc1-4faa-a5e6-b14a251a67cb.description: The movement of a gas or fluid by the transfer of heat energy through the gas or fluid itself.

3c591f2e-1e29-4bbc-afbe-f29587616a43.title: radiation
3c591f2e-1e29-4bbc-afbe-f29587616a43.description:
The emission of energy as electromagnetic waves or as moving subatomic particles.

OR

The energy or particles that are released during radioactive decay.

444c600c-5ad3-4cc5-b5f8-5e6edb4daf90.title: food chain
444c600c-5ad3-4cc5-b5f8-5e6edb4daf90.description: A sequence of organisms that begins with a producer and ends with a consumer that shows the flow of energy and matter.

d2ebe625-271a-4fff-b7ed-a81bc0b8c2c1.title: lunar cycle
d2ebe625-271a-4fff-b7ed-a81bc0b8c2c1.description: The pattern of changes seen in the appearance of the Moon's shape over time.

050d796a-e7b1-4068-a7cd-4c0c2f33338d.title: translucent
050d796a-e7b1-4068-a7cd-4c0c2f33338d.description: Allowing some light to travel through, but not clear.

af475d27-67d0-4856-8696-6a13027cc5eb.title: transparent
af475d27-67d0-4856-8696-6a13027cc5eb.description: Allowing all light to travel through so objects behind can be clearly seen.

28c48378-5daa-4b79-8247-a22130256951.title: opaque
28c48378-5daa-4b79-8247-a22130256951.description: The quality of a material which means that light does not pass through it.

c81467f8-9383-454a-9768-b5c39ee0951b.title: consultation
c81467f8-9383-454a-9768-b5c39ee0951b.description: The involvement of representatives from the relevant Aboriginal Community(ies) in the planning, appropriate implementation and assessment of the syllabus. To pursue the idea of teaching an Aboriginal Language, a wide range of local Aboriginal organisations should be approached in person. To ensure that all owners and Custodians are reached, the consultation process should be ongoing and will take time.

ee48807c-edc4-484c-8c70-e27aebaeb62a.title: reserves
ee48807c-edc4-484c-8c70-e27aebaeb62a.description: Land reserved by the Crown for Aboriginal Peoples, established in the 19th century, administered and controlled by governments. In NSW the regulatory body was the Aborigines Protection Board.

9ddc4246-e2b5-4173-9b49-13034e6b2d5d.title: missions
9ddc4246-e2b5-4173-9b49-13034e6b2d5d.description: Living areas established initially by churches and later by the Aborigines Welfare Board, and ruled under the provisions of the Aborigines Protection Act.

4017ebca-fbf1-4766-a4b0-0792b60147da.title: Aboriginal-controlled
4017ebca-fbf1-4766-a4b0-0792b60147da.description: Local Aboriginal Community management of processes guided by locally endorsed Cultural protocols.

a539ee9e-f9ea-4fc4-a926-e779d0d14cd0.title: Community(ies)
a539ee9e-f9ea-4fc4-a926-e779d0d14cd0.description:
Community(ies) is about interrelatedness and is central to shared conceptions of belonging. Aboriginal Peoples may belong to more than one Community. Important elements of Community are identification with Country or location, family ties and shared experience.

See local Aboriginal community

a93ab88c-1d4f-4ed4-8658-9d8c6545ad28.title: Custodianship
a93ab88c-1d4f-4ed4-8658-9d8c6545ad28.description: In Aboriginal Communities, the practice of maintaining and passing on particular elements of Cultural significance, e.g. Language, stories, songs, rituals and imagery.

516e6b93-da01-41bc-ac0c-e7c854535459.title: Aboriginal enterprise
516e6b93-da01-41bc-ac0c-e7c854535459.description: These can be owned by individuals, Communities or can be an extension of an Aboriginal organisation, and are usually staffed by Aboriginal People. Aboriginal enterprises can be social enterprises or based on certain protocols such as benefit-sharing.

79fedf01-c8ac-4451-9a0a-a64aed278025.title: Aboriginal organisation
79fedf01-c8ac-4451-9a0a-a64aed278025.description: An entity with a particular purpose, which is initiated, managed and maintained by Aboriginal People. Aboriginal organisations usually provide services for the direct or indirect benefit of Aboriginal People. They are usually not-for-profit, and may be reliant on Aboriginal Community member volunteers.

1f0d2ef0-5c42-4f59-8370-0a8cd53db2a6.title: land
1f0d2ef0-5c42-4f59-8370-0a8cd53db2a6.description:
Used by Aboriginal Peoples to describe their spirituality, ecosystems, Dreaming(s), all living things, including totems, all physical factors such as sacred sites, water, air and geographical factors.

See Country/Place

76ac4435-7f6c-4d06-af21-af4d98c22921.title: invasion
76ac4435-7f6c-4d06-af21-af4d98c22921.description: The forced takeover of land and people.

1a0b15ad-aaaa-4fff-b071-d446b49cbf16.title: Customary
1a0b15ad-aaaa-4fff-b071-d446b49cbf16.description:
Relating to customs or practices associated with a particular culture, society, place or set of circumstances. Similar to the term 'traditional', 'Customary' is used in reference to aspects of Aboriginal Cultures in pre-invasion contexts.

See traditional

e27725d9-67b0-42fc-8425-cf4b024fe38b.title: dispossession
e27725d9-67b0-42fc-8425-cf4b024fe38b.description: The removal of people from their lands which had been occupied and cared for by their ancestors over thousands of years.

f9c9706e-42a7-414a-b7e1-56fb017bb319.title: racism
f9c9706e-42a7-414a-b7e1-56fb017bb319.description:
Prejudice, discrimination or unconscious bias on the basis of colour, culture or national origin.

See discrimination

334e36b9-8cb2-4317-ad23-c8e3f93db6ba.title: language revitalisation
334e36b9-8cb2-4317-ad23-c8e3f93db6ba.description: A type of language program in which the goal is to encourage younger speakers to use the target language as fluently as older speakers.

dc794e6c-0104-4548-ae0a-3ad8a1b6cbdd.title: handtalk
dc794e6c-0104-4548-ae0a-3ad8a1b6cbdd.description: A form of communication that consists of hand signs, gestures and expressions.

067b3248-5006-44d6-82c6-03019d81c022.title: research methodology
067b3248-5006-44d6-82c6-03019d81c022.description:
The methods used to identify and analyse a specific topic of research.

Indigenous Research methodology is centred on ethics, undertaken with Indigenous Peoples on collaborative projects.

d31b6b68-54cb-48d1-b614-59211b376fe0.title: traditional
d31b6b68-54cb-48d1-b614-59211b376fe0.description:
A term widely used to refer to pre-invasion Aboriginal life, Culture and social organisation, or the continuation of aspects of Aboriginal Cultures. The term ‘traditional’ must be used with care, as individuals and groups may find this term offensive. The word ‘Customary’ is often used to convey a similar message.

See Customary

3b852426-9f6e-4cc1-8abc-d6262783faae.title: Peoples
3b852426-9f6e-4cc1-8abc-d6262783faae.description:
The term ‘Peoples’ acknowledges the plurality and diversity of Aboriginal Cultures, Torres Strait Islander Cultures, and international Indigenous Cultures.

See Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

72190d28-cc44-42c9-8e52-eadbd1f23a1a.title: design solution
72190d28-cc44-42c9-8e52-eadbd1f23a1a.description: A product, service or environment that has been created for a specific purpose or intention as a result of design thinking, and design and production processes.

e934bc56-6bad-4d73-b8a9-a4817ce4a692.title: design brief
e934bc56-6bad-4d73-b8a9-a4817ce4a692.description: A statement clarifying a project task and defining the need or opportunity to be resolved. It usually identifies the users, design criteria, constraints, resources and timeframe.

d5031841-def6-4c32-ab27-1a8c0dfff094.title: universal design principles
d5031841-def6-4c32-ab27-1a8c0dfff094.description: Guidelines used to design products, spaces or systems that can be used by everyone, no matter their age, ability or background.

1ad5425b-849d-47ea-97ca-8603e2ef521f.title: incremental innovation
1ad5425b-849d-47ea-97ca-8603e2ef521f.description: Small gradual improvements made to an existing product, service or process.

cb31e6c3-393f-4699-a2a8-8910bfb0f892.title: disruptive innovation
cb31e6c3-393f-4699-a2a8-8910bfb0f892.description: Innovation that significantly changes or replaces an existing product, process or service.

a61c56d5-a717-4c91-b17e-e28fdb238720.title: radical innovation
a61c56d5-a717-4c91-b17e-e28fdb238720.description: Groundbreaking innovation that creates a new product, service or process and has a significant impact on the market or ways of doing things.

58b440fb-4b5b-41dc-ae73-ada171c9a208.title: end user
58b440fb-4b5b-41dc-ae73-ada171c9a208.description: An individual or group who will use the final product, system, environment or event in a real-life setting.

0ed66e23-c365-46cf-9550-2e86c284e841.title: entrepreneurship
0ed66e23-c365-46cf-9550-2e86c284e841.description: The process of starting and growing a business by turning ideas into opportunities. It involves identifying a need in the market, developing innovative solutions, and managing the risks and rewards to build a successful and profitable venture.

c00c8ec7-4a61-4bdb-8ead-0e2cc49c4dd2.title: strengthening (of languages)
c00c8ec7-4a61-4bdb-8ead-0e2cc49c4dd2.description: Improving the status and recognition of Aboriginal Languages, including the allocation of funding and resources, raising the prestige of the target language and the development of new words, where applicable.

fbd87553-e8cb-42b6-8f42-4a8ee818a78c.title: ecology
fbd87553-e8cb-42b6-8f42-4a8ee818a78c.description: In a languages context, ecology is used to describe the view that languages can be studied as living entities that are interrelated and that relate to their environments.

34a32d8f-f736-4db1-9068-3a6cda1a6302.title: target language
34a32d8f-f736-4db1-9068-3a6cda1a6302.description: The Aboriginal Language in which it is intended that a student will gain proficiency.

8fd0016a-4630-49b7-ad48-37f48a9012a9.title: scaffold
8fd0016a-4630-49b7-ad48-37f48a9012a9.description: A framework to support the production of original text.

930625b9-92a9-432a-9c66-ec0e6a3944ad.title: nonverbal communication
930625b9-92a9-432a-9c66-ec0e6a3944ad.description: Manually coded forms of communication in which the body is manipulated to convey meaning. These are often used in place of spoken languages. For Aboriginal Peoples nonverbal communication exists alongside spoken language(s) and are usually associated with particular Cultural protocols, e.g. relationships, ceremony, local Community.

3770121e-f6b0-412c-b681-13aa569b257d.title: perspective
3770121e-f6b0-412c-b681-13aa569b257d.description: A way of regarding situations, facts and texts, and evaluating their relative significance.

c14a1bbc-1efa-4152-af53-4bde608c6945.title: linguistic
c14a1bbc-1efa-4152-af53-4bde608c6945.description: Relating to the systematic study of language.

c428e323-1036-47ea-adb0-69158833c342.title: view/viewing
c428e323-1036-47ea-adb0-69158833c342.description: Observing and comprehending a visual text, e.g. diagram, illustration, photograph, film, television documentary, multimedia. This sometimes involves listening to and reading accompanying written text.

44114ecd-e620-4655-9172-8a600c3ba78e.title: Imperialism
44114ecd-e620-4655-9172-8a600c3ba78e.description: Ideology affecting the organisation of societies, involving a nation expanding its authority over other territories (e.g. colonisation, use of military force, economic control or by other means).

441858f2-1019-4044-9cd4-5e9e6c60852e.title: International Indigenous Peoples
441858f2-1019-4044-9cd4-5e9e6c60852e.description: Refers collectively to the first peoples of a land in international communities.

1cc052e0-ca4e-4bd5-ba3f-6bce07832b43.title: egalitarianism
1cc052e0-ca4e-4bd5-ba3f-6bce07832b43.description: The idea that all people are equal, sharing the same rights – political, social and civil.

6c0b808d-d0e1-4260-9b0c-e8a22d2e9aec.title: Chartism
6c0b808d-d0e1-4260-9b0c-e8a22d2e9aec.description: A workers’ movement established in the 1830s, named after the 6 main aims in its People’s Charter and focused on the political rights of the working classes.

956cd55b-43e9-427a-8281-7d20269d19ae.title: Magna Carta
956cd55b-43e9-427a-8281-7d20269d19ae.description: A historic charter signed in 1215 limiting the monarch’s power and establishing some legal rights to English people.

1afbdd1b-502c-49c0-8ba1-87c856393d6a.title: before common era (BCE)
1afbdd1b-502c-49c0-8ba1-87c856393d6a.description: A dating system to denote an abbreviation of ‘before common era’.

c45da144-4a0c-4a21-b553-f6f98e6e13b8.title: common era (CE)
c45da144-4a0c-4a21-b553-f6f98e6e13b8.description: A dating system used to denote an abbreviation of ‘common era’.

cd6dc678-793d-4a37-b58c-aed790ea4f0c.title: Doctrine of Discovery
cd6dc678-793d-4a37-b58c-aed790ea4f0c.description: Legal and philosophical concept that enabled European powers to claim lands inhabited by non-Christians. Key elements included papal bulls and terra nullius.

47708e9c-d1bf-4a39-986e-da51e6c368d1.title: Stolen Generations
47708e9c-d1bf-4a39-986e-da51e6c368d1.description: The generations of Aboriginal children forcibly removed from their families in the 20th century as a result of the policies of Australian governments.

7e58cd80-ddb0-4998-a32f-5456433879e5.title: constitution
7e58cd80-ddb0-4998-a32f-5456433879e5.description: The fundamental rules that establish how a country is governed, typically establishing the role and powers of parliament, the executive and the judiciary.

4a1a7ac0-848f-46f7-b263-d9bd486e9745.title: division of powers
4a1a7ac0-848f-46f7-b263-d9bd486e9745.description: Australia has 3 levels of government: federal government, state and territory government and local government. Each level has different responsibilities as outlined in the Australian Constitution.

8f5f1c95-749e-41c4-9030-6209a005d340.title: separation of powers
8f5f1c95-749e-41c4-9030-6209a005d340.description: In the Australian Constitution the separation of powers distributes the power to govern between the Parliament, the executive and the judiciary to ensure checks and balances.

21db23c7-a151-4010-8586-9a70aa7e0358.title: ANZAC
21db23c7-a151-4010-8586-9a70aa7e0358.description: Refers to the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps (ANZAC) troops who first fought at Gallipoli in Turkey from April to December 1915.

a38c795e-0100-4cb5-8daf-acb02b7c60d4.title: biomes
a38c795e-0100-4cb5-8daf-acb02b7c60d4.description: A major terrestrial region defined by its climate, vegetation and animal life.

4fe308af-7888-466a-aed2-de9d5ac3f257.title: landscapes
4fe308af-7888-466a-aed2-de9d5ac3f257.description: An area that has evolved over time, created by a combination of geological, geomorphological, biological and cultural layers.

a0ad12c5-50c4-4f5d-8340-d7a119eae279.title: landforms
a0ad12c5-50c4-4f5d-8340-d7a119eae279.description: The individual surface features of the Earth as identified by their shape.

65dd12f4-3402-4599-81e1-ffc5c8475ade.title: water resources
65dd12f4-3402-4599-81e1-ffc5c8475ade.description: A natural resource existing in different forms, irregularly distributed and useful to people and their activities.

ea2e1197-2307-422d-ba31-1362ede9f116.title: range of scales
ea2e1197-2307-422d-ba31-1362ede9f116.description: The varying frames of reference used for viewing and analysing the world in spatial terms. These are commonly described as local, national, regional and global. These scales can be used to develop an understanding of places, environments, natural and human phenomena, geographical patterns and processes, and management. They represent the geographical way of investigating the world.

07c29a3d-ee14-4588-9c4d-5da72ab9a6c4.title: liveability
07c29a3d-ee14-4588-9c4d-5da72ab9a6c4.description: An assessment of the quality of a place. The concept of liveability has been linked to a range of factors, e.g. health, sense of safety, access to services, cost of living, comfortable living standards, mobility and transport, air quality and social participation.

bfb87b83-1974-4789-943a-6086244f3106.title: photographs
bfb87b83-1974-4789-943a-6086244f3106.description: Photographs taken from different locations, e.g. from earth, in the air or from space or from different angles.

bb4b683a-7d12-4537-b7a0-c9857370bce0.title: environmental change(s)
bb4b683a-7d12-4537-b7a0-c9857370bce0.description: Alterations in natural environments over time, driven by both natural processes and human activities.

49a97a4a-8801-4f2d-bf29-a3f52a3b352c.title: tectonic activity
49a97a4a-8801-4f2d-bf29-a3f52a3b352c.description: Processes and movement associated with the Earth’s tectonic plates. These movements can cause the land to be pushed upwards, sink downwards, or be translated horizontally.

5a8578a9-7645-4762-81cd-4c26c3121a57.title: geomorphic hazard
5a8578a9-7645-4762-81cd-4c26c3121a57.description: A hazard event originating in the lithosphere, e.g. volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, tsunamis and mass movement (landslides or avalanches).

39add946-2fd1-498d-89c5-4d7fa5c04964.title: altitude
39add946-2fd1-498d-89c5-4d7fa5c04964.description: Height of a feature above sea level.

fda9d08a-fc7f-476d-9e4a-f096bf5ba7c3.title: fronts
fda9d08a-fc7f-476d-9e4a-f096bf5ba7c3.description: A boundary between 2 air masses of different temperatures and humidity.

935991b0-ff40-4e84-b820-e89f3949264e.title: local relief
935991b0-ff40-4e84-b820-e89f3949264e.description: The difference in altitude between the highest and lowest points in a small geographical area.

65d3c5fe-846c-4bce-9dd1-230e219fa7b1.title: spot heights
65d3c5fe-846c-4bce-9dd1-230e219fa7b1.description: A specific point most commonly found on a topographic map that indicates the exact elevation or altitude above sea level.

5763453e-c159-44ec-8040-736fe243885c.title: linear scale
5763453e-c159-44ec-8040-736fe243885c.description: A line on a map showing the relationship between distances on a map and distances in the real world.

7d8e5070-8562-4c5b-8f25-b2004d1f990f.title: consumption
7d8e5070-8562-4c5b-8f25-b2004d1f990f.description: The act of using or purchasing goods and services which can impact on the environment, economy, individuals and society.

ab4a49ce-c4df-4832-823f-0b141578e7c9.title: trade flows
ab4a49ce-c4df-4832-823f-0b141578e7c9.description: The movement of goods, services or capital between regions or countries.

f040b701-7478-4795-8f18-57b4541c0791.title: hydrological hazard
f040b701-7478-4795-8f18-57b4541c0791.description: A hazard event originating in the hydrosphere, e.g. floods and droughts.

c19e993a-a944-4092-ba1b-8ee9db5a7209.title: atmospheric hazard
c19e993a-a944-4092-ba1b-8ee9db5a7209.description: A hazard event, originating in the atmosphere, e.g. a storm or tropical cyclone.

38cff7a4-8fb0-4ca4-b769-d6e123bc748d.title: hydrological processes
38cff7a4-8fb0-4ca4-b769-d6e123bc748d.description: The movement of water in the Earth’s system that shapes and influences environments.

1ab3117f-b1fd-465f-ba62-adc61c4cf5d0.title: catchment area
1ab3117f-b1fd-465f-ba62-adc61c4cf5d0.description: The area drained by a river or water body. Also known as a river basin.

b5cf2205-d25a-47eb-91a9-87b792398bbe.title: water scarcity
b5cf2205-d25a-47eb-91a9-87b792398bbe.description: Lack of sufficient available water resources to meet the demand due to water shortage (physical), lack of money to use an adequate water source (economic) or unequal distribution of water resources.

1e82c54c-5766-4a30-9b29-8ea608a9e4f4.title: environmental quality
1e82c54c-5766-4a30-9b29-8ea608a9e4f4.description: Characteristics of a local environment that affect human wellbeing, such as pollution, access to open space, traffic volume, and visual effects of buildings and roads.

df073c87-4ef3-4487-9f26-e2920c347373.title: internal migration
df073c87-4ef3-4487-9f26-e2920c347373.description: The movement of people living in one defined area to another within the same country.

2758c2f1-2cf0-4909-8db6-b6b7d64224a4.title: urban planning
2758c2f1-2cf0-4909-8db6-b6b7d64224a4.description: Designing and organising the layout of cities and towns.

85e48f42-af26-4e11-9d56-80b5bf68c315.title: international migration
85e48f42-af26-4e11-9d56-80b5bf68c315.description: The voluntary or forced movement of people between countries.

6d4f8da1-f1c2-4aec-8f53-49baa154377e.title: development
6d4f8da1-f1c2-4aec-8f53-49baa154377e.description: Economic, social and political changes that improve the wellbeing of people.

a49dc84b-2ef6-414d-8f79-b4d78adacbd8.title: spatial inequality
a49dc84b-2ef6-414d-8f79-b4d78adacbd8.description: The uneven distribution of resources, opportunities or conditions across different areas.

c962f801-c5bc-4edf-a527-a81f5507ca0c.title: agricultural production
c962f801-c5bc-4edf-a527-a81f5507ca0c.description: The use of land for cultivating crops and raising livestock to produce food, fibres and industrial materials.
